title: Ghanaian entrepreneur Mary Nyamekye Asamoah wins Africa Travel 100 award
body: Ghanaian tourism and aviation entrepreneur Mary Nyamekye Asamoah has been honoured with the Africa Travel 100 Tour Operators Award 2026 at the 22nd edition of the Akwaaba Travel Market in Nigeria. Madam Asamoah, Chief Executive Officer of Spotless Travel and Tours and Spotless Aviation and Professional Training Institute, was among a select group of tourism professionals from across Africa recognised for their contributions to the continent’s travel and tourism industry. Her recognition follows years of work in aviation, travel, tourism and professional training, with a focus on creating travel experiences and empowering young people to pursue careers in the sector. Madam Asamoah’s interest in tourism and aviation began at an early age, leading her to pursue a career in the aviation industry. She started her professional career as a cabin crew member with Starbow Airline, where she gained experience in aviation, hospitality and customer service while developing a deeper passion for travel and tourism. She later transitioned into the travel and tourism industry and established Spotless Travel and Tours, through which she has organised tours for individuals and groups across Africa and beyond. The tours have provided opportunities for travellers to explore different destinations, cultures and experiences while contributing to the promotion of tourism across the continent. Driven by her entrepreneurial vision, Madam Asamoah subsequently established Spotless Aviation and Professional Training Institute to provide training and practical exposure to young people interested in aviation, hospitality and tourism. As part of the initiative, she uses an aircraft as an office and training environment to give students a practical appreciation of the aviation industry. Her work has particularly focused on equipping young people with the skills, knowledge and confidence to build careers in aviation, hospitality and tourism. The Africa Travel 100 recognition adds to her profile as a tourism and aviation entrepreneur committed to developing both the industry and the next generation of professionals. Madam Asamoah’s long-term ambition is to establish and operate her own airline, a goal she continues to pursue through her experience in aviation, tourism, travel and professional training. Her journey from cabin crew member to tourism entrepreneur and aviation educator reflects an effort to combine travel business development with skills training and youth empowerment. The Akwaaba Travel Market, one of Africa’s major travel and tourism trade events, brings together tourism stakeholders, travel professionals, destinations and industry players to promote partnerships and opportunities within the African travel market.

title: Zamfara empowers 300 youths with skills, starter packs
body: The Zamfara State Government has graduated 300 indigenes trained under the Government Enterprise and Empowerment Programme (GEEP), with each beneficiary receiving a starter pack to establish a business. The programme was implemented in partnership with the European Union (EU), the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) and other development partners to promote sustainable livelihoods and economic empowerment. The Secretary to the State Government, Malam Abubakar Nakwada, disclosed this in a statement on his social media platform after attending the graduation ceremony alongside Deputy Governor Mani Mummuni. Nakwada said the initiative reflected Governor Dauda Lawal’s administration’s commitment to equipping young people with practical skills and resources to become self-reliant. He said the administration regarded skills acquisition as a sustainable approach to tackling unemployment and improving the economic well-being of residents. “Skills acquisition is a sustainable means of empowerment and livelihood. The state government will therefore continue to equip young people with relevant skills and capital to become self-reliant and productive members of society,” he said. The SSG explained that the starter packs were intended to help beneficiaries establish businesses in their respective areas of training and contribute to the state’s economic growth. The graduation ceremony attracted government officials, representatives of development partners and beneficiaries who completed various vocational and enterprise-based training programmes. The state government said it would continue to strengthen partnerships with local and international organisations to expand youth empowerment opportunities and improve livelihoods across Zamfara.

title: Troops overrun Lakurawa enclave in Sokoto, kill terrorists
body: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have overrun a Lakurawa terrorist enclave in Waria Forest, Tangaza Local Government Area of Sokoto State, neutralising several fighters and recovering weapons and five motorcycles. The operation was conducted on Thursday, October 15, 2026, during a clearance mission aimed at dismantling terrorist hideouts and denying the group freedom of movement. The Media Information Officer of Operation Fansan Yamma, Lt. Col. Aliyu Danja, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday. Danja said troops of Sector 2 advanced through identified terrorist enclaves around Alela, Bilange and Kandam villages towards Waria Forest, where they made contact with the fighters. He said the ensuing gun battle saw the troops overpower the terrorists with superior firepower, forcing them to abandon their positions and flee deeper into the forest. According to him, the troops pursued the fleeing fighters and neutralised some of them. “Further exploitation of the area led to the destruction of the terrorists’ camps and all life-support structures, as well as the recovery of weapons and five motorcycles,” Danja said. He added that troops had maintained a strong operational presence in the area, sustaining clearance operations to deny the terrorists freedom of action and improve security in surrounding communities. Danja said the operation underscored the commitment of Operation Fansan Yamma to dismantling terrorist enclaves, denying armed groups safe havens and restoring peace and security across its joint operations area. He said the Theatre Command commended the troops for their courage, resilience and sustained operational efforts. The command also urged members of the public to support ongoing military operations by providing timely and credible information about suspicious movements and activities in their communities. The post Troops overrun Lakurawa enclave in Sokoto, kill terrorists appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Gov Lawal seeks global partnerships to transform Zamfara rural communities
body: Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal has called for stronger partnerships with international development organisations to improve living conditions in rural communities and strengthen the state’s agrarian economy. Lawal made the call while speaking at an international summit in Ethiopia, where he highlighted his administration’s commitment to sustainable development, improved social services and economic empowerment. He said his vision was to build a Zamfara where every child had access to opportunities, quality healthcare, education, adequate nutrition and a better standard of living. The governor said agriculture remained central to the state’s economy but noted that insecurity had prevented farmers in some communities from accessing their farmlands. “Zamfara State is clearly an agrarian economy. However, we have a big challenge in insecurity. And insecurity has made it difficult for farmers to access their farmlands to produce what they consume, not to talk of exports,” he said. Lawal said his administration was determined to address the challenges through investments in community-focused programmes and collaboration with development partners. He cited the state government’s partnership with UNICEF, noting that the provision of counterpart funding had helped facilitate interventions in healthcare, education and social development. “We are very conscious of keying into all the development partners. For example, UNICEF. We always contribute our counterpart funding to match whatever may come from such partners. This makes things easier to have a better livelihood,” he said. The governor stressed that development programmes should not only deliver immediate results but also remain sustainable and benefit future generations. “For every programme that we have in place, when you look at the success story, the next question is: how sustainable is that programme?” he asked. He said his participation at the summit was aimed at exchanging ideas with other leaders and learning from successful development models that could be adapted to Zamfara’s circumstances. Lawal also called for collective efforts among governments and development organisations to improve the livelihoods of rural populations. “What do we do to make this thing easy for our people, as responsible leaders for our respective communities?” he asked. He said his administration would continue to combine security efforts, social investments and partnerships with development organisations to improve living conditions across the state.

title: Ukrainian special unit destroys Russian drone operator training center, military intelligence says
body:
Ukrainian units destroyed a Russian training center for drone operators in Khorly, in occupied Kherson Oblast, Ukraine's military intelligence agency (HUR) said on Oct. 15.
Service members of the HUR special unit "Shamanbat," together with the 426th Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment, conducted an operation overngiht on Oct. 11 to destroy the training center for drone operators of Russia's 18th Combined Arms Army, HUR said .
The operation also destroyed the residence of the Russian officer corps, in particular of those training the sabotage groups of the 18th Army, HUR added.
The intelligence agency said that its operation completely destroyed the training center. In a video released together with the statement, details of the operation and its aftermath can be seen, showing several drone strikes on the training facility.
The Russian 18th Combined Arms Army was formed in August 2022 “to free up more experienced units to fight on key axes" in Ukraine, according to the U.K. defense ministry. The formation is likely "an amalgamation and uplift" of other units operating in Kherson Oblast, including the 22nd Army Corps, which normally forms the Russian garrison in occupied Crimea, the ministry said.

title: Zamfara, UNICEF train pit emptiers to sustain ODF status
body: The Zamfara State Government, in collaboration with the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), has intensified efforts to sustain the state’s Open Defecation Free (ODF) status through improved faecal sludge management. The initiative included a capacity-building programme for traditional pit emptiers and faecal sludge evacuators across Anka, Bukkuyum, Kaura Namoda and Maru local government areas. The programme was designed to improve sanitation services, protect public health and the environment, and support the state’s efforts to achieve and sustain ODF status. The training featured three days of classroom sessions and five days of practical demonstrations, equipping participants with skills in safe pit emptying, occupational health and safety, and proper faecal sludge management. Four manual emptying devices, locally referred to as “manual golfers”, alongside other innovative tools and personal protective equipment, were provided to improve the safety and efficiency of sanitation workers. The practical sessions also involved the safe emptying of 40 filled pits, with emphasis on appropriate treatment and disposal of faecal sludge. Speaking on behalf of the state government, the Programme Manager of the Zamfara State Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency (RUWATSAN), Dr Abubakar Nasir Galadima, represented by the Director of Sanitation, reaffirmed the government’s commitment to sustainable sanitation. He said safely managed sanitation was central to achieving Sustainable Development Goal 6.2, which seeks to ensure access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene for all. The government noted that achieving sustainable sanitation required more than ending open defecation, stressing that human faeces must be safely contained, emptied, transported, treated and properly disposed of or reused. Galadima highlighted the importance of behavioural change, market-based sanitation, private-sector participation, affordable services and stronger institutional capacity in achieving sustainable results. He thanked UNICEF and FCDO for supporting initiatives aimed at improving sanitation and protecting vulnerable communities across the state. The lead facilitator, Abdulsalam M. Abdullahi, said the training was designed to transform traditional pit emptiers into safer, more efficient and professional service providers. He said sanitation management did not end with the use of toilets, adding that faecal sludge must be safely managed throughout the sanitation service chain to prevent environmental contamination and protect public health. Abdullahi said the initiative would also strengthen sanitation-related livelihoods and promote organised service delivery through market-based solutions. The training brought together pit emptiers and representatives of RUWATSAN, the Zamfara State Environmental Protection Agency (ZEPIA), the Ministry of Environment, the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) and media organisations. Participants commended the state government, UNICEF, FCDO and RUWATSAN for providing the training, practical demonstrations, sanitation tools and protective equipment. The initiative is expected to help protect water sources, prevent sanitation-related diseases, safeguard workers’ health and dignity, create livelihood opportunities and sustain the state’s ODF achievements.

title: Obuasi SHTS abuse: Sanction all officials who failed to act – Moving Masculinity
body: Founder of Moving Masculinity, Esther Amarh, has called for sanctions against all officials who failed to act on allegations of sexual abuse involving female students of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. Her comments follow a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni, which revealed that municipal authorities, education officials and other influential figures had received reports concerning alleged sexual abuse by the Obuasi Senior High Technical School headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, months before his suspension. She says accountability must extend beyond the suspended headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, to every institution and official who received complaints but failed to take appropriate action to protect the students. Speaking on Joy FM’s Middaynews on Thursday, October 15, Ms Amarh called for an audit to establish which officials and institutions failed to act on the complaints, insisting that those found culpable must face consequences. “There must be consequences, not just to what the teacher or the individual did. There must be consequences to inaction. There must be an audit done of exactly who did not do what,” she said. She warned that without accountability for officials who ignore reports of abuse, similar incidents would continue to occur in schools. Ms Amarh said officials who failed to perform their duties should face measures that could affect their salaries and promotion prospects. “If you’re given tasks and you fail to do them, there are consequences to your failure to do what you have been asked to do,” she added. She argued that such sanctions must be strong enough to deter others from neglecting their responsibilities, adding that appeals to morality and conscience alone had not been sufficient to address the problem. Ms Amarh described the case as evidence of a systemic failure to protect children in schools, arguing that authorities only responded when the allegations attracted public attention. “As a nation, we should be collectively outraged by this ongoing systemic failure to protect girls, children, and boys. This sexual abuse often happens to boys as well. The only tool that these authorities paid attention to was national shame and exposure. Not conscience, not morality, not the right of those girls to have an education, and not their own structures and systems,” she said. Ms Amarh said her experience working on issues relating to sexual abuse over the past seven to nine years had shown a recurring pattern in which students reported abuse but received little or no response from authorities. “It is exactly the same scenario: a girl reports, inaction, silence, no action. It escalates, more girls, more lives ruined, more education interrupted,” she said. She urged the country to treat sexual abuse in schools as a national public health crisis rather than isolated incidents affecting individual students.

title: Gov Lawal flags off 95km road project in Tsafe to boost security
body: Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal has flagged off the construction of a 95-kilometre road in Tsafe Local Government Area, saying the project will improve security operations, facilitate transportation and stimulate economic activities. The governor performed the flag-off ceremony on Sunday for the construction of roads linking Yandoton Daji, Cediya, Doka, Yan Waren Daji, Hayin Alhaji Bedi, Unguwar Joji and Yankuzo to Tsafe, alongside five bridges. The project has been divided into two phases, with SKY Construction Company awarded the 47-kilometre first phase and Setraco Construction Company Limited handling the remaining 48 kilometres. Speaking at the ceremony, Lawal said the project covered predominantly agricultural communities that play an important role in the state’s economy. He said the government prioritised the project as part of efforts to restore peace and stability in the area. “As a responsible government, we are committed to ensuring the safety and well-being of our people. That is why we have prioritised this road project as a key intervention to restore peace and stability in Zamfara State,” he said. The governor said the road would improve the movement of goods and enhance the mobility of security agencies, thereby strengthening their operational capacity and response to threats and attacks. He added that the project was part of his administration’s broader infrastructure renewal programme aimed at reconnecting communities and addressing long-standing infrastructure deficits. Lawal cited ongoing road projects, including the Gusau-Magami-Dansadau Road, Zurmi-Rukudawa Road and Mallamawa-Bukkuyum Road, with a spur to Masamar Mudi, as part of the administration’s efforts to improve connectivity. He said the Tsafe road project was expected to go beyond transportation by stimulating economic activities, strengthening security and improving the living conditions of residents. The governor also pledged that the government would ensure timely completion of the project, given the difficult circumstances facing communities in the area. He directed the Ministry of Works and Infrastructure to ensure effective supervision, quality assurance and strict compliance with approved engineering standards. “Contractors handling government projects must understand that Zamfara State expects value for money, quality craft and infrastructure capable of withstanding the test of time,” he said. Lawal expressed optimism that the road would strengthen ties among communities and contribute to the state’s economic growth and development.

title: NATO’s provocations prompt Russia to prepare military response — envoy
body:
VIENNA, October 15. /TASS/. NATO holds nuclear exercises near Russian borders, compelling Moscow to prepare an adequate military response, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) Dmitry Polyansky said.
"NATO has launched its annual exercise Steadfast Noon to practice handling nuclear weapons. The maneuvers involve troops from the alliance’s 17 member states. NATO aircraft are practicing nuclear missions, moreover, in close proximity to Russian borders. Naturally, we are forced to prepare an adequate military response to such provocations. Any state that respects itself would behave in a similar way in our place," the Russian envoy said in a speech at a meeting of the OSCE Permanent Council, the text of which was obtained by TASS.
The diplomat said he wondered if Brussels understood that such actions could lead "to a direct nuclear conflict on the continent."

title: 2027: Atiku, Obi, Duke, Makinde no match for Tinubu, APC declares
body: …Says OBJ/Atiku spent N300b on nonexistent roads …’Ex-VP wants to scrap NELFUND while charging millions in own varsity’ By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has declared that Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Donald Duke and Seyi Makinde are no match for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election. The quartet are the presidential candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), People’s Redemption Party PRP and the Allied People’s Movement (APM), respectively. National Chairman of the party, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, made the declaration on Thursday while receiving the Forum of APC House of Representatives Aspirants, led by Hon. Danjuma Mohammed, at the party’s national secretariat in Abuja. “No political party, as it stands today, has a more credible candidate than President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. We have facts; we have records that if we put them vis-à-vis any other candidate that is on this ballot, none match our own candidate. None. I mean, none. None,” he declared. He said the opposition could not stand a side-by-side comparison of records. “Show the scorecard of other presidents, of other candidates, and then we now put them side by side Mr President, and none of them come close to matching Mr President, even in terms of building institutions.” OBJ/Atiku On roads, Yilwatda said Nigerians could not point to anything built under the ₦300 billion road budget released when Obasanjo was president and Atiku was in his government. “We were here live. When the president gave road projects of over ₦300 billion, when another person was the Minister of Works, we couldn’t find even the road that was patched with that budget. We are struggling to find the roads. “Show me one road, a span of 500 kilometres, that was constructed with that money, just one. You can’t find it, but I can pinpoint many roads across the country that were constructed just in three years,” he stated. Yilwatda then listed what he said the Tinubu administration had completed or had under construction. “From Abuja to Kaduna is over 441 kilometres. From Abuja to Kaduna to Kano, it is under construction. We are almost near completion.” On the Trans-Saharan Superhighway, he said, “We’ve done almost 30, 40 per cent of that one. Tell me, which president has done that much? And that span alone is over 1,400 kilometres of roads. Just that span alone, before you take the one from Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.” He also pointed to the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline project. “That same gas will be used for fertiliser. That same gas will be used for CNG. That same gas will take gas to homes. That same gas will fire turbines for electricity to power homes and power industries, and you tell me that Mr President has not done well?” The APC chairman also criticised Atiku’s position on the student loan scheme, which he said he would scrap if elected. “I just listened to one of the spokespersons of the ADC, your former party, who was saying, How can President Bola Ahmed Tinubu be giving ₦20,000 to students?” He said such critics were out of touch with ordinary Nigerians. “They don’t know the value of ₦20,000 to an ordinary man on the streets.” Yilwatda, a former university lecturer, said he knew the cost of school fees first-hand. “I know how many students dropped out of school because they could not afford school fees. I taught them.” He told the story of a student who saved part of the ₦20,000 monthly upkeep, bought a second-hand refrigerator and began selling iced fish to schoolmates. “That’s how that ₦20,000 naira is building homes, and somebody is saying that when he comes, the first thing he would do is scrap it.” Then he turned on the critics’ own institutions. “But they all have their universities. They charge in, you know, in millions of naira, but they come back and say that the money we are giving the students is too small. “Meanwhile, even students in those institutions have access to student loans. So we are supporting their own universities too.” Earlier, Mohammed told the APC leadership that the forum was formed in 2022 under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) “with the primary objective of uniting aspirants who participated in the party’s primary election but did not emerge as candidates.” He said its mission then was to mobilise support for Atiku and his running mate, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa. “Following subsequent political developments, many members of our forum have joined the All Progressives Congress.” Mohammed said members were “united by our resolve to support the direction of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and his Vice President, Kashim Shettima, for a second term.” The forum, he said, draws members “from across the 360 federal constituencies in Nigeria. He added: “We are not seeking to establish a parallel structure or undermine existing party organs.” He asked the party to approve and support “the production and nationwide distribution of these important campaign materials in major local languages across multiple media formats” and proposed a political conference in each of the six geopolitical zones to disseminate them. “We finally believe that united aspirants constitute a formidable political force,” Mohammed said. Yilwatda assured the group of a place in the party’s machinery. “We have a directorate that works with you already, and I will link you up with the directorate so that the work will start.” He also drew on his own electoral setbacks to urge the aspirants not to lose heart. “I contested for governorship election on the Plateau. I lost. I went to the Supreme Court. I lost at the Supreme Court. When I returned back to serve the party, I never grumbled. “ On the party’s strength, he said, “Our party has over 261,000 Exco. Just excos of the party, not to talk of members. We want to convert those numbers to victory, and we need to form that partnership. Partner with us, work with us, and victory is sure for all of us.” The post 2027: Atiku, Obi, Duke, Makinde no match for Tinubu, APC declares appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: REVENUE: Zamfara IGR rises to N32.3bn
body: Zamfara State’s Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) rose from N25.4bn in 2024 to N32.3bn in 2025, the state Auditor-General, Alhaji Abubakar Danmaliki, has said. Danmaliki disclosed this in Gusau while presenting the 2025 audited financial statements and annual audit activity report covering ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) in the state. He said his office audited 98 MDAs during the year, covering revenue and expenditure, with audit queries issued to the affected agencies. According to him, while some of the queries had been resolved, others remained outstanding. The Auditor-General said the audit identified issues relating to non-compliance with financial regulations, procurement laws and public expenditure management reforms. He, however, said the 2025 financial statements were prepared in line with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) Accrual Basis and fairly presented the state’s financial position as of December 31, 2025. Danmaliki said the audit covered the state’s financial position, financial performance, cash flow, changes in net assets or equity, budget performance, accounting policies and accompanying notes. He added that there was improved expenditure control and adherence to budgetary discipline across the MDAs during the period under review. However, he identified some areas requiring government attention, including incomplete fixed asset registers, unretired advances and imprests, and weaknesses in stores records and inventory management. He said the issues had been documented in the audit report, alongside recommendations for corrective action. Danmaliki urged accounting officers to respond promptly to audit queries and called on the government to enforce compliance with financial laws and sanction officials found to have violated financial regulations. He also recommended that all MDAs update and maintain comprehensive fixed asset registers in line with IPSAS Accrual requirements. The Auditor-General called for sustained training of accounts and audit personnel to strengthen financial management and accountability in the state. He said the reports were presented in fulfilment of his constitutional mandate under Section 125(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, and Section 85 of the Zamfara State Audit Law 2021. The reports comprised the audited general-purpose financial statements of the Zamfara State Government for the year ended December 31, 2025, and the annual audit activity report covering the state’s MDAs. Danmaliki commended Governor Dauda Lawal for supporting his office and promoting transparency, accountability and good governance. He also appreciated the State House of Assembly’s Public Accounts Committee, the Ministry of Finance and the Office of the State Accountant-General for their cooperation. The event was attended by representatives of the Head of Service, the Public Accounts Committee, the Clerk of the State House of Assembly, the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, audit officials, former auditors-general and representatives of various MDAs.

title: Defense Forces strike Rubikon personnel concentration point, drone launch base near Donetsk – General Staff
body:
The Ukrainian military have struck a concentration point for personnel of the Rubikon unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) unit in Zaporizhia region, as well as a facility used for the storage, preparation, and launch of enemy strike drones near Donetsk, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports.

title: Lucy Agyepong honoured for excellence in engineering education at maiden GAAS Women’s Awards
body: Dr Lucy Agyepong, Vice President, Institutional Advancement at Academic City University, has been recognised for her pioneering leadership in engineering education at the maiden Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences (GAAS) Women’s Awards. She received the Education Excellence award at the 1 st GAAS Women’s Awards. The Academy’s recognition of Ing. Dr Agyepong emphasises the growing importance of engineering education in preparing Ghana’s youth for a rapidly changing, technology-driven world. A citation presented to Ing. Dr Agyepong commended her pioneering leadership in engineering education, innovation, mentorship and the advancement of emerging technologies. It noted that as founding Dean of Engineering at Academic City University, she led the introduction of pioneering programmes, including Biomedical Engineering, Robotics and Artificial Intelligence. “Her leadership demonstrates the importance of creating educational environments where students can engage with new technologies, develop practical expertise and prepare themselves to contribute meaningfully to Ghana’s engineering and innovation landscape,” the citation added. Speaking after receiving the award, Ing. Dr. Agyepong expressed her appreciation for the recognition and acknowledged her students and colleagues for their support and contributions towards the achievement. “This award belongs to every student who dared to study a new field and every colleague who believed we could build something different. When we started, programmes like Robotics and Artificial Intelligence were still unfamiliar to many families, but we were convinced that Africa’s future depends on young people who can design, build and innovate with these technologies. I am grateful to GAAS for this honour,” she said. She also encouraged young women to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering and mathematics, and urged institutions to invest in mentorship. “Every young woman who walks into an engineering laboratory should see that there is a place for her and that others have gone ahead to make the path easier. “Mentorship is how we multiply impact. If each of us lifts one more girl into this field, within a few years we will have a generation of women shaping Ghana’s technological progress,” she added.

title: Ukraine and Japan plan prefabricated backup crossings for Kyiv’s bridges: 720 meters of structures already delivered
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukrainian and Japanese officials discussed establishing backup bridge crossings in the event of Russian strikes, preparing municipal infrastructure for winter, and Japan's continued assistance with Ukraine's recovery, Ukraine's Minister for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport, Mykola Kalashnyk, reported on 14 October. Russia is targeting Kyiv's bridges to paralyze the city and break civilian morale, defense analyst Hamish de Bretton-Gordon wrote in The Telegraph. On 1 and 2 October, Russia attacked Kyiv's Southern Bridge, then struck the Northern Bridge on 3 and 4 October. Ukraine is now working with international partners to establish backup bridge crossings that could maintain connectivity even if major routes are damaged. The discussions took place during a meeting between Minister Kalashnyk, Japan's Ambassador to Ukraine Yo Osumi, and Osamu Hattori, head of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) office in Ukraine, according to the statement. Ukraine's Minister for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport Mykola Kalashnyk during a meeting with Japan's Ambassador to Ukraine Yo Osumi and JICA Ukraine Office Chief Osamu Hattori, October 2026. Photo: Mykola Kalashnyk/Telegram Backup crossings could prevent logistical disruptions if major bridges are damaged Kyiv's Southern Bridge, for example, plays a critical role in logistics because freight traffic uses it, transport planning expert Dmytro Bespalov noted in an article for Ukrainska Pravda . At the same time, installing additional metal structures to reinforce bridges could be dangerous given their technical condition and existing load levels, he said. One potential solution is to establish backup bridge crossings. Ukraine and JICA have agreed to continue working together on engineering solutions for setting up these crossings. Japan has already delivered 720 meters of prefabricated bridge structures to Ukraine, which are expected to be used to create alternative routes if Russia's attacks damage major bridges, Kalashnyk said. The initiative is intended to help maintain transportation links, ensure the delivery of critical supplies, and preserve evacuation routes for civilians. The flags of Japan and Ukraine displayed on a screen during a meeting between Ukraine's Minister for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport Mykola Kalashnyk, Japan's Ambassador to Ukraine Yo Osumi, and JICA Ukraine Office Chief Osamu Hattori, October 2026. Photo: Mykola Kalashnyk/Telegram Ukraine prepares water utilities and boiler plants for winter amid the threat of Russian infrastructure strikes During the meeting, Ukraine and JICA discussed equipping water utilities with backup power supplies, addressing the need for modular boiler plants, and obtaining equipment to ensure uninterrupted heating and water services. Ukraine has already submitted lists of the necessary equipment to JICA for consideration as part of a new emergency assistance project, Kalashnyk said. An intercepted document outlining an alleged Russian plan for strikes against Ukraine this winter reportedly describes attacks on 60 critical infrastructure facilities using up to 1,000 missiles, drones, and aerial bombs. Potential targets include electrical substations, hydroelectric power plants, thermal power plants, boiler facilities, and infrastructure related to water supply and wastewater management. Kyiv during a blackout caused by Russian strikes on energy infrastructure, 11 October 2026. Photo: Yan Dobronosov The document also describes potential strikes on facilities in Kyiv, Kharkiv, Odesa, and several other cities. Such attacks could disrupt electricity, heating, water supply, and wastewater services. title: Shipments of petroleum products from Far Eastern ports hit four-year high — Bank of Russia
body:
VLADIVOSTOK, October 15. /TASS/. The highest volume of shipments of petroleum products in the last four years was recorded in August at ports in the Far East, according to the Russian Central Bank’s report.
"In August, cargo turnover at Far Eastern ports increased compared to July, being nearly a quarter higher than the 2025 average for the third consecutive month. This growth was driven primarily by liquefied gas and petroleum products. Shipments of petroleum products in August reached a four-year high despite fuel export restrictions. This was partly related to the rerouting of some supplies from southern ports to Far Eastern ports due to shipping restrictions there. Shipments of oil and coal remained high supported by steady demand from Asian countries," the report said.
LNG shipments have increased following the completion of scheduled maintenance at one of oil and gas projects on Sakhalin. In August, the number of container trains carrying imports from Far Eastern ports was double what it had been at the beginning of the year. The cost of maritime shipments from Asian countries reached an 18-month high in September.

title: One guard accused in Davitadze prison rape case left Georgia’s penitentiary service in March
body: Giorgi Varabiovi, a guard at Rustavi Prison No 6 who participated in the search of prisoner Giorgi Davitadze in a de-escalation room, handed in his resignation in March, according to the service. The service said his departure was not in any way connected to Davidatze’s case. Davitadze has claimed that prison staff raped and humiliated him in a prison de-escalation room in December 2025. ‘The person left the job of his own decision. We cannot link his departure to anything’, the service said. Varabiovi was the only guard wearing medical gloves during the incident, as seen in video footage released by the authorities, which attracted interest online. OC Media also contacted Giorgi Varabiovi for comment. This article will be updated if a response is received. Davitadze’s allegations became public on 2 October, when he raised them at the Tbilisi Court of Appeals. Prisoner alleges guards raped him, Penitentiary Service denies claim Georgia’s Penitentiary Service released footage which they claim shows officers searching and restraining Giorgi Davitadze. OC Media Lana Kokaia Before the investigation was officially closed, the Special Penitentiary Service denied the allegations and released video footage of the incident, which it said showed no violence. Public Defender Levan Ioseliani also said his office had found no evidence of physical violence in the footage. The Prosecutor General’s Office announced on Monday that it had ended its investigation into the alleged sexual assault, concluding that no violence or criminal act had taken place against Davitadze. The agency said its investigation included interviews with dozens of witnesses, analysis of hours of video footage, and several expert examinations. ‘They beat us’: More inmates claim abuse from staff as Georgia’s prisoner protests continue The inmates say they are demonstrating in solidarity with Giorgi Davitadze, who alleges prison guards raped him. OC Media Lana Kokaia Davitadze’s family disputed the findings. His parents accused Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze of influencing the investigation’s outcome, while his lawyer, Salome Januashvili, said the decision would be appealed to the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) after all domestic legal procedures had been exhausted. The allegations sparked public outcry and expressions of solidarity from other prisoners. Several detainees who protested have claimed that they were physically and verbally abused in response. Davitadze, the son of former Tbilisi City Council member Avtandil Davitadze, is serving a 17-year prison sentence after being convicted of stabbing Interior Ministry employee Shalva Peradze. His family links the alleged abuse in prison to the case involving Peradze.

title: Kremlin comments on Russian diesel coming to global markets, assets situation
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Russian diesel flowing into global markets, the situation with assets in Europe, and Ukrainian strikes on energy facilities were the main topics Thursday's briefing by Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov.
TASS has compiled the key statements made by the Kremlin representative.
- Russian President Vladimir Putin will speak via video link today at a congress of the All·Russian public organization "Business Russia."
- The remaining events on the head of state’s schedule will be non·public.
- Ukraine didn't abide by the moratorium on energy site strikes: "I would like to remind you of yesterday’s statement by Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak. He said that, in fact, there was no moratorium on Ukraine’s part. Strikes on our refineries and energy sector facilities continued during those days. This is why there is no new development here."
- The vigorous efforts of the United States and its negotiators in the peace process "are being thwarted" by Ukraine and Vladimir Zelensky personally, as they are unwilling to pursue peace: "The Kiev regime continues to carry out strikes against these [energy] facilities, thereby undoubtedly coming into serious conflict with the peace efforts of the United States and American negotiators, who are indeed making very vigorous efforts to somehow move the peace process forward."
- Moscow is not aware of alleged attempts by the United States to unblock Russian assets in Europe by taking them under its management, as reported by the Financial Times: "We know nothing about this. These are the issues on the agenda of the dialogue between the Americans and Europeans, as stated in media reports."
- "We don’t know how reliable these reports are."
- The situation on the global energy markets is now complicated and tenuous, which is due, among other things, to restrictions on the export of Russian oil and petroleum products: "Indeed, the energy markets and oil markets are currently on shaky ground globally. Many factors contribute to this downturn in the energy market. This includes, of course, Russia’s inability to bring significant volumes of its oil and petroleum products to the export markets."
- The Kremlin did not disclose the countries that expressed the desire to buy Russian diesel fuel in addition to the United States. "It’s hardly worth discussing this in public, for obvious reasons."
- The entry of Russian diesel into the global energy markets will contribute to their stabilization, although it won’t be able to stabilize them completely: "At the moment, fairly large quantities of diesel are being released. This diesel has begun to enter global markets, and this will have a certain positive effect on the stabilization of the oil markets. Although it won’t be able to fully stabilize them - this also needs to be taken into account."
- The position of European countries regarding the agreement between Russia and the United States on diesel is pernicious: "We continue to see a destructive position on the part of European countries. They not only did not welcome this deal, they subjected it to rather harsh criticism -- both personally US President Donald] Trump and similar decisions by the American administration."
- There is currently no information about the alleged imminent visit to Russia by US emissaries Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner: "There is no information on this matter yet."
- The European Union’s attempts to block Russian athletes’ access to international sports competitions run counter to the ideals of Olympism and the principle that sports should lie outside the framework of politics: "This goes against the ideals of Olympism; against the general understanding that sport should be outside of politics. As such, this is an attempt to politicize sport and is unacceptable from the perspective of Olympism and from the perspective of the status of the host country, the country that is hosting international competitions."
- By not allowing Russian athletes to participate in international competitions, the EU is trying to influence their outcome: "Here we can see attempts by certain countries to influence the outcome of the competitions by deliberately excluding the strongest athletes from the competitions."
- The Russian gymnasts who were denied Dutch visas to compete at the World Championship in Rotterdam are the best in the world, and everyone knows that: "I want to remind you that our gymnasts, those who were denied visas, are actually the strongest in the world, they went there to win the championship. Everyone in the know is aware of that."
- Moscow will continue talks with international sports federations to defend the interests of its athletes: "The Russian side will continue its contacts with international sports federations, with the IOC (International Olympic Committee - TASS), with other international sports authorities to protect the interests of our athletes.

title: October 7 families to hold mass rally demanding state inquiry three days before Israeli elections
body: Just three days before the Knesset elections, the October Council will protest at Hostage Square at 7:30 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 24, it announced on the third anniversary of the October 7 massacre.The rally is “intended to place the demand of the October 7 families – for a full investigation into the failure, the determination of responsibility, and the drawing of lessons – at the center of the public agenda,” the October Council said in a statement.The rally will be led by bereaved families, former hostages and their families, and residents of the Gaza Envelope, as well as citizens who have been advocating alongside the council for more than two years to demand the establishment of a state commission of inquiry into the events of October 7.The rally will be attended by the leaders of the political parties who have pledged to establish a state commission of inquiry. Yashar's Gadi Eisenkot; B'Yachad co-leaders Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid; Yisrael Beiteinu chairman Avigdor Liberman; and Democrats leader Yair Golan are reportedly expected to attend.The council has marked it as the “last major public event” before the elections.Hostage families demand establishment of a state commission of inquiry, backed by party leaders The council is composed of more than 1,500 bereaved families, former hostages, and survivors of the massacre and previously accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's circle of attempting to erase the memory of the October 7 attack. The council has repeatedly called for the establishment of a state commission of inquiry to investigate the October 7 attack, reportedly asserting that “those who deny its significance should not be allowed to bury the truth”.The state commission of inquiry has the capacity to conduct comprehensive investigations and make recommendations that are both personal and systemic.Despite Netanyahu's repeated pledges that those responsible, himself included, would be held to account, Israel has yet to establish a commission of inquiry into the intelligence, military, and political failures surrounding October 7. Legislation proposing a coalition-backed, politically appointed commission of inquiry passed its first reading in the Knesset in July 2026. The bill passed with 59 votes in favor, with the opposition boycotting the vote and arguing that the legislation was an attempt to block a genuine investigation by a state commission.The bill did not complete its final readings before the Knesset dissolved. However, the coalition brought it to a first reading so it could be carried over under the continuity law and resume in the next Knesset.Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

title: AFCON 2027: Sports Minister ‘convinced’ Black Stars will qualify despite losing opening two games
body: Sports and Recreation Minister Kofi Iddie Adams says he remains confident that the Black Stars will qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), despite losing their opening two matches in the qualifiers. Ghana sit at the bottom of Group C after a 2-0 defeat to Ivory Coast in Bouaké and a disappointing 4-2 loss to The Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium. The back-to-back defeats have also led to the departure of former Portuguese head coach Carlos Queiroz as tactician of the senior national team. “I must admit that nobody would want to be in my situation when the Black Stars played against The Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium,” Adams said while speaking on Asempa FM. “It was difficult to watch the team lose. I could not believe what happened, but I am convinced the team will qualify for the AFCON tournament,” he added. Ghana will face Somalia in a double-header at the Accra Sports Stadium in November, with the Black Stars needing victories to revive their qualifying campaign. A temporary technical team is expected to be set-up for the upcoming games. The 2027 AFCON tournament will be co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

title: Cyber hit on a defence prime would cost capacity, warns MP
body: A cyber attack on the scale of the one that stopped Jaguar Land Rover would, if it struck a defence prime or a munitions supplier, take British industrial capacity out of the fight as well as money out of the economy, the Labour MP Graeme Downie has told the UK Defence Journal. Downie, the member for Dunfermline and Dollar, was asked what an attack of that size against a defence manufacturer would mean for the country. “I think the implications are the same, but with the added that you’ve probably taken down or reduced direct UK industrial capacity,” he said. “That obviously has a short-term impact, but also then huge knock-on effects to supply chain, availability of skills, raw materials, and lots of other things. So it would be a more direct attack, but it would nonetheless still have a huge economic impact, and then possibly knock on down to our industrial capacity.” The comparison he was working from is the attack on Jaguar Land Rover, which his report identifies as the costliest cyber attack in British history. Downie said its effects travelled a long way past the company’s own balance sheet. “What was striking is not only did that meaningfully affect UK GDP, reducing it by I think it was 0.1 per cent, in an economy that’s only growing by you know 1 per cent a year, that’s a significant number,” he said. “It’s noteworthy that it also affected Bank of England interest rate decisions and could have delayed an interest rate cut because of the performance of the economy. So not only was it costly to a large British company and all of the knock-on to supply chain and everything else, but that actually hit British mortgage payers potentially and cost them money.” Asked what defence firms themselves could do about the risk while government works out how to measure it, Downie said the burden does not sit with them. “I don’t think there’s anything defence firms can do in the meantime. I think at the moment this is something that really is on government to start publishing the cost of attacks,” he said. “I think there’s probably things government can do with businesses to not compel them to publish the cost of a cyber attack, for example, because that is difficult. But I think you can probably compel them much faster to have in place the right protections against cyber attack, and I think government just needs to be much quicker and more proactive.” His prescription for the National Cyber Security Centre is that it should arrive without being asked, and leave with a number. “NCSC and other parts of government need to be much stronger at not only being there to assist when asked, but actually going in and assisting, not only to fix the problem as they did with JLR, for example, but also, while we’re here, we are going to find out how much this has cost your business, and then find a way to publish that.” Downie’s report puts the cost of Russian hostile activity to the British economy at between £2 billion and £2.5 billion, a figure that excludes the additional defence spending the Russian threat has driven. He said the exclusions were deliberate and the real number is a good deal larger. “What we did with all the figures was we took very conservative estimates because I wanted to make sure these figures were credible and were only what we could absolutely find,” he said. “I’m hoping that we will have more information out in the coming weeks and months as other information becomes available to us. I think it will be significantly bigger. But as I say, what’s important is that we don’t start spreading misinformation and unattributed sources. I think we’ve got to be really careful as we’re introducing this concept to the British public about how much Russian activity costs us.” The Jaguar Land Rover attack halted production for weeks from the end of August last year and has been estimated by the Cyber Monitoring Centre at around £1.9 billion, the largest figure it has put on a single cyber event in the United Kingdom. Britain’s defence manufacturers sit on the same kind of integrated production systems, with the added exposure of long single-source supply chains for forgings, energetics and specialist components, where the loss of one plant for a few weeks cannot be made up elsewhere. One of the four recommendations in The Putin Tax , published this month, asks the Ministry of Defence to begin costing physical attacks on British interests. The post Cyber hit on a defence prime would cost capacity, warns MP first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Kuwait drone shield to cover the sea as well as the air
body: The counter-drone system Kuwait is buying from the British firm MARSS will defend against seaborne drones along the coast as well as airborne ones, using sonar alongside radar and electro-optical sensors feeding a network of command centres, according to the company. MARSS, an EOS company, will act as prime contractor and systems integrator on the £370 million contract, installing sensors across a network of sites that report into central command centres. Its NiDAR command and control platform fuses that data into threat assessments and provides what the company describes as hemispherical coverage against airborne and coastal seaborne drones. The contract also covers an initial supply of hard-kill interceptors and soft-kill jammers. Johannes Pinl, chief executive of MARSS, said: “Countering drones and aerial threats is not about any single system. It is about an intelligent, layered architecture that detects, decides and defeats within seconds, and MARSS has built exactly that. “Over the coming 24 months, MARSS will integrate the sensors and effectors that protect Kuwait’s people, critical infrastructure and national assets, backed by British engineering and new skilled jobs here in the UK.” Doctor Andreas Schwer, chief executive of EOS, said: “Air defence is being redefined by the drone. Nations can no longer afford to answer low-cost threats with high-cost interceptors, and they need integrated systems that can respond faster than the threat. MARSS’ NiDAR is the intelligence layer in EOS’ counter-drone strategy, connecting sensors and effectors into a single, scalable architecture. Kuwait’s decision to deploy this capability nationwide shows where the market is heading, and it positions EOS as a leading provider of integrated counter-drone defence.” Having both soft-kill and hard-kill effectors run through the same command system gives operators layered defeat options and a choice of response for each engagement, the company said, with NiDAR using AI to classify threats automatically and recommend an engagement, shortening the time between detection and defeat. MARSS said the contract builds on NiDAR systems it has already fielded in the Gulf, which it said have been in operational use throughout the recent crisis in the region, and extends that approach to a national scale. Delivery will be phased over 24 months and followed by a multi-year integrated logistic support programme. A training package running over several months will put MARSS personnel on the ground to train Kuwaiti operators across the sensors, the effectors and NiDAR itself, and a team will deploy to Kuwait for the duration, with recruitment already under way. The commercial side of the deal was announced by the Ministry of Defence earlier, including the £370 million value, the roughly one hundred jobs expected across MARSS and its British supply chain, production proposed for Bristol, and the contract’s place within Taskforce Sabre, the government and industry effort to help Gulf states buy what they need quickly. Britain has already supplied Kuwait with the Rapid Sentry ground-based air defence missile system, and the Royal Air Force’s ORCUS counter-drone system is operating in the country. NiDAR itself covers air, surface, sub-surface and land, detecting, tracking and classifying threats and recommending responses, and MARSS says it has more than sixty deployments worldwide. The company has been working on AI-enabled command and control for around twenty years, including research with the European Union, NATO and defence agencies. EOS is an Australian group listed on the ASX with divisions covering defence and space. Its defence products include remote weapon stations, high energy laser weapons and drone interceptors, and NiDAR sits inside that portfolio as the command layer. MARSS is exhibiting NiDAR at SOFEX in Jordan from 27 to 29 October, where it will be shown integrated onto vehicle platforms alongside EOS remote weapon stations. The post Kuwait drone shield to cover the sea as well as the air first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Breaking: Nigeria’s inflation rate drops to 14.63%
body: The headline inflation rate fell by 0.76 percentage point to 14.63 per cent in September from 15.39 percent in August 2026, representing the third consecutive month of decline since June. The development was driven by a further ease in the core basket to 13.29 per cent in August from 13.29 per cent in August. The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) disclosed this today in its Consumer Price Index (CPI) report for September 2026. NBS said: “In September 2026, the headline inflation rate stood at 14.63%, down from 15.39 per cent in August 2026, and stood at 20.98 per cent in the same month of the preceding year (September 2025). “Looking at the movement, the September 2026 headline inflation rate showed a decrease of 6.35 per cent compared to the September 2025 (20.98 per cent) headline inflation rate. “On a month-on-month basis, the headline inflation rate in September 2026 was 0.06 per cent, which was 0.65 percentage points lower than the rate recorded in August 2026 (0.71 per cent). “This means that in September 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was lower than the rate of increase in the average price level in August 2026. Likewise, food inflation declined by 0.02 percentage points to 19.59 per cent in September from 19.57 per cent in August. The post Breaking: Nigeria’s inflation rate drops to 14.63% appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Wide majority of Americans oppose livestreaming Hasan execution: ABC/Post/Ipsos poll
body:
A slim majority support the Fort Hood shooter's execution by firing squad.
Eight in 10 Americans say the execution of former Army officer Nidal Hasan, who was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding another 32 in a 2009 shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, should not be livestreamed , according to an ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll conducted using Ipsos' KnowledgePanel .
The poll, released Thursday morning, came out just hours before President Donald Trump announced the livestream will no longer take place.
"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," Trump wrote in a social media post Thursday.
Hasan described the attack as an act of jihad and is scheduled to be executed in December at the same base where he committed the attack. Trump approved an execution by firing squad , which would be the Army’s first execution since 1961.
Last week, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth vowed to make the execution public and confirmed it would be livestreamed. But Trump and his advisers were mulling whether to no longer livestream Hasan's execution , sources familiar with the matter told ABC News, amid a hesitancy over whether broadcasting the execution could super charge anti-American propaganda or reflect poorly on the U.S.
Vice President JD Vance said last week that he wasn't sure whether there would be a livestream , adding that he wouldn’t watch it if there were.
The Pentagon had earlier maintained that the livestream was going to move forward, with a Defense official saying Tuesday in a statement: "The Secretary is correct. It will be live streamed. Details will follow."
The Department of Defense did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump's cancellation of the livestream.
The military has not used a firing squad for an execution since 1945. Officials had been preparing to use lethal injection if Trump authorized an execution, according to internal documents reviewed by ABC News.
Majorities across partisan groups oppose livestreaming Hasan’s execution including 91% of Democrats, 83% of independents and 64% of Republicans. About a third of Republicans say Hasan’s execution should be livestreamed on the internet.
Clear majorities of almost all demographic groups say Hasan’s execution should not be livestreamed.
Even 69% of those who support Hasan’s execution by firing squad do not think it should be livestreamed.
A 55% majority of MAGA Republicans -- who make up about 6 in 10 Republicans -- say Hasan’s execution should not be livestreamed. That grows to 79% among non-MAGA Republicans.
And 65% of those who voted for Trump in 2024 said Hasan’s execution should not be livestreamed, along with 51% of those who strongly approve of how Trump is handling his presidency.
Although there’s wide opposition to streaming Hasan’s execution, Americans do not feel the same way about his actual execution: A slim 53% majority of Americans supports Hasan’s execution by firing squad while 42% oppose it.
Support for the death penalty for people convicted of murder overall is on a downward trend over the past three decades. It peaked at about 8 in 10 in 1988 and 1994, but fell to 6 in 10 by 2013, according to Gallup polling . By last October, 52% of Americans favored the death penalty for someone convicted of murder.
In 1985, Gallup found 62% of Americans saying that the death penalty was a deterrent to murder and 31% saying it was not. By 2004, that had flipped: 35% said the death penalty was a deterrent and 62% said it was not.
There are wide partisan divisions on Hasan's execution with 8 in 10 Republicans in support, along with half of independents and about one-third of Democrats. A 64% majority of Democrats oppose Hasan’s execution by firing squad.
MAGA Republicans are the most likely to support Hasan’s execution by firing squad (87%). Seven in 10 non-MAGA Republicans support Hasan’s execution by firing squad.
More men (60%) than women (46%) support Hasan’s execution by firing squad, and more adults 50 and older (58%) support it than those under 50 (48%).
Americans with a college education are split roughly evenly on whether Hasan should be executed by firing squad, but those without a college degree support it by a 55% to 37% margin.
See PDF for full results and detailed methodology.
Methodology: This ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll was conducted Oct. 9-13, 2026, among 2,545 U.S. adults and has an error margin of +/- 2 percentage points overall, but larger among subgroups.
ABC News’ Liz Schreier and Steve Beynon contributed to this report.
Email ABCNEWS.Polls@abc.com to be added to ABC News’ polling distribution list.
More ABC News polls can be found at abcnews.com . Media contacts: Jeannie Kedas and Van Scott .
