title: CUTS welcomes VAT collection on cross-border digital services, urges fair treatment of Distance Learning students on overseas programmes
body: A leading research and public policy think tank CUTS International, Accra, has welcomed the implementation of real-time tax collection on taxable cross-border digital services as a necessary step towards protecting Ghana’s revenue base and ensuring fair competition. CUTS also commended the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) for the dispute resolution arrangements for wrongful deductions, while urging Government to review the treatment of tuition for recognised foreign distance learning programmes. The combined charge commonly described as “20% VAT” comprises 15% VAT, the 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy and the 2.5% Ghana Education Trust Fund Levy. Real-time collection does not introduce a new tax on these services. Collection through participating payment providers improves enforcement of existing tax obligations on qualifying digital services. The use of an online payment channel alone should never determine tax liability. Exempt supplies must retain their exemption. Digital delivery must not erode the tax base As purchases move from physical products to electronic delivery, Ghana’s tax administration must follow the underlying consumption. Otherwise, a growing share of spending would escape collection, leaving a widening revenue gap and placing more pressure on businesses and consumers already meeting their obligations. Microsoft Office illustrates the point. A customer purchasing a genuine Microsoft Office CD from a VAT-registered local retailer paid VAT as part of the taxable sale. The same customer now downloads software or pays for a Microsoft 365 subscription online. Electronic delivery changes the distribution method. Collecting tax on the taxable digital purchase applies the consumption tax principle to the modern form of the product. “A software purchase should not escape tax because the customer receives a download instead of a CD. As commerce moves online, tax collection must follow. Leaving taxable digital imports outside effective collection would create a growing hole in Ghana’s revenue base,” said Appiah Kusi Adomako, Esq., Director, West Africa Regional Centre of CUTS International. Similar changes have occurred with music albums and films once bought on CDs or DVDs and now accessed through paid streaming services. Video games once purchased on discs now arrive through downloads and subscriptions. Antivirus software once sold in boxed packages now renews online. In each case, the relevant comparison is between taxable supplies serving similar needs, subject to the applicable legal exemptions. Effective collection also supports fair competition. Ghanaian suppliers accounting for VAT should not lose customers because competing foreign suppliers avoid collecting the same tax on comparable taxable services. A broader, fairly administered tax base reduces unequal treatment between businesses selling into the same market. Revenue must support public services and fiscal stability “Taxes are the subscription we pay to live in a civilised society. Government finances Free SHS and other social interventions through public revenue, including taxes. Individuals and businesses will feel the cost of this implementation, but a broader tax base helps Ghana raise its tax-to-GDP ratio, finance development and reduce dependence on borrowing from international capital markets,” Mr. Adomako said. CUTS stressed the matching duty on Government to spend prudently, reduce waste and account publicly for revenue. Stronger collection supports fiscal stability when accompanied by sound expenditure management. Banks and suppliers should disclose the service price, statutory taxes and bank charges separately so customers understand each deduction. Wrongful deductions require prompt redress CUTS commended the GRA’s provision for addressing wrongful charges through participating banks and payment providers. “A tax system earns public trust when errors are corrected quickly. The GRA deserves commendation for including a resolution process. Banks must make complaints easy to submit, give customers reference numbers and refund wrongful deductions promptly,” Mr. Adomako said. CUTS urged the GRA to publish clear complaint channels, resolution deadlines and an escalation route for unresolved cases. Customers should retain invoices and transaction records. Banks and foreign suppliers must coordinate collection so a customer does not pay Ghanaian VAT twice on the same supply. Distance learning requires equal treatment CUTS is concerned about applying the combined charge to tuition for recognised foreign distance learning programmes while comparable qualifying education supplied by approved institutions in Ghana benefits from VAT exemption. The fairness of the policy must reflect the nature of the education and the recognition of the provider, rather than the location of its teaching platform. The University of London provides a concrete example. Its detailed Ghana tax notice states the University has registered with the GRA and lists 15% VAT plus two levies of 2.5% each, producing a combined 20% charge on payments from students resident in Ghana from since 2022. This is collection under Ghanaian requirements, rather than a separate UK tax on Ghanaian students. “Two students living in Ghana and pursuing comparable recognised qualifications deserve fair tax treatment. Charging one student because the university delivers the course from abroad, while exempting comparable tuition supplied locally, raises a serious question of equity. Education policy should support access to skills,” Mr. Adomako said. Distance learning enables students to pursue qualifications while working and meeting family responsibilities in Ghana. Higher tuition costs risk excluding learners unable to afford overseas residence or travel. Recognised degree and professional programmes need separate consideration from general commercial content subscriptions. CUTS called on the Ministry of Finance, the GRA and the Ministry of Education to clarify the current exemption rules and establish a transparent route for recognising qualifying foreign distance learning programmes for equivalent treatment. Where legislation requires amendment, Government should pursue the necessary change. Any relief should use clear accreditation criteria and cover the relevant levies as well as VAT. The GRA should also reconcile supplier collection with bank collection, including payments to universities already charging Ghanaian taxes. Any duplicate or otherwise wrongful deduction must be refunded. CUTS supports effective collection on taxable digital consumption and urges Government to apply the same commitment to fairness when reviewing education charges.

title: Trump's Envoy for Global Partnerships: Sport can reopen doors that politics kept closed
body:
- During their recent telephone conversation - marking the resumption of regular high-level contacts - President Donald Trump and President Vladimir Putin agreed to foster closer relations between our countries, including in the realm of sports. Specifically, the presidents expressed support for organizing friendly matches between leading Russian and American hockey players from the KHL and NHL in both nations. Do you believe this idea has the potential to materialize?
- Yes, I believe it can materialize. President Trump understands that sport can reopen doors that politics has kept closed. Hockey is a natural place to begin because the United States and Russia share extraordinary talent, history and respect for the game.
But we should not stop at hockey. Football is the world's game, and with FIFA and the relevant national federations, I would also welcome an international friendly between our two national teams.
Perhaps sooner rather than later, our great nations can meet again on a football pitch - not to pretend that one match can resolve every disagreement, but to show that competition can reopen conversation.
Football unites the world because it belongs to everyone. My role in Global Partnerships is to help turn good ideas into practical conversations. Hockey and football can both remind us that rivalry does not have to mean hostility.
- As the US President's Special Representative, you have repeatedly publicly advocated for the reinstatement of the Russian flag and anthem at international sports competitions. How do you assess Russia's prospects of participating fully and without restrictions at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics?
- I have consistently supported the principle that athletes should not become permanent substitutes for political negotiations. The return of the Russian flag and anthem for Paralympians in Italy was a meaningful step, and I welcomed it. I am optimistic that continued progress can create a credible route toward fuller Russian participation at Los Angeles 2028.
America should host Games that are secure, fair and open to every eligible athlete. That would reflect President Trump's confidence in American leadership and Secretary Rubio's belief in practical engagement backed by clear rules.
- Russian and American athletes have a long-standing tradition of competing for top honors in numerous sports - hockey, basketball, swimming, running, figure skating, gymnastics, and others. Do you think that the absence or limited participation of Russian athletes in major international competitions diminishes the value of victories for American athletes, depriving them of strong and worthy opponents?
- The best champions want to beat the best. When major athletes are absent for reasons unrelated to their individual conduct, the competition loses something and the public knows it. That does not take away the medals earned by American athletes, who compete under the rules placed before them, but the greatest victories are the ones achieved against the strongest possible field. American and Russian athletes have elevated one another for generations. Real competition creates respect, and respect is one of the few diplomatic currencies that never loses value.
- Amidst the widespread politicization of sports, is there an opportunity for the United States and Russia to set an example of fair and equal cooperation? How can we demonstrate that the true spirit of sport remains alive and well? What concrete steps can be taken to achieve this goal?
- Yes. The United States and Russia can compete fiercely while cooperating fairly. The first steps should be practical: establish a joint sports working channel, develop the proposed hockey series, explore a FIFA international friendly between our national football teams, restore youth and coaching exchanges, support university competitions, invite retired champions to serve as goodwill ambassadors and create clear pathways for eligible athletes to return under transparent rules.
President Trump believes in peace through strength and in agreements that produce visible results. Sport offers exactly that kind of opportunity. We do not need to agree on everything before athletes and fans are allowed to meet. Perhaps sooner rather than later, the first whistle on a football pitch can begin a new conversation. Sometimes the handshake after the match is what makes the next diplomatic step possible.
- You met Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyaryov in Bishkek recently. How did that meeting go, and what issues did you discuss?
- I had a constructive and direct conversation with Minister Degtyaryov. We discussed sport, Los Angeles 2028 and the potential for sporting engagement between Americans and Russians. I came away believing there is an opportunity here.
The United States and Russia have produced some of the greatest athletes in history And I think we sometimes forget what an extraordinary achievement that is.An elite athlete can spend ten, fifteen or twenty years preparing for moments that may last only seconds or minutes.
President Trump has always believed in celebrating excellence and winners. Sport is one of the purest places where you can see what excellence requires.
And great athletes understand something else. You can desperately want to defeat your opponent and still respect him. That lesson is valuable far beyond sport. That is why I believe we should think bigger.
I would like to see an American-Russian football match. National teams if the circumstances allow it. If that cannot happen immediately, then explore a legends match or another exhibition format.
Bring young players around it. Bring coaches together. Give children in both countries the opportunity to meet athletes they admire.
- Do you plan further meetings with Russian officials? Would you like to travel to Russia for talks?
- If there is a serious purpose and the proper channels support it, yes, I would go to Moscow. I am not interested in travelling simply for a photograph. I am interested in whether something useful can be accomplished.
That is one of the qualities I admire about President Trump's approach. He is willing to talk. He is willing to negotiate. But ultimately he asks: what is the result?
Secretary Rubio brings that same focus to American diplomacy - clarity about American interests combined with a willingness to engage seriously when engagement can produce something.
Let's explore an American-Russian football match. Let's explore serious American-Russian hockey cooperation. Let's build on what has already happened in wrestling.
President Trump and President Putin have already discussed American-Russian hockey games. That creates an interesting starting point.
I would particularly like to explore a USA-Russia Hockey Legends event.
Think about what that could represent. Great American champions. Great Russian champions. The athletes people grew up watching.
Then put young players around them. Coaching clinics. Youth exchanges. Meetings between academies.
Alexander Ovechkin is an obvious example of the extraordinary connection sport can create.
A Russian athlete came to Washington and earned the admiration of millions of Americans through performance, longevity and dedication.
American athletes have built the same respect internationally.
People recognize excellence. That is powerful. I would like us to use it.
Football gives us enormous global reach. Hockey gives us a remarkable shared tradition.
Wrestling has already proven that Americans and Russians can meet and compete.
And then we can look beyond those three sports.
Why shouldn't the United States and Russia create more opportunities for their athletes and young people to meet?
We do not have to agree on every political question before an American child can kick a football with a Russian child.
We do not have to solve every diplomatic dispute before two Olympic champions can sit together and tell young athletes what it takes to become great.
These ideas are exploratory. I am not announcing confirmed teams, dates or venues.
But I am saying very clearly that I believe they are worth pursuing.
My job in global partnerships is to find serious opportunities, open doors, bring credible people together and help move good ideas toward execution.

title: Russian Activist Fined Over ‘Party of Crooks and Thieves’ T-Shirt
body:
A court in the Russian city of Kostroma has fined an activist for displaying “extremist symbols” over a photograph of him wearing a T-shirt with a slogan mocking the ruling United Russia party, the RusNews news outlet reported .
Andrei Tarasov, a former parliamentary candidate for the liberal Yabloko party, was fined 1,000 rubles ($12) by Kostroma’s Sverdlovsky District Court. The T-shirt bore the words “I’m against the party of crooks and thieves” alongside an image of a person kicking a bear, United Russia’s symbol.
An expert enlisted by the Interior Ministry deemed the slogan extremist on the grounds that it was attributed to the late Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny.
The expert’s assessment said the phrase “delegitimized the ruling party in the eyes of voters” and “serves as a marker of opposition affiliation.”
The case followed a complaint by Communist Party member Sergei Shpotin, who ran for governor of the Kostroma region in 2025.
Shpotin complained that his fellow party members were being “dragged through the courts” while “this new liberal gets away with absolutely everything.”
The phrase “party of crooks and thieves” has long been used to describe United Russia. Opposition politician Boris Nemtsov used it during a Radio Liberty broadcast in 2010, and Navalny later popularized it on his LiveJournal blog.
The slogan was widely adopted by opposition groups and individual voters during the 2011 parliamentary election campaign.
Banners, flags and stickers reading “Down with the party of crooks and thieves” became a familiar sight at mass protests in 2011-2012, held against the backdrop of Vladimir Putin’s planned return to the presidency.
A June 2012 poll by the independent Levada Center found that 42% of respondents agreed with the description of United Russia as the “party of crooks and thieves.”

title: Shield AI Delivers First V-BAT to Taiwan Coast Guard
body: Shield AI delivers the first V-BAT autonomous aircraft to the Taiwan Coast Guard Administration, enhancing maritime domain awareness with partner AIDC. Shield AI press release Defense-tech company Shield AI announced the first delivery of its V-BAT to the Taiwan Coast Guard Administration (CGA) with its partner Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC). Over the coming months, twelve V-BATs will be delivered to the CGA. Shield AI’s V-BATs were competitively selected by the CGA in July 2026 for its “Shipborne UAV” program. On October 7, the CGA presented its newly arrived V-BATs at the Port of Taipei to Minister Kuan Bi-Ling of the Ocean Affairs Council and Secretary General Joseph Wu of the National Security Council. Shield AI engineers demonstrated aircraft setup within minutes, displaying V-BAT’s ease of operations and advanced technological capabilities for maritime security. CGA will utilize V-BAT as a ship-based capability to maintain persistent Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) for surveillance, coastal patrols and law enforcement operations. Vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft eliminate the need for runways and improve deployment flexibility while optimizing costs and reducing personnel requirements. Partnering to build local expertise, Shield AI will train Coast Guard operators and maintenance personnel while simultaneously creating a robust localized support system for the V-BATs with AIDC. “V-BAT will give Taiwan’s Coast Guard the maritime domain awareness and intelligence picture needed across the Taiwan Strait and its maritime borders,” said Brandon Tseng, Shield AI president and co-founder. “V-BAT already does this for the U.S. Coast Guard, helping intercept more than 100,000 pounds of narcotics last year alone. Extending those same capabilities to Taiwan helps keep the Strait safe from illegal activity and hostile actors. It gives Taiwan the sovereignty it needs to protect its own waters.” Last year, Shield AI and AIDC entered into an agreement to advance Taiwan’s sovereign defense capabilities, strengthen its aerospace industrial base, and enhance collaborative technological innovation. The companies have engaged in strategic collaboration through sustainment, training, autonomy integration, and other technical initiatives to ensure Shield AI’s products can be deployed, supported, and scaled in Taiwan. “CGA’s V-BAT adoption demonstrates what can be achieved by combining Shield AI’s world-class technology with AIDC’s localized expertise. Shield AI has strengthened its local presence and footprint in Taiwan over the past year and consistently shown its willingness to integrate, sustain and support advanced autonomous systems in Taiwan with local partners. This gives us the reassurance that it is not just delivering a capability but is also vested in helping build the local expertise and infrastructure that will enhance our maritime security for years to come,” said Jennifer Chuang, President of AIDC. V-BAT is a Group 3 uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) featuring a ducted-fan design, more than 12 hours of endurance, and a heavy-fuel engine. Designed, tested, and deployed for contested electronic warfare environments, V-BAT delivers ISR and targeting capability at significantly lower cost and logistical burden than larger systems. Its single-engine, enclosed-rotor design enables safe, unassisted launch and recovery from ship decks, urban rooftops, and austere environments, making it particularly effective for maritime and expeditionary operations. The post Shield AI Delivers First V-BAT to Taiwan Coast Guard appeared first on Naval News .

title: Online ads helped deliver Israeli spyware to devices visiting Al Jazeera, 120,000 websites
body: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday.Its services gave Israel's Candiru, a spyware company blacklisted by the US government, and other Israeli surveillance firms access to advertising platforms run by Google, Comcast, Russia's Yandex, and others, according to separate reports from the Canadian cyber watchdog group Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant.The reports show how the online advertising business, long a subject of privacy concerns, can also serve as a channel for sweeping espionage campaigns."The way online advertising works today is a systemic security threat," Wolfie Cristl, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, told Reuters. "For states, the private sector, civil society, and everyone else alike."Discover-Tech's online ads, often for ordinary products such as phones or earpods, reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its various partnerships, Citizen Lab said.Discover-Tech could identify and track users who visited sites or used apps with the malicious ads, and it would sometimes also try to extract phone numbers from some smartphone users, the researchers said. Ads only needed to load on a website for the spying to occur.Some ads would be used to help plant spyware from Candiru on users' devices, both research groups said, though Confiant said that ads it tied to Candiru were a tiny fraction of Discover-Tech's overall volume.Confiant cofounder Jerome Dangu said Discover-Tech was pumping out at least 10 million ads per day all around the world and that data-sharing arrangements - called cookie matching - allowed it to track people even beyond the reach of its advertisements."Very likely hundreds of millions of people would have been touched by Discover-Tech," Dangu said.Discover-Tech, which was founded in 2020, did not return messages left via its contact form. A LinkedIn message and emails sent to its chief executive, Dekel Boni, were not returned.Reuters' attempts to reach Candiru's owners were not successful. The US Commerce Department blacklisted Candiru in 2021 for allegedly supplying spyware that was used to maliciously target government officials, journalists, activists and academics.Candiru spyware used to compromise Al Jazeera devicesCitizen Lab said a powerful form of Candiru spyware delivered through Discover-Tech's ads had been used to compromise 45 Windows devices at the Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025, something it said it was able to confirm because the media group had shared its network logs with the group. Al Jazeera did not return messages seeking comment.In a statement, Al Jazeera said it "condemns the spyware attacks targeting a number of its staff" and that it was taking steps to protect its employees and its systems. "Those responsible must be held accountable," it said.Dangu of Confiant said that the malicious ads had been shown to users in "hundreds of networks in sensitive categories," including the Pentagon, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court. He also said that some regions, such as Gaza and the West Bank, were particularly saturated by the Israeli firm's ads."You go to almost any site in Palestine - any site - you find a Discover-Tech ad. It gives them a very complete visibility on the digital activities of an entire country," he said.Citizen Lab also said it had similar evidence showing the malicious ads were shown to people in the United Nations, NATO, the European Commission, and more than a dozen other national governments. Other networks the ads appeared in included chip-related firms such as Nvidia, Sandisk, Broadcom, and Micron, as well as several media organizations in Mexico, Israel, and Europe that were not identified.In addition to identifying Candiru and a couple of other surveillance vendors, Citizen Lab said it was able to glean some details about where Discover-Tech's users might be based because the firm inadvertently exposed its authentication logs to the internet, showing people logging in from internet protocol addresses in Israel, Europe, and the Gulf.Discover-Tech being frozen out of online ad marketDiscover-Tech is now being frozen out of parts of the online ad market.Google said in a statement that it had collaborated with Citizen Lab and Confiant on the investigation and kicked Discover-Tech off its ad platforms "for systematically violating our policies."IAB Europe, the European-level association for the digital marketing and advertising ecosystem, said in an email that it suspended Discover-Tech from its list of globally approved vendors last week after an audit identified policy violations.Comcast ad tech subsidiary Beeswax removed Discover-Tech from its platform "following recent activity," Comcast said in a statement. Yandex did not return Reuters messages seeking comment.Advertising-driven surveillance is increasingly being seen as a national security threat. Earlier this year, the Pentagon said it had received reports that US forces deployed to ​war zones had been targeted using location data harvested by ad tech firms and data brokers. Branches of the military have since disabled ad tracking on some devices.

title: Leave the Chiefs and fix the Galamsey Problem: Dr Solomon Owusu Advises President Mahama
body: Your Excellency, I write to respectfully inform you that I completely disagree with you on your appeal to the Chiefs in the mining areas, concerning their support for the government’s fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. I can confidently tell you that these Chiefs will never take any action because they are already aware and some connive with the galamseyers on their respective lands. Please, when you met the Chiefs, did you enquire from them about how the galamseyers get access to their lands to operate? Do the Chiefs allocate the lands to the galamseyers? Do the Chiefs report the illegal miners to the law enforcement agencies? Do the Chiefs collect money from the galamseyers? Do the Chiefs collect a certain percentage of the production output from the galamseyers? Please find out from them. Your Excellency, I would like to remind you that Chiefs don’t have the state power to combat galamsey, but you have all the powers in Ghana that can be applied without fear or favour. Also, solving the galamsey problem was one of the key reasons that Ghanaians voted massively for you, after we realized that President Akufo-Addo’s solution didn’t work. Unfortunately, Ghanaians haven’t witnessed any significant improvement in your galamsey fight since you assumed office. The water bodies continue to be polluted and silted at their worst stages. I must be honest with you: using the military to fight illegal miners alone won’t solve the problem. The fact remains that both the licensed small-scale miners and the unlicensed illegal miners (galamseyers) both pollute the rivers and degrade the lands. Since independence in 1957 to date, no government, including this administration, has come up with a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) that the miners can follow to ensure truly responsible mining activities, where the miners can operate without polluting water bodies and protect the lands. With the current approach used by your administration, you can arrest all illegal miners (galamseyers), but the problem will still remain because the licensed small-scale miners will still pollute the water bodies and degrade the lands. This approach failed the NPP government; it has failed you since you won power, and it will continue to fail you if you don’t change the strategy and the approach. How can we practice the same wrongful strategy and expect different results? This is just a heads-up. Let’s not forget that the previous administration tackled the problem, using a similar NAIMOS approach, including Operations Vanguard, Operations Halt 1, 2 & 3, and Galamstop. Again, in 2022, the previous government initiated the River Wardens, similar to the Blue Water Guards, but it didn’t work because of poor implementation. I am surprised that this government is still applying the same failed solutions, instead of considering a technical approach that will enable the miners to operate without polluting water bodies with minimal land disturbance. Your Excellency, lots of Ghanaians are disappointed in you as the President about how the galamsey matters are handled under your watch, because you presented a fine manifesto to convince us. It’s sad that this issue of national concern demands huge sums of money, but it looks like your budgetary allocations disregard the importance of addressing this galamsey problem. If the Lands Minister needs US$10 billion and the Finance Minister allocates US$12.5 million, approximately 0.13% (not even 0.5% or 1%) , then there is a problem, and it indicates unwillingness to address the problem. Furthermore, Goldbod’s functions state clearly that part of the proceeds would be used to support responsible mining across the country, in collaboration with the Ministry responsible for Mines. Goldbod receives over 80% of its gold from the artisanal and small-scale miners, helping immensely in the stabilization of the economy, but it is not an institution mandated to address mining issues. In my humble opinion, it’s time Goldbod allocates money to the Lands & Natural Resources Ministry to help address the galamsey issues from a technical perspective, instead of mandating itself to execute mining projects. My dear Uncle and President, I would like to crave your indulgence: you have only until next year, 2027, to fulfil your galamsey solution promise to Ghanaians and the world; nobody will listen to any further promise on mining from the NDC party in 2028. You still have a few months to prove yourself, so please take action now by stopping the politicisation, adopting a technical solution, and committing financial resources for the Lands Minister to work. Thank you.

title: Polish seizure leaves UK out of pocket by over one million
body: Assets bought by the Ministry of Defence under a short-term contract were seized by the Polish authorities during an investigation into the supplier and could not be recovered, producing a fruitless payment of £1.039 million, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked what the specific nature of the payment was, referring to the losses section of the department’s annual report and accounts for 2025 to 2026. Luke Pollard, the Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, said: “The fruitless payment of £1.039 million related to assets procured under a short-term contract let in line with existing normal processes. This included a due diligence visit to verify manufacturing capabilities, supply chain and deliverability of the requirement. The procurement formed part of a project involving multiple government stakeholders, which increased its complexity. The assets were subsequently seized by the Polish authorities as part of an independent investigation into the supplier which was unrelated to the Ministry of Defence’s procurement activity. As a result, the assets could not be recovered or returned to the Department.” A second loss in the same accounts was also put to the minister, asked about the nature of the fruitless payment recorded against Project SERAPH, Mr Pollard said: “A fruitless payment of £1.354 million was made to Deloitte following the termination for convenience of the Project SERAPH contract. The payment was made in accordance with the contractual terms and was negotiated by the Department.” Termination for convenience is the clause that lets a customer end a contract without the supplier being at fault, and the payment is what the department owed Deloitte for doing so. No explanation was given for why the contract was cancelled. The post Polish seizure leaves UK out of pocket by over one million first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Japan Denies Spying Claims After Russia Arrests Journalist
body:
Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Thursday denied Russia’s allegations of espionage after the FSB security service arrested a Japanese journalist.
“There is no such fact,” Takaichi told reporters when asked about Moscow’s claims that the reporter was acting on behalf of Japanese intelligence.
She said details remain sparse surrounding the arrest of Yuki Imai, a correspondent for the northern Japanese newspaper Hokkaido Shimbun, in Far East Russia’s Sakhalin region.
Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Wednesday that Japan had not been able to contact the individual and did not know about the arrest until the official announcement from Moscow.
The FSB accused Imai of collecting and storing information on Russia’s defense capabilities for intelligence purposes that it said could be used against Russian security.
Russia’s Ambassador in Tokyo Nikolai Nozdrev, who was summoned by Japan’s foreign ministry to lodge its protest, hit back Thursday with his own accusations that Japan enlists reporters into intelligence gathering.
Nozdrev said it was “unacceptable that Japanese special services recruit private persons, including Japanese journalists accredited in Russia, for ‘collaboration’ through the collection of classified information.”
Takaichi said Tokyo intended to focus on “the protection of Japanese nationals.” The Hokkaido Shimbun said the reporter’s safety was its top priority.
The case adds to long-running tensions between Russia and Japan, which have yet to sign a formal World War II peace treaty due to a territorial dispute over the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories.
Imai's arrest comes days after Japanese law enforcement in Osaka apprehended a 28-year-old Russian national linked to the international ransomware group Qilin and extradited him to Germany to face cybercrime charges.
