title: More than 100 ice-class mercantile ships to be created for Northern Sea Route
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. More than 100 ice-class commercial fleet vessels will be built for the Northern Sea Route, Russian Minister for the Development of the Far East and Arctic Alexey Chekunkov said.
"To the eight nuclear-powered icebreakers that we already have, which is a unique fleet on a global scale, another four will be added, and an ice-class commercial fleet totaling more than 100 vessels will be created," the minister said.
The work is underway to develop the infrastructure of the Northern Sea Route, Chekunkov noted.
"The infrastructure is primarily for logistics, to ensure that the products from these production facilities can be delivered to global markets, and to make their construction possible. The key infrastructure project is the development of the Northern Sea Route, but it also includes the development of railways, including the Northern Latitudinal Railway, the development of inland waterways, the development of our ports, the satellite constellation development, emergency and rescue fleet infrastructure, and the expansion of the fleet itself," he added.

title: Russia’s international reserves down $9.7 bln over week to $723.5 bln — Central Bank
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Russia’s international reserves edged down by $9.7 bln over the week and totaled $723.5 bln as of October 9, 2026, the Central Bank said.
"International reserves as of the close of business on October 9, 2026 stood at $723.5 bln, having decreased over the week by $9.7 bln or by 1.3%, largely as a result of negative revaluation," the regulator informed.
Reserves totaled $733.2 bln as of October 2.
Russia’s international reserves are highly liquid foreign assets available with the Bank of Russia and the Russian government. They comprise foreign currency, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), a reserve position in the International Monetary Fund and monetary gold. Following the onset of Moscow’s special military operation in Ukraine Western countries slapped sanctions against the Bank of Russia. Apart from freezing Russia’s gold and foreign currency reserves, all transactions related to management of the regulator’s reserves and assets, as well as transactions with any legal entity, organization or body acting on behalf or at the direction of the Central Bank, were prohibited.

title: ‘No person is walang kwenta’: Groups, friends defend Josh Aquino amid podcast controversy
body: MANILA, Philippines – Podcasts have given ordinary people a platform to speak their minds. Some give us a chance at self-reflection, while others offer comedic relief. But what happens when the jokes being thrown around in the latter begin to draw more offense than laughter? In a Machong Chismisan podcast episode published on October 5, Kris Aquino’s son Josh became the subject of mockery as the show’s host, Tito P, referred to him as “ walang kwenta (useless).” While the controversial episode has already been taken down, the Machong Chismisan podcast was not spared from public scrutiny, with groups and newsmakers attesting that the hosts had crossed the line with their remarks. National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) director Melvin Matibag also confirmed to Boy Abunda in a text message on Thursday, October 15, that he has ordered the NBI’s cybercrime division and special action unit to probe the podcast’s hosts and file the necessary complaints. The Machong Chismisan podcast’s contract has also been terminated by The Pod Network “effective immediately.” Family friends come to Josh’s defense Figures who know Josh personally were quick to come to his defense — with Abunda expressing outrage over the incident on an episode of Fast Talk With Boy Abunda . The talk show host said he was puzzled that a group of men who appeared to be intelligent and educated could make such cruel remarks about another young man with a disability. Abunda recalled that when Josh’s mother, Kris Aquino, was actively seeking treatment in the US, it was his job to gather everyone each morning for a prayer. “Hindi po walang silbi si Josh. Mali po ang inyong ginawa. Labag sa batas ng Diyos at sa batas ng tao ang inyong ginawa. Napakasakit. Napakasakit, hindi lamang para sa pamilya, pero para sa lahat ng mga pamilya, ng mga bata, ng mga magulang na may kapansanan, na may disability ang kanilang mga anak,” Abunda emphasized. (Josh is not useless. What you did was wrong. What you did is against the teachings of God and the law. It hurts. It hurts, not just for Josh’s family, but for all the families, children, and parents of those with disabilities.) Abunda recommended that Kris press charges against the podcast — citing RA 7277, or the Magna Carta for Disabled Persons, which penalizes those who publicly ridicule persons with disabilities. “Labag sa batas ang ginawa ng mga podcasters na ito. Congratulations, you got the attention of everybody, at hindi dito nagtatapos. Dapat ito’y pag-aralan, dapat tayo’y magreact. Dapat pag-usapan, para maenlighten ang maraming tao. I am sorry for what happened to Josh,” Abunda added. (What these podcasters did is against the law. Congratulations, you got the attention of everybody, and it doesn’t end here. This should be studied, and we should react. It should be talked about, so we can enlighten even more people. I am sorry for what happened to Josh.) Meanwhile, Mark Leviste, who was previously in a relationship with Kris, stepped in to publicly defend Josh. “I love him like my own son, and my children love him like their own older brother. He is one of the kindest, sweetest, most prayerful, and loving people you will ever meet. Sinuman ang tunay na nakakakilala sa kanya ay mauunawaan kung bakit labis na nakasasakit sa aming mga nagmamahal sa kanya ang mga binitiwang salita tungkol sa kanya,” (Those who truly know Josh understand why it hurts to hear these words be thrown against him.) Leviste asked that the people behind Machong Chismisan take full responsibility for what transpired, personally apologize to Josh and his family, and ensure that the incident does not happen again. “You may call yourselves comedians or podcasters, but freedom of expression does not exempt you from accountability! There’s a difference between making people laugh and turning someone into a laughingstock. When your foolish words and slapstick humor demean someone, especially because of his disability, you cross a line that should never be crossed!” Leviste wrote. Designer Michael Leyva, a longtime friend of Kris, also came to Josh’s defense — personally vouching for Josh’s kindness. “Making Kuya Josh the subject of your so-called ‘Machong Chismisan’ podcast and mocking his disability is not something that I or any of us should simply let slide,” he said in an Instagram story . ‘Blatant discrimination’ Even the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) had to issue a warning for content creators to be careful about making derogatory statements towards individuals with mental disabilities not just as an act of compassion, but to uphold their human rights. And for the National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA), it no longer becomes comedy when one’s dignity is involved, but instead, it is “blatant discrimination.” “Creators bear a responsibility to foster respectful and inclusive digital spaces, ensuring that all content is approached with sensitivity and mindfulness. NCDA also calls on the public and social media users to refrain from sharing, reposting, and engaging with any material that demeans, mocks, or exploits vulnerable individuals,” the NCDA wrote. In the same vein, the Council for the Welfare of Children reminded content creators and media practitioners of the influence they hold over shaping public opinion. The Down Syndrome Association of the Philippines encouraged Machong Chismisan ’s hosts — and in effect, all content creators — to engage with individuals with autism, Down syndrome, and other disabilities for them to hear their stories and use their platforms “to build understanding rather than ridicule.” “No person is walang kwenta (useless). Every person with autism, Down syndrome, or any disability has inherent dignity and worth. Using their condition as a punchline is not comedy. It is cruelty that hurts thousands of Filipino families who live this reality every day,” the group wrote in its statement. The Autism Society of the Philippines also advised against patronizing content creators and podcasts “not capable of basic respect.” “Freedom of expression must never come at the expense of the rights and humanity of persons with disabilities,” the group said. – Rappler.com

title: Uzbekistan Introduces Life Imprisonment for Rape of Children Under 14
body: Uzbekistan has introduced penalties of 15 to 25 years in prison or life imprisonment for rape and certain other serious sexual offenses against children under 14. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has signed a law eliminating the statute of limitations for prosecuting these crimes. The amendments affect five codes and six laws and expand legal protections for children against physical and psychological violence, including abuse by relatives and educational staff. For intentional crimes resulting in a child’s death, suspended sentences and early release on parole will be prohibited. “Violence against a young child can never be tolerated, and punishment must be inevitable and uncompromising,” Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, wrote on her Telegram channel . Children who have experienced or witnessed violence will be entitled to free state-funded legal assistance from the moment they become involved in legal proceedings. If a parent, adoptive parent, guardian, or another relative is suspected of the crime, a representative of the guardianship authorities must also protect the child’s interests during the investigation and trial. In schools and other educational institutions, staff responsible for teaching or caring for children can be dismissed if held legally responsible for violence against a child. The legislation was approved following a high-profile case in the Namangan region, where reports emerged of alleged sexual violence against a five-year-old girl at a state-run kindergarten in the Uchqurgan district. The case sparked public outrage and debate over appropriate punishment for those responsible. Mirziyoyeva previously stated that responsibility should extend to both the direct perpetrators and officials whose negligence may have allowed the alleged assault to take place. According to the Oliy Majlis, Uzbekistan’s parliament, 445 criminal cases involving the rape of children under 14 were opened in the country between 2022 and 2025. The amendments passed the lower house of parliament on September 30, following a first reading on September 29, and were approved by the Senate on October 2.

title: Pay attention to teachers and give them what is due – Ho District GNAT tells government
body: The Ho District chapter of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) has urged the government to pay attention to the teaching force and provide good working conditions. The Ho District Chairperson of the Ghana National Association of Teachers, Madam Rose Tippong, believes this would encourage teachers to give their best on and off the field and avert strike action. She said this during a healthy lifestyle exercise to commemorate World Teachers’ Day, following a two-week industrial strike by teacher unions. The event featured several healthy lifestyle activities, including a 4-kilometre health walk and health screening exercises to help members understand their health status. Female teachers also participated in breast cancer screening as a first step towards combating the disease, which is best treated when diagnosed early. The Ho District Chairperson of the Ghana National Association of Teachers, Madam Lois Tippong-Asare, said the initiative aims to ensure a healthy teaching force in her jurisdiction. “We have doctors from our home, a regional hospital, or the boat team, who are taking our members through screening, especially for breast cancer. “And this month also happens to be Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and so they are screening ladies. We also have doctors from other hospitals who are here to screen for non-communicable diseases. And so we are just doing this to make sure that our members are healthy”, she said. She underscored the importance of a healthy teaching force and called for better working conditions for teachers. “If the government will not take care of us, then we must take the initiative to take care of ourselves. That is what we’re here today. And so we are adding the government also. It should pay attention to get it. and give what the data is due”, she said. The Ho District Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Teachers, Jonathan Lewis Kemevor, recounted the teacher unions’ demands, urging the government to prioritise teachers’ well-being. “And our demand is just apt. We have to respect the teacher. We are talking about the promotion, uh, placement of their rightful funds and payment of arrears. We are talking about deprived teachers allowance”, he explained.

title: Robbery, harassment and fraud rise across England and Wales
body: Robbery, harassment and fraud are among the offences that rose in England and Wales in the year to March 2026, according to the Office for National Statistics. The broader Crime Survey for England and Wales estimated 9.6 million incidents overall, which reveals no major statistical change from the previous year. However, as some crimes fell, others rose. Police recorded 87,362 robberies, up 10 per cent. That rise came from business robberies, which increased 91 per cent to 29,669. The ONS says this was mainly because police were told to record shop thefts involving violence or threats as robbery from April 2025. Robberies of personal property fell by 9 per cent. Recorded rape rose 4 per cent to 74,727. Violence without injury edged up 2 per cent, while violence with injury fell 3 per cent. The ONS cautions that police figures for these offences are not a reliable guide to trends, as they can be affected by changes in recording and by more victims coming forward. Harassment rose 6 per cent in police records, but the ONS says those figures are not a good indicator of trends. Its survey found a statistically significant rise in repeated harassment: from 2.3 per cent to 3.5 per cent of adults aged 16 and over, or about 1.7 million people. The estimates are interim. The survey also found that the number of adult fraud victims rose 10 per cent to 3.8 million. Bank and credit account fraud incidents increased 15 per cent to about 2.8 million. Total fraud incidents reached 4.5 million, with no statistically significant change.

title: Strengthen humanitarian interventions for disaster victims, vulnerable groups – DNKI
body: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – A nonprofit organisation, De Norsemen Kclub International (DNKI) has called on its members, governments and well-meaning individuals to strengthen humanitarian interventions for disaster victims and vulnerable groups across Nigeria and beyond. The organisation made the call as it marked its 2026 Humanitarian Day, observed annually on October 15, with the theme, ‘Humanity First: Advancing Hope, Dignity and Community Wellbeing’. In a statement marking the occasion, DNKI International President, Chief Oliver Patrick Ityohegh, urged Norsemen worldwide to demonstrate brotherhood through practical acts of compassion, charity and support for individuals and communities in need. He stressed that humanitarian service should go beyond annual celebrations and become a way of life, reflected in daily interactions and collective efforts to build a caring, inclusive and peaceful society. According to him, DNKI chapters across the world should intensify community-based interventions aimed at alleviating hardship, supporting vulnerable populations, promoting development and strengthening unity among members. “Our guiding principle, ‘Service to Humanity,’ is more than a motto; it is a responsibility that calls on every Norseman to make a meaningful difference in the lives of others”, Ityohegh said. He noted that charitable outreach, relief distribution and community support could help restore dignity to disadvantaged persons and bring hope to those facing difficult circumstances. The DNKI president expressed concern over natural and human-induced disasters affecting communities in Nigeria and other parts of the world, noting that emergencies often leave families displaced, livelihoods destroyed and vulnerable people struggling to meet basic needs. He urged the organisation’s chapters and members to sustain and expand support for disaster-hit communities through the provision of food, clothing, medical assistance and other essential relief materials, subject to available resources. Ityohegh also called for greater attention to displaced persons, widows, orphans, persons with disabilities, the elderly and other vulnerable groups requiring support to rebuild their lives. He appealed to federal and state governments to strengthen emergency response systems, improve disaster preparedness and ensure the timely delivery of relief services during crises. He said prompt intervention, effective coordination, adequately equipped emergency agencies and sufficient resources were critical to saving lives, reducing suffering and restoring hope to affected communities. The organisation also commended the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Federal Fire Service (FFS), State Emergency Management Agencies (SEMAs), humanitarian groups and voluntary organisations for their contributions to rescue operations, disaster response and relief efforts. While acknowledging their efforts, Ityohegh emphasised the need for stronger collaboration among government agencies, civil society organisations, community leaders, the private sector and voluntary groups to address humanitarian challenges more effectively. He reaffirmed DNKI’s commitment to promoting human welfare through responsible engagement, humanitarian outreach and community-focused initiatives. According to him, even small acts of kindness can transform lives, restore hope and inspire others to contribute to the wellbeing of society. “As we celebrate this year’s Humanitarian Day, I encourage every Norseman to look beyond personal interests and embrace the greater responsibility of making our communities safer, stronger and more humane”, he said. He urged members to uphold the values of love, unity, integrity and selfless service, stressing that compassion and practical assistance must remain central to the organisation’s activities. “Humanity must always come first. Together, we can advance hope, preserve human dignity and build communities where compassion is practised, the vulnerable are supported and no one is left behind”, Ityohegh added. The post Strengthen humanitarian interventions for disaster victims, vulnerable groups – DNKI appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 2027: Tinubu Charges Betta Edu, APC Women to Secure Women’s Votes
body: Jonathan Eze President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has charged Dr Betta Edu, Director of Women Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, members of the Women’s Directorate, all APC Women and other campaign leaders to intensify grassroots engagement and mobilise women across the country to secure victory for the party in the 2027 general election. The President gave the charge on Wednesday afternoon at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa, Abuja, where he acknowledged the invaluable contributions of Nigerian women to the nation’s political development and expressed confidence in their capacity to play a decisive role in determining the outcome of the forthcoming election. Tinubu commended women for their longstanding commitment to the APC and their contributions to the party’s electoral successes, noting that their organisational abilities, numerical strength and influence within families and communities make them indispensable to the party’s re-election project. “ Women are the greatest mobilizers” He urged members of the campaign council, particularly the Women Mobilisation Directorate under Dr Edu, to translate the enthusiasm and support of women into a well-coordinated nationwide campaign capable of delivering electoral victory for the APC. The President’s charge places the women’s mobilisation structure at the centre of the party’s strategy for securing a renewed mandate for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, with particular emphasis on reaching voters at the grassroots, strengthening existing political networks and sustaining direct engagement with communities across the federation. For Dr Edu and her team, the task is to consolidate the support of women in markets, rural communities, professional associations, cooperatives, faith-based organisations and other social networks, while ensuring that the administration’s policies and programmes are communicated effectively to prospective voters. The Women Mobilisation Directorate has already established an ambitious target of securing 40 million women’s votes for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket through an expansive mobilisation framework covering 176,846 communities, as well as structures across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. The strategy is designed to take the campaign beyond major rallies and political gatherings by strengthening ward-level organisation, household engagement, community outreach, and polling-unit mobilisation. Tinubu’s recognition of women’s contributions also reinforces the importance of their participation beyond election periods. Women remain central to household economic management, community development, small businesses, agriculture, education, and social welfare, giving them considerable influence in shaping public opinion and political choices. The President’s charge is therefore expected to galvanise APC women leaders and grassroots organisers into a more coordinated effort to present the administration’s record, explain its policies and engage citizens on the issues that matter to their daily lives. The mobilisation drive is also expected to build on the activities of First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, whose engagement with women and support for empowerment initiatives have featured prominently in the campaign’s preparations. At the October 5 pre-inaugural Women’s Summit and Empowerment Programme in Abuja, the First Lady brought together women stakeholders from across the country, while the programme featured the distribution of livelihood-support items, including motorbikes and farm trucks, to beneficiaries. The gathering also underscored the campaign’s determination to connect political mobilisation with women’s economic participation. Dr Edu has consistently expressed confidence in the ability of APC women to secure victory for the President in 2027. She has called for unity, discipline, and sustained grassroots engagement, arguing that the party’s women must work as a coordinated network rather than rely solely on high-profile campaign events. The inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council formally advances the APC’s preparations for the next general election, bringing the party’s political structures and mobilisation machinery into sharper focus. With the President’s marching orders now placing renewed emphasis on women’s electoral contribution, the responsibility before Edu and other campaign officials is to turn political enthusiasm into measurable grassroots participation and votes. For the APC, the 2027 contest will require more than endorsements and public declarations. It will demand sustained contact with voters, credible communication of government policies, and an organisational structure capable of reaching communities across the country. Tinubu’s message to the women’s mobilisation team is clear in its political implication: women must not merely participate in the campaign; they must be organised, empowered and strategically positioned to help deliver the party’s electoral objective.

title: Authorities knew of abuse allegations against Obuasi headmaster months before suspension – JoyNews investigation
body: JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni has revealed that authorities were aware of allegations of sexual abuse involving suspended Obuasi Senior High Technical School headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, months before the Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, directed the Ghana Education Service to suspend him. The headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, is the subject of the documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, which examines allegations of sexual abuse involving female students. The investigation found that complaints and petitions concerning alleged sexual harassment and assault of female students had reached municipal authorities, education officials and other influential figures, but Mr Abdulai remained in office until JoyNews began making inquiries. The Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) of Obuasi, Faustilove Appiah Kannin, said she received a report about the alleged abuse shortly after assuming office. She told JoyNews: “I was there when the former sports master of the school called me to inform me that the headmaster had slept with one of the students. As a mother and a municipal chief executive, I had to invite the parent.” Asked when the incident was reported, she responded: “I think it was last year, early last year.” Kumasi Mayor Richard Ofori-Agyemang Boadi, popularly known as Zuba, also disclosed that he had intervened following allegations of sexual abuse involving Mr Abdulai. The mayor, who is also a native of Obuasi, said he was informed of the allegations during a visit to the town at a time when tensions at the school threatened to trigger a riot by students. “So I went to Obuasi one day, and it was all over that there was heat at Obuasi Sec Tech, and the boys were going to riot on that evening. “I was told that there’s an allegation that the headmaster of the school had molested one of the female students. And the headmaster is someone who’s been known to me for so many years, even before I became the mayor of Obuasi. So I asked that they call him for me.” Mr Abdullah has since been suspended as headmaster of Obuasi SHS following the controversy.

title: Global coal prices may decline a little in 2027 — Deputy Energy Minister
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. The international prices for thermal and met coal could decline slightly next year, Russian Deputy Minister of Energy Dmitry Islamov told reporters on the sidelines of the Russian Energy Week 2026 international forum.
"Regarding the price environment for next year, we expect it to remain the same. Prices might be just a few percent lower," he said.
The financial performance of the sector is driven by global prices, coal export volumes, and fluctuations in the ruble exchange rate, Islamov told TASS earlier. The profit margins of Russian coal exporters heading eastbound have increased from zero to 10-15%, while those heading westbound have risen to 2-10%.
The Russian Energy Week international forum is being held in Moscow from October 14 to 16. Roscongress Foundation is the event organizer. TASS is the information partner of the Russian Energy Week.

title: Kallas: Understandable why Ukraine targets Russia's oil revenues
body:
EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas made the remarks ahead of a European Council meeting in Brussels, Ukrinform reports.
"The majority of Russia's funding for the war comes from oil revenue. So clearly, Ukraine wants this war to stop, and that is why cutting off the funding for the war is the way to do it," Kallas said.
She expressed her conviction that the West should "put pressure on Russia" rather than force Ukraine to surrender in order to end the war, adding that the EU was "very committed."
As Ukrinform reported, a two-day meeting of the European Council began today. Support for Ukraine is scheduled to be discussed tomorrow.
President Volodymyr Zelensky is due to address the leaders of EU member states tomorrow morning.

title: Zelenskyy arrives in Brussels
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has arrived in Brussels for a working visit, during which he will take part in a meeting of the European Council and hold talks with partners.

"Today, important meetings are scheduled with the NATO Secretary General, the President of France, and the Prime Ministers of Poland, Denmark, and Belgium. I will also have an audience with the King of the Belgians, Philippe. Tomorrow, meetings are scheduled with the Presidents of the European Council and the European Commission, as well as with the Prime Ministers of Hungary, Finland, and Sweden," the President said on X Thursday.

The President emphasized that everyone in Europe wants the war to end, and that this requires signals of strength—specifically, greater, tangible pressure on Russia and increased defense support for Ukraine.

title: Price of Russian diesel for US subject to commercial negotiations — Novak
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. The price of Russian diesel fuel for the US market is a matter of commercial negotiations, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters on the sidelines of the Russian Energy Week (REW) forum.
"This is a subject of commercial negotiations," Novak said, when asked whether diesel prices for the US would be based on market benchmarks or include a discount.
Answering a question about a potential license extension beyond April 2027, the deputy prime minister noted: "No such talks are underway at the moment. As for an extension, it is probably too early to say. We will see how the situation develops."
Novak also stressed that only diesel supplies are currently being discussed, with no negotiations on other commodities taking place.
Earlier, Novak told TASS that Russia was immediately lifting restrictions on diesel exports ahead of schedule, noting that the country is a key supplier of the fuel to the global market. Russia is ready to supply additional diesel volumes to the US market and all partners – 300,000 tonnes in October, rising to 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes in December, with potential volumes reaching up to 3.5 million tonnes per month in the future.
The Russian Energy Week international forum is being held in Moscow on October 14-16, supported by the Russian government, the Ministry of Energy, and the Moscow city government. The event is organized by the Roscongress Foundation, with TASS serving as the forum's information partner.

title: US teenager appears in court over alleged Hindu temple shooting plot
body: A man has been arrested after an investigation into threats of a potential mass shooting that could have targeted a Hindu temple near Chicago. Alexandros Paporakis, 19, from Palatine, Illinois, appeared in court on Wednesday. He was charged with one count of making a terrorist threat and one count of unlawful possession of a weapon for possessing a rifle with a barrel less than 16in long, the BBC’s US partner CBS reports. Police said they found a manifesto in which Paporakis identified as a white supremacist and wrote about his hatred for non-white people. Prosecutors said the defendant told a colleague on the phone that his gun jammed and sent messages showing an AR-style rifle, CBS reports. Other messages showed how the gun failed to fire when he pulled the trigger, and a photo of himself in a tactical vest, according to prosecutors. This colleague and another coworker from the Taco Bell where Paporakis worked called police on Sunday to report the incident. Palatine Police Chief William Nord said that officers “recovered a rifle, they recovered loaded magazines, hundreds of rounds of rifle ammunition, as well as body armour,” while searching Paporakis’ home. Officers and the FBI were also able to examine Paporakis’ electronics and electronic communications, where they said they found the manifesto. “Reading through the manifesto, he did state some extremist ideologies and talked about violence, he talked about mass killings and how he wanted to carry out this mass shooting,” Nord said, according to CBS. Prosecutors allege that Paporakis’ colleague told police the defendant had spoken about being a white supremacist while at work, and made disparaging comments about people of other races. Prosecutors said that on Saturday, Paporakis told a worker he was planning “it” at a Hindu temple in Aurora, and said Sunday “was going to be a special day”, before calling and sending the messages to his colleague the next day. Police said that a specific intended location in the alleged threats has not been confirmed, and the investigation remains open. Local Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi said he was “horrified” by the incident. In a statement posted on Facebook, he said: “Every American deserves to live and worship without fear, and we must stand together against hatred in all its forms.”

title: Zelensky arrives in Belgium, prepares to meet Prime Minister De Wever
body:
BRUSSELS, Belgium — President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Belgium on Oct. 15, where he plans to meet Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever to discuss finances before taking part in an EU leaders' summit.
"All of us in Europe want this war to end. And for that to happen, strong signals are needed — more real pressure on Russia and more defense support for Ukraine," Zelensky wrote on social media upon arrival.
Already in Brussels with my team to attend the European Council meeting and hold talks with our partners. Important meetings are scheduled for today with the NATO Secretary General, the President of France, and the prime ministers of Poland, Denmark, and Belgium. I will also… pic.twitter.com/YcoGk7t6So
The social media post mentions a meeting with the Belgian prime minister, plans for which the Flemish newspaper De Morgen first reported on Oct. 13.
That meeting was likewise confirmed by a Ukrainian diplomat, who told the Kyiv Independent it is expected to take place at 8 p.m. local time.
On top of the agenda for Zelensky is building consensus for the use of some 200 billion euros ($227 billion) of Russian assets immobilized in Europe, the lion's share of which is held in Belgium's Euroclear.
Ukraine upped its advocacy efforts this week to try and get EU countries to back the idea, previously shot down in December, with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha publishing an opinion piece with Politico — the news outlet that claimed in December 2025 that De Wever was "Russia's most valuable asset," which provoked a strong response from the Belgian leader.
The topic is expected to come up during the ongoing European Council summit, but with no definitive conclusion this time, no matter how positively a De Wever-Zelensky meeting might go.
Zelensky will attend the summit only on the morning of Oct. 16 and, on the sidelines, is expected to meet with Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar.
The Magyar meeting is significant as the first bilateral between the two leaders and comes days after Ukraine adopted a long-awaited law to bolster the rights of Ukraine's Hungarian-speaking minority , which was also required to advance its EU membership bid.

title: Vantaa confirms 122 layoffs, Espoo numbers still unclear
body:
Both cities began restructuring talks with staff representatives in August, with a combined total of over 500 jobs on the line.
The cities of Espoo and Vantaa plan to make hundreds of employees redundant after the conclusion of restructuring talks with staff representatives.
When the negotiations were announced in August , the City of Vantaa said it was seeking savings of 15 million euros, which could lead to the loss of about 200 jobs, while the City of Espoo said up to 300 employees faced redundancy.
On Thursday, the City of Vantaa announced that an estimated 122 people would be laid off, while a further 81 employees would be offered a new position within the organisation as an alternative to redundancy.
Some 20 of the redundancies will affect people in senior positions, such as directors, managers and supervisors.
In addition, 44 workers will face changes to the terms of their employment, 15 fixed-term contracts will not be renewed once they expire, and natural attrition will lead to the loss of a further 21 positions, the City said.
In a statement, the City said that the restructuring will minimise as much as possible the impact on the services provided to Vantaa residents.
Meanwhile Helsingin Sanomat reported on Thursday that the City of Espoo plans to lay off or significantly change the employment contracts of some 130 workers following the conclusion of redundancy talks.
This figure is smaller than the number initially suggested at the outset of the negotiations, and the City said in a statement that the actual number of redundancies could be reduced even further.
The City's statement does not however provide much detailed information about the number of redundancies and, according to HS, Espoo Mayor Kai Mykkänen (NCP) declined to comment further beyond the content of the press release when contacted on Wednesday.
The exact number therefore remains unclear, with Espoo's Communications Director Johanna Pajakoski noting that the figures reported by HS are estimates from the negotiation proposal, made before the talks took place.
The City of Espoo is seeking savings of approximately 10 million euros, with staff expected to find out the true number of layoffs next Monday.

title: Implementing the Four-Point Proposition on Mining Cooperation to Write a New Chapter in China-Africa Common Devt
body: By Yu Dunhai On October 13, 2026, Chinese President Xi Jinping put forth a four-point proposition on advancing China-Africa mining cooperation during his meeting with President Duma Gideon Boko of Botswana, who was on a state visit to China. Grounded in the profound transformation of the global critical minerals landscape and Africa’s urgent need for independent development, and anchored in the broader context of traditional China-Africa friendship, the proposition charts the course for China-Africa mining cooperation in the new era. As the Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria, I am keenly aware of the strategic vision, forward-looking perspective, and practical relevance of these four points. They present a concrete embodiment of the concept of a China-Africa community with a shared future, and provide strong support for Nigeria and other African countries in transforming their resource endowment into development dividends. Drawing on the realities of China-Nigeria mining cooperation, I would like to share with Nigerian friends a deeper understanding of the rich substance of this four-point proposition. First, we must adhere to the principle that African resources belong to Africa. This is the fundamental premise of mining cooperation with African nations. Africa has long been locked at the lower end of global industrial and value chains by an inequitable international division of labour–a historical injustice that must be corrected. Resource sovereignty is an integral component of national sovereignty, and the ability to control one’s own resource destiny is the cornerstone of sustainable development for African countries. China fully understands and respects Africa’s legitimate aspirations. We have always respected the development paths independently chosen by African countries and stand ready to share our experience to help them formulate mining development plans suited to their national conditions. China supports Nigeria and other African countries in independently charting their mining development paths, ensuring that decision-making power and the benefits of resource development remain firmly in their own hands. Second, we must uphold the principle of pursuing the greater good and shared interests, and seeking mutual benefit and win-win results. This is the core philosophy of China-Africa mining cooperation. In conducting mining cooperation, China and Africa must uphold a correct view of righteousness and benefit. China never pursues unilateral maximization of benefits in its cooperation with Africa, and always adheres to win-win cooperation and common development. In Nigeria, Chinese enterprises involved in energy and mining sector not only bring capital and technology, but also adhere to localized operations, and attach importance to skills training and community contributions. The Chinese Embassy will continue to guide Chinese enterprises in Nigeria to enhance their operational capabilities, transfer green technologies, strengthen public welfare assistance, drive local employment and talent training, and promote South-South cooperation in the mining sector. Third, we must pursue high-quality development. This is the direction of progress for China-Africa mining cooperation. Promoting local processing, extending industrial chains and increasing value addition are the key pathways for Africa to convert resource advantages into development strength. China has always been a doer in supporting Africa’s development and will continue to drive the transformation of China-Africa mining cooperation towards higher industrial value addition. We will deepen the alignment between China’s 15th Five-Year Plan and Nigeria’s “Renewed Hope” Agenda, push projects further into deep processing and high-value-added segments, and help Nigeria build a more complete industrial system. In this way, resources can truly become a driver of modernisation rather than a source of so-called “resource curse.” Fourth, we must maintain a fair and open cooperation environment. This is an important safeguard for mining cooperation with Africa. Africa’s resources should never be turned into tools of geopolitical rivalry. Any attempt to politicize or instrumentalize African resource issues as well as to create confrontation and division will seriously damage the fundamental interests of the African people. China consistently advocates open cooperation and fair competition. We welcome all parties that genuinely wish to support Africa’s development and stand ready to work with African partners to maintain a stable and predictable market environment for mining cooperation, thereby creating more favourable conditions for enterprise investment and operations. China is ready to join hands with Nigeria in rejecting any attempt to treat mineral resources as bargaining chip in geopolitical games, ensuring that resource development always serves development and benefits the people. I would like to emphasise in particular that the Chinese government requires all Chinese enterprises and citizens in Nigeria to strictly abide by Nigerian laws and regulations and to operate in a lawful and compliant manner. We maintain a zero-tolerance policy toward illegal mining and other criminal activities. China supports Nigeria in taking strong measures to strengthen mining governance. The facts show that the overwhelming majority of Chinese mining enterprises in Nigeria operate in accordance with the law, actively fulfil their social responsibilities and protect the environment. Isolated and inaccurate allegations that exaggerate individual cases or distort the facts are neither fair nor conducive to the overall China-Nigeria friendship and cooperation. We stand ready to work with the Nigerian side to further regulate market order, jointly combat illegal mining, and foster a healthy and transparent business environment. China and Africa share a common future and a bright outlook. Mechanism platforms such as the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation continue to provide solid support, while the dividends of China’s zero-tariff policy for all diplomatic partners in Africa continue to unfold, creating favourable conditions for deeper China-Africa cooperation. I am convinced that as long as both sides uphold mutual respect and mutual benefit, we can turn Africa’s resource endowment into tangible development outcomes, deliver greater benefits to the Chinese and African peoples, and make greater contributions to building a China-Africa community with a shared future. China stands ready to work hand in hand with Nigeria and other African countries to fully implement President Xi Jinping’s four-point proposal on China-Africa mining cooperation, write a new chapter of high-quality development in China-Africa mining cooperation, ensure that Africa’s resources truly serve the development of the African people, and make China-Africa mining cooperation a model of South-South cooperation and an important force in advancing Africa’s modernisation. *H.E. Yu Dunhai is Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria

title: Ronaldo must return to Portugal after dispute is resolved — Vitinha
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Vitinha has expressed hope that Cristiano Ronaldo will return to the Portugal national team after resolving his dispute with coach Jorge Jesus. Vitinha said he wanted the disagreement involving the 41-year-old forward to be settled amicably, adding that Ronaldo’s return was what everyone in the team hoped for. Speaking to TNT Sports on Wednesday after PSG’s 4-2 victory over Manchester City, Vitinha said the recent international break had been marked by heightened emotions. “It was a turbulent international break — full of high emotions,” he said. “For my part, I just hope everything gets resolved for the best. I hope he [Ronaldo] returns and that everything turns out fine. The truth is, that’s what we all want. I hope he comes back and everything is sorted out.” Ronaldo left the Portugal camp during the international break following a disagreement with Jesus over his playing time. The Al Nassr forward subsequently apologised to his teammates in a social media statement but also accused Jesus of “breaking his word” to him. Ronaldo said he would accept whatever punishment the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) imposed while reaffirming his desire to continue representing his country. The FPF provisionally suspended the Portugal captain, although a final disciplinary decision has yet to be announced. Details of the proceedings are expected to remain confidential until the investigation is concluded. Ronaldo remains Portugal’s record goalscorer, with 146 goals in 234 appearances for the national team. Vitinha featured in all four of Portugal’s Nations League victories during the international break. Portugal are scheduled to face Denmark and Wales in their next two matches in November. The post Ronaldo must return to Portugal after dispute is resolved — Vitinha appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Academic City donates paediatric rehabilitation staircase to Ga East Hospital
body: Academic City University has donated a paediatric rehabilitation staircase to the Ga East Municipal Hospital to support physiotherapy and rehabilitation services for children receiving treatment at the facility. This donation comes at a time when health authorities are urging innovators to design low-cost medical equipment with health workers from the drawing board, so that devices meet local needs and can be maintained by local engineers. The presentation followed an innovative project undertaken by Level 400 Biomedical Engineering students of the university as part of their academic work. The project began about two years ago when the students took courses in Medical Devices and Technologies and Rehabilitation Engineering. As part of the courses, they were required to identify a clinical need and develop a practical solution to address a biomedical challenge. During a visit to the Ga East Municipal Hospital, the students engaged with the Physiotherapy Department and observed that although the department had a rehabilitation staircase for adults, it lacked one specifically designed for paediatric patients. To address this gap, the students designed and developed a paediatric rehabilitation staircase, which they submitted as part of their academic requirements. Recognising its potential to improve patient care, the university’s Biomedical Engineering Department further refined the design, structure and aesthetics of the student-developed device. These improvements aimed to make the staircase more durable, practical and suitable for use in the hospital’s paediatric rehabilitation activities. Presenting the equipment, the Coordinator of the Biomedical Engineering Department, Mr Jacob Quarshie, said the project demonstrated what could be achieved when classroom learning was tied to real needs in the community. “Our students did not simply sit in a lecture hall and write an examination. They went to the hospital, listened to the clinicians, and found a problem affecting children. This staircase is the result, and we are proud to hand it over to the hospital,” he said. Upon receiving the equipment, the Chief Nursing Officer at Ga East Municipal Hospital, Ms Veronica Momo-Blabi, expressed gratitude to Academic City for the gesture. She said the hospital would put the device to immediate use and take good care of it so that many more children would benefit.

title: Kaduna To Establish Post Basic Nursing College In Rigasa
body: Governor Uba Sani has signed an Executive Bill establishing the Kaduna State College of Post-Basic Nursing Sciences in Rigasa, Igabi Local Government Area, to address shortage of specialist nurses and to improve medical services. A statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki, disclosed the bill was signed on Wednesday, as a strategic investment in skilled manpower development under the Governor’s ongoing health sector reforms. The Commissioner explained that the ‘’institution is expected to expand advanced nursing training, produce specialists in critical fields and improve maternal and child care, emergency response and intensive care services across Kaduna State.’’ ‘’Under the Kaduna State College of Post-Basic Nursing Sciences, Rigasa Law, 2026, the institution will operate as a specialized tertiary training college, with its main campus in Rigasa. ‘’There will be provisions for additional campuses, schools and training centres, subject to regulatory approvals,’’ the statement clarified. Maiyaki explained that the College will offer programmes in midwifery, psychiatric and mental health nursing, perioperative nursing, paediatric nursing, accident and emergency nursing, intensive care nursing, public health nursing, as well as administration. According to him, Governor Uba Sani’s assent to the bill ‘’represents a significant investment in developing the skilled workforce required to address critical personnel shortages and strengthen clinical expertise.’’ ‘’Beyond professional training, the College will promote research, continuous professional development and partnerships with teaching hospitals, universities, specialist facilities and other accredited institutions. ‘’The law also establishes a Governing Council to provide strategic direction and institutional oversight, alongside an Academic Board responsible for high standards, research and professional training,’’ he added. The Commissioner pointed out that ‘’all programmes will be subject to the accreditation and regulatory requirements of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria and other relevant authorities.’ He noted that the legislation complements Governor Uba Sani’s broader reform agenda, including the upgrading of 255 primary healthcare centres, rehabilitation of 16 General Hospitals and sustained investments in workforce recruitment and development. Maiyaki however argued that investments in medical infrastructure must be matched by qualified professionals capable of delivering specialised services, particularly in underserved communities. He maintained that the College of Post-Basic Nursing Sciences would help build a pool of specialist nurses, enhance institutional capacity and contribute to better health outcomes for generations to come. The statement reaffirmed Governor Uba Sani’s commitment towards developing the institution into a centre of excellence for specialist nursing education, research and clinical training, to advance his vision of accessible, quality and people-centred medical services in Kaduna State.

title: Russia remained top crude oil supplier to India in September — newspaper
body:
NEW DELHI, October 15. /TASS/. Russia remained the largest supplier of crude oil to India in September 2026 despite the growth in purchases of Russian hydrocarbons by Chinese companies, The Times of India news outlet reports, citing Kpler analytical firm.
According to Kpler data, oil imports from Russia to India reached 1.82 million barrels per day in September, while China's daily purchases of Russian oil mounted to 1.49 million barrels last month.
In the near future, China will continue to compete with India in terms of oil import volumes from Russia, Kpler forecasts. In October, deliveries of Russian oil to Indian importers will remain generally stable, reaching 1.8-1.9 million barrels per day.
India is the world's third-largest importer and consumer of oil. The country meets more than 88% of its hydrocarbon requirements through purchases abroad.

title: President Sheikh Mohamed offers condolences to Saudi King after airport strikes
body: UAE leaders have sent condolences to Saudi Arabia's King Salman bin Abdulaziz following attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which left several people dead and hundreds injured. President Sheikh Mohamed expressed his sincere sympathy for the victims of the attacks and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, and Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed, Vice President, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Presidential Court, sent similar condolences to King Salman. Sheikh Dr Sultan bin Muhammad Al Qasimi, Ruler of Sharjah, also sent his condolences to the Saudi King. King Khalid International Airport has been shut since an attack on Saturday killed 13 people and injured more than 300, the deadliest on the kingdom in more than ​a decade. On Sunday, another strike killed one person and injured nearly a dozen others. The Houthi rebels have launched attacks other airports in Saudi Arabia in the past week, hitting sites not only in the capital but in Abha, Jazan and Najran, with a projectile also damaging the airport serving Dammam. The strikes have disrupted air travel across the region, including flights from the UAE. Emirates, flydubai and Air Arabia have cancelled a number of flights to Saudi destinations, while Etihad Airways has cancelled services between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until October 18.

title: Ukraine detains a gas station worker and a Telegram commenter suspected of scouting targets for Russian strikes
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) detained two men suspected of scouting targets for Russian strikes on Sloviansk and Dnipro, the agency reported on 14 October. Catching both early let it secure Ukrainian reserve command posts and the gas stations the alleged agents had been hunting, the agency added. Sloviansk anchors the northern end of the Fortress Belt , the chain of fortified cities that has held Ukraine’s defense of Donetsk Oblast since 2014. Russia is pushing to seize them, and its aircraft bombed a residential area of Sloviansk on 11 October. Where Ukrainian convoys stop and troops gather is exactly what Russian handlers allegedly asked these suspects to supply. A gas station worker suspected of filming convoys The first suspect worked at a gas station complex in Sloviansk, Donetsk Oblast. Russian intelligence allegedly reached him through a former classmate who left for Russia after the full-scale invasion and now works for its special services, the SBU said . He then allegedly used his phone to secretly film Ukrainian army convoys at or near gas stations. He was allegedly supposed to send the photos and videos to Russia to help it prepare a targeted strike. He also allegedly drove his own car around other gas stations and bridges that the Defense Forces use for logistics. Spotted through Telegram comments The second suspect, a former Pokrovsk resident, moved to Dnipro in 2024 and settled in a dormitory. Russian intelligence noticed him through pro-Kremlin comments he posted in Telegram chats, investigators say. A female handler in Russia allegedly tasked him with guiding missile and drone attacks on places in the city where Ukrainian troops and equipment were concentrated. He allegedly scouted on foot or took public transport to reach outlying districts. Explore further Ukrainians think their own security service is calling—it’s Russia recruiting saboteurs Officers seized computers and smartphones containing evidence of the men’s alleged work for Russia. Both are suspected of treason under martial law and of unauthorized dissemination of information on Ukrainian troop movements or deployment, under Articles 111(2) and 114-2(2) of the Criminal Code. They remain in custody without bail and face up to life imprisonment with confiscation of property. The SBU’s office for Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts ran the operation under the Donetsk Oblast Prosecutor’s Office.
