The SBN network published hateful digital content to incite petty criminals and vulnerable youth. With the formal UAPA tag, Indian law enforcement and intelligence agencies now possess absolute statutory powers to freeze the financial assets, choke the micro-payment channels, and systematically dismantle the domestic remnants of such sophisticated cyber-espionage apparatus.
The Threat and the Way Forward
The transformation of cross-border espionage proves that India's national security challenge is no longer a localized border issue; every smartphone is now a potential point of entry for hostile intelligence networks.
To counter this invisible offensive, India urgently requires robust digital counter-measures. Intelligence agencies must launch aggressive public awareness campaigns alongside tech platforms to educate vulnerable demographics. Simultaneously, law enforcement must enforce stricter tracking of micro-UPI and cryptocurrency trails tied to cross-border handlers, paired with proactive social media monitoring. Protecting India's digital youth demands a unified, tech-driven shield to dismantle these predatory traps before they compromise sovereignty.

title: Chinese national, 18 others jailed over terrorism in Kebbi
body: A Federal High Court in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, has sentenced three men, including a Chinese national, Ripin Liu, to various terms of imprisonment for terrorism-related offences and illegal possession of firearms. Aliyu Hadari and Umar Musa Uzzi were sentenced to 15 years’ imprisonment, while Liu was sentenced to six years. The Chinese national was arrested with a Beretta pistol and convicted in connection with the offences. Delivering judgment, Justice Emmanuel Gakko of the Federal High Court, Birnin Kebbi, held that the prosecution had established beyond reasonable doubt that the defendants provided logistical support to terrorists and conspired to commit terrorism, contrary to the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. The court heard that the defendants were intercepted along Yauri Road while travelling in a vehicle allegedly acquired specifically to transport kidnap victims to a forest hideout. The court also ordered the forfeiture of the vehicle and a Bajaj motorcycle to the Federal Government after establishing their connection to the offences. In a separate development, the court sentenced Mohammed Bello Ibrahim, alias Banki, to four years’ imprisonment without an option of a fine, while Abubakar Siddi received three years’ imprisonment without an option of a fine. Mohammed Bako, Bello Dantiye, Aliyu Dandaula and Abubakar Usman were also sentenced to three years’ imprisonment each without an option of a fine. Buba Alhaji Umaru, who was arrested in Bagudo Local Government Area after allegedly crossing into the country from a neighbouring country with a locally fabricated pistol, was sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. John Zweme received two years and six months’ imprisonment with an option of a fine, while Aliyu Bako and Sani Alaramma were each sentenced to two years’ imprisonment with an option of a fine. The police command also secured the conviction of six persons identified as economic saboteurs: Sani Tanko, Ibrahim Hamza, Samson Sunday, Abdulrahman Isah, Adamu Musa and Masudu, for vandalising and stealing electric cables in the Sakaba area of Kebbi State. They were sentenced to various terms of imprisonment ranging from three to eight years.

title: ‘I don’t make music for awards, I make it to connect people’ – Rocky Dawuni
body: Four-time Grammy nominee Rocky Dawuni says his music career is driven by a desire to inspire connection, unity and positive change, rather than win awards. In an exclusive interview on Joy Prime’s Prime Time , hosted by George Quaye, the Ghanaian international reggae and Afro-Roots star reflected on his journey from Ghana to the world stage and how he has remained consistent for more than two decades. Rocky Dawuni is currently Ghana’s most nominated artiste at the Grammys, with four nominations to his credit. His first Grammy nomination came in 2015 when his sixth studio album, Branches of The Same Tree , was nominated for Best Reggae Album. He earned his second nomination in 2021/2022 with Voice of Bunbon Vol. 1 in the Best Global Music Album category, followed by his third nomination in 2023 with the single Never Bow Down , later listed as Neva Bow Down , in the Best Global Music Performance category. His fourth nomination came at the 67th Grammy Awards for his uplifting single Rise , which competed in the Best Global Music Performance category at the 2025 Grammys against works by global artistes, including Angélique Kidjo and Soweto Gospel Choir, Arooj Aftab, Jacob Collier and Sheila E. Speaking on Joy Prime, the artiste said that while the nominations were humbling, they had never been his driving force. Known for his signature Afro-Roots sound, which blends reggae, Afrobeat, highlife and soul, Rocky said his authenticity was what had sustained him. “I’m a proud African, and I make sure the identity of my roots is always reflected in my music,” he has often stated in past interviews. On Prime Time , he reiterated that Ghanaian music has a unique spirit that resonates globally when delivered truthfully. He also urged young artistes to focus on their message and originality rather than trends. Beyond music, Rocky Dawuni has built a career as an activist, UN Goodwill Ambassador and cultural ambassador for Ghana. Last year, he was among five distinguished creatives honoured with diplomatic passports by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for their global contributions to Ghana’s image. He has also used major platforms such as CARIFESTA XV in Barbados to promote Pan-African solidarity, describing such appearances as a “homecoming, reconnection and spiritual bonding”. The reggae legend also highlighted the need for more structural support for Ghana’s creative arts industry and called for national unity and prayer. His message aligns with the ticker on the show inviting the public to the October edition of the Monthly Intercessory Prayers for Ghana. Rocky Dawuni was celebrated on the show for not only raising Ghana’s flag high but also demonstrating that conscious music can break international barriers.

title: After Trump, Musk tells Ukraine’s president to go. Zelenskyy says he won’t resign and will never accept Ukrainian land as Russian
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Tech billionaire Elon Musk wrote on X on 15 October: “And so the slaughter continues … Time for Zelensky to go.” Four days earlier, he had posted that Zelenskyy had gone too far, after US President Donald Trump said it was time for Ukraine to get a new president. Asked by Morgan on 14 October whether he would resign, Zelenskyy said he would not: “It’s my responsibility.” Musk’s post comes as Washington squeezes Kyiv instead of Moscow: Ukraine’s military satellite links slowed , US missile warnings went missing, and the US threatened to cut intelligence unless Kyiv stops hitting Russian refineries. Land and elections Zelenskyy said elections could not be held under constant Russian attack: “ From the point of security, you can’t do elections.” Of any future president, he said: “I’m sure the new man or woman will defend our country.” He also reminded Trump that Crimea and parts of Donbas were already occupied when he took office, under another president, long before the full-scale invasion. “I’m a realist, and I understand that people are more important than one kilometer or two kilometers. It’s not about kilometers. It’s about land and homes,” he told Morgan. Zelenskyy has said Ukraine is ready for elections if a full 60-day ceasefire is in place. Numerous sources told The Atlantic that Trump sees Zelenskyy as the main obstacle to a peace deal and related business deals with Russia. One Trump adviser said he is also an obstacle to Trump’s hopes for the Nobel Peace Prize. Starlink Ukrainian forces reported restrictions on Starshield, the SpaceX satellite system they use for battlefield communications and drone operations, and Zelenskyy warned the decision would cost lives. On 14 October, Musk said Starshield is owned and controlled by the US government, which sets its limits, and that commercial Starlink cannot be used for offensive military action. Zelenskyy told the FT he did not know whether the decision was SpaceX’s or the US government’s, adding: “I think it’s about SpaceX.” A senior US official told Axios the Trump administration had nothing to do with the restrictions. Intelligence and refineries On two consecutive nights, air raid alerts in Kyiv sounded only after Russian ballistic missiles were already approaching or striking the capital. Zelenskyy said Ukraine received no warning from partners of the launches on 12 and 13 October, which hit civilian infrastructure and a major power plant. A Ukrainian official told CNN the loss of intelligence “will give Russians a real leverage on a frontline.” A European official questioned Washington’s explanation that weather caused the gaps in missile warnings. Trump denied halting intelligence sharing. Washington had warned it could suspend intelligence sharing if Ukraine kept striking Russian refineries, Axios reported . A US official disputed that any explicit threat was made. Sources told CNN the US had also threatened to halt European purchases of US weapons for Ukraine. Zelenskyy told the FT the warning came through military channels. To lower energy costs before next month’s midterm elections, Trump has pressed Kyiv to stop refinery strikes, CNN reported . Zelenskyy said he felt betrayed after Trump announced a diesel supply deal with Russia. On 14 October in London, he told the FT that Ukraine would resume strikes on Russian oil refineries. Read also “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government”: Musk says Trump, not SpaceX, is behind cut hitting Ukraine Fears that Ukraine will lose Starlink are back after Musk backed Trump against Zelenskyy. Adviser says profit makes cutoff unlikely Energy truce with strings attached: Kyiv reportedly told to spare Russian refineries or lose US intelligence and arms

title: EU-Gulf summit in Saudi Arabia postponed due to security concerns
body: The EU and Gulf states have agreed to postpone their summit that was due to be held in Saudi Arabia on October 24, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.The sources confirmed remarks by Bulgaria's Prime Minister Rumen Radev, who earlier on Thursday said he had understood the meeting would be scrapped due to security concerns."Unfortunately, as far as I know, this meeting in Riyadh will be postponed, maybe for security reasons," Radev told reporters on arrival at a summit of EU leaders in Brussels.EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said discussions about the summit were ongoing. "You will hear when there is something to announce," she told reporters in Brussels.Saudi coalition intercepts Houthi drones, missilesOn Tuesday, the Saudi-led coalition said that it intercepted three missiles and two drones fired by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi terrorists towards Riyadh and Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran.The initial interception announcement regarding Dhahran came after loud booms were heard in the area, six sources told Reuters on Tuesday, with the coalition saying that missile fragments fell in a nearby residential area.Four people were injured and 15 homes sustained limited damage in Riyadh after debris from two intercepted missiles fell on the Saudi capital, the state news agency SPA reported on Wednesday, citing the Civil Defense spokesperson.

title: Trump’s envoy calls return of Russian flag, anthem to Paralympians meaningful step
body:
WASHINGTON, October 15. /TASS/. The return of the Russian flag and anthem to Russian Paralympians at the Olympic Games in Italy was a "meaningful step," US Special Envoy for Global Partnerships Paolo Zampolli said in an interview with TASS.
"I have consistently supported the principle that athletes should not become permanent substitutes for political negotiations. The return of the Russian flag and anthem for Paralympians in Italy was a meaningful step, and I welcomed it. I am optimistic that continued progress can create a credible route toward fuller Russian participation at Los Angeles 2028," said the diplomat who works both in the White House and the US State Department.
The six Russian Paralympians competed in Italy under their national flag and anthem, winning eight gold, one silver and three bronze medals to finish third in the overall standings. The 14th Winter Paralympic Games were held in Italy from March 6 to 15, 2026.
The full text of the interview is available on the TASS website: https://tass.com/world/2202537 .

title: Hungarian PM Magyar hopes that meeting with Zelenskyy in Brussels will help ‘open new chapter’ in relations
body:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar hopes that a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, scheduled for Friday morning in Brussels, will "open a new chapter" in their relations. However, he does not anticipate Ukraine’s accession to the European Union in the near future, noting that the entire process could take 15–20 years.
He made these remarks to journalists in Brussels on Thursday upon his arrival for a meeting of the European Council.
"On Friday morning, I am set to have a brief meeting here, at the Council building, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy... We shall see what we can discuss in more detail during those 10–15 minutes. I hope we reach a point where a new chapter [in our relations] truly opens, and we might be able to meet in Berehove, where a Hungarian-speaking majority resides," Magyar stated.
When asked whether there is a specific date for Ukraine’s EU accession, the Hungarian Prime Minister noted that "no such date exists." "Look at the Western Balkan countries—they have been trying to join for 15 years. They have begun accession negotiations, yet one could argue they are not much closer to joining now than they were at the start. I don't believe it is possible to determine [an accession date]," he emphasized.
Magyar stressed that he "believes in accession negotiations based on merit." "We do not believe in 'greater' or 'stronger' membership, in passive membership, or in parallel membership; we believe in genuine membership. But that could take 15 or 20 years," he said.
The Hungarian prime minister also pointed to the example of Turkey: "Look at Turkey—it wanted to join for decades, but now it doesn't really want to anymore. The mere fact that someone begins negotiations means nothing in itself. I think this is a good thing for us; everyone can see the historic success we have achieved in just a few weeks—namely, that we have been able to strengthen the rights of the Hungarian minority living there in the Carpathians—or the rights of a future Hungarian minority—regarding education, the use of language, and official procedures. From this perspective, it is a positive outcome for us. That is diplomacy. We asked for guarantees, and it seems we have received them from the Ukrainians," said the Hungarian leader.

title: Farmer jailed for three months over assault on wife in viral video
body: A 30-year-old farmer, Emmanuel Kwofie, has been sentenced to three months’ imprisonment with hard labour for assaulting his wife in an incident that went viral on social media. The Agona Nkwanta District Police Command secured his conviction on Wednesday, October 14, after he pleaded guilty to the assault charge before the Agona Nkwanta District Court. According to a statement issued by the Western Regional Police Command, Kwofie and his wife, Diana Mensah, a second-hand clothing trader, live together at Domeabra in the Agona Nkwanta Municipality. Police investigations established that on October 8, Kwofie accused his wife of having an extramarital affair and subjected her to a severe beating, as captured in the viral video. He was arrested on October 12 and arraigned before the court two days later. The court, presided over by His Worship Kuma Selorm Dzata, convicted him on his own plea and sentenced him to three months’ imprisonment with hard labour.

title: Fry and Sim face off in Vancouver, but other mayoral candidates reject spoiler label
body:
Vancouver mayoral candidates Ken Sim and Pete Fry view each other as their main rival in the battle for City Hall.
But while recent polling suggests the mayoral race is indeed a faceoff between incumbent Sim and two-term Green Councillor Fry, there are three other big-name candidates who reject the label of spoiler.
Kareem Allam — Sim’s former chief of staff turned litigation adversary — is running with the Vancouver Liberals, which is not affiliated with the federal party.
“The pollsters don’t always get it right. Municipal government is also the hardest level to poll. It’s got its tricks and nuances, especially in an at-large system,” he said in an interview Tuesday.
The Vancouver race culminates Saturday, when municipalities across British Columbia go to the polls.
Interest in the Vancouver race appears high. The City of Vancouver says more than 103,000 people have voted in advance, up 60 per cent from roughly 65,000 voters over five advance days in 2022.
Sim, who is campaigning for a second term as mayor with the right-of-centre ABC Vancouver, said while he would be the first to admit he didn’t get everything right during his tenure, he believes he can lead the city in the right direction.
“We’ve gotten some pretty significant things done, but there’s way more work to do,” he said in an interview Wednesday.
Other candidates include Rebecca Bligh, a two-term councillor who helped get Sim elected with ABC Vancouver in 2022 and is now running with Vote Vancouver, and TEAM candidate Colleen Hardwick, a former councillor.
Allam, Hardwick and Bligh all rejected the notion their candidacies could split the centre or centre-right vote.
“The question is not left or right. The question is about who we are serving at city hall,” Hardwick said Tuesday.
Bligh said she was running to govern for Vancouver’s ignored middle class, and polling did not change how she campaigned.
“It’s anyone’s race,” she said in an interview Wednesday.
Fry, son of longtime Liberal MP Hedy Fry, has acknowledged benefiting from the narrowing of the progressive field, after the withdrawals of William Azaroff from OneCity Vancouver and Stephanie Allen for COPE Vancouver.
After ending his candidacy, Azaroff appeared at City Hall with Fry, who praised him for running a serious campaign that “raised real issues” such as housing, small business and affordability.
“I think folks are excited to be able to talk up a viable alternative to Ken Sim as the mayor of Vancouver and really reset,” Fry said in an interview Tuesday.
He added that Azaroff’s withdrawal was recognition that he was the person best suited to defeat Sim.
Bligh said she’s a progressive candidate with a centrist platform. Meanwhile, Allam said he believed he was taking votes from Sim and Fry equally.
The candidates’ platforms all emphasize quality-of-life issues, including affordability and public safety. Sim’s promises include a zero per cent property tax increase.
The election ballot also includes two plebiscite questions on public safety.
The non-binding questions ask voters if they’re in favour of the city “strengthening its laws to forbid open-air hard drug use in public spaces,” which is already illegal in B.C. The other asks if the city should ask the province to convert portions of the old St. Paul’s hospital into a “secure medical facility” with 100-plus involuntary care beds.
Hardwick called the questions a “populist election tactic,” while other critics said they aren’t realistic.
Sim said strengthening the city health bylaw — regulating conduct such as smoking in common areas — would allow officers to issue tickets or confiscate drugs without arrests. The involuntary care question, he said, is about asking the province to fulfil its accountability to people who pose a risk to their own safety or others.
Fry said he supports managing drug use in public spaces, but differs from Sim in believing that people should be diverted to supervised consumption sites or shelters.
His platform focuses on housing, transportation and the economy. “Folks should be able to have a good life in this city, he said.
Bligh said Sim’s property tax freezes protect wealthy landowners and undercut critical services. She said she would work with the federal government to leverage city-owned land and provide free transit for youth.
Hardwick said the key to livability in Vancouver is effective city planning. She said she wanted to repeal the city’s official development plan and re-establish neighbourhood planning offices
Allam said he wants to bring youth back to Vancouver by improving affordability through jobs and housing, and investing in parks and community centres.
He said his platform cuts across ideologies, and distanced himself from Sim, who filed a lawsuit in May 2025 alleging Allam falsely accused him of drinking and driving.
Sim faces his own defamation lawsuit from councillor Sean Orr, filed after falsely accusing Orr of distributing illegal drugs in comments to Chinese-speaking reporters.
For now, the focus is on the ballot box.
“I think people will be surprised at the results,” Allam said.

title: Police arrest eight in Okaishie operation targeting illicit drugs and medicines
body: The Ghana Police Service has arrested eight suspects in an intelligence-led operation targeting the alleged sale and distribution of narcotic substances and unregulated pharmaceutical products at Okaishie Drug Lane in Accra. The arrests were made on Friday, 9 October 2026, as part of efforts to clamp down on the illegal trade in substances that could pose risks to public health and safety. In a statement, the Police Service said the operation targeted individuals suspected of selling and distributing narcotic substances and pharmaceutical products outside the appropriate regulatory controls. The eight suspects have been identified as Jeremiah Chinedu, 33; Godsway Dabla, 29; Nwaiyo Charles, 64; Nwachukwu Kanawu, 41; John Divine; Gideon Edioke, 29; Ikechukwu Paul, 60; and Okwesibieze Precious, 23. During the operation, the police retrieved suspected Tramadol tablets in strengths of 225mg and 250mg, Rohypnol tablets, codeine-containing products, Benyling products and other assorted pharmaceutical substances. The items have been secured as exhibits to support ongoing investigations. The Police Service said all eight suspects remained in custody as investigations continued into the alleged activities. The operation forms part of the Ghana Police Service’s efforts to tackle the illegal sale and distribution of narcotic substances and unregulated pharmaceutical products. The Service reiterated its commitment to combating the trade, citing the need to protect public health and safety. “The Police remain committed to combating the illicit trade in narcotic substances and unregulated pharmaceutical products to protect public health and safety of all,” the statement said.

title: Russian Rapper Navai Detained at Kazakhstan Border on Suspicion of Drug Smuggling
body: Russian rapper Navai Bakirov, known professionally as Navai, was detained on October 13 while entering Kazakhstan from Kyrgyzstan. A Kazakh court has since ordered him held in custody as police investigate suspected drug smuggling and unlawful possession of narcotics. Police in Kazakhstan’s Zhambyl region said officers and border guards discovered and seized a narcotic substance during a search of his vehicle at the Korday checkpoint . They have not identified the substance or disclosed the quantity seized. Navai had performed in Bishkek the previous day as part of a Central Asian concert tour. His concert scheduled for October 14 in Astana was canceled, with organizers citing technical reasons. Kyrgyzstan’s State Border Service has launched an internal investigation into how the musician passed through its Ak-Zhol checkpoint. The service said it would take action if any violations by border officials were uncovered. Navai is a singer of Azerbaijani descent who rose to prominence as part of the duo HammAli & Navai. The duo’s popular songs include “Pustite Menya na Tantspol” (“Let Me on the Dance Floor”), “Pryatki” (“Hide and Seek”), and “Devochka-Voyna” (“Warrior Girl”).

title: Burnaby school district says cyberattack may have leaked student, parent info
body:
Public school officials in Burnaby, B.C., say hackers may have obtained student and parental information in a recent cyberattack.
The Burnaby School District says in an online notice that the ransomware attack it suffered on Sept. 21 affected school websites and portals, internal network services and phone lines.
The notice says hackers copied and stole files that may have contained lists of parent, guardian and student names and contact information, as well as birthdates, grades and school names.
It says the hackers may also have obtained registration forms, kindergarten assessment notes and detailed lists of students on specialized learning plans.
The school district says the matter is in the hands of the RCMP and B.C.’s privacy commissioner, adding that its system security is being evaluated to prevent further breaches.
It says staff, students and their families have been offered registration with TransUnion’s fraud alert service and encourages them to be wary of any suspicious communications.
“We understand that incidents of this nature are concerning and we remain committed to keeping the Burnaby Schools community updated throughout this process, as the investigation proceeds and additional information becomes available,” the notice says.

title: Riyadh Fashion Week postponed to next year in latest Saudi event shake-up
body: Riyadh Fashion Week has been postponed until next year, organisers said late on Wednesday, a day before the event was scheduled to begin in the Saudi capital. The fourth iteration of the annual fashion event was to run from October 15 to 20, bringing together local and international designers for six days of runway shows and industry meetings. The changes come amid heightened regional tension and Saudi security concerns, although organisers of Riyadh Fashion Week have not publicly linked their decision to the situation. The decision is the latest in a series of changes to Saudi Arabia's cultural and entertainment calendar, after the postponement of the Red Sea International Film Festival and the cancellation of this year's Soundstorm music festival. View this post on Instagram The Red Sea International Film Festival, originally scheduled to take place in Jeddah from December 3 to 12, has been pushed back to the last quarter of 2027. Organisers said the decision followed a review of the event's timing and logistical requirements, but did not give a more specific reason. Meanwhile, the Joy Awards , which are usually held in January and have attracted leading Arab and international stars to Riyadh, are reportedly set to be scrapped in 2027 amid a broader reassessment of spending on major entertainment events. The General Entertainment Authority and MBC Group, organisers of the ceremony, have yet to officially confirm the move. First held in 2023, Riyadh Fashion Week was launched as part of efforts by the Saudi Fashion Commission to promote the kingdom's growing fashion industry and provide a platform for local designers to reach international audiences. The event has since grown in prominence, attracting major international labels alongside established and emerging Saudi talent. Last year's edition featured British fashion house Vivienne Westwood , which opened the event, while Stella McCartney made her Saudi debut with a runway show that brought the week to a close. The programme also highlighted regional designers, reflecting the event's ambition to establish Riyadh as a destination on the international fashion calendar. Organisers have yet to announce the dates or programme for the 2027 edition.

title: CBN’s rate cut appropriate, monetary stance still tight — IMF
body: …Inflation decline supports monetary policy recalibration …Calls for structural reforms to attract private investment, create jobs …Warns against relying solely on oil revenues to finance development The International Monetary Fund, IMF, has endorsed the Central Bank of Nigeria’s, CBN, decision to adjust its monetary policy stance, saying the move was appropriate given the significant progress recorded in reducing inflation, even as monetary conditions remain tight. The Fund also urged the Federal Government to mobilise more revenue from non-oil sources, deepen structural reforms to attract private investment and create jobs, and ensure that savings from subsidy reforms are channelled towards vulnerable Nigerians. Speaking at a press briefing on Its Regional Economic Outlook for the Sub Saharan Africa, October 2026, during the ongoing IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings, Bangkok, Thailand, Director, African Department, Zeine Zeidane, said Nigeria’s progress in reducing inflation had provided room for a recalibration of monetary policy without necessarily signalling a shift towards monetary easing. He said the CBN’s decision to reduce the real interest-rate burden was appropriate, given the improvement in the inflation outlook, but stressed that monetary conditions remained restrictive. “Now, on the question on monetary policy, what I can say is that, in the case of Nigeria, they have made significant progress towards lowering inflation because it has been coming from a high level, and they had a high real interest rate. “So, they decided to normalise the monetary policy to lower that real interest rate, which is appropriate in our view. It’s the right thing to do. “And it’s not easing yet because the stance itself remains a tight stance. So, the qualification that the central bank did is the right one, in our view,” Zeidane said. Zeidane however, stressed that Nigeria needed to complement its monetary policy efforts with fiscal and structural reforms capable of strengthening economic growth, attracting investment and creating jobs. Defending the decision of the Fund to upgrade its forecast for Nigeria’s economic growth in 2026 to 4.2 per cent, Deputy Director, African Department, Montfort Mlachila, said Nigeria was benefiting from improved international oil prices, which had boosted foreign exchange receipts and contributed to the improvement in external reserves. He said the increase in foreign exchange inflows had also supported liquidity in the economy, while the decline in inflation had improved the overall macroeconomic environment. “So, in terms of growth, Nigeria is benefiting from the improved oil prices, which has raised the amount of foreign exchange receipts and, therefore, reserves have also improved, and there’s more liquidity in the economy. “So, we are upgrading the growth this year from 4.0 last year to 4.2, and a similar level, 4.3 next year,” Mlachila said. He attributed the projected growth partly to favourable external conditions, particularly higher oil prices, while identifying services as the principal driver of domestic economic expansion. “Growth this year is largely driven, apart from benefiting from the very propitious external environment, growth in the economy is mostly driven by services. “And also, one thing which has happened over the past several months, starting in 2025, is a significant decline in inflation, which has improved the overall macroeconomic situation and availability of foreign exchange,” he added. Despite the improving outlook, the IMF warned that Nigeria needed to reduce its dependence on oil revenue and strengthen domestic revenue mobilisation to create the fiscal space required to finance development priorities. Zeidane said the government should prioritise revenue mobilisation outside the oil sector while continuing reforms to improve the country’s attractiveness to private investors. He said: “Our advice for the government has always been to, on one side, mobilise more domestic revenue outside the oil sector to create fiscal space for education, health infrastructure, to make sure that, but at the same time, continue the structural reform to be more attractive for the private sector. “This is a country that has a lot of dynamism, a lot of young entrepreneurs, and a young, tech-savvy population. So, there is, and it’s a large market, very attractive for private investment in general. “But it’s important to do structural reform in terms of governance, business environment, as I said, integration, and so all of these will certainly help accelerate growth and create jobs.” The IMF’s recommendation comes amid the government’s efforts to stabilise the economy following major policy changes, including exchange-rate reforms and the removal of petrol subsidies, which have increased the cost of living for households and raised concerns about the distribution of the benefits of reform. On social protection, Zeidane said governments needed to give priority to protecting vulnerable citizens, stressing that this principle was central to the IMF’s policy advice across countries and not peculiar to Nigeria. “On the question on subsidies, what I want to say is that, as an institution, we recommend in general to governments to pay great attention to social protection and to protect the most vulnerable component of society. “It’s not specific to Nigeria. If you look at our programme, we have many programmes where we have always an integrative target on social spending. We care a lot about the most vulnerable component of society,” he said. He argued that broad-based subsidies, particularly energy subsidies, often disproportionately benefit wealthier households, meaning that governments spend substantial resources supporting consumers who may not require assistance. “Our advice on subsidies is that if you look at subsidies in general, and in particular energy subsidies, they benefit the wealthiest component of society. So, if you do a certain amount of subsidies, most of it is going to those who don’t need it,” Zeidane said. According to him, the appropriate response is not necessarily to withdraw subsidies abruptly, but to phase them out gradually and ensure that the resulting savings are used to support households that need assistance. “And our advice in many places has been to phase these subsidies gradually and make sure that what you save from the subsidy reform is well targeted to those who actually need it. “It’s better to support people who need support than supporting products that actually can affect both your fiscal position, but also, for oil importers, for example, the level of import bill that you have. “So, it’s important to have a targeted system of support to the most vulnerable component of society,” he added. The post CBN’s rate cut appropriate, monetary stance still tight — IMF appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Zelensky: Four Su-34 aircraft destroyed at Russian airfield, two more hit
body:
The head of state announced this on Facebook , Ukrinform reports.
"Last night, Ukraine's Defense Forces struck an airfield in the Voronezh region. Four Su-34 aircraft were destroyed and two more Su-34s were hit. The Russians used them to terrorize our people. These very warplanes were ready to launch new attacks on Ukraine and were loaded with aerial bombs," Zelensky said.
He confirmed that a "Long Neptune" missile was used against the target.
The president also confirmed the use of long-range weapons against a site used to store and launch attack drones in Russia's Oryol region. "A target was also hit in the Black Sea," he added.
"These are our justified responses to all of Russia's terror against Ukraine. Russia is prolonging the war, so our long-range operations will continue," Zelensky assured.
As Ukrinform previously reported, the Ukrainian Navy stated that Ukrainian forces had struck six Su-34M bombers at the Borisoglebsk military airfield in Russia's Voronezh region using the Neptune coastal missile system.
The Su-34M aircraft can carry several guided and high-explosive aerial bombs, as well as various types of missiles. They are among the Russian military aviation's key assets for conducting guided-bomb attacks on Ukrainian Defense Forces positions and frontline settlements.
The Ukrainian Navy emphasized that hitting the Su-34M aircraft significantly weakens Russia's aviation capabilities and reduces the intensity of tactical aviation operations along the affected sections of the front. It added that Ukrainian forces would continue striking Russian military targets to systematically degrade Russia's combat capabilities.

title: How ex-SUG president died at NYSC camp – Official
body:
A member of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), Etimbuk Daniel, has been confirmed dead while undergoing his compulsory three-week orientation course at the NYSC camp in Enugu State.
PREMIUM TIMES learnt that Mr Daniel was the immediate past president of the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of the Akwa Ibom State University.
The deceased hailed from Akwa Ibom State, South-south Nigeria.
Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom announced this in a statement by his spokesperson, Ekerete Udo, which was posted on Facebook on Wednesday.
Mr Eno described the death of the former SUG president as a painful and devastating loss, not only to his family but to the entire student community of Akwa Ibom State.
“I received with sadness the news of the tragic passing of Comrade Etimbuk Daniel, a promising young leader whose life was cut short while answering the call to serve our nation,” the governor was quoted as saying in the statement.
He condoled with the bereaved family, leadership and members of the National Association of Akwa Ibom State Students, as well as the entire student community of Akwa Ibom extraction across the world over the loss.
“Our youths are our future, and losing such a brilliant young man, with a bright future ahead of him, is deeply painful. His passing represents a huge loss to our State and the student community he served with dedication.
“At this difficult moment, I pray that God Almighty grants his family, friends, colleagues and the entire student community the fortitude to bear this painful loss,” the governor stated.
He did not specifically mention when the former SUG president died in the NYSC camp.
Meanwhile, the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) earlier alleged that fake drugs and delayed medical attention might have contributed to the death of the former students’ leader at the NYSC camp.
NANS President Akinteye Afeez, in a statement posted on Facebook on Sunday, said he received a report of Mr Daniel’s death with “a rude shock.”
Mr Afeez said the information available to the students’ indicated that the late Daniel complained of a headache and was administered some medication while at the NYSC camp.
“Unfortunately, his condition reportedly worsened after taking the drugs. He requested to be taken to the hospital, but the necessary approval allegedly came too late, and he passed away before he could be taken for medical attention,” he said.
The NANS president continued: “We were further informed that the doctor later identified the drugs administered to him as fake.
“These are deeply troubling allegations that require a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding his tragic death.”
Mr Afeez stressed that the student community had now entered into mourning even as he condoled with the family, friends, colleagues, and the entire Akwa Ibom State University community over the loss.
“The menace of fake drugs continues to pose a grave threat to lives in our society, and this tragic incident underscores the urgent need for accountability, proper medical care, and stronger measures to protect the lives of our young people,” he said.
“NANS is mourning this painful loss, and our further actions and official position on the matter will be communicated in due course.”
PREMIUM TIMES could not independently verify the claim that the NYSC member died after a fake drug was administered on him.
Also the paper could not immediately confirm that the former SUG president passed after approval to transfer him to the hospital came late.
Like Governor Eno, Mr Afeez did not specifically mention when Mr Daniel died at the NYSC camp.
However, there are indications that the former students’ leader died in the first week of October given that he posted last on Facebook on 4 October, about six days before the report of his death surfaced.
PREMIUM TIMES attempted to contact the NYSC Enugu State Secretariat on Wednesday to respond to allegations that a fake drug was administered on him and that the approval to move to the hospital came late.
A mobile phone number belonging to the NYSC Enugu State Secretariat was unreachable when our reporter dialled the phone line.
The secretariat was also yet to respond to a text message sent through the mobile number on Wednesday.
This newspaper also sent the same enquiry to the secretariat’s email address on Wednesday. But the secretariat was yet to respond as of the time of filing this report.

title: David Agyemang Yeboah: Marriage is not the problem; your approach is
body: As conversations about marriage continue to dominate radio discussions and social media, an important question has emerged: Is marriage still worth it for young people? From concerns about financial pressures and infidelity to stories of broken homes and failed relationships, many people are questioning whether marriage remains a worthwhile aspiration. These concerns deserve attention. However, as we contribute to this discourse, we must be careful not to allow painful experiences to become a blanket judgment against an entire institution. Perhaps the question is not whether marriage is the problem, but whether we are adequately prepared for what it requires. Marriage is an institution. It cannot lie, betray trust, refuse to apologise or neglect responsibilities. People do these things. Yet, when relationships fail, we often blame marriage itself without examining the attitudes, choices and behaviours that contributed to the breakdown. This distinction matters because the way we frame public conversations can influence how people understand social institutions. When individual experiences become sweeping generalisations, we risk replacing thoughtful reflection with fear, cynicism and misconceptions. Marriage, like any significant human commitment, requires more than love and attraction. It demands emotional maturity, honest communication, patience, mutual respect, commitment and a willingness to grow together. It also requires people to understand themselves and what they are prepared to contribute to a shared life. Preparation must therefore go beyond financial stability and the ability to organise a wedding. Couples need to learn how to navigate disagreements without humiliating each other, discuss difficult issues without resorting to insults and manage expectations without turning every disagreement into a contest of power. Marriage counsellors often emphasise the importance of communication, conflict resolution and emotional awareness in building healthy relationships. These skills do not eliminate disagreements, but they can help couples address them constructively before resentment becomes deeply rooted. Unfortunately, we sometimes invest more energy in preparing for weddings than preparing for marriage. We celebrate the ceremony but pay insufficient attention to the responsibilities that follow. We must also reconsider the mentality with which some people approach relationships. It is reasonable to expect love, security and support from a partner. But a relationship becomes unbalanced when our attention is fixed entirely on what we stand to gain, rather than what we are willing to contribute. Marriage is not just about finding the right person; it is also about becoming a responsible partner. The Bible offers a useful principle in Ephesians 4:2, which encourages believers to be humble, gentle and patient, bearing with one another in love. These qualities are particularly relevant in marriage, where two people with different backgrounds, personalities and expectations must learn to live together. Patience does not mean tolerating abuse, and humility does not require one person to surrender their dignity. Rather, both partners must be willing to listen, acknowledge their mistakes, apologise sincerely and make meaningful changes. A healthy marriage cannot be sustained by the demands of one partner alone; it requires the consistent effort of both. This is not an argument that everyone must marry or that every failed marriage is the fault of both partners. Marriage is a personal choice, and no one should be expected to endure abuse to preserve it. Rather, it is an invitation to deepen the conversation beyond the familiar question of whether marriage is worth it. As a society, we should be asking how we can better prepare those who choose marriage for its emotional, practical and relational responsibilities. We must also be careful about the lessons we draw from failed marriages. The experiences of people who have suffered betrayal, neglect or abuse deserve to be heard, not dismissed. However, their experiences should encourage honest conversations about the warning signs of unhealthy relationships, the importance of setting boundaries and the need to seek professional support when necessary. Proverbs 15:22 reminds us that plans can fail without counsel, but succeed with many advisers. Premarital counselling, honest conversations about finances, children, family expectations and personal values can help couples identify potential areas of conflict before they make a lifelong commitment. Such preparation is not a guarantee of success, but it can help people make more informed decisions. My position is simple: we should neither romanticise marriage nor condemn it indiscriminately. We should acknowledge its challenges, learn from failed relationships and encourage healthier attitudes towards commitment. Perhaps it is time to stop asking only whether marriage is worth it and start asking what it takes to build a healthy one. After all, a wedding may bring two people together, but their values, character, choices and actions help shape the marriage they build.

title: Zelensky says Ukraine's patience has run out as Kyiv strikes Russian refinery despite US pressure
body: Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian refineries with a strike at an installation in the Ryazan region, the regional governor said on Thursday, after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky voiced his anger at a "dangerous" withdrawal of US intelligence.Since US President Donald Trump's surprise announcement of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday, Kyiv had refrained from attacking Russian refineries, which the US leader had blamed for raising diesel prices on global markets.But Zelensky had voiced increasing frustration with Russia's continued attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, which he said on Wednesday had left 600,000 people without power. He warned that Ukraine would not suspend its own attacks indefinitely if Russia did not reciprocate and also criticized what he said was Trump's favoritism toward Russia.In an interview with the Financial Times published on Thursday, he said Ukraine's patience had run out."The block (on attacking refineries) is out. We're done,” he told the newspaper.Pavel Malkov, the governor of Ryazan, said in a post on Telegram that a major Ukrainian drone attack on the region had sparked a fire at an oil refinery."The material damage is now being assessed. Emergency services are working at the scene," he said.In his interview, Zelensky criticized Washington's eagerness to strike business deals with Moscow and Trump's apparent admiration for Russia's Vladimir Putin.Trump calls for Ukraine to replace Zelensky after announcing Russia diesel dealTrump on Saturday called for Ukraine to replace Zelensky and railed against Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, one day after announcing a diesel supply deal with Russia, aiming to lower fuel prices that have soared since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February.Despite Ukraine's suspension of refinery attacks, Ukrainian officials complained that they had not received any US early-warning alerts in recent days for incoming Russian ballistic missiles.They also said the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite communications service had been slowed across the country, hampering frontline operations and medium-range strikes against Russian military sites.Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X/Twitter that Starshield - the military version of Starlink - was owned and controlled by the US government, which decided on any limits on speed.Zelensky has said that Ukrainian military officials were warned by their US counterparts that Washington would block intelligence unless they halted strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.In the FT interview, Zelensky said the suspension was presented to Kyiv as a technical glitch, but he dismissed the idea that failures of the Starlink satellite system might have been caused by a fault.“It was not a technical problem, it was the will,” he told the FT.Zelensky demands US interceptors in exchange for halting strikes on refineriesAsked whether Ukraine would be open to halting energy strikes as a way of repairing relations with the White House, he told the newspaper he could only agree if, in return, he was given more US-made Patriot interceptors, calling it the “minimum” that would be acceptable."We didn't destroy any relationship," he said, claiming it wasn't up to him to repair US-Ukraine relations.Ukraine claims to have damaged six Russian military aircraftUkraine's military said on Thursday it had damaged six Russian Su-34M military aircraft in an overnight strike on the Borisoglebsk airfield in Russia's Voronezh region.In a Telegram statement, Ukraine's military general staff said it had confirmed damage of varying degrees to all six aircraft.The Su-34M is a large fighter-bomber, costing tens of millions of US dollars apiece and frequently used by Russia to drop devastating glide bombs onto Ukrainian cities near the frontline.Ukraine said on Telegram that it used its Neptune coastal missile system in the attack.Reuters could not independently verify the battlefield reports.Kremlin condemns Ukraine refinery strikes as ceasefire violationThe Kremlin said on Thursday that Ukraine's targeting of Russian energy infrastructure ran counter to US peace efforts, after a Ukrainian drone struck a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region overnight.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that Russia did not perceive that Ukraine had ever complied with an energy ceasefire announced last week by Trump. Ukraine says it paused such strikes for three days but resumed them after Russia continued to attack its own energy sector.Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

title: Russia’s Tu-160 missile carrier remains world’s best supersonic aircraft — Tupolev CEO
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. The Tupolev Tu-160 supersonic strategic missile carrier continues to rank as the best aircraft in its class, said Yury Abrosimov, CEO of the Tupolev company (part of the United Aircraft Corporation, UAC, which is part of the Rostec state corporation).
"The Tu-160 strategic missile carrier is still the best supersonic aircraft in the world, outperforming a comparable aircraft system used by the United States. The Tu-160 holds 46 official world records, including those for flight duration and range," the UAC quoted him as saying.
According to Abrosimov, the modernized version of the aircraft, the Tu-160M, retains the exterior design of the original Tu-160 but is "built on an entirely new technological foundation, incorporating digital technologies, with 80% of its systems and equipment modernized."
"The aircraft’s onboard avionics, including flight and weapons control systems and navigation systems, have been completely overhauled, and the engines have been modernized," he added.
The program to resume production of the modernized Tu-160M was launched by decision of President Vladimir Putin. Under a state contract between the Russian Ministry of Industry and Trade and the Tupolev Design Bureau, the design documentation for the Tu-160M aircraft was fully digitized in a short period. Additionally, the technology for vacuum welding of titanium components was restored, airframe assembly production resumed, and a new consortium was formed with leading industrial enterprises in metallurgy, aircraft manufacturing, mechanical engineering, and instrument engineering, most of which are part of the Rostec State Corporation.

title: Lawyer sues Standards Authority over used-vehicle import restrictions
body: A private legal practitioner has sued the Ghana Standards Authority (GSA), seeking to stop it from enforcing new rules that bar the importation of certain used vehicles. The lawyer, Alex Dodoo, Esq., through his lawyers, Dodoo & Partners, filed the suit at the High Court (General Jurisdiction) in Accra on October 5, 2026. The GSA’s Director-General’s Office received the writ of summons on October 9. The Authority has eight days from service to enter an appearance, failing which judgment may be given in its absence. Mr Dodoo is asking the court to declare that strict enforcement of the National Vehicle Standards prohibiting the importation of used vehicles is contrary to law and unlawful. He also wants an order restraining the GSA from enforcing the standards as set out in its public notices of August 3 and August 14, 2026, plus costs. The notices In the August 3 notice, the GSA announced strict enforcement of the National Vehicle Homologation and Conformity Assessment programme from October 1. New vehicle manufacturers and assemblers, as well as used vehicle importers, distributors and dealers, were required to register with the Authority. The August 14 notice set out the administrative framework for enforcement. According to the statement of claim, it listed used vehicles to be barred from entry: those submerged or damaged by flood, burnt or fire-damaged, with broken, cracked, bent or twisted chassis or safety cage, assembled from spare parts, lacking speedometers reading in kilometres per hour, or over 15 years old. The plaintiff also says the notice bars vehicles not inspected in the country of origin by a GSA-approved third-party body with a Certificate of Conformance issued. The legal argument Mr Dodoo’s case is that the GSA can only prohibit imports of goods that fail to meet a prescribed mandatory standard, or act pursuant to a statute. He argues the National Vehicle Standards have not been declared mandatory by any law or instrument. He contends that only the Minister responsible for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry can declare a standard mandatory, and that no notice to that effect has been published in the Gazette. By treating the standards as mandatory, he argues that the GSA is usurping the Minister’s power and will keep acting unlawfully unless the court compels it to stop. The writ describes the GSA as the body corporate responsible for establishing and maintaining standards for goods and services produced, procured or imported into the country.

title: Ukraine to restart strikes on Russian oil refineries, Zelensky says
body: Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, Volodymyr Zelensky has said, as he accused the US of withdrawing crucial support. The Ukrainian president said he had restricted such attacks for three days at Washington’s behest, while Russia had continued striking Ukrainian energy infrastructure. “We’re done,” he told the Financial Times. Zelensky also accused the US of withdrawing intelligence-sharing on Russian strikes to pressure Kyiv into ending the attacks altogether after it struck a deal to import Russian diesel, and said a slowdown of Starlink satellite services used by Ukraine’s military was deliberate. The Kremlin said Ukraine had “attempted a large-scale attack” on an oil refinery south of Moscow early on Thursday. According to Russia’s defence ministry, four missiles and dozens of drones were intercepted and the falling debris had caused a fire at the site in Ryazan. Zelensky meanwhile said dozens of Ukrainian cities had come under Russian attack in the past day. He previously said he would agree to the so-called “energy ceasefire” announced by US President Donald Trump on Sunday if Moscow also abided by it. But he accused Russia of ignoring the proposed deal within hours of it being announced, with strikes leaving hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians without power. The Kremlin never said it agreed to the deal. Zelensky agreed that he felt betrayed by the US when asked by Piers Morgan on Wednesday night, after Washington appeared to withdraw key elements of its support. The Ukrainian leader told the FT that Ukrainian officials had been told by US counterparts that “if you will not stop [the strikes], we will block intelligence”. Ukraine’s military relies on US early-warning alerts of incoming Russian aerial attacks to mount air defences, limiting successful strikes, while Starlink internet uplinks are used throughout its war effort. There were suggestions that the slowdown to Starlink services was due to a technical fault – something owner Elon Musk appeared to deny was the case, suggesting it was the Trump administration. Trump denied halting intelligence-sharing. “It was not a technical problem, it was the will,” Zelensky told the FT. Sources in Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence told the BBC early on Thursday that Starshield services – the military-focused version of Starlink – had been restored. They said officials were still working to clarify “the reasons and circumstances behind yesterday’s restrictions”. Zelensky spoke to the FT during a visit to London on Wednesday which also included a meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Downing Street – who announced the UK would speed up delivery of lightweight multirole missiles to Kyiv. European leaders have also rallied around Zelensky, with the matter expected to dominate their summit in Brussels later on Thursday The Ukrainian president told the newspaperhe would now only halt strikes on Russian oil infrastructure – which Kyiv says are vital to cutting off revenue streams to its war machine – if the US supplied more Patriot air defence missiles. Ukraine has suffered a shortage of the US-made defences since the outbreak of the Iran war consumed stockpiles. Striking a more defiant tone than recently, the Ukrainian president told the newspaper his American counterpart had an affinity for autocratic leaders like Russia’s Vladimir Putin. He said it was not up to him to mend US-Ukrainian relations given the events of the past week. “We didn’t destroy any relationship.” Tensions have previously frayed between the two leaders. After returning to the White House last year, the pair shared a fiery Oval Office meeting in which Trump implied Zelensky was the main block to a peace deal. Zelensky has since walked a careful diplomatic line, showing willingness towards US-brokered deals while stressing that the terms of any peace deal must be just. But he criticised the agreement between Russia and the US to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel to the US and global marketplace, struck last week, as the US effectively investing in Russia’s war effort. That deal was the latest effort by Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war. That conflict has sent the cost of petrol – and in particular diesel – skyrocketing, souring his standing with the American public. Zelensky told the FT: “The question will be: when will the next deal be? Maybe it will be gas. Definitely it will be gas.” With Russia continuing to strike Ukraine, Zelensky suggested the disruptions to US support were no coincidence. High-speed internet via Starlink satellites is used by the Ukrainian military to guide drones and communicate with the front line. Ukrainian officials have said they were not warned before a speed limit was imposed on the uplink. Its sister service Starshield is provided under a US Department of Defense (DoD) contract. Musk denied that his company SpaceX was responsible for restrictions on the system, suggesting the US government could be responsible for the slowdown. He wrote on Wednesday that the systems were owned and controlled by the US government and “any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [Trump].” The Trump administration has not commented on the issue. The BBC has approached the White House and the DoD for comment.

title: No Vacancy In Senate Presidency, Senators Declare
body: The Senate on Thursday unanimously took a resolution declaring that there is no vacancy in the office of the Senate President currently being held by Sen. Godswill Akpabio. The declaration followed comments during plenary by Akpabio, who cautioned the public against misinterpreting his comments on the bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide. Sen. Akpabio, who said his remarks on the bill (which scaled second reading on Tuesday) were being twisted, underscored that terrorists have no religion and that those destabilising the country are not Nigerians. He added that suicide is forbidden as a Christian, and that discussions around decriminalisation are in line with modern legislative practice. He warned that no one who kills others in the name of suicide should expect heaven or paradise and urged television commentators to be wary of misrepresenting Senate proceedings. He further noted that his ADC of 19 years is a Muslim, insisting he would never speak disparagingly about any religion. In a now charged atmosphere, the Senate President continued by announcing that with the positions of President and Vice President already settled, the Senate Presidency is now the target of political attacks. In support, Senator Fasuyi backed the motion by Senator Monguno, affirming that the seat of the Senate President is not vacant and will remain occupied by Senator Godswill Akpabio. Meanwhile, another lawmaker, Sen. Babangida Hussaini, reaffirmed Akpabio’s contributions to his state, endorsed his return, and raised concerns over hard drugs and substance abuse, which he said must be addressed to defuel criminality, bandits, and terrorism in the country. Akpabio, on Tuesday’s plenary, was alleged to have said that anyone who attempted suicide in Nigeria must succeed or risk being sent to prison, as the Senate debated a bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and establish a framework for suicide prevention. Akpabio was said to have made the remarks while Senator Asuquo was explaining the provisions and objectives of the proposed legislation. Presenting the bill, Asuquo had said it would replace the criminal punishment for attempted suicide with a system focused on medical assessment, treatment, referral and continued support for survivors. “The bill goes beyond removing criminal penalties. It establishes a coherent legal and institutional framework through which government agencies, health facilities, first responders and communities can prevent suicide and respond effectively when a person is at risk,” the Senate President was quoted to have said. He explained that under the proposed framework, people who survive suicide attempts would receive appropriate clinical care rather than face prosecution and imprisonment. “A police station or correctional facility should not be the default destination for a person who requires urgent clinical care,” Asuquo said. He added that the bill would also provide a basis for coordinated suicide prevention services, including crisis helplines, referral pathways and follow-up support for survivors. Explaining the consequences of criminalising attempted suicide, the senator was reported to have said the existing law could encourage people attempting suicide to ensure that they died rather than survive and face prosecution. Responding, Akpabio was quoted to have asked whether the proposed law was intended to prevent people from succeeding in their suicide attempts. Asuquo answered in the affirmative but clarified that the problem was the threat of imprisonment for those who survived. “The fact that you can go to jail and go to prison for attempting and surviving suicide ensures that the person attempting suicide will do everything within his power to ensure that he kills himself,” he said. Akpabio, however, allegedly maintained that attempted suicide remained a criminal offence under the existing legal framework. “But that’s what we are saying now, that as far as we are concerned, we are saying that suicide is a crime for now. And therefore, if you attempt it, you better succeed. If you don’t succeed, we will send you to prison,” the Senate President said. He subsequently alleged to have added that a person who failed to die by suicide could be sent to prison and later rehabilitated. The exchange highlighted the central argument behind the proposed legislation: whether survivors of suicide attempts should face criminal prosecution or receive medical and psychological support. The bill seeks to shift the response from punishment to prevention, treatment and rehabilitation, to ensure that people experiencing suicidal crises can access appropriate care. The post No Vacancy In Senate Presidency, Senators Declare appeared first on Channels Television .

title: FAAC shares N2.428trn among FG, states, LGs
body: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) has shared N2.428 trillion among the Federal Government, state governments and local government councils as revenue accrued to the Federation Account and proceeds from Value Added Tax (VAT) for September 2026. According to a communiqué issued at the end of the committee’s meeting in Abuja, the amount was higher than the N2.338 trillion shared in the preceding month. The total distributable revenue comprised N1.672 trillion in statutory revenue and N756.587 billion from VAT. The committee disclosed that gross revenue for September stood at N3.913 trillion, out of which N131.758 billion was deducted as the cost of collection, while N1.352 trillion went to transfers, refunds and savings. The communiqué stated that gross statutory revenue of N3.096 trillion was recorded in September, an increase of N246.384 billion over the N2.850 trillion recorded in August. However, gross VAT revenue fell to N816.872 billion in September from N834.843 billion in August, representing a decline of N17.972 billion. Of the N2.428 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received N832.242 billion, while state governments received N799.872 billion. Local government councils received N560.660 billion, while N236.049 billion was shared among benefiting states as 13 per cent derivation revenue from mineral resources. A breakdown of the N1.672 trillion distributable statutory revenue showed that the Federal Government received N756.583 billion, state governments got N383.749 billion, and local government councils received N295.855 billion. The benefiting states also received N236.049 billion as derivation revenue. From the N756.587 billion distributable VAT revenue, the Federal Government received N75.659 billion, state governments got N416.123 billion, while local government councils received N264.805 billion. FAAC said revenue from Petroleum Profit Tax, Hydrocarbon Tax, petroleum royalties, import duty, Common External Tariff levies and excise duty increased significantly during the period. However, receipts from Companies Income Tax, Capital Gains Tax, Stamp Duties, VAT, mineral royalties, gas-flaring penalties and fees, and miscellaneous oil revenue declined. The post FAAC shares N2.428trn among FG, states, LGs appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Pope’s cancer operation already reshaping papacy
body: With Pope Leo XIV recovering in hospital on Thursday following his lung cancer operation, questions are swirling about how the illness could change his papacy, less than two years after his election. The 71-year-old leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics had a part of his lung removed on Tuesday and is undergoing further tests to determine if he is cancer-free or needs further treatment. In the meantime, the Chicago-born pontiff is expected to spend at least a few days recovering at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome. He was out of bed after a “good night”, the Vatican said on Thursday, and sources said the pope is upbeat. But experts said the unexpected diagnosis will fundamentally change the papacy in some ways. “Illness acts as a crossroads in a pontificate — it either accelerates its momentum or diminishes its power,” Vatican watcher Giacomo Galeazzi wrote in La Stampa daily on Thursday. Mikael Corre, Vatican correspondent for France’s La Croix newspaper, told AFP the way Leo is perceived has shifted. “No-one expected to be waiting for medical bulletins again so soon — certainly not with this particular pope, who was 69 at the time of the conclave” in which he was elected, he said. When Leo’s predecessor, Pope Francis, spent more than five weeks in hospital in early 2025, the Vatican began issuing regular medical bulletins detailing the pope’s medical treatment and the critical episodes when his life was in danger. In May 2025, tennis-mad Leo — a keen gym-goer — became the youngest man chosen to lead the Church since John Paul II almost 40 years earlier. “He was the ‘athletic pope’ who also proved to be a great traveller. “He may remain both but he will now also be a pope whose health is constantly scrutinised,” Corre said. – ‘Prudent’ – Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20 and his near-term travel plans are uncertain, including a demanding scheduled trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17. He is expected initially to have a scaled-back schedule, with fewer commitments and fewer public engagements. “I think he is going to want to jump right back into things as much as he can. I think he’ll push himself,” said US Vatican expert Elise Ann Allen, who has written a biography of the pope. “But he’s also very prudent. Leo understands his limitations and he’ll listen to them,” she told AFP. The world’s first American pope has gradually imprinted his style on the Church leadership, speaking out on some of the world’s most pressing issues, from conflicts to artificial intelligence. He has also proved unafraid to criticise world leaders or defend himself against US President Donald Trump’s attacks. “We’re not going to see him change his style,” Allen said. “Scares like this have a way of crystallising things for you, of what’s important,” she said. “He will be even more determined, I think.” – ‘Shift priorities’ – Some Vatican insiders think Leo’s illness might “shift his priorities”, meaning fewer trips and more appointments, Corre said. Several appointments are expected soon, in any case. Leo has yet to create any cardinals, the red-hatted Princes of the Church who will vote in the conclave to elect his successor. Five heads of dicasteries — Vatican departments — have also reached retirement age but have yet to be replaced. Leo inherited a divided Church, with liberal and conservative factions that bickered under his predecessor Francis. While he has been tasked with overcoming such polarisation, there are those inside the Vatican who hope Leo’s illness will spur him into replacing close allies of Francis in key dicasteries with more conservative figures, Corre said. Others expect him to forge ahead instead with diplomatic efforts, which have already “brought great stability”, Allen said. “I think this health crisis has eased those frictions even further,” she said. “It’s brought the Catholic Church together in support around Pope Leo in a very strong way,” she said. The post Pope’s cancer operation already reshaping papacy appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: French Foreign Minister calls out Azerbaijan’s ‘provocative’ actions in New Caledonia
body: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot criticised the ‘provocative’ actions of an ‘Azerbaijani group organising conferences in [the New Caledonian capital] Nouméa calling for revolt in the overseas territories’. While he did not mention the name, he was referring to the Baku Initiative Group (BIG), a nominally independent organisation focused on anti-colonial activism. The BIG describes its focus as being ‘dedicated to supporting the struggle of peoples suffering from colonialism and neocolonialism, freedom, independence, and equal rights including the protection of the rights of indigenous peoples and ethnic minorities suppressed by governing authorities’. The bulk of the BIG’s activities are directed at France, with all other conferences focused on allies of Armenia, leading to criticism that the organisation is a geopolitical tool rather than an earnest anti-colonial advocacy group. In the speech on Tuesday, Barrot warned that autocratic countries and their authoritarian-minded ilk are trying to ‘polarise public debate’ as part of their wider war against democracy. Along with the ‘Azerbaijani group’, Barrot mentioned ‘an Israeli firm creating fake French accounts to stage artificial clashes over the Palestinian issue’ and ‘mass online harassment campaigns by Elon Musk’. It is not the first time France has taken issue with Azerbaijan’s self-declared anti-colonial activities targeted at its own overseas territories. In 2024, France accused Azerbaijan of helping foment deadly unrest in New Caledonia, which Baku later denied. In response to Barrot’s latest speech, the Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry again rejected it was doing anything untoward. ‘Accusations that Azerbaijan interferes in the struggle of the peoples living in New Caledonia and other French overseas territories for their rights are entirely unfounded’, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Aykhan Hajizada said on Wednesday. ‘It would be more appropriate for French officials, when speaking about democracy, human rights and the rule of law, to focus first and foremost on the consistent application of these principles in France’s own policies’. Hajizada reiterated that Baku was calling on ‘the French side to put an end to unfounded allegations against Azerbaijan and to uphold the principles of mutual respect, sovereign equality and non-interference in internal affairs in international relations’. Later, French Ambassador to Azerbaijan Sophie Lagoutte responded in kind. Surprising that @AzerbaijanMFA feels targeted & takes such a negative stance, while French minister @jnbarrot did not accuse "the Azerbaijani government" or "officials" in this statement. He only referred to "an Azerbaijani group", consistently presented as fully independant...🤷‍♀️ https://t.co/nC0cVfeF6j — Sophie Lagoutte 🇫🇷 (@Sophie_Lagoutte) October 14, 2026 Apparently undeterred, the BIG has since continued to agitate for decolonial policies in New Caledonia and other French overseas territories. These statements have included explicit calls from activists of the indigenous Kanak people of New Caledonia that ‘we cannot allow France to continue its colonial policy’ in the territory.

title: EU attempts to ban Russian athletes from tournaments contradict Olympic ideals — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Attempts by the European Union to ban Russian athletes from international sports competitions run counter to the ideals of the Olympic movement and the principle that sports should lie outside the framework of politics, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said in response to a TASS reporter’s question on Thursday.
"This does not fit in with Olympic ideals or the general understanding that sports and politics should be separate," Peskov argued as he criticized attempts to politicize sports and actions that he said were inadmissible in terms of Olympism and the status of a country hosting international tournaments.
Earlier, Politico reported that European countries are mulling sanctioning Russian athletes or cutting EU funds for sports federations that welcome Russians back. The options also include visa restrictions, the newspaper added.
The World Artistic Gymnastics Championship will take place from October 17-25 in Rotterdam. On October 13, the Netherlands refused to issue visas to Olympic champions Angelina Melnikova and Victoria Listunova, as well as to Anna Kalmykova.
Thus, the EU is trying to influence the outcome of competitions, Peskov argued. "These are attempts by individual countries to affect the course of contests, deliberately banning the best [athletes] from taking part," he continued.
According to Peskov, everybody knows that the Russian gymnasts who were denied Dutch visas are the world’s best anyway. "I’d like to remind you that our gymnasts to whom [the Netherlands] denied entry visas are the world’s best, and they were traveling there to win. Anybody who knows anything knows that," the Russian presidential spokesman said.
Meanwhile, Russia will stay in touch with international sports federations to defend the interests of its athletes, the Kremlin spokesman pledged.

title: Russia to export up to 125 mln tons of coal in eastern direction this year
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Russia's coal exports in the eastern direction could reach 123-125 mln tons by the end of 2026, Deputy Energy Minister Dmitry Islamov said, adding that total coal exports from the country this year are projected at 211 mln tons.
"The development of the Eastern [Railway] Polygon is still our primary objective. The development of the Eastern Polygon is not just Russian Railways’ project, but a project for the coal industry. We estimate the volume of freight transported eastward at around 123-125 mln tons this year," he said on the sidelines of Russian Energy Week.
According to the Russian Energy Ministry’s figures, coal shipments in the eastern direction reached 118.2 mln tons in 2025, an increase of 6.1% compared to 2024.
The Russian Energy Week (REW) International Forum is taking place in Moscow from October 14 to 16. It is being held with the support of the Government of the Russian Federation, the Ministry of Energy of the Russian Federation, and the Government of Moscow. The Roscongress Foundation organizes the forum. TASS is the information partner of Russian Energy Week.

title: List of Champions League top scorers after Matchday 2
body: Erling Haaland, Ermedin Demirović and Nicolò Tresoldi are joint top scorers in the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League after Matchday 2, with four goals each. According to UEFA, the trio lead the scoring chart following the conclusion of the second round of league-phase fixtures on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. Five players are immediately behind them with three goals apiece. Tresoldi, who plays for Club Brugge, made a major move up the rankings after scoring a hat-trick in his side’s thrilling 4-3 victory over Inter Milan on Tuesday, October 13. The forward had previously scored a penalty in Club Brugge’s Matchday 1 defeat to Aston Villa. Manchester City striker Haaland joined him on four goals after scoring twice in his team’s 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday.
