The Norwegian has scored all four of City’s goals in the competition so far. Stuttgart forward Demirović also reached four goals after scoring in his team’s 3-0 victory over Slovan Bratislava. He had opened his Champions League campaign with a hat-trick against Viking in September. Liverpool’s Bradley Barcola, Paris Saint-Germain duo Ousmane Dembélé and Ferran Torres, Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane and Aston Villa forward Nicolas Jackson are next on the list with three goals each. Barcola scored a hat-trick in Liverpool’s 6-3 victory over LASK, while Kane netted twice in Bayern Munich’s 3-3 draw against Viking. Jackson also scored twice as Aston Villa defeated Fenerbahçe 6-0. The results leave a closely contested race for the Champions League Golden Boot, with several established forwards and emerging talents already making their mark early in the league phase. title: 16 killed, 34 wounded in Tonj East violence
body: At least 16 people were killed and 34 others wounded in intercommunal violence involving the Akok Deng Achuil and Thiik Majok Makom communities in Ngap Agok and Malual Chum payams in Tonj East County, Warrap State. Tonj East County Caretaker Commissioner Machuei Bith told Radio Tamazuj on Thursday morning that the casualties were reported on both sides of the conflict between Oct. 12 and 13. “An incident occurred between the Akok Deng Achuil community in Ngap Agok Payam and the Thiik Majok Makom community in Malual Chum Payam, in which 16 people lost their lives and 34 others were wounded on both sides,” Bith said. According to the commissioner, the violence followed the killing of a member of the Akok Deng Achuil community by unidentified armed men in Mader Boma, within Ngap Agok Payam, several days earlier. Bith said members of the Akok Deng Achuil community suspected their neighbours from the Thiik Majok Makom community of being responsible for the killing and launched a retaliatory attack on residential areas belonging to the Thiik community on Tuesday morning. “Certain criminals went to Mader Boma in Ngap Agok Payam and killed one person from the Akok Deng Achuil community at around 5 p.m. The community suspected its neighbours from Thiik Majok Makom of killing their member and immediately attacked residential areas belonging to the Thiik community on Tuesday morning without giving us time to investigate,” he said. Bona Malual, chairperson of the Warrap State Civil Society Network, called for calm and an end to recurring communal violence across Greater Tonj. Malual urged the state government to ensure that those responsible for the violence were brought to justice to prevent further loss of life. “We have been calling for an end to communal violence because it has become a daily occurrence across Greater Tonj,” Malual said. “We have also been calling on the state government to ensure that those responsible are taken to court and held accountable for their actions.” The clashes come as South Sudan prepares for elections scheduled for December 2026, amid concerns about security and the conditions needed for a peaceful electoral process. The post 16 killed, 34 wounded in Tonj East violence appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Central Asian Leaders Unveil Initiatives at CICA Baku Summit
body: Kazakhstan has proposed developing a common transport strategy for Asia, Kyrgyzstan has called for expanded joint investment and industrial cooperation, and Uzbekistan has put forward proposals for cooperation on artificial intelligence. The leaders of the three countries presented these initiatives on October 15 at the seventh summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku. The proposals came amid negotiations to transform the forum into a full-fledged international organization. CICA has particular historical significance for Kazakhstan. The idea of establishing the forum was first proposed in 1992 by Nursultan Nazarbayev, then the country’s president, at the United Nations General Assembly. Thirty-four years later, Astana is proposing to use the platform to coordinate transport routes connecting Eurasia’s largest markets. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev called for the development of a CICA Transport Connectivity Strategy. It would cover China’s Belt and Road Initiative, the International North–South Transport Corridor, the Trans-Caspian route, also known as the Middle Corridor, and the TRIPP project, a planned transport link through Armenia. These routes differ in geography and participating countries. The Middle Corridor connects China and Central Asia with European markets through the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey. The North–South Corridor focuses on freight transportation between Russia, the Caspian region, Iran, and India. For Central Asian countries, developing several routes simultaneously means having more export options and reducing dependence on individual transit routes. Tokayev also linked the prospects for improved transport connectivity to better relations between Azerbaijan and Armenia. Opening transport links in the South Caucasus could expand shipping options between Asia and Europe, although the specific arrangements for operating new routes have yet to be agreed upon. Another Kazakh proposal is a CICA Water Partnership Platform for joint research, technology exchange, and water conservation. Tokayev also raised the issue of protecting the Caspian Sea. For Central Asia, water management is closely linked to growing demand from agriculture and the energy sector, as well as the effects of climate change. Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov focused on investment and industrial cooperation. He called on CICA member states to pursue more joint projects and expand digital connectivity. Japarov also invited investment in the Tamchy special financial and investment zone and proposed developing cross-border digital infrastructure. For Kyrgyzstan, which is involved in building new transport routes between China and Central Asia, attracting investment and developing manufacturing have direct economic significance. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented proposals on the responsible use of artificial intelligence, confidence-building, and climate cooperation. He proposed establishing a CICA expert platform to develop common recommendations and coordinate practical measures on AI. Tashkent is pursuing digitalization domestically and is interested in international standards and technological partnerships. However, the proposed platform has yet to be established. The summit also adopted the Baku Declaration and admitted Laos as CICA’s 29th member, marking another step in the forum’s development. It followed an October 8 meeting in the Turkmen resort city of Avaza, where regional leaders agreed to prioritize East–West and North–South transport routes, as The Times of Central Asia previously reported .

title: CIMG awards drive competition among Ghanaian businesses
body: The Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG), says its annual marketing awards have encouraged businesses to rethink how they attract customers, build brands and compete in the market over the past 36 years. The Institute says the awards have promoted better marketing practices and pushed organisations to find more innovative ways to improve performance. The awards were established to raise the profile of marketing in Ghana and recognise individuals and companies whose work demonstrates excellence in the profession. Over the years, the CIMG award has expanded to cover several sectors of the economy, including banking, insurance, manufacturing, telecommunications, hospitality and the media. Recognising businesses and individuals The CIMG National Marketing Performance Awards cover six main areas: personalities, the Hall of Fame, media and marketing communications, business organisations, products and not-for-profit organisations. Individual awards include Marketing Man of the Year, Marketing Woman of the Year, Marketing Practitioner of the Year and Marketing Student of the Year. Companies compete in categories covering industries such as banking, insurance, agriculture, healthcare, retail, e-commerce and telecommunications. The awards also recognise marketing campaigns on television, radio, outdoor and digital platforms. The awards reward consistency and individual achievement. Companies that win in a category for three consecutive years qualify for induction into the CIMG Hall of Fame on their fourth win. Those that maintain their Hall of Fame status for ten consecutive years qualify for induction into the Elite Hall of Fame on their 11th win. They must, however, continue to meet the Institute’s assessment requirements to retain their status. How winners are selected The selection process has changed considerably since the awards were introduced. CIMG initially relied on committees that visited companies and individuals to assess their performance. The process later moved to formal presentations by shortlisted nominees. Today, nominees complete detailed questionnaires, which independent evaluators assess before the results go to the CIMG Governing Council for a final decision. The assessment considers factors such as customer understanding, innovation, market reach, corporate reputation, social impact and contribution to national development. According to the Institute, the assessment panels comprise 60 per cent technical professionals and 40 per cent non-technical members with the competence to evaluate the submissions. Maverick Research and Media Monitoring Services worked with CIMG to collate and assess the results for this year’s awards. Keeping pace with business changes The awards have also evolved to reflect changes in the business environment. New categories introduced over the years have brought areas such as e-commerce, digital media, real estate, private healthcare and courier services into the competition. CIMG has also moved its nomination and assessment processes online, allowing nominees to submit questionnaires digitally and panel members to evaluate entries through the same system. The Institute says it will continue reviewing the criteria to keep the awards relevant to changing business needs and public expectations. Its regulatory responsibilities are supported by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana Act, 2020 (Act 1021), and the 2023 Regulations (L.I. 2479). For CIMG, the challenge is to maintain confidence in the awards while encouraging businesses to take marketing seriously – not simply as a way to sell products, but as a means of understanding customers, improving services and building lasting relationships.

title: Khmelnytsky NPP starts winter readiness check
body:
A commission of Energoatom and the State Energy Supervision Inspectorate began work on October 12 at the Khmelnytsky nuclear power plant (NPP) to check the readiness of the plant's separated subdivision for reliable and uninterrupted operation during the 2026-2027 autumn-winter period.

"The commission's experts are carefully assessing the implementation of organizational and technical measures, analyzing the technical condition of equipment, buildings and infrastructure, and checking the level of staff training for operating in low temperatures," Energoatom said.

Khmelnytsky NPP Director General Andrei Koziura said the plant provided transparent access to all processes so that the experts could objectively assess the state of affairs and point the plant's staff to what still needs to be improved.

title: 2027: APC targets two million votes for Tinubu in Jigawa
body: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Jigawa State has pledged to deliver two million votes to President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, saying it expects to surpass the votes recorded by former President Muhammadu Buhari in the state. The Commissioner for Special Duties and Humanitarian Affairs, Auwalu D. Sankara, made the declaration while addressing supporters at a one-million-man march in Dutse in support of the re-election bids of Tinubu and Governor Umar Namadi. Sankara said the turnout at the rally demonstrated the APC’s strength in Jigawa, adding that the party was confident of securing overwhelming support in the 2027 elections. He attributed the party’s growing support in the state to what he described as the people-oriented policies and leadership of Tinubu and Namadi. According to him, Buhari secured 794,738 votes, representing 71.84 per cent of the total votes cast in Jigawa during the 2019 presidential election. He expressed confidence that Tinubu would surpass the figure in 2027, claiming that the APC had gained ground as opposition members defected to the ruling party. “Despite the popularity of the late President Muhammadu Buhari, he secured 794,738 votes in Jigawa during the 2019 presidential election because of the influence of opposition parties,” Sankara said. “Today, most of those opposition parties have been swallowed by the APC because of its good policies and people-oriented programmes. “I am confident that we will double the votes Buhari received and deliver about two million votes to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.” The commissioner urged residents to disregard what he described as misleading statements by opposition politicians ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also expressed optimism that Tinubu would receive massive support from Jigawa voters, insisting that the President was committed to improving the welfare of Nigerians. Also speaking, the chairman of the movement, Salihu Atafi, said the Tinubu and Namadi administrations had recorded achievements in various sectors in less than three years. “Mr President has made a significant impact on the lives of Nigerians, including through infrastructure development, youth and women’s empowerment, and improved security in some parts of the country,” Atafi said. He urged youths to sustain their mobilisation efforts and work towards delivering the votes pledged to the APC candidates in 2027. title: LIVESTREAM: Maria Ressa, WNYC’s Brian Lehrer discuss democracy in the age of AI
body: MANILA, Philippines – Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Rappler CEO Maria Ressa will join WNYC host Brian Lehrer for a conversation on democracy in the age of artificial intelligence (AI) on Thursday, October 15, in New York (Friday, October 16, Philippine time). The event, “Democracy Dialogues,” is co-presented by New York Public Radio (NYPR) and Rappler and will take place at The Greene Space in Lower Manhattan. Lehrer, host of the Peabody Award-winning The Brian Lehrer Show , and Ressa will discuss the challenges of understanding, defending, and rebuilding democracy at a time when AI is rapidly transforming how people access information and engage with the world. “Democracy Dialogues” is NYPR’s ongoing live event series examining the state of democracy and the roles of journalism, free expression, and an informed public in sustaining democratic institutions. The conversation comes as Ressa releases her new book, The Fight Back: A Citizen’s Guide to Standing Up to Dictators , on October 13. The event will also be livestreamed on WNYC’s website, C-SPAN, and on Rappler’s YouTube channel. Portions of the conversation will air on The Brian Lehrer Show on Friday, October 16, at 10 am Eastern Time. Watch the livestream starting at 7 am on Friday, October 16 (Philippine time), or 7 pm on Thursday, October 15 (US Eastern Time). – Rappler.com

title: ‘Hardly surprising’ many Alberta business leaders staying mum on separation: expert
body:
Some prominent business leaders have taken a public stand on Alberta remaining a part of Canada, but many more remain on the sidelines as a provincial referendum on that question, and others, fast approaches.
Monday’s Alberta referendum vote includes 10 questions: one on whether should Alberta stay in Confederation or move toward a binding separation referendum; five on immigration and four on constitutional matters.
“It’s a mixed bag right now so far,” said Bob Pickard, principal at Leadership Communication Inc., a Calgary-based firm that advises executives and newsmakers on public relations.
“Some leaders have spoken out with conviction. Others have remained quiet.”
Pickard’s firm was one of more than 80 that have signed an open letter from the Calgary Chamber of Commerce warning of the economic fallout if Alberta were to break from Canada.
The chamber and other business advocacy groups have been vocal in warning of the consequences of a split, as well as measures that could make it harder to attract newcomers into the provincial workforce. But relatively few individual corporate CEOs have taken a public stand.
“It’s hardly surprising that a majority of CEOs are not speaking up,” said Richard Leblanc, a professor of governance, law and ethics at York University. “You can alienate customers. You can alienate investors, so there’s more to be lost than gained, generally, by speaking up about a political matter.”
CEOs of public companies answer to their boards of directors and shareholders, who are often loath to take on undue risks to a firm’s reputation, he added. Top executives are often limited to speaking on matters that directly affect the company itself.
“There’s a tradition in Canada of really staying in your lane,” Leblanc said.
But he said there may be times a company’s board of directors agrees that a CEO should speak out on a matter that affects the well-being of the business. Various economic analyses have flagged higher trade costs, decreased investment and reduced employment should Alberta choose to go it alone.
“Sometimes the risk of not doing something can be far greater than doing something and dealing with the blowback,” Leblanc said.
Oilpatch CEOs — many are geologists or engineers by trade — might not have it in their natures to be outspoken on politics, Pickard said. Some might not want to be seen as “showboating” or “grandstanding.”
“They don’t get the top job because of acts of risky courage,” Pickard said.
“Many of them get that top job because they’re cautious careerists.”
But Pickard said the separatism issue goes beyond being a political controversy, and is a legitimate concern for every business in Alberta.
“I think we’ve seen way too much passivity here,” he said. “And what we need is candid, transparent, courageous leadership communication on this most existential of issues.”
Getting board sign-off on a CEO’s public message is no easy feat and there are likely to be divisions among directors, said Leblanc, the York governance expert.
Some corporations have former prime ministers, premiers and cabinet ministers as directors on their boards, who can advise on when and how to weigh in on politics, Leblanc noted.
Atco Ltd.’s board includes former Alberta premier Jason Kenney, who has been a fervent voice in the “stay” camp, as well as former federal cabinet minister Rona Ambrose.
Atco CEO Nancy Southern is among a handful of leaders at big, publicly traded companies to sign the Calgary Chamber’s open letter. Others include the CEOs of AltaGas Ltd., Keyera Corp. and Capital Power Corp., as well as the heads of Berkshire Hathaway Energy businesses BHE Transmission and AltaLink.
“What we kept hearing was people wanted safety in numbers to sign,” said chamber president and CEO Deborah Yedlin. “I’m not sure that safety in numbers actually materialized the way we thought it would.”
The chamber and other umbrella groups can speak on behalf of members, but Yedlin said C-suite voices can have a greater impact because there’s more skin in the game.
“At the end of the day, the chamber is not risking that capital, the companies are.”
Financial disclosures filed with Elections Alberta show Calgary-based energy infrastructure company AltaGas has donated $5,000 to the third-party advertiser group Vote to Stay.
No prominent corporations or executives can be found on the disclosures of pro-separation-referendum groups.
A few top executives have made their views known.
“We believe a strong Alberta and a strong Canada go hand in hand,” Imperial Oil chief executive John Whelan wrote on LinkedIn last month after delivering that message to a Calgary Chamber of Commerce luncheon featuring Alberta Premier Danielle Smith.
Atco’s Southern, who describes herself as a proud Albertan and Canadian, told reporters after the company’s annual meeting in May that she can’t imagine how businesses could operate efficiently if Alberta were to separate.
Cenovus Energy Inc. CEO Jon McKenzie told a conference in mid-2025 — as separatist sentiment bubbled up following the federal Liberals’ election victory — that the movement is rooted in legitimate grievances with federal policy, but is not a constructive way to address those issues. He said he expected separatism to dissipate once those concerns were addressed.
Since that time, Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government has made a number of policy moves embraced by the oilpatch. Several Trudeau-era environmental policies have been rolled back, legislation has been brought in to speed up infrastructure approvals and Ottawa has deemed a new million-barrel-per-day Alberta-to-B.C. pipeline to be in the national interest.
All this, as global geopolitical upheaval casts Canada as a reliable energy supplier.
“We could have a boom in this province that we’ve never seen before,” said Yedlin. “And we could also ruin it if we’re not careful.”

title: U.S. watching for Canadian ‘interference’ in midterms, Hoekstra says
body:
U.S. Ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra says American officials are “closely watching” Canadian politicians for signs of election interference ahead of pivotal midterm elections next month.
During an interview on “The Really Big Show” podcast that was posted last week, Hoekstra said political ads run by the province of Ontario last year could be interpreted as political interference.
U.S. President Donald Trump ended trade talks with Canada in October 2025 after Ontario aired an ad during the World Series using clips of former U.S. president Ronald Reagan criticizing tariffs and supporting free trade.
Hoekstra also cited recent comments by Industry Minister Mélanie Joly and former prime minister Justin Trudeau and suggested they also could amount to interference.
Hoekstra went on to warn Canadian politicians to keep their “nose out” of American politics in the weeks before the midterm elections.
Trudeau criticized the Trump administration during a discussion at Brown University on Sept. 22.
“There is a pattern here of doing things that are driving up prices for your consumers and not necessarily making anything better for America, by fighting with one of your oldest and best allies,” Trudeau said during the conversation.
In the interview, Hoekstra said Joly made comments about targeting retaliatory tariffs at “politically sensitive states.”
Joly pushed back Wednesday, telling reporters Canada would never engage in election interference and would “never accept that also being done to us in Canada.”
Joly said she has been to the U.S. in recent months and has met with Democrats and Republicans.
Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says Canada would never interfere in U.S. elections. Her comments came after U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra said Canadians should keep their noses out of American politics during the congressional midterms. (Oct. 14, 2026)
“Fundamentally, what I’ve done in the U.S. is to attract investments,” she said. “I think I’ll be able to have good news of investments by different American companies to Canada. And that’s exactly what I’m doing and that will continue to be my strategy in the U.S. and also around the world.”
Hoekstra said if any actions by Canadians end up amounting to election interference, the United States will respond.
The ambassador declined a request from The Canadian Press for an interview.
Tension between the United States and Canada has increased since Trump won the presidential election in 2024, and began threatening to turn Canada into the 51st state.
That threat, and his attacks on Canada, have become a focal point of his stump speeches as he actively campaigns in battleground states ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which could end Republican control over Congress.
At a rally in Bullhead City, Ariz., on Wednesday, Trump went after Canada again, listing grievances over dairy sector trade and repeating his claim that Canada treats the United States “very badly.”
He said Canada will end up being the 51st state because “that’s the only way it works.”
“We don’t need them, but they need us,” he said.
The Republicans are under heavy pressure ahead of the midterms, when the entire House of Representatives and one-third of U.S. Senate seats will be contested. While the Republicans currently hold a majority of seats in both chambers, polls suggest the Democrats could win control of both.
Peter Navarro, one of Trump’s trade advisers, warned Ottawa last month against interfering in the midterms and berated Canada over its successful lobbying efforts in the past.
Speaking at the American Growth Summit in Washington, he told the audience that any Canadians in the room intent on lobbying the U.S. government should “get the hell out of our country.”
“The problem you have is you lobby this country, and you’ve been successful in the past and you think you can keep doing that. Memo to Canada: You cannot keep doing that,” Navarro said.
“That game is up and if you interfere in our elections in Maine or Michigan, you will pay even more dearly.”
The Globe and Mail reported recently that Republican political operatives were on the ground in Alberta earlier this year to help the separatist campaign. It also reported that some Alberta separatists went to Washington to lobby for U.S. government support.
In August, Prime Minister Mark Carney ordered the Canadian negotiating team to call off trade talks with the U.S. after accusing the Americans of making unreasonable demands.
Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre was in Detroit on Tuesday to make a case for tariff-free trade in the auto sector.
Poilievre appeared on CNN, where he continued to pitch the benefits of tariff-free trade.
“We have a 200-year-old relationship, there’s always going to be grievances on both sides of the border,” he said. “We have our grievances with the United States even predating this most recent trade dispute, but I would focus on what we can do together.”

title: Netanyahu vs Bar: Who called who is fascinating, but both ignored writing on the wall - analysis
body: The latest broadside from former Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) director Ronen Bar against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu includes some fascinating new revelations and sparks new discussion.The majority of the focus has been on whether Bar had Netanyahu's phone number and whether the prime minister in the past had always taken Bar's calls or sometimes ignored them.These anecdotes are compelling, and the fight over them shows the depth of miscommunication and enmity between the men.While The Jerusalem Post will take them apart to explain what they really mean, the main point is that all of this is a sideshow.Netanyahu wants the debate to focus on the night before the invasion, but that is a straw man.The October 7 disaster was a decade or more in the making, contributed to by failures of the political leadership and the entire defense establishment after the 2021 war with Hamas, and during the internal Israeli fight over the judicial overhaul.The phone call that wasn'tMore on that in a moment, after explaining the phone drama.Presidents and prime ministers do not have their phones attached to their brains while they sleep.Therefore, they have national security staff nearby, who are designated to receive middle-of-the-night calls to wake them if needed.In Netanyahu's case, as I wrote in my new book, In the War Room, a Shin Bet official, under orders from Bar, called Netanyahu's wake-up staff at 6:13 a.m., 16 minutes before the invasion started.The head of the wake-up staff, Netanyahu's personally selected military secretary, Maj.-Gen. Avi Gil decided not to wake him up.This is not the fault of the Shin Bet.Gil was Netanyahu's personal appointee, empowered to make exactly this type of decision: when to wake the prime minister up in the middle of the night.In that sense, Bar did not need to complain that Netanyahu had not given him his personal phone number because Netanyahu would not have picked up such a call while sleeping.Bar's unnecessary attack on this issue was made because of Netanyahu's unnecessary defense: They did not call me on October 7.No one called Netanyahu personally because the procedure was to call his staff, which was followed.Nevertheless, it is somewhat disturbing if Netanyahu was actually withholding contact information from the Shin Bet chief, and it could indicate that he never trusted him because Bar was appointed by Naftali Bennett.When push comes to shove, who is responsible for October 7?But that is immaterial to the question: Who is responsible for October 7?Netanyahu, the IDF, the Shin Bet, and all officials in their positions going back 10-15 years are responsible because they all participated in propagating the idea that Hamas was contained and deterred.They did not push to see whether cutting a peace deal with Fatah in the West Bank would sufficiently weaken Hamas to cause it to be less of a threat, neither did they attack Hamas in a stronger way to topple it militarily, nor did they leave enough soldiers on the border to defend against a ground invasion which they were sure would never come.These were the true October 7 failures of Netanyahu, the IDF, and the Shin Bet.Additionally, they all misread the 2021 war as an Israeli win, when Hamas chief Yahya Sinwar viewed it as a validation of his strategy to ignite a multi-front war against Israel.Moreover, they all mishandled the judicial overhaul internal fight in a way that led to the country being seen as vulnerable to attack by Hamas. Relations between Netanyahu and top defense establishment figures were so bad in July 2023 that he refused to receive certain critical intelligence briefings lest they expose him to various potential criticisms after the fact.At the end of the day, whatever happened on the eve of October 7 was a tiny part of the story; whether Netanyahu gave his cell phone number to Bar or not does not impact the bottom line. And the person whom the prime minister chose to decide whether to wake him up decided not to, because he, like everyone else in Israel, could not imagine that Hamas would actually do what they did a very short while later.

title: Nigeria’s image: Clarity, competence, not propaganda, will restore trust — Momoh, Peterside
body: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Chairman of the Advisory Board of the Nigerian Reputation Management Group (NRMG), Dr John Momoh, has said Nigeria does not need propaganda to improve its international image, but clarity in policymaking, consistency in governance and competence in service delivery. Momoh said the country’s reputation would improve when government policies were clearly communicated and public services worked effectively. He spoke in Abuja on Thursday at the inaugural Nigeria Reputation Day, themed, “Own the Narrative: Shaping Nigeria’s Reputation Together.” The Channels Television chairman said Nigerians were more interested in effective governance and tangible improvements in their lives than publicity campaigns aimed at promoting the country’s image. “Nigerians are not asking for miracles. They are asking for clarity, consistency, competence. When policy is clear and service works, reputation takes care of itself,” he said. Momoh warned against presenting an overly flattering picture of Nigeria while ignoring the challenges confronting its citizens. “Owning the narrative does not mean lying to ourselves. It does not mean polishing this country until it shines in a press statement while our people are still struggling. Nigerians are too smart for that. We see through spin,” he said. He noted that Nigeria had contrasting realities, including frustrations associated with its institutions and the resilience demonstrated by its citizens through innovation, creativity and enterprise. Citing examples of innovation and cultural influence, Momoh referenced young people using drones to deliver medicine in Enugu and the international popularity of Afrobeats. He described reputation as the cumulative effect of people’s experiences and interactions with a country rather than the outcome of a publicity campaign. “Reputation is not what we say about ourselves. It is what people feel when they deal with us. It is not a campaign with a start and end date. It is daily deposit into a trust account,” he said. Addressing private sector leaders, Momoh said their business practices and treatment of employees also influenced Nigeria’s reputation, noting that the quality of products, fair workplace practices and fulfilment of promises contributed to public trust. He urged media organisations and creative professionals to prioritise accuracy amid the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate convincing but potentially misleading content. “In an age where AI can clone a voice in 30 seconds, be first with truth, not first with rumour,” he said. Momoh also encouraged journalists to scrutinise those in power while reporting credible progress and positive developments. He urged Nigerians at home and abroad to speak honestly about the country, arguing that criticism and patriotism could coexist. “Criticise, because we must. But we can love Nigeria honestly,” he said. Also speaking at the event, former Director-General of the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), Dr Dakuku Peterside, described national reputation as a strategic asset with implications for investment, trade, tourism and international relations. Peterside said Nigeria’s size and economic significance placed it under international scrutiny, making the way the country was perceived an important consideration in its global engagements. “Every nation tells a story about itself. And every nation also lets others tell that story for it, whether it admits this or not. Nigeria is the most populous Black nation on earth, one of Africa’s largest economies. So world is watching. What matters is who shapes what it sees,” he said. He described reputation as “the invisible highway along which capital, trade and talent flow,” warning that a damaged national image could increase business costs, limit opportunities and undermine trust. According to him, a country’s reputation can influence investment decisions, the treatment of its citizens at international borders, tourism and the confidence of foreign partners. Peterside said efforts to improve Nigeria’s image must be supported by tangible achievements, effective institutions and the lived experiences of its citizens. “The strongest narrative Nigeria can project is one our actions consistently affirm and our people can confidently believe in,” he said. He argued that international portrayals of Nigeria had often focused on poverty, disorder and sensational events, overlooking other aspects of its history, cultural heritage and achievements. While acknowledging that some negative portrayals reflected genuine challenges, Peterside said they did not capture the full complexity of the country. He cited the artistic traditions of Nok terracotta and Benin bronze casting, as well as the contributions of Nigerian scholars, writers and Nobel laureates to global thought. He also referenced the continued debate over the restitution of Benin artefacts taken during the British expedition of 1897, many of which remain in overseas collections. Peterside further highlighted Nigeria’s cultural diversity, noting that its more than 250 ethnic groups continued to contribute to the country’s social, economic and cultural life. He said Nigeria needed to play a more active role in shaping how it was understood internationally, rather than attempting to silence criticism. According to him, the country’s reputation would be strengthened when its institutions, achievements and everyday realities provided credible evidence to support the image it sought to project. The post Nigeria’s image: Clarity, competence, not propaganda, will restore trust — Momoh, Peterside appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NSA regional director Emmanuel Reagan files nomination to contest NDC Ashanti Regional Organiser position
body: The Ashanti Regional Director of the National Service Authority (NSA), Emmanuel Fynn Reagan, has officially filed his nomination to contest the Ashanti Regional Organiser position of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), pledging to unite party members and strengthen the party’s electoral fortunes in the region. Mr Reagan, who is the current deputy regional youth organizer, made the commitment after submitting his nomination forms at the party’s regional secretariat, where he expressed confidence in the party’s ability to make significant electoral gains in a region traditionally dominated by the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP). He said his ambition was to help dismantle the perception that the Ashanti Region remains an impregnable electoral stronghold of the NPP, insisting that no constituency should be considered beyond the NDC’s reach. “I promise the good delegates of the NDC that when they give me the mandate, the issue of stronghold will be a thing of the past,” Mr Reagan stated. He added that the party was poised to make significant inroads in the region, urging members not to underestimate the NDC’s chances of winning parliamentary seats currently held by the opposition. “The NDC will make a lot of inroads in the Ashanti Region, and nobody should dream that the NDC cannot win certain seats in the region,” he said. Mr Reagan emphasised that reversing the party’s electoral fortunes in the Ashanti Region would require purposeful leadership, integrity, credibility and a well-coordinated grassroots mobilisation strategy. According to him, the party needs leaders who are respected, capable and committed to strengthening its structures while building confidence among constituents ahead of future elections. He urged delegates to elect leaders who could unite the party, galvanise the grassroots and position the NDC to compete effectively across constituencies in the Ashanti Region. Mr Reagan expressed optimism that, with the right leadership and collective commitment, the NDC could expand its parliamentary representation and improve its electoral performance in the region.

title: Russia receives no official proposals on 'peace plan' for Ukraine — Lavrov
body:
BAKU, October 15. /TASS/. Russia has not received any official proposals on the so-called peace plan for Ukraine, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told reporters.
"We have certainly read the reports from The Washington Post, The New York Times, and other sources because they are widely circulating right now. But we have not received any official proposals," he said following his participation in the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku, responding to a TASS question about reports circulating in the media on the US and Europe’s preparation of a "peace plan" for Ukraine.
"If we go by what has been leaked to the press, there are four points. The last one calls for an immediate ceasefire along the line of engagement. There are no ideas in the leaks I’ve seen on how to move toward long-term, sustainable peace rather than a truce that will inevitably be violated by Ukraine and its European allies. Not a word is said about this," the top diplomat emphasized.
In this regard, Lavrov added that the Western press "consists, in essence, of leaks and rumors."
Earlier, The Washington Post reported, citing sources, that Washington and Brussels are working on a joint peace proposal that would provide Russia and Ukraine with financial and security benefits, as well as lay the groundwork for resolving territorial disputes. According to the article, the draft agreement would consist of four points and include a proposal for Russia to conclude security and economic agreements with Europe, forming the basis for regional stability.
The newspaper noted that the diplomatic impetus for developing the new settlement plan came from a meeting in Florida attended by American, European, and Ukrainian negotiators.

title: Diesel shipments to start any moment, gasoline imports: statements by Novak
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Russian oil companies are ready to start shipments of diesel fuel to global markets at any moment, with commercial terms being negotiated now, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters on the sidelines of Russian Energy Week.
Moscow plans to continue importing gasoline at least until the end of 2026 for supplying the market and replenishing reserves, he added.
TASS has gathered Novak's key statements.
The first supplies of Russian diesel to the US could take place in at least 2-3 weeks: "To carry out the shipments, it is necessary to conclude a contract and load the fuel, charter a vessel and dispatch it to the consumer, which takes 2-3 weeks. Therefore, it is probably necessary to conclude an agreement as soon as possible."
Russian oil companies are ready to start supplying diesel fuel to global markets at any moment: "Our companies are ready to [start] shipments immediately, at any moment."
Negotiations on commercial terms are "currently underway."
Russia plans to continue importing gasoline at least until the end of 2026 for supplying the market and replenishing reserves: "We will continue imports at least until the end of the year as we need to both supply the domestic market and increase reserves, which went down in the summer period to meet domestic demand."
The volume of imported gasoline on the Russian market remains stable at 10%.
Authorities are currently discussing the possibility of banning the export of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) by non-producers until the end of 2026: "No decision has been made yet, but overall, given the current state of the LPG market, the Energy Ministry is considering this option. We will see what proposals it puts forward."

title: Video: Bright light could be the secret to surviving Finland's darkest months
body:
As the days get darker, health experts say a simple light therapy lamp could help ease the seasonal slump — and now's the time to start using one.
With winter approaching and the days getting shorter, health experts are recommending light therapy lamps to help offset seasonal symptoms linked to reduced sunlight.
According to sleep cycle expert Dr. Timo Partonen , October marks the ideal time for those prone to seasonal symptoms to begin using a therapy lamp.
During this period, many people experience changes in sleep patterns, mood, energy levels, and appetite, including increased sugar cravings.
Research has shown that regular exposure to bright light in the morning can help ease these symptoms. Experts recommend using a light therapy lamp for approximately 30 minutes between 6am and 10am, at least five days a week.
Partonen notes that when used correctly, light therapy can reduce fatigue, improve mood, and increase both physical activity and sociability.
While daylight hours will continue to decrease in the coming months, this trend will reverse after December 21, the winter solstice, after which days will gradually begin to lengthen again.
