title: Kyiv’s 3 Main CHP Plants Stop Producing Power
body:
Kyiv’s three main combined heat and power plants are no longer producing electricity, leaving the capital more dependent on supplies from elsewhere in Ukraine, according to a report published on Thursday, Oct. 15.
Ekonomichna Pravda reported , citing sources at an energy company, that CHP-5, CHP-6 and the Darnytsia plant, also known as CHP-4, had lost their ability to generate electricity. Their contribution previously could reach approximately 1.3 gigawatts.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The report concerns the capital’s largest plants rather than the disappearance of every source of electricity within Kyiv. It also identified smaller distributed generating facilities already operating in the city.
Russian forces targeted all three plants again overnight on Oct. 13-14 , Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky said on Wednesday. Energy infrastructure supplying the capital and central Ukraine was also attacked.
Emergency crews began firefighting, clearing debris and carrying out priority repairs at the affected facilities.
The loss of major local generating capacity leaves Kyiv more exposed to damage along the transmission network bringing electricity into the capital.
The city remains connected to Ukraine’s national grid, but available generation elsewhere cannot compensate for damaged delivery infrastructure unless sufficient power can reach consumers.
Lawmaker Serhiy Nahorniak told Kyiv24 on Oct. 13 that Kyiv’s electricity consumption reaches approximately two gigawatts during peak winter hours. He identified damage to transmission infrastructure as a major risk alongside problems at the city’s power plants.
DTEK Kyiv Grids explains that national grid operator Ukrenergo determines restrictions based on the condition of the wider system.
Distribution companies then deliver the available electricity to households and businesses and implement those restrictions.
Damage can also leave neighboring buildings with different supply conditions because they are connected to different lines or substations.
Restoring one connection therefore does not necessarily restore service throughout a district.
Ekonomichna Pravda described outages of up to 20 hours a day as a worst-case winter scenario involving severe cold, further major attacks and restrictions on electricity deliveries.
That is a conditional assessment, rather than an announced timetable for the capital.
Earlier this month, Oleh Popenko, head of Ukraine’s Union of Utility Consumers, warned that further attacks could leave Kyiv facing 14-16 hours without electricity daily .
“Further strikes could result in Kyiv already facing schedules of 14 to 16 hours without electricity in October,” he said.
The length of future outages will depend on additional damage, repairs, available generating capacity, imports and the ability to move electricity through the grid.
On Thursday, DTEK’s official outage page said scheduled stabilization cuts were operating in Kyiv under Ukrenergo’s instructions.
The company warns that emergency restrictions can interrupt published schedules when operators need to balance the system urgently. Such cuts can occur without the advance notice associated with scheduled outages.
The consequences extend beyond household lighting. Water pumps, heating equipment, hospitals, transportation, and communications all need reliable electricity.
Following Wednesday’s attack, Kyiv authorities reported water supply disruptions in several districts , saying reduced voltage prevented pumping equipment from operating normally.
Some facilities stopped in an emergency, leaving residents with reduced pressure or no running water.
The electrical operating status of the three CHP plants should also be distinguished from the availability of heating across the entire city.
Kyiv’s heat supply includes other facilities, while electricity is needed to operate equipment that moves water and heat through distribution networks.
In an Oct. 14 update on emergency preparations , city authorities said Kyiv had prepared approximately 700 generators for water and heating facilities, together with 70 mobile boiler units.
Three diesel power stations with a combined capacity of 16 megawatts had been built to provide backup electricity for water supplies.
Authorities said another 40 megawatts was planned by the end of the year.
The city also reported 480 generators at healthcare facilities and independent water wells at 15 hospitals.
More than 6,000 generators, inverters and batteries had been purchased for residential buildings through municipal energy-resilience programs.
These systems are intended to sustain individual facilities and essential services during interruptions. They provide a smaller reserve alongside the capital’s connection to the national grid, rather than replacing the output previously available from its largest power plants.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Supreme Court hears challenge of law clearing path for Ontario Place redevelopment
body:
The Supreme Court of Canada plans to hear arguments Thursday from a coalition challenging the constitutionality of legislation that smooths the way for major changes at Ontario Place.
The case unfolding in Canada’s top court could reverberate far beyond the Toronto waterfront park that opened in 1971.
Over the years, the theme park featured a spherical theatre that showed movies on a huge screen, children’s play areas, a revolving concert stage and several pavilions suspended above the water.
The provincial government wants to redevelop Ontario Place to include an elaborate spa operated by a private company, a relocated Ontario Science Centre, revamped play and shoreline areas, a parking facility and a provincial police detachment.
The coalition Ontario Place Protectors challenged the province’s Rebuilding Ontario Place Act on the basis that it insulates state action from scrutiny by the courts and therefore violates the Constitution.
The coalition also argued that exemptions from environmental and heritage laws and municipal noise regulations amount to a breach of public trust.
An Ontario judge dismissed the application in 2024 and a challenge of the ruling in the provincial Court of Appeal was also unsuccessful.
Writing on behalf of a unanimous Court of Appeal, Justice Grant Huscroft said there was no doubt that the provincial government’s decision to redevelop Ontario Place is strongly opposed by a number of concerned citizens and organizations.
Political opposition to the plan has not swayed the government and the coalition has turned to the court in an effort to stop it, Huscroft said.
“But there is no basis for the court to do so. The court is not an alternative forum for resolving political grievances. The only legitimate question for the court is whether the impugned provisions of ROPA violate the law or the Constitution,” he wrote.
“They do not, and the appeal must be dismissed.”
In January, the Supreme Court agreed to hear the Ontario Place Protectors’ case.
The coalition says provincial superior courts have historical and inherent jurisdiction to review laws and government actions protected under section 96 of the Constitution Act, 1867, and to provide effective remedies when governments do not respect the limits on their powers.
The coalition says the Rebuilding Ontario Place Act’s scope is unprecedented and appears to violate section 96 by removing the essential core powers of the courts.
It argues the legislation severely limits or entirely eliminates the ability of courts to hold Crown officials accountable through declaratory actions, damage awards and injunctions when they have acted beyond their powers.
The coalition is also seeking to have the doctrine of public trust acknowledged as an unwritten constitutional principle rooted in English common law and inherited by Canada.
It argues the doctrine of public trust maintains that natural and cultural assets are essential to public welfare and must be safeguarded by the state in its role as trustee.
Margie Zeidler, the daughter of Ontario Place architect Eberhard Zeidler, remembers visiting the park as a child.
“It was extraordinary. It was a public place,” she said in an interview. “You could have a picnic in the forest. You could watch films at Cinesphere. You could watch any musical performance at the forum.”
Zeidler, a member of the Ontario Place Protectors coalition, says the provincial government’s actions have made the fight about more than just the historic theme park. “It became more, not about Ontario Place, but about, wait a minute, what democracy are we living in here?” she said. “I didn’t know governments could do that.”
In their written submission to the Supreme Court, the Crown and the Ontario attorney general say the case should be dismissed.
The immunity provided by the provincial legislation does not go as far as the coalition alleges, the submission says: “(The act) does not make Ontario Place a lawless zone.”
Rather, it immunizes the Crown, its servants and agents from civil causes of action arising from specific circumstances, the submission says.
The Crown and attorney general also urge the court to reject the claim that the legislation is invalid because of the doctrine of public trust.
“The novel doctrine articulated by the Appellant is not an unwritten constitutional principle, and even if such a doctrine existed in law, which is denied, there is no evidence in the record that could warrant applying this far-reaching new doctrine to Ontario Place,” the submission says.
The case has attracted submissions from interveners, including several provinces, First Nations, civil liberties groups and environmental organizations.
The Supreme Court often reserves its decisions until a later date, meaning a ruling in the case might not come until next year.

title: Merlin helicopters head to Scotland to protect sub force
body: Four Merlin Mk2 submarine hunters and around ninety sailors moved at short notice from Cornwall to Prestwick to work over the approaches to the Clyde, tracking a new attack submarine on her dive trials and screening the waters around Britain’s submarine base, according to the Royal Navy. The deployment, run under the name Operation Iceblast, took crews and aircraft from 824 and 814 Naval Air Squadrons out of Royal Naval Air Station Culdrose and set them up at HMS Gannet for a fortnight of operations. Captain James Hall, the commanding officer at Culdrose, said: “Operation Iceblast demonstrated exactly what Culdrose and Merlin Helicopter Force are designed to do. That is to deploy at short notice and deliver warfighting readiness from a forward location with a world-class anti-submarine warfare capability, whenever and wherever it is required.” The crews oversaw the arrival of HMS Agamemnon, the newest Astute class boat, into His Majesty’s Naval Base Clyde, then used their dipping sonar to track her while she carried out dive trials. Hunting a friendly submarine of the latest type is about as demanding a target as a Merlin crew will get. Alongside that, the detachment worked with NATO partners including Norwegian and German forces during Exercise Strike Warrior, the large workout for the UK Commando Force that has just finished in Scotland. That included standing search and rescue watch while Royal Marines practised boarding operations with the German supply ship FGS Berlin. Further sorties went into monitoring strategic areas of the North Atlantic. A drone team from Culdrose’s 700X Naval Air Squadron worked in parallel, providing additional security around the Clyde to protect the submarine force. Captain Hall said: “This exercise tested our ability to operate across multiple sites simultaneously. Together, these activities demonstrated the agility, readiness and professionalism of our personnel. “The strategic environment demands constant vigilance. Operational deployments such as Iceblast ensure that our people, aircraft and support teams remain ready to protect the UK’s interests, contribute to NATO security alongside our Norwegian partners, and provide the capabilities required to support the nation’s nuclear deterrent.” He said the exercise was built to test whether the air station could deploy and sustain anti-submarine warfare operations away from its home base near Helston, and that working from Gannet gave a realistic rehearsal of dispersed operations with the logistics and command and control complications that come with them. Lessons from the fortnight will be folded into future procedures and training. The post Merlin helicopters head to Scotland to protect sub force first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Kyrgyzstan Expands Foreign Worker Quotas While Citizens Work Abroad
body: Kyrgyzstan plans to allow up to 120,000 foreign nationals to work in the country in 2027, even as more than 700,000 of its own citizens have worked abroad this year. Although official estimates are lower than four years ago, the country remains heavily dependent on money sent home by migrant workers, particularly those in Russia. According to the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic, Kyrgyzstan received approximately $3.5 billion in transfers from abroad in 2025, more than 90% of which came from Russia. The Ministry of Labor, Social Security, and Migration reported that 736,600 citizens had worked abroad so far in 2026, compared with 798,400 in 2025. The largest group, more than 472,000 people, was reported to be in Russia in March. Approximately 70,000 were working in Kazakhstan, 60,000 in the United States, 35,000 in Turkey, and 20,000 in Germany. In 2022, the authorities estimated that 1.118 million Kyrgyz citizens were working abroad, including more than one million in Russia. However, the figures do not establish exactly how many people have returned home and how many have moved to other countries for work. Russia has tightened its migration requirements and stepped up enforcement of residency regulations. In a report covering the second half of 2025 , the International Organization for Migration (IOM) found that 94% of emigrants surveyed had left to find employment or better economic opportunities. Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev discussed these changes in labor migration during a parliamentary committee meeting on October 13. According to Kulubaev, more Kyrgyz citizens are choosing Turkey and the U.S. for employment, while demand for workers from Kyrgyzstan remains strong in South Korea and Japan. He said representatives from some European countries had offered to accept workers from Kyrgyzstan on the condition that the country accommodate migrants from Afghanistan and African nations. Kulubaev did not disclose which countries had made the offer, saying only that Bishkek rejected the proposal. There has been no public confirmation of the arrangement from the European participants in the negotiations. Within Kyrgyzstan, the unemployment rate fell from 5.8% in 2020 to 3.2% in 2025. The decline coincided with growth in construction, trade, and services, although employment figures alone do not show how much wages have increased or how many former migrants have found jobs at home. During a recent visit to the Batken region, President Sadyr Japarov again urged citizens working abroad to return home . The initial quota for foreign nationals arriving to work in Kyrgyzstan for 2025 was 25,000 people. The limit was raised to 100,000 for 2026. Expanding the quota allows businesses to recruit more employees from abroad, particularly for construction, manufacturing, and other industries where employers face staffing needs. According to the Ministry of Labor, by December 2025, approximately 18,900 Chinese, 11,700 Bangladeshis, and 8,300 Pakistanis had received work permits. An IOM study conducted in the first half of 2025 found a substantial presence of workers from Uzbekistan, approximately 10,800 people. The largest numbers of foreign workers covered by the survey were in the Jalal-Abad region, Bishkek, and the Chui region. The organization linked the concentration in Jalal-Abad to a construction boom that has increased demand for labor in the region.

title: Obuasi SHTS: Number of students alleging sexual abuse rises to 16
body: JoyNews Investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni says the number of female students alleging sexual abuse by the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School rose from 14 to 16 during his investigation. Speaking on Joy FM on Thursday, October 15, about his latest documentary, Manasseh said the initial information he received concerned five students. However, when he arrived at the school to investigate, the number increased to 14. Two additional students subsequently came forward, alleging similar encounters with the headmaster, bringing the total to 16. According to Manasseh, the additional accounts emerged as his investigation into the alleged abuse progressed. “Those who spoke, I have their names on record. When I went there, the number was 14; I am told two more names were added, so we have 16,” he said. His documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow , examines allegations against the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. Manasseh also expressed concern about what he described as widespread awareness of the allegations within the Obuasi community, including among members of the National Democratic Congress, despite an apparent reluctance to speak publicly. The allegations remain subject to investigation. READ ALSO: Obuasi SHS head accused of sexually abusing students is NDC Juaben secretary seeking chairmanship

title: Coastal highway: Wabara demands probe of N15trn project
body: … Accuses Tinubu govt of breaching procurement rules … Questions contract award, environmental assessment and subsequent realignment By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Former Senate President and Chairman of the Board of Trustees (BoT) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Senator Adolphus Wabara, has called for a comprehensive investigation into the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project, raising concerns over alleged breaches of procurement and other statutory requirements. Wabara accused the President Bola Tinubu-led Federal Government of failing to ensure compliance with due process, transparency and accountability in the award and execution of the project. In a statement, the former Senate President questioned whether the contract had been awarded in accordance with the Public Procurement Act, 2007, and other applicable legal and regulatory requirements. He also raised concerns about the engineering design, environmental impact assessment and legislative approvals for the project, urging the relevant authorities to establish whether all necessary procedures were followed. Wabara said the controversies surrounding the proposed 750-kilometre highway had raised questions about the management of public infrastructure projects under the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administration. He stressed that projects of such strategic importance should be subjected to transparent procurement processes and appropriate regulatory oversight. The PDP BoT chairman argued that questions surrounding the contract award, funding and environmental assessments warranted an independent review to determine whether the project complied with established requirements. He also questioned the decision to realign sections of the highway towards existing roads, reportedly in response to climate change and other environmental concerns. According to him, the development underscored the need to examine the adequacy of the original engineering plans and environmental assessments. Wabara called for a comprehensive investigation into the conception, approval, contract award and implementation of the project, urging the relevant authorities to establish the facts and address any irregularities found. He said public infrastructure projects should remain open to scrutiny, regardless of the level of government responsible for their execution. “The secrecy, lack of public accountability and utter disregard for statutory frameworks are alarming and unacceptable in a democracy,” he said. Wabara maintained that major infrastructure projects should be executed in accordance with the law, transparent procedures and established accountability mechanisms. He also argued that the scale of public resources committed to the coastal highway made transparency essential, particularly amid the economic challenges facing Nigerians. The former Senate President said citizens were entitled to information on how contracts were awarded, how public funds were utilised and whether the necessary legal and regulatory requirements had been met. He urged the Federal Government to provide clear answers to the concerns raised and called on the relevant authorities to ensure accountability if any breaches were established. The post Coastal highway: Wabara demands probe of N15trn project appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Bombs, missiles cannot force Iranian nation to surrender
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 15 (MNA) – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that bombs and missiles cannot force the country to surrender.
“Bombs and missiles can’t force a nation to surrender, but if we become divided internally, the enemy will achieve its goal,” Pezeshkian said on Thursday during a ceremony marking the National Nurses Day.
The Iranian president also warned against enemyies' plots to exploit internal divisions and existing problems in a bid to weaken the country’s power and unity.
He further stressed that the Iranian people have decided to stand firm in the face of the enemies, who are increasing pressure on the country by using various means, including restrictions on transport and communication routes.
"The enemy believed that electricity, water and gas shortages, fuel issues, environmental challenges, banking problems, budget deficits, and pension fund issues could divide the Iranian society. However, the people’s resilience and solidarity proved these expectations wrong,” he added.
Pezeshkian lauded the sacrifice of the county's nurses and other medical staff, as well as those who stood firm in the most difficult circumstances to protect the country’s security and territorial integrity.
He also urged officials to avoid words or actions that could undermine national unity and called on them to employ all available resources towards reinforcing public trust.

title: Trump’s New Press Secretary Faces Questions Over Legal Qualifications
body: The White House was facing mounting questions Wednesday over new press secretary Katie Zacharia’s legal credentials, after a faltering first day in the job when she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam. A US watchdog group filed a complaint with the State Bar of California, asking it to investigate whether President Donald Trump’s spokeswoman, the public face of the administration, had broken the law by repeatedly presenting herself as a lawyer without a license. Campaign for Accountability said Zacharia had described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit. “Ms. Zacharia has represented herself as a lawyer repeatedly to buttress her reputation and credibility,” said the group’s executive director, Michelle Kuppersmith. “The State Bar should investigate whether Ms. Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials,” she added. Trump described Zacharia as “an attorney” when announcing her appointment Friday, but journalists have found no record of her being licensed to practice law in any US state. “I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials,” Zacharia said in a statement to AFP, without clarifying whether she held a US law license. Newly appointed White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia speaks during her first press briefing in the James Brady Briefing Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on October 13, 2026. (Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP) | Jim WATSON / AFP Zacharia has not specified where, if anywhere, she was admitted to the bar. Asked by reporters Tuesday where she had passed the bar exam, Zacharia replied, “When I moved to China.” Failed Bar Exam California’s state bar confirmed to US media that it had no record of Zacharia holding a license under either her married or maiden name. Zacharia, 41, graduated from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law. The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Zacharia sat the California bar exam after graduating but did not pass, citing a source familiar with the matter. Foreign nationals cannot sit China’s bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms. Zacharia previously worked for a law firm in Beijing, according to her professional profile. The controversy followed a rocky first appearance as White House press secretary on Tuesday, when Zacharia read extensively from prepared notes during a briefing lasting just 14 minutes. Newly appointed White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia speaks during her first press briefing in the James Brady Briefing Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on October 13, 2026. (Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP) | Jim WATSON / AFP She took questions from only three news organizations, all considered sympathetic to Trump, and stumbled over some answers, at one point accidentally referring to the president as her husband. Her performance drew criticism from former White House press secretary Jen Psaki, now a TV news host, who compared it to a “Saturday Night Live” comedy sketch. Trump, however, praised Zacharia’s debut, telling reporters: “I thought she was very good.” Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public defenders of Trump’s second administration. AFP The post Trump’s New Press Secretary Faces Questions Over Legal Qualifications appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Starlink resumes working in Ukraine — news agency
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Starshield, SpaceX’s military and intelligence satellite program that uses Starlink infrastructure, has fully resumed operations in Ukraine, the RBC-Ukraine news agency reported, citing sources.
According to its information, the Ukrainian Defense Ministry continues to be in contact with SpaceX to determine the causes and circumstances of the previous day's service restrictions.
Earlier, Vladimir Zelensky called the shutdown of Starlink for Ukraine a mistake and asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to restore service. In turn, Sergey Beskrestnov, an advisor to Zelensky and an expert in communications and unmanned systems, reported that SpaceX had limited the operating speed of Starlink terminals for the Ukrainian military to 160 kilometers per hour. According to him, this "disrupted a number of operations."

title: Ingushetia authorities use quote from notorious Soviet security chief Dzerzhinsky in public letter
body: The Malgobek department of Russia’s Investigative Committee in Ingushetia responded to a complaint by local resident Ibragim Tochiev with a quote from Felix Dzerzhinsky, the founder and first chairman of the All-Russian Extraordinary Commission (VChK, also known as the Cheka), one of the predecessors of the Soviet state security agencies. ‘The fact that you are free is not your merit, but our failure’, the letter sent to Tochiev in response to his complaint about the investigator’s inaction reads. The human rights organisation Team Against Torture (‘Komanda protiv pytok’, ex-Committee Against Torture) published a screenshot of the document. It is not known who prepared and sent the letter. Tochiev challenged the decision not to open a criminal case following his complaint about the alleged abuse of authority by security personnel. On 24 June, security forces arrived at his home in the village of Verkhniye Achaluki in Malgobek district. According to Tochiev, the officers did not identify themselves or explain why they had come. They tied him and his brother, Tamerlan, up before taking them outside. Ibragim alleges that several officers beat him while others held him down. He was then taken to the Malgobek district police department, where, he says, he was threatened and held for about a day. Medical professionals subsequently diagnosed him with a concussion and bruising. The administrative case brought against Tochiev contains a different account of the incident. According to this version, Tochiev loudly objected to the officers’ actions, used obscene language and called them ‘enemies of Allah’. This behaviour was cited as the reason for the use of force. Tochiev also alleges that the security forces took flash drives containing footage from CCTV cameras in the yard, as well as the phone of his sister, who had filmed the incident. In August, a court found Tochiev guilty of disobeying police officers. He links the prosecution of his family to a long-running dispute over their house and land, as well as to their complaints about law enforcement officers. The Tochiev family has been in dispute with the authorities over property in Verkhniye Achaluki for several years. According to the local independent media outlet Fortanga , in 1989 the family purchased a house and plot on Sovkhoznaya Street from a mobile mechanised construction unit. Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, the paperwork was delayed, and the family moved into the renovated building in 1994. In 2019, the family’s head, Alauddin Tochiev, registered the property in his name. Local authorities later claimed that the house and land belonged to the republic. According to the administration, the building had previously housed a school, and the family had occupied and converted it into a home. The Tochievs insist that they have documents confirming their ownership rights. In 2024, the family succeeded in having an eviction ruling overturned and the case sent back for reconsideration. In March 2025, the Malgobek City Court partially upheld the prosecutor’s claim, ruling that the family had no rights to the house or land, but refused to order their eviction. In December of the same year, the Supreme Court of Ingushetia upheld the decision. The prosecution, republican ministries and village administration had failed to provide conclusive evidence that the disputed land and building belonged to the state. A criminal case involving theft and arson was subsequently opened against Tamerlan Tochiev. He spent about a month in a detention facility before being placed under house arrest. OC Media was told by Team Against Torture that the criminal case against Tamerlan Tochiev is still under investigation. However, because he has a psychiatric condition that makes detention in a pre-trial detention centre unsuitable, he was released subject to a travel restriction. Law enforcement agencies in Ingushetia have previously used quotations from literary figures to illustrate their publications. Before 2020, the press service of the Ingushetia Interior Ministry published materials featuring quotes from Honoré de Balzac, Victor Hugo, and Leo Tolstoy. ‘Iron Felix’ and the rehabilitation of Soviet history Felix Dzerzhinsky was a revolutionary of Polish origin, a Soviet state official and the founder of the first iterations of the Soviet security service. Established in December 1917, the VChK was one of the first agencies of the Soviet political police. In Soviet historical tradition, Dzerzhinsky became known as ‘Iron Felix’. The VChK and the agencies that succeeded it — the OGPU (‘Joint State Political Directorate’), NKVD (‘People’s Commissariat for Internal Affairs’) and KGB (‘Committee for State Security’) — were part of the history of Soviet political repression. The modern Federal Security Service (FSB) is regarded as the institutional successor to this tradition. The phrase ‘The fact that you are free is not your merit, but our failure’ is often attributed to Dzerzhinsky, although there is no documentary evidence that he actually said it. In 1958, a monument to Dzerzhinsky was erected in Moscow’s Lubyanka Square, in front of the building that housed the Soviet state security agencies. It was created by sculptor Yevgeny Vuchetich and architect Grigory Zakharov. Following Dzerzhinsky’s death in 1926, the square had for a time borne his name. On 22 August 1991, following the failure of the attempted coup in the Soviet Union, the monument was dismantled. Protesters had gathered around it and attempted to topple it, after which Moscow authorities decided to remove it. The sculpture was later transferred to Muzeon Park of Arts on Krymsky Val, where it remains today. The possibility of returning the monument to Lubyanka Square has been raised repeatedly in subsequent years. In May 2026, exiled opposition journalist Mikhail Zygar reported , citing sources, that a decision had been made to return the monument to the square after all.

title: Soldiers, terrorists killed in midnight terror attack on Borno military base
body:
About 20 security officers and an unspecified number of terrorists were killed during a Tuesday midnight terror attack on a military base in Borno State .
Security sources told PREMIUM TIMES that the attack, by jihadists either belonging to Boko Haram or the rival Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), targeted the military base in Mairari, Guzamala Local Government Area (LGA).
Corroborating one another, the sources said 15 soldiers and five members of the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) were killed in the encounter.
The LG chairperson, Umar Sheriff, confirmed the attack to Punch, saying military operatives repelled it. Locals also told the newspaper that many terrorists were killed.
However, the military has not released any official statement about the attack. The spokesperson for Operation Hadin Kai, a joint task force in the North-east, Mohammed Goni, has not responded to a PREMIUM TIMES enquiry into the incident.
Last month, an ISWAP attack on a military position in Mairari was repelled by military forces with aerial support. Four ISWAP terrorists were killed in the attack, and a cache of weapons including a camera was recovered.
Boko Haram insurgency has lingered for more than a decade, with experts warning that the war is not close to its end as a new generation of fighters now dominates the battlefield amid challenges posed by the increasing use of new technologies.

title: NIS vows justice after officer killed in Niger attack
body: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) has vowed to bring the perpetrators of an attack on two of its personnel in Niger to justice, following the death of one officer and serious injury to another. The Service Public Relations Officer, Deputy Comptroller of Immigration (DCI) Akinsola Akinlabi, said this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja. He said the incident occurred on Oct. 6, when two personnel conducting routine surveillance were violently attacked by unidentified assailants. “Sadly, one of the officers, Assistant Superintendent of Immigration (ASI) I. U. Babangida, tragically lost his life, while the other, Insp. A. K. Musa, sustained serious injuries but managed to escape and is currently receiving medical attention. “The fallen officer has since been laid to rest in accordance with Islamic rites. The Service honours his sacrifice and unwavering commitment to duty,” he said. Akinlabi extended the Service’s condolences to the deceased officer’s family, colleagues and loved ones, while wishing the injured personnel a speedy recovery. He assured both families of the service’s continued support and assistance during this difficult period. The spokesperson added that the NIS was working with the Nigerian government and relevant security agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for the attack and ensure they face justice. (NAN) The post NIS vows justice after officer killed in Niger attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: ‘Where did the millions go?’: Calls for probe into Patriarch’s funeral spending
body: Davit Okitashvili, president of Georgia’s Chamber of Culture, has called on the Prosecutor General’s Office and the State Audit Office to investigate spending on Patriarch Ilia II’s funeral, accusing former Culture Minister Tinatin (Tika) Rukhadze of damaging his reputation and raising questions about the use of public funds. Patriarch Ilia II, head of the Georgian Orthodox Church, died aged 93 on 17 March. He was buried at Tbilisi’s Sioni Cathedral on 22 March. The Culture Ministry, then headed by Rukhadze, was involved in organising the funeral. The Finance Ministry allocated ₾5.6 million ($2.1 million) for organising the funeral. Of that amount, ₾3 million ($1.2 million) was allocated to the Culture Ministry. Questions about the money allocated for Patriarch Ilia II’s funeral have been raised in the media since September. On 14 September, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said that, according to preliminary figures, ₾3 million ($1.1 million) had been allocated for the funeral, of which only ₾722,000 ($270,000) had been spent. ‘If someone had wanted to steal money, they could have easily used up the entire ₾3 million’, Kobakhidze said . He said that the figures were preliminary and that he would examine the matter further before presenting more detailed information to the public. Okitashvili, a supporter of the ruling Georgian Dream party, published a critical post on Facebook targeting Rukhadze, who was culture minister at the time of the funeral. He called for full disclosure of the expenses and asked the relevant authorities to examine her possible involvement in financial decisions related to the event. In his post, Okitashvili also accused Rukhadze of attempting to isolate him from representatives of Georgia’s cultural sector and restricting the activities of the Chamber of Culture. He alleged that Mamuka Mdinaradze, a former Georgian Dream leader who has since left politics, had acted as Rukhadze’s ‘patron’. OC Media contacted Rukhadze for comment on Okitashvili’s allegations. ‘I publicly call on Georgia’s Prosecutor General’s Office and the State Audit Office to examine and make full information about the expenses related to the Patriarch’s funeral available to the public’, Okitashvili wrote , attaching what appears to be an AI-generated image depicting Tinatin Rukhadze holding a cup of coffee and Mamuka Mdinaradze wearing numerous medals. An image shared by Okitashvili depicting Tinatin Rukhadze holding a cup of coffee and Mamuka Mdinaradze wearing numerous medals. ‘What sums were spent? Who received public funds? How were the procurements carried out, and was every penny spent for its intended purpose? Ms Tika, where did the millions go?’, he asked. Okitashvili claimed that during Rukhadze’s tenure, the Chamber of Culture and he personally faced repeated obstacles intended to restrict the organisation’s activities and damage his reputation. He also alleged that Rukhadze had sought to prevent cultural figures from communicating with him, stop a project to unveil stars honouring prominent cultural figures, and evict the Chamber of Culture from its office at the Tbilisi Philharmonic Hall. Okitashvili further alleged that Rukhadze had referred to him as ‘Bidzina [Ivanishvili]’s agent and [Tea] Tsulukiani’s tail’, and claimed she had repeated the phrase in conversations with other people. Okitashvili did not provide documentary evidence for these allegations. OC Media contacted Georgia’s Prosecutor General’s Office and the State Audit Office to ask whether they intended to launch an investigation into Okitashvili’s allegations. Georgian Dream MP Tengiz Sharmanashvili said the Prosecutor General’s Office was obliged to examine Okitashvili’s allegations and question him about the evidence supporting them. ‘If those arguments are substantial and there are questions to be answered, the Prosecutor General’s Office will also question Ms Rukhadze about all this. It will question Mdinaradze, Sharmanashvili, Petriashvili, and everyone else, if there are grounds to do so. That is how it should act. So, let us wait for the legal procedure’, Sharmanashvili told the media . On 16 September, Andria Jaghmaidze, head of the Georgian Orthodox Church’s public relations service, said the Church had known from the outset that most of the allocated funds had not been spent. ‘Particularly during that period, we were in frequent communication with Ms Tika Rukhadze, and we knew from her that organisations and private individuals had mostly declined fees or salaries for various services’, Jaghmaidze stated. He added that Kobakhidze had publicly confirmed this and expressed hope that the late Patriarch’s name would no longer be used in what he described as unfounded accusations and defamation.

title: Man charged in alleged plot potentially targeting Hindu place of worship in Illinois
body:
"The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated," police said.
A 19-year-old Illinois man has been charged with felony crimes for an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting at a Hindu place of worship in the Aurora area, police said.
Alexandros Paporakis of Palatine was arrested Sunday after the Palatine Police Department received information from the Mount Prospect Police Department about an imminent potential mass shooting, police said at a news conference on Thursday.
The information came from an individual who reported receiving "concerning electronic communications" from Paporakis, police said.
"I think we were very fortunate that something much much worse didn't happen," Palatine Police Chief William Nord said during the news conference, praising the individual who came forward with information about Paporakis' alleged plans. "The communications given that day necessitated an immediate response."
Nord revealed on Thursday that investigators identified a red Honda RDX registered to Paporakis entering the parking lot of a "known Hindu temple" in Aurora at 12:25 p.m. local time on Sunday and exiting the parking lot about 13 minutes later. Nord did not identify the temple.
"At the time, it appeared that the offender was driving the vehicle and was alone in the vehicle," Nord said.
After leaving the temple parking lot, the suspect drove to his home in Palatine, where he lived with his mother.
Nord said Paporakis was arrested at his home, where investigators served a search warrant.
Authorities said they recovered a rifle, multiple loaded rifle magazines, hundreds of additional rounds of rifle ammunition, tactical equipment and other items during a search. Investigators said they also recovered a tactical vest containing body armor and a patch displaying imagery associated with white supremacist extremism.
Paporakis' mother was contacted by investigators but has declined to cooperate in the investigation, according to Nord. The mother has not been charged with any crime connected to the mass shooting plot.
He said investigators are also working to determine where and how Paporakis obtained the rifle and ammunition found at his home.
"Our investigation has revealed that, and confirmed as of right now, that he has been alone in this planning," Nord said. "We're still trying to determine why the October date was significant for him."
Officers from the Palatine and Mount Prospect police departments coordinated a response and took Paporakis into custody as he was leaving his residence on Sunday evening, police said.
In the days following his arrest, detectives reviewed electronic communications and examined a document attributed to Paporakis titled, "Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter's Manifesto)," which contained statements expressing white supremacist and extremist ideologies, including references to violence against people of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent, police said.
The Aurora Police Department was notified of the potential threat by Palatine and Mount Prospect Police. Aurora police subsequently contacted Hindu places of worship in their jurisdiction to make them aware of the information, authorities said.
"The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated," Nord said in an earlier statement. He also thanked the person who initially reported the information and the FBI for its assistance.
Paporakis has been charged with one count of making a terrorist threat, a class X felony, and one count of unlawful possession of a rifle with a barrel shorter than 16 inches, a class 3 felony, police said. He appeared at a detention hearing Wednesday at the Cook County Third Municipal District Courthouse in Rolling Meadows, where a judge ordered him detained.
"The FBI aggressively works alongside our local and state law enforcement partners to identify, investigate, and dismantle any threats of violence driven by radical ideologies," Ryan Whalen, the FBI Chicago special agent in charge, said.
"Thanks to the swift action by the Palatine and Mount Prospect Police Departments, the subject was taken into custody without harm to our community," Whalen continued. "The FBI values these strong partnerships and will continue to use every law enforcement and prosecutorial resource available to bring any offender using fear or violence to justice."
Paporakis' next court appearance is set for Oct. 30 at 9 a.m. ET.

title: 2 ships ablaze off Romanian Black Sea coast, search on for missing sailors
body:
Rescuers were searching for seven missing crew on Thursday from one of two chemical tankers that caught fire overnight just outside Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea , after Russian drones strayed into national airspace, Romanian officials said.
Romanian President Nicusor Dan said the two ships had been struck by drones but declined to say whether they were Russian.
“Two air drones hit them,” Dan told reporters in Brussels ahead of a summit of EU leaders, adding only a few hours had elapsed since the strikes, and Romania was waiting for more information.
“There will be a reaction from the Romanian state,” he added.
The two ships hit overnight were both anchored in the Black Sea near the mouth of the Sulina canal leading into the Danube River, a major shipping route used by Ukraine as Russia has attacked Ukraine’s own Black Sea ports. One was in Romanian waters, the other just outside.
The incidents follow drone strikes on at least five other cargo ships near the coasts of Romania and neighboring fellow NATO member Bulgaria over the past 10 days. At least 23 sailors were lost from those strikes, which took place just outside NATO’s territorial waters.
Romania’s naval authority said it received an emergency alert from the San Marino-flagged tanker Wine Trader. Seven of its 12 crew were missing and 5 were rescued. The ship was hit 13 nautical miles southeast of the Sulina canal, one mile outside Romanian waters.
The interior ministry said it had sent two Black Hawk helicopters to the search and rescue mission, as well as two ships with medical staff on board.
“At the moment, the rescue cannot be done safely because of very big waves,” it said in a statement.
Late on Wednesday, the Comoros-flagged chemical and oil tanker Yara J also caught fire, 8-10 miles southeast of Sulina, inside national waters. Romanian authorities initially said it was not clear whether it had been attacked. All its crew were safe.
Romania shares a 614-km (381-mile) border with Ukraine, much of it along the Danube. It has reported repeated breaches of its airspace by Russian drones over the past four years.
Both Wine Trader and Yara J caught fire near the mouth of the Danube River’s Sulina Canal leading to the Black Sea, where ships often anchor waiting to pass because of delays from weather and congestion. Both ships were empty of cargo.
Increasing attacks on Black Sea shipping connected with the Russia-Ukraine war in recent months have threatened to cause a global food crisis, as both countries are major exporters of grain, as is Romania.
“We’re looking at the Black Sea as a global food artery,” Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Toiu told a security conference in Warsaw earlier this week.
“It is currently, unfortunately, the deadliest sea when it comes to the number of casualties of sailors in the last months. That means we need to increase our investments in deterrence, defense.”
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said EU leaders would discuss on Thursday a proposed moratorium on attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea. Dan and Radev will meet NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte later on Thursday.
Russia has been bombing Ukraine’s Black Sea ports, forcing Kyiv to rely increasingly on Danube River ports and shipping routes close to the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania. For its part, Ukraine has targeted Russian ships near the mouth of the Don River in the Azov Sea.

title: The Download: reviving frozen pig kidneys and boosting nuclear power
body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Pig kidneys that were “frozen” for a year have been brought back to life Pig kidneys that were cooled to -150 °C and stored in a freezer for months have been successfully rewarmed and shown to work again for the first time, say scientists. The kidneys, which are similar in size to human ones, were left in a glass-like state, in one case for over a year. Once they had been rewarmed, tested in machines, and transplanted into pigs, the kidneys regained their color and made urine—key signs they were working. The results are a big milestone. But the team still needs to establish whether the approach could work for humans. Dissect what the breakthrough means for organ transplantation . —Jessica Hamzelou How much more can nuclear power plants give? In this age of rising electricity demand, people are trying to squeeze every last bit of power out of every power plant. Over the past few weeks, there’s been big news about the nuclear industry trying to do just that. Constellation, the largest nuclear operator in the US, announced plans to add nearly a gigawatt of new capacity across 11 existing nuclear reactors at six plants. On October 5, the Department of Energy awarded Vistra a $4.2 billion loan to upgrade three plants. Pushing existing reactors to produce more could quickly provide more clean power for data centers. But just how much additional power can we count on? Read the full story to find out . —Casey Crownhart This story is from The Checkup, our weekly climate and energy tech newsletter. The company has more than 150 electric buses on the road in Kenya and Rwanda, with a reservation list of 1,200 customers. Now it’s targeting another major source of pollution on the roads: trucks. title: You cannot govern by proxy, campaign through surrogates, expect votes — Obi’s media office tells Tinubu
body: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Peter Obi Media Office has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his decision not to accompany the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council to every campaign event ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying he cannot govern by proxy, campaign through surrogates and expect Nigerians to renew his mandate. The media office of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, said the President must personally defend his record in office rather than rely on political allies and party chieftains to campaign on his behalf. In a statement signed on Thursday by its spokesman, Idris Zekeri, the office argued that although political surrogates could speak for the President, they could not assume responsibility for his policies and performance. It said the President could not delegate accountability or leave political allies to defend his administration while Nigerians continued to grapple with the effects of government policies. Tinubu had said he would not accompany the APC Presidential Campaign Council to every campaign event ahead of the 2027 general elections, citing the need to prioritise governance, economic obligations and efforts to attract investors. The President made the declaration on Wednesday in Abuja while inaugurating the APC Presidential Campaign Council, urging its members to lead the party’s mobilisation efforts nationwide while he attended to matters of state. He reportedly agreed with concerns that electioneering should not interfere with his responsibilities as President, stressing that the country required his attention. Reacting, the Obi media office challenged Tinubu to explain his administration’s performance directly to Nigerians. The statement read, “President Bola Tinubu reportedly says the demands of governance may keep him away from the campaign trail. Nigerians deserve to ask: If he cannot make time to face the electorate, why should surrogates be sent to ask for their votes? “The President cannot delegate accountability. He cannot outsource the defence of his record to political allies, party chieftains, and praise singers while millions of Nigerians struggle with the consequences of his government’s policies. “Surrogates can speak for the President, but they cannot answer for his failures. They can repeat his promises, but they cannot make those promises a reality. They can campaign in his name, but they cannot carry his responsibility.” The office further challenged Tinubu to explain how the performance of his administration had affected the cost of food, transportation, electricity, housing and other necessities. “If the administration has delivered on its promises, why should the President be reluctant to defend that record before Nigerians himself? If the economy is improving, let him explain how that improvement is reflected in the cost of food, transportation, electricity, housing, and necessities. If his policies are working, let him face the citizens who want to know when the hardship will end,” it said. The statement argued that governance should not be treated as a reason to avoid public scrutiny, maintaining that a candidate seeking another term must be prepared to account for his record. “Governance is not an excuse to avoid accountability. In a democracy, governance is the very record a candidate must defend before asking for another mandate,” the office said. It added that Nigerians were being asked to assess Tinubu’s policies, promises and performance, rather than those of the political allies campaigning on his behalf. “The Nigerian people deserve a direct conversation with their President, not a relay of rehearsed talking points from political messengers,” the statement said. The office urged Tinubu to explain his administration’s achievements, address unfulfilled promises and respond to questions from Nigerians if he wanted them to renew his mandate. “A President who seeks the people’s mandate must be prepared to face the people. Surrogates may carry the message, but they cannot carry the burden of accountability,” it added. The post You cannot govern by proxy, campaign through surrogates, expect votes — Obi’s media office tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ghana’s economy grows by 7.4% in July 2026
body: Data published by the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) shows that the country recorded a year-on-year economic growth of 7.4 percent in July 2026 compared to the same period last year. This was contained in the latest Monthly Indicator of Economic Growth (MIEG) released by the GSS. Sector by sector, the data shows that Agriculture increased by 3.7 percent. The Industry sector recorded an increase of 5.4 percent. The increase was attributed to the growth observed in the mining and quarrying sub-sector. The Services sector grew by 12.2 percent. The expansion in activity was mainly driven by Information & Communication sub-sector. Explaining the data, the GSS said the services sector was the main contributor to the July 2026 7.4 percent growth. The sector contributed 63.8 percent to the overall growth of the 7.4 percent in economic activities. Industry contributed 20.5 percent while agriculture contributed 14.1 percent. Net Indirect taxes contributed 1.6 percent. Agriculture increased by 3.7 percent in the same period under review. This was driven by the crops and livestock subsector. July 2026 MIEG PPT Download

title: 6 Injured After Russian Drone Lands Near Pechersk Residential Building in Kyiv
body:
A Russian drone attacked civilians near a residential building in Kyiv’s Pechersk district on Thursday morning, injuring six with at least three hospitalized.
A Kyiv Post correspondent heard an explosion about a block away around 10 a.m., and Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko later confirmed that a five-story building was damaged.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“In the Pechersk district, a drone crashed in an open area near a five-story residential building. The facade, part of the roof, and the windows of the building were damaged,” he wrote .
He later said six were injured and three were hospitalized.
“The number of casualties in the Pecherskyi district has increased to six. Three of the injured have been hospitalized,” Klitschko wrote .
The attack comes as Russia escalates drone attacks on Ukrainian cities, with daytime attacks increasingly common as Russia’s use of jet-powered drones spiked to nearly 3,500 in September.
Kyiv Post’s correspondent on the scene confirmed the damage, and a community swimming pool and a school were also damaged across the road, with broken glass littering the streets.
The aftermath of a Russian attack after a drone struck a courtyard in Kyiv’s Pechersk district on Oct. 15, 2026. (Photo by Leo Chiu / Kyiv Post) Other Topics of Interest Ukrainian Navy Strikes 6 Russian Su-34M Bombers Using Neptune Missiles Ukraine’s naval forces reported fires and secondary explosions at Borisoglebsk airfield in Russia’s Voronezh region, saying the strike also destroyed aviation support equipment.
The aftermath of a Russian attack after a drone struck a courtyard in Kyiv’s Pechersk district on Oct. 15, 2026. (Photo by Leo Chiu / Kyiv Post)
Along the road, sounds of sweeping glass inside houses were also heard as the shockwaves shattered glass on balconies.
The site of the attack is also located near a farmer’s market, though the market itself appears to be relatively unharmed by the attack.
Recent attacks have disrupted water supplies across Kyiv, with Russia stepping up attacks on Ukraine’s energy grid ahead of winter. Ukrainians interviewed by Kyiv Post have named water disruptions among their main concerns and urged authorities to act before the coldest months arrive.
Leo Chiu is a journalist and editor based in Eastern Europe since 2015. He has witnessed two presidential elections in Belarus and traveled widely to conflict zones and contested regions, producing reporting that bridges the gap between major developments and local realities.

title: MIIF records GH¢7.82bn in mineral royalties in first nine months of 2026
body: The Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF) recorded GH¢7.82 billion in mineral royalty receipts between January and September 2026, representing a 106% increase over the GH¢3.79 billion recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. The strong performance was driven by higher gold prices, the implementation of the sliding-scale royalty mechanism, resilient production levels and enhanced monitoring of mining activities by the Fund’s Technical and Operations Department. MIIF is targeting approximately GH¢9 billion in mineral royalty receipts by the end of 2026. Large-scale gold mining remained the leading contributor, generating approximately GH¢7.66 billion in royalties during the first nine months of 2026, compared with GH¢3.54 billion over the same period in 2025. This represents an increase of approximately 116%, accounting for the overwhelming majority of total mineral royalty receipts. “Mid-tier” gold mining also recorded significant growth, with royalty receipts rising from approximately GH¢55.31 million in the first nine months of 2025 to GH¢110.34 million during the corresponding period in 2026, representing an increase of approximately 99%. Among non-gold minerals, quarry royalties increased to GH¢11.35 million from approximately GH¢10.8 million in the first nine months of 2025, representing growth of about 6% increase in 2026. Sand royalties also increased by approximately 41%, rising from GH¢390,274 in the first nine months of 2025 to GH¢550,871 during the same period in 2026. In contrast, limestone royalties declined from GH¢7.08 million to GH¢4.84 million. The decline is attributed to reduced production, particularly during the second quarter, when increased rainfall disrupted mining activities and constrained output. The third-quarter results build on MIIF’s strong performance in the first half of 2026, when the Fund recorded more than GH¢5.3 billion in mineral royalty receipts, compared with approximately GH¢2.64 billion during the corresponding period in 2025. Commenting on the performance, Chief Executive Officer of MIIF, Mrs. Justina Nelson, reaffirmed the Fund’s commitment to responsible financial management and the effective utilisation of mineral revenues for the benefit of the Republic of Ghana. She emphasised that MIIF’s mandate extends beyond mineral royalty receipts to include strategic investments across the mining value chain through equities, fixed-income securities and alternative investments, with the objective of generating sustainable returns for the Republic. As it works towards its annual target of approximately GH¢9 billion, MIIF remains committed to maximising the value of Ghana’s mineral wealth and ensuring that mineral revenues contribute meaningfully to sustainable national development. The Fund continues to discharge its statutory mandate under the Minerals Income Investment Fund Act, 2018 (Act 978), as amended, to maximise the value of dividend and royalty income accruing to the Republic and manage Ghana’s mineral wealth in a beneficial, accountable and sustainable manner, for the benefit of present and future generations.

title: Trump’s envoy says sports can reopen doors in relations between US, Russia
body:
WASHINGTON, October 15. /TASS/. US Special Envoy for Global Partnerships Paolo Zampolli said sports could reopen doors in Russia-US relations that have been closed because of politics.
"[US] President [Donald] Trump understands that sport can reopen doors that politics has kept closed," the diplomat who works within both the White House and the US State Department told TASS in an interview on Thursday.
According to him, "hockey is a natural place to begin because the United States and Russia share extraordinary talent, history and respect for the game." "But we should not stop at hockey," Trump’s envoy argued.
The full text of the interview is available on the TASS website: https://tass.com/world/2202537 .

title: FG, States, LGs Share ₦2.4trn September 2026 Revenue
body: A total sum of N2.428 trillion, being September 2026 Federation Account Revenue, has been shared to the Federal Government, States and the Local Government Councils. A statement from the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation’s Director (Press and Public Relations), Bawa Mokwa, on Thursday, noted that the revenue was shared at the October 2026 Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) meeting held in Abuja. The N2.428 trillion total distributable revenue comprised distributable statutory revenue of N1.672 trillion and distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue of N756.587 billion. A communiqué issued by the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) indicated that total gross revenue of N3.913 trillion was available in the month of September 2026. Total deduction for cost of collection was N131.758 billion, while total transfers, refunds and savings N1.352 trillion. According to the communiqué, gross statutory revenue of N3.096 trillion was received for the month of September 2026. This was higher than the sum of N2.850 trillion received in the preceding month by N246.384 billion. Gross revenue of N816.872 billion was available from the Value Added Tax (VAT) in September 2026. This was lower than the N834.843 billion available in the month of August 2026 by N17.972 billion. The communiqué stated that from the N2.428 trillion total distributable revenue, the Federal Government received a total sum of N832.242 billion and the State Governments received a total sum of N799.872 billion. The Local Government Council received N560.660 billion, while the sum of N236.049 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting State as derivation revenue. On the N1.672 billion distributable statutory revenue, the communiqué stated that the Federal Government received N756.583 billion and the State Governments received N383.749 billion. The Local Government Councils received N295.855 billion, and the sum of N236.049 billion (13% of mineral revenue) was shared to the benefiting States as derivation revenue. From the N756.587 billion distributable Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue, the Federal Government received N75.659 billion, the State Governments received N416.123 billion, and the Local Government Councils received N264.805 billion. In September 2026, Petroleum Profit Tax (PPT), Hydrocarbon Tax (HT), Petroleum Royalties, Import Duty, CET Levies and Excise Duty increased significantly, while Companies Income Tax (CIT), CGT & SDT, Value Added Tax (VTA), Mineral Royalties, and Gas Flared Penalty, Rental Gas Flared Fee and Misc. Oil Revenue decreased considerably. The post FG, States, LGs Share ₦2.4trn September 2026 Revenue appeared first on Channels Television .

title: DFSA fines immigration firm Hayman-Woodward Dh1.67m for unlicensed services
body: The Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA) has fined the Dubai unit of Hayman-Woodward Global Mobility Services (HWW DIFC) $454,367 (Dh1.67 million) for providing unauthorised services for more than six years. HWW DIFC was found to have carried out client services in or from Dubai International Financial Centre without being registered as a designated non-financial business or profession (DNFBP), DFSA said in a statement on Thursday. The company is incorporated in the DIFC, but its business activities are only permitted for management consultancies and document clearing services. The DFSA found that HWW DIFC breached DNFBP regulations, specifically by acting as a formation agent of legal persons, and providing a registered office, business address, correspondence and administrative address for companies and legal persons. The unauthorised services were provided to 71 clients between August 2018 and February 2025. HWW DIFC also signed agreements with three free zones outside the DIFC to assist in company set-ups and other customer service provider transactions. The penalty comprises the fine and a disgorgement, or the surrender of any profits obtained from unlawful acts. The fine, however, was reduced by 30 per cent, from $522,047.05, after Hayman-Woodward agreed to settle the case. “The DNFBP regime is a key component of the DFSA's framework for mitigating money laundering and other financial crime risks within the DIFC,” said Alan Linning, managing director for enforcement at the DFSA. “Businesses that provide company service provider and other DNFBP services can present elevated financial crime risks and are therefore subject to appropriate regulatory oversight and supervision.” Authorities in the UAE have been vigilant in cracking down on entities that breach regulations as part of efforts to maintain the Emirati financial system's integrity and reliability. Earlier this month, the DFSA imposed a Dh401,000 fine on wealth management services firm Vault Wealth for conducting transactions without authorisation. Last week, the Registration Authority of Abu Dhabi's ADGM imposed fines totalling $100,000 against PKF Accountants and Business Advisers over regulatory failings. The UAE Central Bank has also imposed fines on lenders that have violated rules, especially those on anti-money laundering. “The DFSA remains committed to developing, administering and enforcing world-class regulation of financial services within the DIFC,” the authority said. It added it will continue to take “appropriate enforcement action to protect users and prospective users of financial services and to preserve confidence in the DIFC’s regulatory framework”.

title: The Costa GUI
body:
Costa is a small and lightweight application which runs on top of MS-DOS or compatible operating systems. It replaces the DOS-prompt with a clean, user-friendly interface - a so-called GUI (Graphical User Interface). Costa comes packed with a bunch of useful accessories and can be used with or without a mouse.
Developed by Jacob Palm , a Danish IT-professional and hobby developer, the first release of Costa came way back in 2004. Over the years - and through several releases - Costa has gradually evolved into what it is today, with new releases still coming out regularly as of 2025.
Costa is provided free of charge, and the source code is open sourced for anyone who wants to have a look. To see what others think of Costa, have a look at Costa on the Web on the blog.
You can download the latest version of Costa now, free of charge. To get started, simply unzip the downloaded archive and run Costa. Full documentation is included in the download.
Since September 2017, the full source code has been available for free under the MIT license. Visit Codeberg to see the source code, and to pull a copy for your own use.
Looking for older versions? Check the archive , which also has a complete log of changes in every version.
