title: ECHR opens proceedings againt Hungary over detention, 'torture' of Ukrainian bank staff
body:
The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) has opened proceedings in six cases against Hungary over the alleged torture and unlawful detention of Ukrainian Oschadbank employees in spring, the state-owned bank said on Oct. 15.
The cases stem from a March incident that took place during Hungary 's election campaign, when Viktor Orban was still prime minister. Hungarian authorities detained seven Oschadbank employees on suspicion of money laundering as they traveled from Austria to Ukraine through Hungary in two bank vehicles carrying $40 million, 35 million euros, and 9 kilograms of gold.
The employees were released the day after their detention, while the cash and gold were returned to Ukraine in May.
The cases were brought by six staff members of a state-owned Ukrainian bank who say they were tortured and illegally detained. A similar case is expected to be filed on behalf of a seventh worker.
Kyiv previously condemned the incident, calling it "hostage-taking" and "state terrorism." Ukraine's Foreign Ministry said the staff were subjected to "physical and psychological pressure."
"The fact that the ECHR has accepted the complaint and opened proceedings indicates that there are reasonable legal grounds for the case, that it has legal merit, and that the court intends to examine it on its merits," the bank's statement read .
The bank staff applications cite Articles 3 and 5 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which prohibit torture and protect the right to liberty and security.

title: Sugar production to keep high export potential of Russia — Central Bank
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Sugar production in Russia for the 2026-2027 season is projected to reach 6.3 million metric tons in line with industry analyst estimates, the Bank of Russia said in its regional economy report seen by TASS.
"The sugar content of the new harvest across the country is generally on par with 2025 levels (13.3% compared to 13.4% last year). The sugar beet harvest is expected to exceed last year's volume. According to industry analysts, sugar production nationwide could reach 6.3 million tons in the 2026-2027 season. As a result, Russia's high export potential will be maintained," the Central Bank said.
According to flash data from industry analysts, the planted areas and harvesting rates for sugar beet are lower than last year, driven by delayed sowing in the central regions. As of late September, approximately one-third of the planted areas was harvested, yielding 17.3 million metric tons of sugar beet (a 13.2% decrease compared to last year). However, yields are significantly higher than last year on account of the southern regions.
Consumer sugar prices continued to grow year-on-year in September (they were declining in September 2025). The current price growth was driven by the gradual depletion of stocks, as well as an increase in exports amid rising global prices.

title: 7 Open-Source AI Tools That Can Replace Paid Subscriptions
body:
Find open-source alternatives to OpenAI API, Midjourney, Claude Code, Notion, Wispr Flow, Grammarly, and NotebookLM that you can run locally or self-host for more privacy, control, and lower cost.
AI subscriptions add up surprisingly fast. I pay for quite a few of them myself, and after a while you start wondering: is all of this really worth it? Is there an open-source alternative? Can I run it locally and privately? And can I do that without giving up too much in performance or quality?
For many of the tools we use every day, the answer is now yes . You can replace cloud AI assistants with local large language models (LLMs), paid coding tools with open-source coding agents, image-generation platforms with local workflows, and apps like Notion with self-hosted alternatives. You can even replace cloud dictation with a fast speech-to-text app that runs entirely on your own machine.
The open-source ecosystem has improved a lot, and many of these projects are no longer just experimental alternatives. They are polished tools that you can actually use every day. For this guide, I picked seven open-source AI tools that can replace common paid subscriptions while giving you more control, privacy, and often no recurring cost at all.
I use llama.cpp almost every day whenever I want to run a local LLM or test a newly released model. It is one of the best tools for running quantized models efficiently on your own hardware, and it is highly optimized across CPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, Apple Silicon, AMD GPUs, and other platforms.
What makes llama.cpp especially useful is that it is not just an inference engine. Its built-in server gives you an OpenAI-compatible API and a web interface, so you can chat with your model in a UI similar to ChatGPT or connect it directly to applications that normally rely on paid APIs. That makes it a practical alternative to both monthly LLM subscriptions and per-token API costs.
The models you can run locally are also getting much better. Qwen3.8-27B is one of the strongest open agentic coding models you can use today. With llama.cpp, you can serve it locally, test it through the web UI, or expose it as an API, while getting coding and agentic performance that is competitive with frontier models such as Claude Opus 4.8 .
For me, that is the real appeal of llama.cpp: I can download a strong new model, run it privately, test it locally, and use it as an API without paying every time I send a prompt.
ComfyUI is a powerful open-source alternative to tools such as Midjourney, Adobe Firefly, and other hosted image and video generators . It uses a visual node-based interface, so instead of hiding the generation process behind a single prompt box, you can see and control how models, prompts, LoRAs, ControlNets, upscalers, and other components work together.
What makes ComfyUI especially useful is how much more it can do beyond basic image generation. You can use it for image editing, inpainting, outpainting, upscaling, reference-based generation, segmentation, and compositing , and it supports modern editing models such as Flux Kontext and Qwen Image Edit. It also supports video generation with models such as Wan, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo, and CogVideoX, so the same interface can cover both image and video workflows.
That is why I see ComfyUI as more than just a Midjourney replacement. Once you get comfortable with the workflows, it becomes a complete local creative AI platform for generating, editing, and automating images and videos, while giving you much more control than most hosted tools.
Pi is a fast, open-source alternative to coding agents such as Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and OpenAI Codex . I use it almost every day because it can build projects, debug code, find issues, edit files, run commands, and handle multi-step coding tasks directly from the terminal.
What I especially like is using Pi with local models. I can run a model through llama.cpp , expose its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and connect Pi to it. llama.cpp handles the inference, while Pi gives the model the agentic coding capabilities needed to actually work on a project.
That gives you a complete local coding-agent setup without depending on a paid subscription. It is fast, flexible, and a great way to experience agentic coding with your own local models.
AppFlowy is one of the best open-source alternatives to Notion if you want more control over your data. You can use it for documents, notes, wikis, tasks, databases, Kanban boards, calendars, and team collaboration, while keeping the familiar all-in-one workspace idea that makes Notion so useful.
What I like about AppFlowy is that it is not just a small note-taking app. It has native desktop apps for Windows, macOS, and Linux, mobile apps, a web version, offline support, and options for self-hosting. You can also use its AI features for writing and editing, so it is getting closer to a complete productivity workspace rather than just a Notion clone.
The main appeal is control . You can keep your workspace local or run AppFlowy on your own infrastructure instead of putting everything inside another SaaS platform. One caveat is that AppFlowy's current server-side self-hosting stack has moved toward an open-core/commercial model, while its web and Flutter clients remain open source, so the self-hosting story is a little more complicated than it used to be.
Handy is a fast, open-source dictation app that works completely offline. It is built with Tauri, Rust, React, and TypeScript , and the workflow is simple: press a shortcut, speak, and Handy transcribes your voice locally and pastes the text directly into whatever app you are using. That means you can dictate into ChatGPT, coding agents, documents, emails, terminals, or basically any text field without sending your audio to the cloud.
It supports local Whisper models with GPU acceleration as well as Parakeet V3 for CPU-friendly transcription. The project reports around 5× real-time transcription speed for Parakeet V3 on a mid-range i5, so it feels fast enough for everyday dictation.
That is what makes Handy such a good alternative to paid dictation tools. You get fast, private, system-wide voice typing with no subscription, no cloud processing, and no per-minute transcription cost.
LanguageTool is a strong open-source alternative to Grammarly for grammar, spelling, punctuation, and style checking. Its open-source core supports more than 25 languages, including English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Polish, and Dutch, and it catches many contextual mistakes that a basic spell checker would miss.
What makes it especially useful is that you are not forced to use the hosted service. You can run your own LanguageTool server locally or self-host it , which gives you more privacy and lets you integrate grammar checking into your own applications through its HTTP API.
For everyday writing, emails, documents, and browser-based work, the free and open-source core is already very capable. LanguageTool also offers paid cloud features, but if your main goal is solid grammar and style checking without depending on another subscription, the open-source version is a very practical replacement.
A lot of people I know use tools like NotebookLM to study documents, research topics, and build a searchable knowledge base around their own files. SurfSense gives you a similar experience, but with much more control. It is open source, self-hostable, and can connect to your documents as well as sources such as YouTube, GitHub, Notion, Slack, Linear, and web search .
You can upload files, search across your saved knowledge, ask questions, and get answers with citations . It also supports report generation, podcasts, and multiple retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques, while letting you choose from many different LLM and embedding providers.
The part I like most is that you can self-host SurfSense and keep much more of the stack under your control . It even supports local models through tools such as Ollama , so you can build a private research assistant around your own data instead of depending entirely on a hosted platform.
Open source does not always mean completely free. You may still need good hardware, spend some time setting things up, or accept that some hosted tools are more polished.
But the gap is much smaller now. You can run strong local models, generate and edit images, code with agents, manage knowledge, dictate, proofread, and build private research workflows without depending on a separate subscription for everything.
For me, the biggest benefit is not just saving money. It is control . You choose the model, where your data lives, and how the tools connect together.
So before paying for another AI subscription, it is probably worth checking whether a good open-source alternative already exists.

title: Estonia to provide additional EUR 10M for Ukraine through NATO’s PURL initiative
body:
Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal announced this at a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, who was visiting Estonia, Ukrinform reports, citing the Estonian government’s website .
Michal said Russia’s increasingly risky actions and growing number of hybrid attacks were aimed at diverting attention from support for Ukraine. He stressed that the allies would respond jointly to Russia’s actions and continue providing substantial assistance to Ukraine.
“This year, our military assistance to Ukraine amounts to 0.28% of GDP. Last year, it was 0.35%. We have also supported Ukraine through NATO’s PURL initiative with €21 million, and we will soon contribute a further €10 million to this mechanism,” Michal said.
He expressed hope that other NATO members would also find opportunities to increase their contributions to the initiative.
Michal emphasized that Ukraine’s experience was exceptionally valuable for developing the defense capabilities and defense industries of NATO member states. He said that NATO membership would provide Ukraine with the most reliable long-term security guarantee and would benefit all allies.
The Estonian Prime Minister also noted that strengthening NATO’s deterrence and defense capabilities sent a clear message to Russia: the Alliance takes threats seriously and is determined to protect its security.
As Ukrinform reported, Chair of the NATO Military Committee Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone said that the Alliance had supplied Ukraine with $10 billion worth of US weapons under the PURL program.

title: WHO urges faster action to end lead exposure which kills 3.5 million annually
body:
Countries must accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure, which is estimated to cause more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year and affects hundreds of millions of children, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Thursday.
The UN agency issued the call ahead of International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week , which runs from 18-26 October.
Although exposure is entirely preventable, fewer than half of countries had confirmed legally binding controls on paint containing lead, according to the agency’s latest global assessment.
The risks to children are particularly dangerous because their developing brains and nervous systems are highly vulnerable to the toxic effects of lead.
“Lead poisoning should not be stealing children’s potential in 2026,” said Bruce Gordon, interim director of WHO ’s Department of Environment, Climate Change, One Health and Migration.
“We know where many exposures come from and we know how to prevent them. Countries now need to move upstream, removing lead from products and environments before it reaches a child's bloodstream.”
Lead contamination can occur through paint, cookware, cosmetics, spices, informal recycling and industrial sources. There is no known safe level of contact, and even relatively low exposure can cause irreversible harm.
Lead poisoning affects multiple organs and contributes to health problems such as cardiovascular and kidney disease in adults and irreversible damage to the brain, health and development of children.
Lifelong consequences include learning difficulties, behavioural issues and poor health. As symptoms may not be immediately visible, many cases go unnoticed until significant damage has already occurred.
WHO Member States have recognized lead exposure as a pressing public health concern and mandated the agency to develop a Global Action Plan on Lead Mitigation that will be presented to the World Health Assembly (N-dash) – WHO’s governing body (N-dash) – next year.
The agency will also launch the PREVENT Technical Package on Lead Poisoning Prevention in 2027, to provide countries with practical guidance to identify priority sources of exposure, determine which interventions can have the greatest impact, strengthen and enforce regulations and monitor progress.
Last year, WHO joined partners in the Lead Poisoning Prevention Initiative to build and improve laboratory capacity to test blood lead levels, thus enabling early detection of lead exposure.
Capacity building and technical support will be implemented in locations in Brazil, India, Nepal and in six countries in sub-Saharan Africa: Ethiopia, Ghana, Malawi, Rwanda, South Africa and Tanzania.

title: Ledger’s new hardware wallet is an Android phone without the phone
body:
Ledger has announced its latest crypto-centric hardware effort, the Android-based Atom, a device that resembles a phone but is instead designed to be used alongside one. It arrives at a tricky time for Ledger, which has been forced to cease sales of some of its hardware across southeast Asia following hardware tampering in its supply chain, which has reportedly seen over $86 million worth of crypto stolen from across some users’ accounts.
While Ledger’s previous hardware wallet signers have been compact devices, running custom software and often with E Ink displays, the Atom is the spitting image of a regular Android smartphone. In fact it essentially is an Android phone, except for the fact that its eSIM capabilities have been limited to data-only, with no support for texting or calls.
The Atom runs on both Android OS and Ledger OS, which sits on its own secure element chip, allowing you to move into a secure environment for tasks like crypto transactions. Two Atom users can also send encrypted messages to one another using regular Android messaging apps, with the messages decrypted within Ledger OS on the recipient’s device. Ledger has designed the device with AI agents in mind, including a partnership with OpenClaw, designed so that agents can handle financial tasks without getting full access to digital wallets, with physical approval required to complete transactions.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Ledger-Atom-4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Ledger-Atom-10.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Ledger-Atom-9.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Ledger-Atom-11.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Ledger-Atom-7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
Ledger says that the Atom is “not designed to replace your phone.” The company’s head of PR, Phillip Costigan, told me that Ledger recognized it was unlikely to be able to produce a device capable of competing with top Android handsets on camera and other specs, and so didn’t try to. The Atom is in fact intentionally limited in some respects: the 6.77-inch OLED display is only 60Hz, it runs on a Qualcomm Dragonwing chip rather than Snapdragon, and it only has a single rear camera and a 4,000mAh battery. Still, it will receive five years of Android OS updates, and at least seven years of support for spare parts, including a user-replaceable battery. It also has a physical privacy switch, which cuts power to the camera and microphone “at a circuit level.”
The launch couldn’t come at a worse time for Ledger. The company has confirmed reports that at least one of its hardware signers was sold by a reseller with “an unauthorized hardware implant,” which read users’ 24-word recovery phrases and transmitted them elsewhere using an eSIM. The discovery has forced Ledger to pause sales across southeast Asia, and at German retailer MediaMarkt. Reports suggest that over $86 million worth of crypto may have been stolen from across affected users, though Ledger hasn’t confirmed the scale of the losses.
That would be enough to give anyone pause before buying new Ledger hardware, at least from a third-party seller. Still, the company says that the Atom has been designed with physical anti-tampering measures, which it claims would have blocked the screen reader implants involved in the recent incident:
> Core protection: A protective enclosure surrounds the Secure Element, MCU, and FPGA, and it is designed to detect any attempt to drill into or open this area.
> Display and back cover detection: Ledger Atom detects when the display or back cover is removed. The back cover is paired with the device, so it cannot be swapped with a cover from another Ledger Atom.
> Tamper-evident packaging: Ledger Atom’s packaging is designed to show whether it has been opened before it reaches you.
The Atom will be available from summer 2027. Reservations are open now, with a refundable $100 deposit to secure a Founder’s Edition device for $849. After the launch, the price will rise to $899.

Last year, Amazon bought Bee , a relatively unknown startup with a $50 always-listening AI wearable that summarized every conversation you had. Today, the e-commerce giant is announcing two new Bee devices — and a new subscription to go with them. First is the $74.99 Bee Frontier, an updated version of the original Bee device. And coming soon is the $99.99 Bee Eclipse, a credit-card-shaped gadget that snaps magnetically onto the back of a smartphone.
Both devices are framed as gadgets to help you stay present in the moment. They listen to your daily conversations and then provide summaries, transcripts, insights, and to-dos based on what happens throughout the day. Conceptually, they’re similar to other AI note-taking gadgets like Plaud NotePin and Limitless AI . Users can also integrate Bee devices with services like Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple HealthKit, and photos. Doing so lets Bee’s AI take some actions on your behalf, like drafting emails or sending calendar invites based on your conversations.
The main difference between the two products is form factor. The Bee Frontier can be worn as a Fitbit-like band on the wrist or as a clip-on pin. It’s been slightly redesigned from the prior model so that the recording button is more prominent, and it’s now available in three colors. Like the previous version, it has dual microphones, a recording indicator light, and roughly seven days of battery life on a single charge. It also has an IP67 water resistance rating.
Meanwhile, the Eclipse is meant as a non-wearable alternative and is envisioned for more professional use cases. Its larger size allows for a bigger battery, getting 21 days on a single charge. It, too, has a recording indicator light.
While these devices are free to use, Amazon is also introducing a Bee Pro subscription for $11.99 a month. The free tier gets users conversation summaries, recaps, and 14 days of memory. The subscription gets users “unlimited” summaries, suggested to-dos, daily memories, a personal chat assistant, conversation templates, third-party app integrations, and a desktop app. But the big marquee feature for the subscription is Amazon and Alexa Plus compatibility.
The Amazon integration is opt-in, and doing so will enable the device to surface shopping suggestions based on your conversations. For example, if your spouse asks you to buy cat litter, you might see a product card reminding you of that on your Amazon homepage or an Amazon button linking out to the product in the Bee mobile app. The Alexa Plus integration is meant to be a hands-free way to access your various Bee summaries and insights.
It’s an interesting time for Amazon to introduce these products, given the recent backlash against so-called surveillance tech . On that front, Amazon told The Verge in a press briefing that Bee devices encrypt transcripts, summaries, and to-dos via its “ Private Compute ” security architecture and don’t store audio recordings. Bee devices can also be programmed to automatically stop recording if no sound is detected after a certain period of time. As for whether transcripts are attributable, that depends. Upon setup, Bee’s AI is trained on the individual user’s voice. All other speakers are not automatically identified unless you ask them to also allow Bee’s AI to train on their voice. Whether that’s enough to assuage any privacy concerns, well, that depends on your definition of a recording .
The Bee Frontier is available starting today for $74.99 in black, green, and lavender. The Eclipse is “coming soon” for $99.99 and is available in black, pink, yellow, and silver.

title: Ukraine Says Missile Strike Destroyed 6 Russian Warplanes at Voronezh Airfield
body:
Ukraine’s Navy said Thursday that it destroyed six Russian Su-34M fighter-bombers in an overnight missile strike on the Borisoglebsk military airfield in southwestern Russia’s Voronezh region.
The Navy said the attack was carried out using its Neptune coastal missile system. It also reported damage to equipment supporting flight operations, a fire and secondary explosions.
Ukrainian monitoring channels published satellite images purportedly showing damage to an aircraft parking area. The reported destruction of the six warplanes could not be independently verified.
Last night, Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck an airfield in the Voronezh region. Four Su-34 aircraft were destroyed and two more Su-34s were hit. The Russians used them to terrorize our people. These very warplanes were ready to launch new attacks on Ukraine and were loaded with aerial bombs. Our Long Neptune missile was used to strike the target. I thank the warriors of the Ukrainian Navy for their precision! Our long-range sanctions also reached a site in the Oryol region used to store and launch attack drones. A target was also hit in the Black Sea. These are our justified responses to all of Russia’s terror against Ukraine. Russia is dragging out the war, so our long-range operations will continue.
Russian authorities did not acknowledge a strike on the airfield.
Voronezh region Governor Alexander Gusev said air defenses intercepted 33 drones and “several jet-powered aerial targets.” Falling debris damaged outbuildings at several private homes and a car in the regional capital, Voronezh, he said.
Residents of Borisoglebsk reported explosions and a large fire, with smoke visible from several parts of the city.
The military airfield lies about 6 kilometers (3.7 miles) east of Borisoglebsk.
Russia uses Su-34 fighter-bombers to launch guided glide bombs at Ukrainian positions and populated areas. The Su-34M is an upgraded version of the aircraft.
In September, Ukraine’s military said it had destroyed a Russian MiG-29 fighter jet near the Millerovo airfield in the Rostov region and a Ka-27 helicopter near the Yeysk airfield in the Krasnodar region.
Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces had previously reported striking four aircraft at the Shagol airfield in the Chelyabinsk region: two Su-57 fighters, a Su-34 and another Sukhoi aircraft of an unidentified model. Those targets were about 1,700 kilometers (1,056 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

title: NDC member challenges Dennis Yeboah Twumasi’s eligibility for Bono Regional Secretary elections
body: A member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Bono Region, Frank Boateng Brew, has petitioned the party’s regional elections authorities to investigate Dennis Yeboah Twumasi’s eligibility to contest the 2026 Bono Regional Executive Elections as Regional Secretary. In a petition addressed to the Bono Regional Director of Elections, Mr Brew is challenging Mr Twumasi’s eligibility on grounds that he currently holds, or has held, a government-appointed position as Deputy Managing Director in charge of Finance and Administration at Metro Mass Transit Limited (MMT). The elections are scheduled for November 14 and 15, 2026. Mr Brew, who identifies himself as a member of the Bono Regional Youth Working Committee and the Sunyani East Youth Working Committee, argues that Mr Twumasi’s position falls within the categories of government appointees required by the party to resign from their appointments at least six clear months before filing their nominations to contest internal executive positions. According to the petition, the directive issued by the party’s General Secretary applies to persons appointed by the President or the government, including ministers and deputy ministers, chief executive officers, managing directors and their deputies, as well as metropolitan, municipal and district chief executives. Mr Brew cites information on Metro Mass Transit Limited’s official website, particularly its management team section, as evidence of Mr Twumasi’s position in the company. He contends that the appointment brings the aspirant within the scope of the party’s directive and raises questions about whether he has satisfied the resignation requirement. The petitioner is asking the Bono Regional Elections Directorate to establish whether Mr Twumasi has resigned from his position at MMT. If he has, Mr Brew wants the party to obtain a certified true copy of the resignation letter acknowledged by the company to verify compliance with the requirement. He further argues that the party must apply its election guidelines consistently, pointing to the reported disqualification of Dzifa Gunu during vetting in the La Dadekotopon Constituency over an alleged failure to resign from a government appointment six months before filing nomination. He believes the same standard should apply to all aspirants seeking executive positions in the party. “If it is established that Mr Dennis Yeboah Twumasi failed to comply with the mandatory resignation requirement as issued by the party,” the petitioner states, he respectfully requests that the party take the appropriate action and refrain from clearing him to contest the position. Mr Brew maintains that the petition is not motivated by personal animosity or hostility towards the aspirant but is intended to promote fairness, transparency, equal treatment and strict adherence to the party’s rules. Copies of the petition have been sent to the NDC General Secretary at the party’s national headquarters in Accra, the National Elections Directorate, the Bono Regional Vetting Committee and Mr Twumasi. The Bono Regional Elections Directorate’s response to the petition, as well as any confirmation of Mr Twumasi’s resignation status, was not included in the document provided. The allegations and eligibility concerns therefore remain subject to verification and a determination by the party’s appropriate electoral authorities.

title: Police arrest four over missing human heads, suspected ritual hands in Kwara
body:
The police in Kwara State have arrested four men in connection with two separate incidents involving the alleged removal of human heads from graves and possession of suspected human hands for alleged money-making rituals.
The Commissioner of Police in the state, Adekimi Ojo, disclosed this while briefing journalists at the command headquarters in Ilorin.
In the first incident, two suspects, Abu Jimoh and Ayo Jimoh, were arrested over the alleged exhumation of graves and removal of heads from buried bodies at a cemetery in Omupo, Kwara State.
Mr Ojo said the investigation began in May 2026 after residents visiting the cemetery to bury a deceased person discovered that some graves had been disturbed and the heads of the bodies buried there were missing.
He said police operatives arrested the two suspects at about 5 a.m. on 8 October while they were allegedly digging graves at the cemetery.
According to the commissioner, the suspects reportedly confessed to the crime during interrogation and identified a herbalist, Mukaila Bello, as the alleged buyer of the missing human heads.
Police said investigations were ongoing and that they would arraign the suspects after the investigation concluded. The information provided did not establish whether police had arrested Mr Bello.
In a separate incident, police arrested two other men, Kamalden Lukmon and AbdulGaniyu Ibrahim, after recovering two suspected human hands during an operation along Bakase Road in Alapa, Kwara State.
The arrests were made around 4 p.m. on 8 October.
Mr Ojo said preliminary interrogation indicated that the suspects intended to use the body parts for money-making rituals.
“During preliminary interrogation, the suspects stated that they intended to use the body parts for money-making rituals,” he said.
The suspects reportedly told investigators that a vigilante member, identified as Abdulrauf Apata, had handed the suspected human hands to them.
The commissioner said the allegation against Mr Apata was being investigated to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine whether other people were involved.
Mr Lukmon and Mr Ibrahim were being held at the command’s Violent Crimes Response Unit as investigators worked to establish the origin of the body parts and identify any possible victim.
The police urged residents to provide credible information to security agencies to support investigations and help prevent crime.

title: Russian troops liberate two communities in Kharkov Region over past day — top brass
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Russian troops liberated two communities in the Kharkov Region over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units are tightening the ring of encirclement in the Kharkov Region and expanding the outer area of control. In the pocket of encirclement, our forces established control of the settlements of Nefyodovka and Chyornoye in the Kharkov Region through active operations," the ministry said in a statement.
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,105 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost over 175 troops and 16 motor vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, roughly 220 troops and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and about 145 troops and two field artillery guns in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost roughly 345 troops and five armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, over 190 troops and a Grad multiple rocket launcher in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and about 30 troops and 13 motor vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North forces are tightening the ring of encirclement of Ukrainian troops in the Kharkov Region and fighting for the liberation of two communities in that area, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units are tightening the ring of encirclement in the Kharkov Region and expanding the outer area of control. In the pocket of encirclement, <…> they continue battles for the liberation of the communities of Nikolayevka and Varvarovka in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
Battlegroup North forces are expanding the outer area of control and continue battles for the settlements of Prikolotnoye, Kotovka and Gogino in the Kharkov Region, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicted more than 175 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed 16 enemy motor vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
In the Kharkov direction, Battlegroup North units "delivered strikes on strongholds of a heavy mechanized brigade and an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Fyodorovka and Maly Burluk in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
In addition, in the Kharkov Region, Battlegroup North units struck manpower and equipment of three mechanized brigades, two motorized infantry brigades and two assault regiments of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Liptsy, Velikiye Prokhody, Zamulovka, Shirokoye, Zarechnoye, Pershotravnevoye, Kurgannoye, Veliky Burluk, Vysoky and Gontarovka, it specified.
In the Sumy direction, Battlegroup North units struck formations of a mechanized brigade of the Ukrainian army and two territorial defense brigades in areas near the settlements of Leninskoye, Barilovka and Pervomaiskoye in the Sumy Region, it said.
Overall, the Ukrainian army lost more than 175 personnel, 16 motor vehicles and two electronic warfare stations in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted roughly 220 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed three enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup West units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Mayaki and Karpovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic, Chervony Oskol and Maliyevka in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 220 personnel, three armored combat vehicles, 14 motor vehicles, three artillery guns and a Grad multiple rocket launcher in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted roughly 145 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy field artillery guns in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup South units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of a mechanized brigade, a mountain assault brigade and an airmobile brigade of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Kramatorsk, Slavyansk, Semyonovka, Vysokoivanovka and Krasny Molochar in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 145 personnel, 33 motor vehicles and two field artillery guns in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center forces liberated 31 buildings in Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic and destroyed roughly 15 Ukrainian troops over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"In Dobropolye in the Donetsk People’s Republic, assault groups of the 51st Army advanced in the town’s northwestern part. Marine infantry assault teams continued advancing in the western part of that community," the ministry said.
During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup Center units liberated 31 buildings and eliminated roughly 15 Ukrainian troops in Dobropolye, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted roughly 345 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed five enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Center units inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of four mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army, a marine infantry brigade and two National Guard brigades in areas near the settlements of Krutoyarovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region, Belozerskoye, Novoyavlenka, Druzhkovka, Starovarvarovka, Vesyolaya Gora, Roganskoye, Yuryevka and Gornyak in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 345 personnel, five armored combat vehicles and 12 motor vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted more than 190 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy Grad multiple rocket launcher in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup East units continued their advance deep into the enemy’s defenses and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two air assault brigades, two assault regiments of the Ukrainian army and two marine infantry brigades in areas near the settlements of Tarasovka, Ivanovka, Kolomiytsy, Chernenkovo, Vasilkovka and Podgavrilovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region, Mirolyubovka and Raiskoye in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 190 personnel, six motor vehicles, a Grad multiple rocket launcher and an electronic warfare station in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated roughly 30 Ukrainian troops and destroyed 13 enemy motor vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Dnepr units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades and a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Orekhov, Balabino and Kushugum in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
"Up to 30 Ukrainian military personnel and 13 motor vehicles were destroyed," it said.
Russian forces struck Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assembly workshops and storage sites and enemy deployment areas over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian army, workshops producing unmanned aerial vehicles and their storage sites, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 145 locations," the ministry said.
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 342 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles and four cruise missiles over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down four Flamingo long-range cruise missiles and 342 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.
Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian combat aircraft, 284 helicopters, 262,470 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,239 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,790 multiple rocket launchers, 36,734 field artillery guns and mortars and 74,611 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.

title: Sheikha Latifa hosts women leaders' majlis in Dubai to discuss innovation and opportunities
body: Sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed has hosted an international gathering of women leaders in Dubai , bringing together voices from 22 countries to explore the future of leadership and innovation. The Women Leading the Future majlis was organised as part of the Annual Meeting of Global Future Leaders, which was delivered through a partnership between the UAE Government, the World Economic Forum and the Dubai Future Foundation. The majlis, on Wednesday, brought together 29 women leaders from government, entrepreneurship, science , technology, finance and culture. Discussions considered the choices, responsibilities and collaboration required to create opportunities for the next generation, with a focus on women's contributions to public leadership, innovation, investment and social change. Sheikha Latifa, chairwoman of Dubai Culture and Arts Authority, emphasised the UAE's commitment to investing in women's capabilities and equipping them with the knowledge, skills and experience to drive sustainable change. She highlighted the growing importance of diverse perspectives as artificial intelligence and emerging technology reshape industries, working practices and everyday life. She also noted the critical roles women play across sectors in fostering integration, harnessing technology to create opportunities and strengthening social cohesion. Shaping humanity's future, she said, was a shared responsibility requiring broader participation and practical, sustainable solutions to tomorrow's challenges. This first Annual Meeting of Global Future Leaders brought together more than 700 leaders and experts from 100 countries, including ministers, officials, 300 Young Global Leaders and 150 UAE government leaders. It served as a forum for international dialogue on developing responses to future challenges.

title: IMF Raises Africa Regional Economic Outlook, Lauds Resilience
body: The International Monetary Fund on Thursday upgraded its growth forecast for sub-Saharan Africa to 4.5 percent this year, with the organization’s regional director welcoming countries’ resilience in the face of a succession of crises, including the US-Iran war. The Fund upgraded its growth forecast for the region by 0.2 percentage points from its last World Economic Outlook update in April, noting that global energy supply adjustments and private sector adaptation helped cushion the shock of the war’s effect. Since late February, global oil, gas and fertilizer prices have skyrocketed as a result of the US war on Iran, with several African countries particularly exposed to the crisis as they are net importers of those commodities. Kristalina Georgieva (R), managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Singapore’s President Tharman Shanmugaratnam (C), and Danny Quah (L), Li Ka Shing Professor in Economics at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, take part in a discussion at the IMF Annual Meetings Curtain Raiser in Singapore on October 7, 2026. Still, IMF Africa Director Zeine Zeidane told AFP that even though growth was resilient, it needed to increase to keep pace with other regions. “Our view is that per capita growth today remains quite weak,” he told AFP at the Fund’s headquarters in Washington. “It would take the region nearly 50 years to double its income. By comparison, Southeast Asia managed to double its income per capita in 15 years.” (L-R) Finland’s Finance Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Riikka Purra, WBG President Ajay Banga, Thailand’s Finance Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and BBC’s Economics Editor Faisal Islam sit during the Building Resilience in a Fragmented World panel at the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group (WBG) at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok on October 13, 2026. (Photo by Lillian SUWANRUMPHA / AFP) The former Mauritanian prime minister noted, however, that countries had broadly been able to maintain current growth rates — even through multiple crises — without jeopardizing their public finances, with debt-to-GDP ratios broadly declining in most countries. This was due to “a genuine effort at fiscal consolidation,” notably through “better mobilization of domestic revenue,” he said. Debt servicing still represents a significant share of public spending — 12 percent of GDP on average, and up to a third in some countries, Zeidane said. “Financing needs continue to absorb a large share of credit available in the economy,” at the expense of other priorities more essential to development. “Instead of having banks that finance economic activity, we find ourselves in a situation where governments’ financing needs are crowding out the private sector,” he lamented. Zeidane said an absence of institutional investors, including corporations and pension funds, was a serious issue for the development of capital markets. “There is real work to be done to mobilize domestic financing,” he said. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva speaks during the Building Resilience in a Fragmented World panel at the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group (WBG) at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok on October 13, 2026. (Photo by Lillian SUWANRUMPHA / AFP) | Lillian SUWANRUMPHA / AFP Climate, Health Risks While African economies have largely managed to deal with global shocks, other threats will likely have a more acute effect on the continent. The El Niño climate phenomenon, in particular, is expected to have a serious impact on African economies. El Niño is a natural phenomenon recurring every two to seven years due to the warming of sea surfaces, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns. Global forecasters predict this year’s event will peak at an intensity never observed in the modern era, compounding the effects of man-made climate change, which drives extreme weather patterns. “We are very concerned because it could have a major effect on agricultural production but also on electricity generation, particularly in southern Africa,” Zeidane said. He added that the IMF was working on models to predict the potential impact on the region. The southern tip of the continent could face a particularly intense drought cycle, while in other parts of Africa, especially in the east, flooding could threaten agricultural production. “A shock like that can have a major impact on food prices, which make up a large share of the consumption basket in Africa,” he warned. Another source of concern is the health situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where an Ebola outbreak is “difficult to contain” and represents “a particular shock for Congo but also for its neighbors.” AFP The post IMF Raises Africa Regional Economic Outlook, Lauds Resilience appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Diri counters Donald Duke, says Lagos-Calabar coastal highway buildable
body:
Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri has faulted former Cross River State Governor Donald Duke’s claim that the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is unbuildable because of the swampy terrain in the Niger Delta, citing roads and bridges constructed in similar conditions in his state.
Mr Diri, in a statement issued by his spokesperson, Daniel Alabrah, and shared on Wednesday by the Bayelsa State Government’s new media platform , said Mr Duke’s criticism did not reflect developments in infrastructure construction in the region.
Mr Duke who is the presidential candidate for the Peoples Redemption Party in the 2027 general elections, described the proposed highway as unbuildable in an interview on Arise News, arguing that the swampy terrain in Bayelsa would make its construction difficult and require numerous bridges.
“The Lagos-Calabar Road is unbuildable. You cannot even go through Bayelsa. Bayelsa is swamp. Even Yenagoa, the capital, is swamp. You will probably have to build about 100 or 200 bridges to go through those swamps,” the former governor said.
But Mr Diri argued that his administration had demonstrated the feasibility of constructing roads and bridges across the state’s difficult terrain.
“I have seen the trending video clip of the former Governor of Cross River State, Donald Duke, on an Arise Television programme.
“To say the least, I feel disappointed that former Governor Duke, who is from our region, made such a comment. Clearly, he is not abreast of current developments in road construction and infrastructure development in our state,” Mr Diri said.
He suggested that Mr Duke’s criticism might have been politically motivated, saying the former governor had failed to consider the project’s importance to the Niger Delta.
“In Bayelsa, we have successfully constructed dual carriage roads and bridges in similar terrain and our state is better for it,” he said.
Mr Diri cited the Nembe-Brass Road, the Sagbama-Ekeremor-Agge Road and the Yenagoa-Oporoma Road as examples of major road projects traversing swampy terrain across the state’s three senatorial districts.
He also cited the 630-metre bridge across River Nun at Angiama community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, describing it as one of the longest bridges in the region.
The governor further referenced the dualised roads in New Yenagoa City and Glory Drive Phases One, Two and Three as evidence that road construction was possible in the state’s swamp and forest environments.
“Yenagoa is not what Duke described it. So, he is wrong. The Lagos-Calabar coastal road is buildable and possible,” he said.
The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is a 750-kilometre federal government project designed to traverse nine coastal states: Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Akwa Ibom and Cross River.
Mr Diri said the project was critical to unlocking economic opportunities and accelerating development in communities along its route, particularly riverine communities that have long faced infrastructure challenges.
He added that the highway was important to the Ijaw people, noting that the Ijaw National Congress had advocated such a project since its establishment in the 1990s.
According to the governor, successive federal administrations had received demands for the project before President Bola Tinubu’s government commenced it.
Mr Diri also said his decision to join the ruling All Progressives Congress is because the interests of his people should take precedence over partisan considerations.
He cautioned politicians against politicising development projects during election seasons, arguing that the consequences of such disputes were often borne by the same citizens whose votes they sought.

title: Popular Nigerian gospel singer Toluwanisings dies
body: One of Nigeria’s most popular gospel singers, Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, known as Toluwanisings, has died, his family has announced. In a statement posted on the deceased’s Instagram page, the family said the singer had “said goodbye to the world” in the early hours of Wednesday, 14 October. They also appealed to fans to remember his wife, children and family in prayer during this period of mourning. The family said burial arrangements would be announced in due course. Toluwanisings was known for his beautiful voice and energetic praise performances that encouraged audience participation, according to some of the tributes paid by his fans on social media. Some of his popular songs include Unreserved Praise, A Very Big God, Onibuore, E Lagbara and Owo Re Meji Meji. There was panic among thousands of his fans on social media after news first emerged of his death on Wednesday before it was later confirmed by the family. Toluwanisings’ death comes months after he was involved in a road accident alongside members of his band. Tributes have continued to pour in from colleagues and fans following the announcement of his death. Among those who reacted are prominent lawyer Pelumi Olajengbesi and comedian Woli Agba, who had earlier called for prayers for the singer.

title: Erdoğan’s chief adviser claims some are trying to ‘cast a shadow’ over Turkey-Azerbaijan alliance
body: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s chief adviser Hasan Nuri Yaşar has claimed that some are attempting to undermine ties between Turkey and Azerbaijan amid growing public controversy over Azerbaijan’s school hijab restrictions. In a post on X on Wednesday, Yaşar claimed that unnamed forces were seeking to distance Baku from Ankara. ‘For some time, we have been witnessing events and comments with dark undertones that could cast a shadow over the national unity between Türkiye and Azerbaijan’, Yaşar said. His remarks come after comments by another Erdoğan adviser criticising Azerbaijan’s school dress code, triggering responses from Azerbaijani political representatives and adding to tensions in public discourse between the two traditionally close allies. He claimed that three unnamed countries, who are allegedly rivals, were secretly developing joint strategies to distance Azerbaijan from Turkey and sever Turkey’s ties with Central Asia. Azerbaijani ruling party condemns Turkey for criticising hijab ban Tensions between Azerbaijan and Turkey appear to be entering a new phase. OC Media Rafig Shahbazov According to Yaşar, these forces are also seeking to introduce new and destructive tactics into the instability caused by the PKK (Kurdistan Workers’ Party) and its affiliates. ‘The position of our state must be carefully monitored on such strategic issues, and we must act with patience and caution’, he added. Yaşar’s remarks come amid recent controversy and protests over Azerbaijan’s ban on hijabs in educational institutions, which Turkish officials have responded to negatively. The two countries have traditionally maintained close ties but recently simmering tensions have bubbled to the surface, centred around disputes about Azerbaijan’s restrictions on religious freedom, Ankara’s distaste of Baku’s alliance with Israel, and questions over Turkish support during the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War. Explainer | What’s behind the Turkey–Azerbaijan spat? A variety of tenuously connected issues have exposed a deeper divide over the unequal power dynamics between Ankara and Baku. OC Media Nate Ostiller Earlier, Oktay Saral, another chief adviser to Erdoğan, described the ban on hijabs in Azerbaijani schools as ‘unacceptable’. His remarks drew responses from Azerbaijan’s ruling New Azerbaijan Party (YAP) and the Azerbaijan–Turkey interparliamentary working group. title: Frozen Russian Assets: Europe Rejects US Control Plan – FT
body:
The US proposed that European countries unfreeze some Russian sovereign assets and place them under Washington’s oversight to help revive negotiations over Russia’s war against Ukraine, according to a report published on Thursday, Oct. 15.
The Financial Times reported , citing four people briefed on the discussions, that US envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner presented the idea during talks in Miami. European representatives rejected it.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“They were told that this was just simply not going to happen,” one person told the newspaper.
The proposal involved transferring some immobilized reserves into a new financial vehicle overseen by Washington. A US official told the FT that possible uses of the assets were being discussed as part of a comprehensive peace agreement, with the mechanisms for releasing and spending the money still under consideration.
The Miami talks brought together representatives of Ukraine, Britain, France, Germany, the European Commission, and NATO alongside American negotiators. The meeting ended without an announced breakthrough.
European officials at the meeting opposed both handing control of the assets to another party and returning any of the funds to Moscow, according to the report.
Western countries immobilized roughly €260 billion ($291 billion) in Russian sovereign assets after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Around €210 billion ($235 billion) remains blocked in the EU, with much of it held through the Brussels-based securities depository Euroclear.
These are Russian central bank reserves, distinct from the private property of sanctioned businesspeople. EU restrictions prohibit transactions involving the management of those reserves, preventing Moscow from freely accessing them.
European leaders have repeatedly said the assets should remain immobilized until Russia ends its war and compensates Ukraine. In December 2025, the EU adopted additional emergency measures prohibiting transfers of the central bank’s assets or reserves back to Russia. Those measures strengthened the freeze without transferring ownership of the underlying reserves to Ukraine.
European governments nevertheless remain divided over how far they should go in using the funds. Belgium has raised legal and financial concerns about proposals to mobilize the principal, while Ukraine has pressed its partners to use Russian reserves more broadly to finance its needs .
The EU currently channels extraordinary earnings generated by the immobilized reserves toward assistance for Ukraine, while keeping the underlying assets frozen.
According to the Council of the EU , the assets have generated €8 billion ($9 billion) in windfall profits. Of that amount, €3.8 billion ($4.2 billion) has reached Ukraine, while €4.2 billion ($4.7 billion) has contributed to repayment of EU-G7 loans or been set aside for that purpose.
Under the current distribution rules, 95 percent of those revenues goes through a mechanism helping Ukraine repay approximately €45 billion ($50 billion) in EU-G7 loans. The remaining five percent support the European Peace Facility, which finances military assistance.
A separate €90 billion ($101 billion) EU support loan for 2026-27 is financed through European borrowing backed by the EU budget. European leaders agreed that Ukraine would repay that loan once it receives Russian reparations, while reserving the EU’s right to use immobilized Russian assets for repayment in accordance with international and EU law.
The dispute therefore concerns more than the location of the reserves: European governments have already tied them to Ukraine’s financing and eventual compensation for war damage.
The latest proposal follows earlier discussions about offering Moscow economic incentives for a limited ceasefire .
Those discussions included releasing some frozen Russian reserves, authorizing a transaction involving Lukoil’s foreign assets, and easing restrictions on Belarusian potash exports. The incentives were reportedly presented as measures that could encourage a partial halt to fighting, including attacks on energy infrastructure or maritime routes.
Ukrainian negotiators sought safeguards in those discussions, including matching financial releases for Ukraine and guarantees of faster military assistance if Russia violated a prospective truce.
Frozen reserves also featured in a 28-point US-backed draft peace plan published in 2025 . That draft proposed investing $100 billion in Russian assets in US-led reconstruction efforts in Ukraine, with Washington receiving 50 percent of the profits. It also envisaged a separate US-Russian investment vehicle.
The new asset proposal comes amid a broader disagreement over sanctions relief. European governments have opposed following Trump’s Russian diesel agreement , arguing that pressure on Moscow should remain in place while Russian attacks continue.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said earlier this week that following Washington’s diesel decision was “out of the question” for Germany and Europe, while maintaining that European governments remained in contact with the US over a common approach to ending the war.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Russian shelling of Kherson kills 2 men – official
body:
Two men were killed as a result of Russian shelling in Kherson, Head of the Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Prokudin reported.
"As a result of the enemy strike, two men sustained injuries incompatible with life. One of the deceased was 67 years old. The identity of the second victim is currently being established by the relevant services," he wrote on Telegram on Thursday.

title: Russian drone strikes Kyiv, injures 7, sets car ablaze
body:
The aftermath of a Russian drone attack in a residential area in the Pechersk District of Kyiv, Ukraine on Oct. 15, 2026. (Serhii Korovayny/The Kyiv Independent)
A Russian drone crashed in Kyiv's Pechersk District, injuring seven people and causing damage to a residential building on Oct. 15, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
Three of the injured people were hospitalied, Klitschko said . The Russian drone crashed near a five-story residential building, damaging the facades of nearby buildings, as well as setting a car on fire, he added .
"The blast wave blew the kitchen door off its hinges, and glass rained down. A neighbor was standing in the middle of the kitchen; she was knocked down by the blast and fell, sustaining injuries. We looked around — we hadn't even had time to react to it all — and everything was covered in glass," Inna Kozub, a local resident, said about the attack.
"I started shaking all over, and tears began to flow ... I was just overcome by panic," she said.
"We live here, my wife called and said that it (the drone) flew here, I was at work. And I sped home quickly. The children were at home, upstairs, just slightly injured," said Ruslan, another resident.
"They heard that the attack was coming, they jumped out into the corridor. The older one carried them out of the room. And then the windows flew out. He threw the little one to the ground and covered them," Ruslan added.
"There are a lot of these attacks now and they say that this is a matter of the Americans stopping helping us," he said.
Another Russian drone attack in the afternoon struck a warehouse in Sviatoshynskyi District, leading to a fire breaking out, Klitschko said .
Kyiv has come under continuous Russian attacks over the last weeks that saw strikes on civilians, as well as the capital's transport and energy infrastructure.
Ukraine's Air Force said Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with 580 Shahed-type and other drones, of which it neutralized 536 across 31 locations.
Overnight on Oct. 13-14, Russia launched a large-scale ballistic missile attack on Kyiv, wreaking destruction in a residential neighborhood and targeting several energy facilities in Kyiv.

title: Basij female unit commander assassinated in latest attack targeting Iranian armed forces
body: A commander in one of the Basij's female units was killed in an attack on Wednesday in Mehrestan, a border county in Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province, Iranian state media reported. The woman was identified as Afsaneh Aghila.Aghila, commander of the Afzal Sisters' Basij unit in Mehrestan, was reportedly assassinated outside her home in front of her children. The IRGC-affiliated Tasnim News Agency alleged that the gunmen had links to Israel and the US, but did not identify the group responsible or provide evidence to support its claim.In a separate incident in the same province, the Islamic Republic News Agency reported that security officer Mohsen Shahriyari was killed while confronting a “terrorist group.”Sardar Mohammadreza Eshaghi, the province's police commander, issued a statement following the killings, describing Aqila as “a woman of faith, courage, and sacrifice.”“I condemn this terrorist act and offer my condolences and congratulations on the martyrdom of these individuals to their comrades, the honorable people of Mehrestan, and the Basij community of Sistan and Baluchestan province,” Eshaghi said.Iranian People's Fighters Front claims responsibility for six attacks Attacks targeting members of the IRGC and other security forces in the province appear to have increased in recent weeks. The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) reported earlier this week that at least 94 people were killed and 33 wounded in 63 armed incidents across southeastern Iran between March 31 and October 10.The People's Fighters Front has claimed responsibility for only six of the incidents HRANA documented. The groups responsible for the remaining incidents remain unknown.Security expert Roger Macmillan told The Jerusalem Post that anti-regime attacks have increased since the Sunni group Jaish al-Adl merged with the PFF. He said there had been significant anger toward the IRGC over its “systematic arrest and torture of their people, many of whom don't even speak Farsi, and were forced into signing false documents, which have seen them convicted of alleged terrorist attacks, and then executed.”He argued that, with the brutal repression of Iranians across the country, the assassinations will continue to worsen.In one of the most notable incidents last week, Tasnim reported that Lieutenant-Colonel Nosrat Eftekhari, deputy for cultural and social affairs of the Law Enforcement Command in the province, was killed in what the agency described as a “terrorist attack.”Earlier this week, Haalvsh, an independent human rights organization and news outlet that documents human rights violations and security incidents in Sistan and Baluchestan, also reported that more than 20 members of the Fatemiyoun terrorist group were killed or wounded in an hours-long clash on Tuesday. The Iran-backed Shia group is composed primarily of Afghan Hazara refugees and migrants, and is both funded and trained by the IRGC.Iranian regime seeking to project strength, public support for BasijThe attacks come as the regime seeks to project an image of strength, cohesion, and public support for the Basij. The Islamic Republic has released numerous images from its Janfada (self-sacrifice) training exercises, prominently featuring women training with guns and drones. Janfada spokesperson Sasan Zare claimed that more than 500,000 women registered within 100 minutes of registration opening for the “National Resistance” battalions, filling the first 1,000 units.Despite the alleged masses who have registered for the self-sacrifice training, the Iran Human Rights Monitor has reported the regime is using violent criminals to fill its ranks, offering conditional release to those willing to suppress protests and signs of dissent.Basing its report on testimonies received from inmates, their families, informed sources within prisons, and field reports from human rights groups, criminals convicted of general, violent, or drug offenses were offered repentance forms in August and September and granted bail after they registered with the Basij.Although reports of personnel shortages in the Basij and IRGC predate the recent attacks, Macmillan suggested that financial desperation could drive people to enlist despite the risk of assassination.

title: Police arrest 24 suspected cultists, rescue abducted teenager in operations across 10 states
body:
The police have arrested 24 suspected cultists in Anambra State and rescued a 16-year-old abductee in Kaduna State , among other operations reported across 10 states.
The Force Public Relations Officer, Ani Iniedu, disclosed the developments in an operational update issued on Thursday, 15 October.
In Anambra, detectives arrested 24 additional suspects over their alleged involvement in a cult clash, following information obtained from suspects already in custody.
The police said two sharpened machetes were recovered, while investigations continued at the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Awka.
In Kaduna, police operatives working with military personnel and local vigilantes raided a bandits’ camp in Gwagwada and rescued a 16-year-old abductee.
The teenager was medically examined, found to be in stable condition and reunited with his family, according to the police.
In Kebbi, police officers and vigilantes confronted about 10 suspected kidnappers during an attempted abduction, killing one of them.
The police said a locally made double-barrelled gun was recovered at the scene, while efforts continued to arrest the fleeing suspects.
In Katsina, police tactical teams responded to a farmland trespass incident involving armed migrant herders.
The police said the group was dispersed, one suspect arrested, and two cows and four sheep recovered.
In Osun, detectives arrested a suspect in connection with the death of a 20-year-old man who was allegedly pushed into a well during an altercation.
Two occupants of a house were also arrested for questioning in Ekiti after a woman was found dead with injuries at her residence.
In Ogun, a police officer was arrested, disarmed and detained following a shooting at a company’s premises that left a local security guard dead and another person injured.
The police did not disclose the officer’s identity or explain the circumstances surrounding the shooting. The case is being investigated by the SCID in Abeokuta.
In Kano, officers recovered an abandoned pump-action rifle along Kasuwar Dogo Village in Ranka after receiving information from a member of the public.
Police teams in Jigawa also responded to an attack on farmers, prompting the suspected attackers to flee into nearby mountains.
The police said they maintained patrols in the area to prevent further attacks.
In Akwa Ibom, the command provided security during former President Goodluck Jonathan’s visit to Uyo. The police said the visit was peaceful and that patrols and other security operations continued.
The police did not specify the dates of the individual incidents or provide details of any charges filed against the suspects.

title: Lagos Trade Fair Complex condemns counterfeit drinks production after NAFDAC raid
body:
The management of the Lagos International Trade Fair Complex Management Board (LITFCMB) has condemned the production of counterfeit drinks and the sale of substandard products within its facility following a raid by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC).
NAFDAC on Tuesday said it seized products worth more than N2 billion and arrested two suspects during the operation.
The agency explained that its investigation and enforcement directorate uncovered more than 20 illegal stores allegedly used to counterfeit popular alcoholic beverage brands, revalidate expired drinks for resale and stockpile banned imported products.
In a statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES on Wednesday, the LITFCMB’s Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer, Veronica Ndanusa, said investigations had begun to establish the circumstances surrounding the activities.
She noted that the complex was meant to support legitimate businesses and would not be allowed to become a centre for producing or distributing counterfeit goods.
“Our facility exists to provide a conducive environment for legitimate businesses to thrive, not to serve as a breeding ground for the production or distribution of counterfeit and substandard products,” Ms Ndanusa said.
She commended NAFDAC for the operation and said the board would work with regulatory and law enforcement agencies to prevent illegal activities within the complex.
Ms Ndanusa warned that anyone found engaging in activities that endanger public health would face the full weight of the law.
She urged traders and business owners to comply with established standards and put consumers’ safety ahead of profit.
NAFDAC urged members of the public to report suspected cases of illegal manufacturing, the revalidation of expired products and the sale of regulated goods through its complaints line on 0800-1-NAFDAC (0800-1-623322).

title: Hezbollah claims ownership of explosive-laden vehicle seized by Lebanese army
body: Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah ⁠said ​on Thursday an explosive-laden vehicle ​seized by the Lebanese Armed Forces last week belonged to the Iran-backed group. Mr Fadlallah said Hezbollah had contacted Lebanese authorities to claim ownership of the vehicle as soon as it was intercepted. Its contents were intended “to confront the Israeli occupation” and Hezbollah's weapons were “pointed exclusively at the [Israeli] enemy”, he added. Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said there would be “no leniency” in the investigation and the government “will not tolerate anyone who dares to toy with the country's security, safety and stability”. About 250kg of TNT-type explosives and 250kg of C4 were discovered in a vehicle bound for Beirut when it was stopped at an Internal Security Forces checkpoint at Dahr Al Baidar in the Bekaa Valley, Then on Monday the Lebanese Armed Forces on Monday said it had seized 200kg of explosives, foiling a smuggling attempt from Syria through the Hermel border region. The Dahr Al Baidar seizure – one of three such interceptions in a matter of weeks – comes as pressure is mounting on the Lebanese government to disarm Hezbollah and bring all weapons in the country under state control. The seizure also caused widespread uproar in Lebanon. While the case is being investigated by a military court, some ministers at a cabinet meeting on Thursday are expected to push for it to be heard by Lebanon's Judicial Council, which deals with serious state security threats. Meanwhile, Hezbollah has remained defiant in rejecting disarmament and says any talks on the fate of its weapons can take place only after Israel halts attacks on Lebanon and withdraws from occupied Lebanese territory. Israel and Hezbollah have engaged in several bouts of fighting since the onset of the Gaza war in October 2023. The latest conflict began on March 2, when Hezbollah fired missiles at Israel in support of Iran in the regional conflict. Israel responded with a devastating military campaign, killing more than 4,000 people and flattening dozens of villages in southern Lebanon, where it continues to occupy vast areas of territory . Direct US-brokered talks between Israel and Lebanon have done little to move the needle, with no real progress on Hezbollah's disarmament or Israel's withdrawal. The interception of the explosive-laden vehicle has prompted fears of renewed political assassinations in Lebanon, a country with a grim history of such killings. In a second incident, about 250kg of TNT-type explosives and 250kg of the explosive C4 were discovered in a lorry bound for Beirut. “I understand the anxiety gripping the Lebanese people upon the news of this truck's interception and the materials it was transporting, especially since C4 has been used in several of the infamous political assassinations in modern Lebanese history,” Mr Salam said in a post on X on Monday. Mr Fadlallah dismissed the Prime Minister's words as an “inflammatory campaign aimed at sowing internal discord” and said Hezbollah would not “deter” the group from “continuing its efforts to defend and liberate their land”. He said Hezbollah had demanded the release of the two men "and the return of the vehicle and everything inside it". He also castigated the government's decision earlier this year to ban Hezbollah's military activities. "For our people, this decision is null and void, has no existence, and has no effects on the ground that we recognise." In the 2000s and early 2010s, several high-profile opponents of the Assad regime in Syria and its Lebanese ally Hezbollah were killed or had attempts made on their lives using explosives. Former prime minister of Lebanon Rafic Hariri was killed along with 20 others when a one-tonne lorry bomb was detonated as his convoy was driving through Beirut on February 14, 2005. Hezbollah members were convicted of that attack by the UN's Special Tribunal for Lebanon.

title: Russian drone strike hits shop in Odesa region, injuring three
body:
The head of state reported this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
“What is happening is Russia’s pointed response to the signals it is receiving from America. Unfortunately, there are dangerous signals about the possibility of further sanctions relief. These sanctions were imposed by the world, by America, Europe, and our partners in response to Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and its war against us. Nothing has changed.
