title: Novaya Gazeta Editor-in-Chief Detained in Moscow
body:
Russian law enforcement officers on Thursday raided the Moscow apartment of Sergei Sokolov, the editor-in-chief of independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta, before taking him in for questioning and subsequently releasing him.
Novaya Gazeta said contact with Sokolov was initially lost at around noon Moscow time before he was scheduled to lead an editorial planning meeting.
The publication said Sokolov was being transported to the Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, for questioning and that a lawyer was on their way to assist him.
Sokolov was later released on Thursday evening after law enforcement questioned him, reportedly in connection with the case against Novaya Gazeta managing editor Oleg Roldugin.
The raid on Sokolov’s apartment was conducted as part of an ongoing criminal investigation opened earlier this spring, law enforcement sources told the RBC outlet.
Meanwhile, sources told the state-run news agency TASS that the investigation centered around the illegal use of personal information.
Investigators charged Roldugin with the same crime earlier this year in April.
Roldugin, a veteran investigative journalist known for reporting on alleged corruption among top Russian officials, denies that he had illegally obtained and published personal information.
Baza, a Telegram news channel with links to Russia’s security services, reported that Roldugin was suspected of acting either, in coordination with, or under Sokolov’s instructions.
The Committee to Protect Journalists called on Russian law enforcement to immediately release Roldugin and stop what it described as the targeted prosecution of Novaya Gazeta.
Novaya Gazeta ceased print publication shortly after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine due to the draconian censorship laws that the government introduced as part of a broader crackdown on the press. The newspaper has continued to publish articles and videos online.
We are facing unprecedented challenges. Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has designated The Moscow Times as an "undesirable" organization, criminalizing our work and putting our staff at risk of prosecution. This follows our earlier unjust labeling as a "foreign agent."

title: Spio-Garbrah proposes debt swaps to fund reparative justice in Africa and Caribbean
body: Presidential Special Envoy for Reparations Ekwow Spio-Garbrah has proposed a debt-swap mechanism that would convert portions of eligible bilateral debt owed by African and Caribbean countries into investments in development priorities as part of efforts to advance reparative justice. The proposal is intended to recognise the lasting economic consequences of slavery and colonialism, rather than treat the conversion of debt solely as a form of debt relief. Speaking on behalf of Dr Spio-Garbrah at the 10th GITFiC Annual Conference on the 3rd Global Debt Initiative, his Programmes Manager, Isaac Obed Sarr, said the mechanism would allow resources that would otherwise go towards servicing eligible debt to be directed into development programmes. “There is neither charity nor debt forgiveness. Debt forgiveness is a concession. Debt converted for reparative purposes is an acknowledgement,” he said. The proposed investments would target education, healthcare, skills development, heritage restoration and industrial capacity. Mr Sarr stressed that the proposed arrangement should not be interpreted as a final settlement of the broader reparations claim. He also said efforts to secure reparative justice must be accompanied by accountability in the use of funds, warning that demands for international redress would be undermined by poor financial management at home. “We cannot ask the world to correct historical injustice while tolerating waste, corruption, and weak institutions at home. Nor demand access to capital by failing to account for its use,” he said. Dr Spio-Garbrah has called for the establishment of a joint technical working group to develop a framework for reparative debt swaps, identify a pilot transaction and coordinate a common African and Caribbean position for engagement with international institutions. His office, Mr Sarr said, is ready to provide technical expertise, support the proposed working group and engage African and Caribbean partners to move the initiative from advocacy to policy. The proposal seeks to link discussions on historical responsibility with practical development investments, while making financial accountability a central part of the process.

title: Defense ministers meeting reiterates importance of cooperation for stability within CIS
body:
CHOLPON-ATA /Kyrgyzstan/, October 15. /TASS/. The meeting of the Council of Defense Ministers of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), held in Cholpon-Ata, has reiterated the relevance and importance of strengthening cooperation within this framework to maintain stability across the Commonwealth, Russian Defense Minister Andrey Belousov said.
"The meeting has once again confirmed the relevance and necessity of developing cooperation within the framework of the Council of Defense Ministers to maintain stability throughout the Commonwealth," he said.
Belousov announced the signing of decisions aimed at enhancing the combat capabilities of national armed forces. "Following the meeting, decisions were signed aimed at further strengthening cooperation and increasing the combat capabilities of national armed forces," the minister reported. He specified that "the work plan for the Council of Defense Ministers for 2027 has been approved."
At the end of the Council meeting, the Russian defense chief described the overall atmosphere as "business-like and constructive." He noted that a range of issues concerning further improvements in combat capabilities was addressed, and that the results and priorities of joint military cooperation--aimed at strengthening Eurasian and regional security amid the current international situation--were analyzed. "In addition, the Council approved the outcomes and proposals for developing joint projects in the fields of military education and military sports, as well as for the planning and organization of activities in the military sphere," Belousov said.
In closing the meeting of the CIS Council of Defense Ministers, the minister thanked all participants for their constructive work together.

title: Ukraine faces loss of key satellite support amid tensions between Trump and Zelenskyy
body:
Trump declared a ceasefire, but both sides are still shooting.
The war in Ukraine has continued to rage in the days after President Donald Trump declared an energy ceasefire there, with Russia targeting civilian and energy infrastructure as the U.S. applies pressure on Kyiv to halt attacks on oil refineries in Russia, which Trump says are to blame for the high price of diesel fuel.
As the president's announcement of a partial ceasefire Sunday -- covering energy infrastructure in both countries -- failed to yield any limits to the fighting, he continued to apply public pressure on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The U.S. government-owned satellite infrastructure used by Ukraine's military for drone navigation and air defense on Wednesday was not operating at its normal functionality, raising concerns that American support for Kyiv was ebbing.
Zelenskyy said on a British television program Wednesday that his country was "losing a strong partner" in the United States, days after he said his military did not receive critical early warnings from partners of attacks that it had come to expect.
Six people were killed in strikes in Ukraine on Wednesday, Zelenskyy said.
A defense ministry official in Kyiv said overnight Wednesday that restrictions placed on Starshield, a satellite communications network owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX but contracted for use under terms set by the Pentagon, "disrupted" a number of "critical missions" in Ukraine.
A Ukrainian source said the restriction gave the Russians "real leverage on [the] frontline" by inhibiting the military's ability to defend against jet-powered Shahed drones. As the hours passed Wednesday, the Starshield limits began to loosen, but remained a concern for Ukraine.
The source said SpaceX did not warn Ukraine of the move or answer questions about the rationale for the halt.
Elon Musk, the chief executive of SpaceX, said on Wednesday that "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government" and "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [President Trump.]"
The White House, Pentagon and SpaceX did not respond to ABC News' requests for comment.
George Barros, an open-source analyst at the Institute for the Study of War, said "US decisions to throttle [Starshield] only harms Ukrainian forces on the defense in Ukraine," noting that Ukrainian forces have never been permitted to use the SpaceX networks for strikes deep into Russia.
"This decision will significantly degrade Ukraine's mid-range strike capability -- a key driver of Ukraine's recent battlefield momentum in 2026," he said in a post on X.
Intelligence sharing from military to military is America's primary contribution to Ukraine's war effort, analysts said, providing key early warnings for Russian strikes and targeting information.
Trump said Tuesday that intelligence sharing was continuing as usual.
A Ukrainian source in Kyiv on Wednesday said warnings did come overnight Wednesday -- but they were late.
European allies of Ukraine would look to fill any gap left by a U.S. drawback on intelligence sharing, but two European officials acknowledge there would still be a gap in Ukraine's intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities.
The battlefield impacts come amid tensions between the U.S. and Ukrainian presidents -- and between negotiators working on a diplomatic solution to the conflict.
Trump has insisted the two sides stop targeting energy infrastructure, but he has focused in particular on Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries. Over the weekend he struck a deal with Moscow to release diesel exports into global markets.
Trump said on Saturday Ukraine should not "hit the refineries, because that's [caused] a world problem."
After a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, Trump said he would authorize a Treasury Department license for the export of Russian diesel, overriding existing sanctions.
Gregory Brew, an energy analyst at the Eurasia Group, said the deal -- which would facilitate the export of some 74,000 barrels a day of diesel, a fraction of the amount Russia exported less than a year ago -- was motivated by Trump's domestic political calculations.
"All of this is being driven by the administration's desire to bring down fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections to try to improve Trump and the Republicans' outlook in that vote," Brew said. "So this is all being driven, I would say, largely by short-term considerations geared around energy prices and the midterm election outlook."
U.S. and Ukrainian negotiators, including Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, met Friday about a potential peace framework in Miami, where tensions rose over the arrangement with Russia.
Made aware of the forthcoming announcement from Trump, Ukrainian negotiators cut the meetings short, according to a source familiar with the Miami talks.
Two days after the Miami talks, Trump on Sunday said Ukraine and Russia did agree to a ceasefire on energy targets, but neither side corroborated the claim. A U.S. official told ABC News Trump's announcement was driven by his frustration with the Ukrainian president to compromise on an energy truce.
Zelenskyy has said he would order his military to abide by a truce only if Putin would do the same.
"If Trump really does want Zelenskyy to make concessions -- either to agree to this energy ceasefire or to permit this this diesel deal [with Russia], or to to bow to a broader deal that is maybe a little bit more favorable to Russia -- he's going to look for ways to to exercise that leverage," Brew said, referring to a potential curtailing of intelligence sharing.
The Kremlin has also been mum about the ceasefire, with Putin's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov saying the diesel deal and a broader peace agreement were on separate tracks.
Peskov reiterated what he called Moscow's consistent position "that we do not want a ceasefire" but instead "want lasting peace."
Trump's pressure campaign on Kyiv may be aimed at facilitating his diesel deal with Russia, Brew said.
"I would imagine that the Russian requirement for this deal to move forward is a halt to attacks on refineries," he said. "Russia needs its refineries to be operating under ideal circumstances in order to ramp back up diesel exports."
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Wednesday that Ukraine remained ready to enter into a ceasefire, conditional on Russia laying down its arms simultaneously. Tensions with the Americans were not new, he said, recalling a Trump outburst in the Oval Office a month into his presidency, when he scolded Zelenskyy publicly.
"In less than two years, Ukraine has gone from 'You don't have the cards' to 'Don't play your cards,'" Sybiha said Wednesday.

title: Alban Bagbin calls for governance reforms and coordinated action to address Africa’s debt crisis
body: Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin has called for reforms to Africa’s governance and economic systems, arguing that indiscipline and governance failures must be addressed if the continent is to break its cycle of mounting debt. He says African countries must look beyond repeated borrowing to meet existing obligations and reconsider the decisions and systems that leave their economies financially vulnerable. Speaking at the 10th GITFiC Annual Conference on the 3rd Global Debt Initiative, Mr Bagbin questioned how long African countries could continue borrowing to settle past obligations. “How long can Africa continue to borrow from the future to pay for the past?” he asked. The Speaker argued that the continent’s debt crisis should not be assessed solely in terms of the amounts owed, countries’ ability to repay or the debt relief creditors are prepared to offer. He acknowledged the effects of historical injustices, including slavery and colonial exploitation, but said African countries must also confront governance shortcomings and reconsider their development choices. “If you behave well, if you are disciplined, my brothers and sisters in the IMF will not come at you. But that is not true. It’s when there is indiscipline and we don’t get things right. Then they are there to come and discipline us,” he said. Mr Bagbin also cautioned against repeating past mistakes in debt relief, citing Ghana’s experience under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) initiative. He called for stronger domestic financial governance alongside a coordinated international framework to address the continent’s debt challenges. “We need a coordinated global framework. But before that, we need it domestically,” he said. The Speaker stressed that African countries must also present a united front in negotiations on debt and broader financial reforms. His remarks place the emphasis on both domestic accountability and international cooperation in efforts to address Africa’s debt burden.

title: INEC Inaugurates 2027 General Election Logistics Committee Today
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will on Thursday inaugurate the 2027 general election logistics committee. Our correspondent, who is monitoring the event, noted that after the inauguration, the leadership of the commission will hold its inaugural meeting with members of the committee. The meeting, which is taking place at the INEC headquarters in Abuja, aims to perfect all logistical arrangements for the forthcoming general election. The committee consists of transport associations including the Nigeria Road Transport Union, Maritime Workers Union, Nigeria Airport Authority, Road Transport Owners Association, as well as the police, Air Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, and members of the paramilitary. The electoral umpire is expected to brief the committee on what is expected of them, to ensure that logistical arrangements and distributions for the general election are hitch-free. The event is part of efforts to optimise operational excellence during the election. The post INEC Inaugurates 2027 General Election Logistics Committee Today appeared first on Channels Television .

title: AAK Academy Ghana trains 22 chocolate and confectionery companies in production techniques
body: FairAfric Ghana Limited in Amanase-Suhum has hosted the second AAK Academy Ghana, a two-day technical training programme aimed at strengthening skills, innovation and product development in Ghana’s chocolate and confectionery industry. Organised by AAK West Africa on October 7–8, 2026, under the theme “Advancing Technical Excellence in Chocolate & Confectionery Production,” the academy brought together representatives from 22 Ghanaian chocolate and confectionery companies. The programme built on the success of the inaugural AAK Academy Ghana held in June 2026 but placed a stronger emphasis on hands-on practical learning and technical application. Participants received practical training in chocolate and compound processing, covering key areas including tempering, tablet production, fillings, pralines and coatings. The programme also addressed sensory evaluation, crystallisation, chocolate bloom, texture and heat stability—critical areas for manufacturers seeking to improve product quality and consistency. The initiative forms part of four commitments made by AAK under its Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Ghana’s Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA). The commitments are intended to strengthen innovation, technical capacity development and value creation within Ghana’s food manufacturing ecosystem. The academy comes at a time when Ghana is seeking to increase the value derived from its agricultural raw materials by moving beyond the export of commodities and expanding the production of higher-value food products for both domestic and international markets. The initiative also creates a link between Ghana’s cocoa and shea value chains and higher-value food manufacturing through Kolo Nafaso, AAK’s shea sourcing programme. The programme works with about 275,000 women shea collectors across West Africa, supporting rural livelihoods while strengthening access to responsibly sourced shea for the food industry. Unlike the first AAK Academy, which focused largely on industry knowledge, market trends and emerging opportunities, the second edition shifted the emphasis towards practical application, giving participants an opportunity to translate technical knowledge directly into production skills. The organisers say the practical approach is intended to help Ghanaian manufacturers improve their capabilities in product development, quality assurance and innovation, ultimately contributing to a more competitive and value-added food manufacturing sector. The second AAK Academy Ghana therefore represents another step towards building technical capacity within Ghana’s chocolate and confectionery industry while strengthening the connection between the country’s agricultural resources and higher-value manufacturing.

title: SA Navy attends seapower symposium in Italy
body:
The South African Navy’s commitment to strengthening international maritime cooperation and naval diplomacy was reflected in the 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium, hosted by the Italian Navy in Venice, Italy.
Held under the theme, “From Regional Waters to Global Influence,” the 6 to 7 October symposium brought together 77 naval delegations from five continents, more than 800 participants and 21 international speakers to deliberate on maritime security, technological innovation and the importance of collective action in safeguarding the world’s oceans.
The symposium’s emphasis on cooperation and shared maritime responsibilities aligns with the naval diplomacy programme championed by the Chief of the South African Navy, Vice Admiral Monde Lobese, who has consistently advocated stronger partnerships among African and international navies to address common maritime security challenges, the SA Navy said.
Central to this approach is the principle of Sisonke, meaning “together”, which Lobese promoted during the Sea Power for Africa Symposium held in Cape Town in 2024. The concept advocates greater unity among African navies through information-sharing, joint maritime operations, professional development and coordinated responses to maritime threats.
“This diplomatic approach has also found expression in the SA Navy’s growing international engagements, including cooperation with the Indian Navy on submarine rescue capabilities and participation in the International Fleet Review and Exercise MILAN 2026 in India, where SAS Amatola represented South Africa alongside international naval forces. These engagements demonstrate the importance of naval diplomacy in strengthening professional relationships, interoperability and mutual understanding,” the SA Navy said.
“The Venice symposium reinforced these principles, recognising that maritime security challenges increasingly transcend national boundaries and that disruptions to regional seas can have far-reaching consequences for international trade, energy security and economic stability.”
For South Africa, strategically positioned along major shipping routes connecting the Atlantic and Indian Oceans, these discussions are particularly significant. They highlight the importance of safeguarding maritime interests, protecting sea lines of communication and contributing to regional and international maritime stability.
The symposium also explored emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and autonomous naval systems, emphasising the need for modern, adaptable and resilient naval forces capable of responding to an increasingly complex maritime security environment.
The gathering concluded with a declaration reaffirming the importance of maritime interconnectedness, respect for national sovereignty, technological innovation, mutual trust and collective responsibility in securing the maritime domain.
“These outcomes resonate with Vice Admiral Lobese’s broader vision of strengthening the SA Navy’s international partnerships while advancing its operational effectiveness, professional development and contribution to maritime security. As the global maritime environment continues to evolve, the SA Navy’s diplomatic engagements remain an important instrument in advancing South Africa’s defence interests and fostering cooperation among friendly navies,” the SA Navy said.
“Ultimately, the symposium reaffirmed a principle central to the SA Navy’s diplomatic outlook: the security and prosperity of the oceans depend not only on individual naval capabilities, but also on the strength of international partnerships and a shared commitment to collective maritime security — Sisonke,” it concluded.

title: Supreme Court Judge Selection Process Restarts After Only Candidate Withdraws
body: Georgia’s High Council of Justice (HCOJ), a body supervising the Georgian judiciary, will restart the selection process for a Supreme Court judge after the sole candidate, Temur Gogokhia, withdrew on October 13, a day after advancing to the final stage. The council had selected Gogokhia for the final stage of the competition on October 12. He withdrew the following day without providing a public explanation. Supreme Court judges are nominated by the HCOJ and approved by the parliament. They are appointed to serve a lifetime term. Applications for the single Supreme Court vacancy will be accepted electronically from October 15 through November 5, 2026. The position became vacant after the death of Supreme Court Judge Giorgi Gogiashvili on July 8. Gogokhia has held various senior positions in Georgia’s judiciary. He was appointed a judge at Tbilisi City Court in July 2017 and became acting chair of its criminal cases panel that October. He was appointed chair in March 2020 and took over as chair of the court’s Criminal Cases Chamber in September 2021. He also served as a member of the High Council of Justice from 2021 to 2024. Previously, he served as a judge and court chair in Poti from 2008 to 2010, Batumi from 2010 to 2012, and Kutaisi from 2013 to 2017. Earlier in his career, he worked in various court administrative positions and as a prosecutor. His name has previously appeared in media and watchdog reports amid scrutiny of possible cases of nepotism and pro-government leanings in the judiciary. In 2023, he was among the HCOJ members who publicly spoke out against the U.S. sanctions on key Georgian judges. Gogokhia’s withdrawal coincided with another development in Georgia’s judiciary. On October 13, Judge Manana Kobakhidze quit the Georgian Constitutional Court, a separate judicial body, after her request to recuse herself from a case brought by the ruling Georgian Dream party seeking to ban several opposition parties was rejected. title: Adwumawura Programme trains second cohort of young entrepreneurs in Bono East
body: Young entrepreneurs in the Bono East Region have completed the training phase of the second cohort of the government’s Adwumawura Programme, with beneficiaries exploring funding and market opportunities to grow their businesses. The programme, implemented under the National Entrepreneurship and Innovation Programme (NEIP), provides entrepreneurship training, startup support and mentorship to young Ghanaians seeking to establish or expand businesses. A Breakfast Meeting with Purpose AGRICo Hub, the region’s designated training service center for the programme, hosted a strategic Breakfast Meeting in Techiman to officially bring the Adwumawura Programme to a close. The event served as a crucial bridge between emerging entrepreneurs and local financial institutions, creating a platform for direct engagement and potential funding opportunities. The atmosphere was electric as young business owners—many of whom had spent the past five weeks immersed in intensive entrepreneurship and business development training—networked with representatives from banks and financial agencies, pitching their visions and exploring avenues for growth. What Beneficiaries Received The Adwumawura Programme offers a comprehensive support package designed to give young entrepreneurs a competitive edge: · Five weeks of intensive entrepreneurship and business development training · Access to grant support and startup equipment · Six months of structured post-training mentorship and coaching This holistic approach ensures that participants are not only trained but also adequately supported as they navigate the challenging terrain of business ownership. “A Programme That Delivers” Speaking at the Breakfast Meeting, Emmanuel Sarkodie, Manager of AGRICo Academy and In-Charge of the Digital Innovation Unit at AGRICo Hub, expressed confidence in the programme’s ability to transform lives. “This programme has what it takes to empower the participants to succeed in their own businesses,” he said. “In the long run, it will help create jobs for the unemployed in our community.” Emmanuel Sarkodie emphasised that the initiative goes beyond mere training—it is a catalyst for sustainable economic development in the region and beyond. Participants Speak: From Local Businesses to Global Markets The beneficiaries themselves were effusive in their praise for the programme, with many describing it as a turning point in their entrepreneurial journeys. One participant noted that the training had helped them “reposition themselves and their businesses by opening opportunities in the global market.” The sentiment was echoed by several others who expressed optimism about the future. “We have been empowered to partner with other agencies like the Association of Ghana Industries (AGI) and the Free Zones to help us export our products,” another participant shared. For these young entrepreneurs, the dream is not just personal success—it is about creating opportunities for others. Many expressed confidence that as their businesses expand, they will be able to “attract more hands,” thereby increasing their workforce and creating jobs for the masses. Targeting Ghana’s Youth The Adwumawura Programme specifically targets young Ghanaian citizens, typically aged 18 to 40, who have viable or existing businesses with the potential to scale. Applications for the 2026 second cohort opened around May 2026, with onboarding and intensive training kicking off in September. The programme aims to support youth-owned enterprises annually as part of broader government efforts to curb youth unemployment and drive local economic growth. A Model for Economic Transformation As Ghana continues to grapple with youth unemployment, initiatives like the Adwumawura Programme offer a glimmer of hope. By combining training, funding, mentorship, and market linkages, the programme is not just creating businesses—it is building a new generation of job creators. The Breakfast Meeting in Techiman was more than a closing ceremony; it was a statement of intent. These young entrepreneurs are ready to take on the world, and with the support of the Adwumawura Programme, they just might succeed.

title: US Navy deploys USV with Carrier Strike Group for first time
body:
The US Navy has deployed an uncrewed surface vessel alongside a carrier strike group for the first time, US officials revealed.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao disclosed the milestone on October 14 during a panel discussion at the Association of the United States Army's annual conference in Washington, D.C. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth also attended the discussion.
“This is the first carrier strike group to ever deploy with a large-size unmanned surface vessel,” Cao said.
He described the deployment as a force multiplier, adding that the vessel could provide additional capabilities to naval forces.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group departed San Diego in late September for a deployment to the Middle East. Leidos had confirmed on September 8 that Seahawk was operating alongside the strike group, describing it as the first medium uncrewed surface vessel to deploy operationally with a carrier strike group.
According to Leidos, Seahawk supports autonomous navigation and perception, enabling it to operate with limited human intervention. Its collision-avoidance capabilities include compliance with the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs) and the ability to avoid hazards. The vessel can also automatically navigate around designated restricted areas, known as Keep Out Zones.
Seahawk can maintain control through alternative communications paths if its primary communications link becomes unavailable. It has also demonstrated GPS-denied navigation, following commanded waypoints without GPS before reintegrating GPS while remaining on track.
Leidos completed delivery of Seahawk to the US Navy in April 2021 under a contract awarded by the Office of Naval Research in December 2017. The contract was valued at approximately $35.5 million.
The vessel is a medium-displacement unmanned surface vessel (MDUSV) featuring a composite trimaran hull. Its fully loaded displacement is 145 long tons, including a fuel capacity of 14,000 gallons.
Designed for extended operations with limited human involvement, Seahawk incorporates mechanical and electrical systems intended to support operation over periods of months without a crew or routine maintenance.

title: Russia’s largest drone attack on Kirovohrad Oblast since the full-scale invasion kills three in Kropyvnytskyi
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia hit central Ukraine’s Kirovohrad Oblast with its largest attack since the full-scale invasion, killing residents of the oblast capital, Kropyvnytskyi, the oblast’s head said . Russian strikes hit more than a dozen oblasts, and Ukraine’s president said Moscow escalated deliberately after sanctions relief. Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine continues on the front line and behind it, where its drones, missiles, and glide bombs strike towns daily. Kyiv is drafting winter crisis plans as Russia targets the biggest cities, and logistics is hit too: Russia struck one retailer’s warehouse hub 10 times in a day. Three dead in Kropyvnytskyi Oblast head Andrii Raikovych counted almost 360 Russian drones over Kirovohrad Oblast and hits on 26 locations, mostly in Kropyvnytskyi. In his words, “the enemy deliberately struck critical infrastructure, transport enterprises, logistics facilities, and residential buildings.” In a post after midnight, he reported a third death and six injured, five of them in hospital. Air-raid alerts around the city ran from 15:20 on 14 October to 05:33, and Suspilne correspondents heard more than 20 explosions in Kropyvnytskyi, the public broadcaster reported . The national emergency service counted 25 struck locations, and rescuers were still putting out fires in the morning, the service’s spokesperson in the oblast said . People and a damaged car in the yard of an apartment block in Kropyvnytskyi after the Russian drone attack of 14–15 October 2026. Photo: Andrii Raikovych/Telegram A wave Kyiv ties to sanctions relief Nationwide, Russia launched 580 drones and two Kh-59 guided missiles from 18:00 on 14 October, and air defenses downed or suppressed 536 drones by 08:00, the Air Force reported . Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia killed three people in Kropyvnytskyi and three in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, where oblast head Oleksandr Hanzha reported two dead. He added that Russia escalated “deliberately, having received a relaxation of sanctions and seeing attempts to pressure Ukraine.” Last week, Washington cleared Russian diesel trade after a call between US President Donald Trump and Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin. Strikes from Kyiv to Odesa Oblast In Kyiv, a drone fell into a residential yard, Mayor Vitali Klitschko wrote , later putting the injured at six. Drones hit two industrial enterprises in Poltava Oblast, its head Vitalii Diakivnych wrote , and a later strike on Poltava injured three people, rescuers said in a preliminary count. Ukraine’s state gas company Naftogaz said a drone set one of its gas production facilities in the oblast on fire, halting its work. Russian guided aerial bombs injured two women and a man in Izium, Kharkiv Oblast, on 15 October, according to preliminary data from oblast head Oleh Syniehubov, who had counted nine injured in the oblast over the previous day. Over that day, Russian attacks killed three people in Donetsk Oblast, the oblast police said , and one in Kherson Oblast, where oblast head Oleksandr Prokudin reported five more injured. title: Russia plans to continue importing gasoline until end of year — Novak
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Russia plans to continue importing gasoline at least until the end of 2026 for supplying the market and replenishing reserves, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters on the sidelines of Russian Energy Week.
"We will continue imports at least until the end of the year as we need to both supply the domestic market and increase reserves, which went down in the summer period to meet domestic demand," he said.
The volume of imported gasoline on the Russian market remains stable at 10%, Novak added.
The Russian Energy Week (REW) International Forum is taking place in Moscow from October 14 to 16. It is being held with the support of the Government of the Russian Federation, the Ministry of Energy of the Russian Federation, and the Government of Moscow. The Roscongress Foundation organizes the forum. TASS is the information partner of Russian Energy Week.

title: Zelensky sets unacceptable conditions for holding elections — Lavrov
body:
BAKU, October 15. /TASS/. Vladimir Zelensky does not want elections; it is evident from the unacceptable conditions he has set forward for holding them, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated.
"Mr. Zelensky has already made it clear that he is not interested in elections because he has set conditions that are obviously unacceptable," the top diplomat told reporters following his participation in the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku.
When asked whether Moscow is ready to make concessions if the presidential election in Ukraine does take place, Lavrov noted: "We’re not going to speculate."
At the same time, the foreign minister warned: "There will be no ceasefire intended to bring him [Zelensky] back to his senses and pump him with weapons."
Zelensky’s presidential term officially expired on May 20, 2024. However, Kiev did not hold the next election, claiming that it is impossible until martial law ends.
On October 10, US President Donald Trump stated that Zelensky should hold elections and that he could have ended the conflict in Ukraine and concluded a peace agreement many times already.

title: Social Security benefits to get a boost. And, Hasan Piker defends his rhetoric
body:
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
Consumer prices in September were 3.7% higher than they were a year ago, according to a Labor Department report . A spike in energy prices linked to the U.S. war with Iran drove up the cost of living. Excluding energy and food prices, core inflation reached 2.6% in September, up from August. The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% increase in benefits for next year after the release of the inflation report. This annual cost-of-living adjustment is based on prices from July, August and September. Some recipients say the increase is not enough .
Rising gasoline and diesel prices pushed inflation higher in September. The cost of living index was up 3.7%, according to a report Wednesday from the Labor Department. Isabelle Souriment/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced he will resume attacks on Russian oil refineries, despite President Trump's request to refrain from doing so. Zelenskyy told the Financial Times that he had ordered commanders to stand down earlier this week, but wouldn't anymore. But Ukraine's ability to conduct these long-range attacks may be limited, as it has seen sudden crippling restrictions to Starshield, the satellite communications system provided by the U.S.
A man shot and wounded by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in New York last week says he didn't know the men who shot him were ICE agents until after he woke up in the hospital. A new petition filed in Brooklyn federal court says the agents — many of them masked — didn't identify themselves before approaching Oscar Belgal's vehicle with their firearms drawn. The filing contradicts the Trump administration's version of events.

California-based Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has emerged as a key target for the GOP ahead of the midterm elections. The president recently labeled him a "terrible liability" and a "communist." In Michigan, political ads attempting to link him to Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayef repeatedly play Piker's most controversial statements, including the infamous "America deserved 9/11." Pearce kicked off the North American leg of his tour in Baltimore, but has sold-out shows in cities such as New York and Los Angeles and has already captivated audiences in Bahrain, Singapore and India.
