title: PM Koretskyi sees grounds for optimism on international financial aid after Parliament’s progress
body:
Koretskyi wrote this on Telegram , Ukrinform reports.
“The Verkhovna Rada has backed several important legislative initiatives under the Ukraine Facility program, our agreements with the IMF and other international support mechanisms. I thank the members of parliament who supported the first set of important decisions for the country, on which our defense capabilities depend,” the statement said.
Koretskyi added that the results of this parliamentary sitting week provided grounds for optimism. The government is continuing its dialogue with lawmakers and hopes to maintain the same constructive cooperation during the next plenary week to ensure that all necessary decisions are adopted on time and Ukraine receives the full amount of international financial assistance.
As reported, on October 15 the Verkhovna Rada passed in its entirety a package of laws on taxing small postal and express shipments worth up to €150 ordered through online marketplaces.

title: Russian diesel to help stabilize global energy markets — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Supplies of Russian diesel to global energy markets will help stabilize them, though they will not be able to fully stabilize them, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a briefing.
"Quite large volumes of diesel are currently becoming available. This diesel has begun reaching global markets, which will have a certain positive effect on stabilizing oil markets, though it will not be enough to fully stabilize them, it is necessary to recognize it," he said.
Asked how the Kremlin assesses global reaction to the diesel deal between Moscow and Washington, and why it is being described as diplomatic, Peskov said: "This is an energy [deal] in the first place, I don’t know why it is being called diplomatic."

title: Qatar condemns Colombia’s opening of embassy in al-Quds
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 15 (MNA) – Qatar’s Foreign Ministry has condemned Colombia’s opening of its embassy to occupied Palestine in al-Quds on Wednesday.
Qatar’s Foreign Ministry has condemned Colombia’s opening of its embassy to occupied Palestine in al-Quds on Wednesday, describing the move as a violation of international law and relevant UN resolutions.
In a statement on X, the ministry reaffirmed Qatar’s “rejection of any measures aimed at altering the legal and historical status of the city of Jerusalem”, while calling on the international community to take action and “confront any attempts to impose a new reality in the occupied city”.

title: ‘Everything Is Gone Now’, Survivors Fear For Future After Latest Nepal Flood
body: Standing beside his house half-buried in thick sludge, Nepali flash flood survivor Ajay Gurung surveyed the wreckage of a life swept away in minutes. The Budhi Gandaki River that once sustained his family tore through central Gorkha district on Sunday, leaving a trail of destruction along the way. The flooding, which swept away 200 houses and five bridges, is the latest in a series of recent natural disasters in Nepal, renewing fears among vulnerable mountain communities. In August, a catastrophic flood in northern Rasuwa district killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing, highlighting the risks posed by Nepal’s unstable mountain terrain. Gurung, 33, said his shop and cattle were washed away by the swollen river as he looked on. “Everything is gone now,” Gurung told AFP. “I now need to look for an alternative place to live.” A trekking guide for nearly two decades, Gurung said he had never seen so many landslides along the Manaslu circuit where he had led countless tours. “In the future, no settlements built along the banks of rivers flowing from the snowy mountains will survive,” he said. Along the Budhi Gandaki, the scale of Sunday’s flood is emerging as residents pick through the mud in search of whatever can be salvaged. Residents walk past sludge-ridden houses along the banks of the Budhi Gandaki river at Soti Bazar in Nepal’s Gorkha district on October 14, 2026, in the aftermath of a flash flood caused by a dry landslide(Photo by PRAKASH MATHEMA / AFP) No deaths have been confirmed, but at least six people are missing, and three hydropower plants were damaged, according to disaster officials. “I had a banana farm. That is also gone,” said Lal Kurmari Thapa. “We are left with nothing but a small hut, which was spared.” Others, she said, lost even more. “Some don’t even have a sheet of roofing left. Budhi Gandaki is flowing over it. They don’t even have clothes.” Minimising Risks Nepal’s rugged geography has long made it vulnerable to floods and landslides. But recurring disasters have heightened anxieties in communities living close to rivers descending from the Himalayas, where scientists warn warming temperatures are increasing risks. The Budhi Gandaki flood came less than two months after the devastating ice-and-rock collapse in Rasuwa district unleashed a torrent of water and debris. Scientists said climate change played a significant role in that disaster. Last month, heavy monsoon rains triggered floods and landslides that killed at least 21 people across the country. Researchers say the disasters underscore the complex dangers facing Himalayan river systems. “Understanding what triggered this flood will be critical for reducing future risks and strengthening resilience,” said Pema Gyamtsho, director general of the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development. Preliminary findings by Nepal’s disaster authority suggest the latest flood was also triggered by an avalanche of rock and ice. “This year there have been back-to-back disasters, and climate change plays a role,” disaster authority chief Dharam Raj Uprety said. “The frequency shows that it has become critical that we monitor our mountains and make our early warning systems more effective.” Authorities said work is underway to strengthen monitoring and adaptation measures so that risks will be minimised when the next disaster strikes. Residents in Nepal’s Gorkha district look at muddy water flowing through the Budhi Gandaki river as an excavator clears sludge from Dhading district on October 14, 2026 in the aftermath of a flash flood caused by a dry landslide(Photo by PRAKASH MATHEMA / AFP) For survivors such as Dil Kumari Thapa Magar, however, the threat no longer feels distant. Weeks ago, she watched the Rasuwa disaster unfold on her phone screen. It has now arrived at her doorstep. “We had closely observed the flooding in Rasuwa. It was quite far away, but we were very worried when we saw it,” she said. “Now, we have become victims of the flood ourselves.” AFP The post ‘Everything Is Gone Now’, Survivors Fear For Future After Latest Nepal Flood appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Adnoc says decade-old contingency plan kept oil flowing throughout Iran war
body: State-owned Adnoc began preparing for major disruption to energy supplies 10 to 15 years ago, building contingency plans and backup infrastructure that helped it maintain oil production throughout the Iran war. “We actually prepared for this scenario in our playbooks 10 years ago, 15 years ago,” Abdulmunim Al Kindy, a board director at Adnoc and chairman of Abu Dhabi energy event Adipec, said on Thursday. Mr Al Kindy, who previously served as executive director of Adnoc's upstream directorate, said the company invested heavily in backup facilities and interconnections that allowed it to switch supply sources and delivery destinations. “[We] built projects at great expense, even though at the time they didn’t make any commercial sense,” he said. “When the time came, we actually kept the lights on.” The company's preparedness extended beyond physical infrastructure to years of emergency drills and scenario planning, giving employees “almost muscle memory” when the crisis struck, he said. Adnoc has increased its oil production capacity by almost 75 per cent over the past decade to 4.85 million barrels per day and is targeting five million bpd by 2027. Last November, Adnoc approved a Dh551 billion ($150 billion) spending plan for 2026 to 2030 to maintain operations and expand production capacity to meet rising global energy demand. Adipec to draw record Asian participation Mr Al Kindy was speaking at a press conference ahead of Adipec 2026, which Adnoc will host in Abu Dhabi from November 2 to 5, as energy security takes on greater urgency following months of disruption to global oil and gas flows. “2026 has demonstrated a fundamental truth – energy security is economic stability,” he said. The event will draw its largest Asian participation yet, with 353 companies and six national pavilions representing China, India, Japan, Malaysia, Singapore and South Korea. Organisers expect more than 239,000 visitors from at least 170 countries, with international visitors accounting for 56 per cent of the total attendance. Three quarters of the 2,250 exhibiting companies are expected to come from outside the UAE. The conference will feature more than 16,500 delegates and 1,800 speakers across 13 programmes. Rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence and industrial growth is bringing “energy security, economic stability and competitiveness” closer together, said Thomas Loffler, executive vice president at organiser dmg events. Demand for exhibition space has prompted organisers to move the opening ceremony to the Abu Dhabi Energy Centre and expand the exhibition's AI and robotics zone. Confirmed speakers include Suhail Al Mazrouei, Minister of energy and Infrastructure; Katherina Reiche, Germany's Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy; Meg O'Neill, chief executive of BP; Richard Jackson, president and chief executive of Occidental Petroleum; Wael Sawan, chief executive of Shell; and Roland Busch, chief executive of Siemens. Last year's Adipec generated $53 billion in business deals across 49,131 transactions, the first time organisers tracked the value of agreements reached during the event. It also contributed $420 million to Abu Dhabi's hospitality and tourism economy, Mr Loffler said.

title: David Dastmalchian was told to change his surname to succeed in Hollywood
body: Early in David Dastmalchian’s screen career, one Chicago casting director saw two possibilities for him: a cab driver or a terrorist. The American actor, whose father was Iranian, had been playing a much wider range of characters on stage to that point, but the auditions coming his way offered little opportunity to do the same on camera. “I remember in the beginning of my career being told, ‘You’re gonna have to change your last name,’” Dastmalchian tells The National . But despite needing the work, he resisted racial typecasting again and again. “I don’t want to do that. I want to be able to go after every role that I could possibly swing for,” he continues. Nearly two decades after his film debut, Dastmalchian has become one of Hollywood's most versatile performers. In his latest starring role, he plays M Bison in director Kitao Sakurai’s new Street Fighter adaptation . The villain joins a career spanning superhero films, science fiction and horror, all under the surname he was advised to change. Set in 1993, the film follows estranged fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo), who are recruited by Chun-Li (Callina Liang) for the World Warrior Tournament. Behind the competition is a conspiracy that draws them back into conflict. Dastmalchian's route into that career began with director Christopher Nolan’s The Dark Knight , released in 2008, in which he played one of the Joker’s accomplices. Casting director John Papsidera brought him in to audition for what would become his film debut. “And thank God for John Papsidera, who came into Chicago and he was casting a movie, and he was willing to see everybody,” Dastmalchian says. “And he saw me as something that other people hadn’t given me a chance to do on camera. “On the stage I always felt like I had an opportunity to swing for the fences with all different types of roles.” Even appearing in one of the biggest films of the decade did not guarantee steady work. In an interview with Backstage , Dastmalchian recalled arriving in Los Angeles without an agent or manager. Despite having The Dark Knight on his CV, he was turned down by the small agencies and management companies he approached. “It was devastatingly humbling to continue to be told, ‘No, we don’t want to work with you,’” he said. He continued auditioning for short films and music videos and attending casting workshops. Few of those auditions produced jobs, but they introduced him to people and helped him build the professional relationships on which his career would come to depend. Nolan later cast him again in Oppenheimer , while director Denis Villeneuve championed his work in the meantime, casting him in Prisoners , Blade Runner 2049 and Dune . Dastmalchian also took a leading role in the Abu Dhabi-produced runaway hit Late Night with the Devil , playing Jack Delroy, a television host whose Halloween broadcast spirals out of control. “I swim in such a giant pool of gratitude, honestly, because it was the people who were willing to see me and see the potential for what’s the human underneath, right?” he says. “That’s the story that you’re always trying to tell.” The actor recognises that nationality and ancestry can be central to how a character is written and performed. His objection, however, is to those factors limiting the roles an actor is allowed to pursue. Having found people willing to give him that freedom, he wants others to have the same opportunities. “I want everybody out there who’s an actor that feels like they want a chance to embrace the art, no matter what they look like, where they’re from, where their parents are from, what language they were raised speaking, to know that all the things we’re dealing with in acting are universal.” Street Fighter is in cinemas now across the Middle East

title: 32nd CJN Sports Competition Begins Friday in Kaduna
body: Alex Enumah in Abuja The 32nd edition of the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) Sports Competition to be hosted by Kaduna State will begin from October 16, the National Sports Association for Judiciary (NASAJ) has announced. NASAJ, in a statement, noted that the competition which will run through October 29, will be officially opened on Saturday, October 17, 2026. The association observed that the Chief Justice of Nigeria Sports Competition has evolved into one of the most anticipated annual events within the Nigerian Judiciary. “Beyond its role as a sporting festival, it serves as a unique platform for fostering unity, friendship, physical fitness, mental well-being, and professional camaraderie among judicial officers and judiciary staff across the federation. The competition also provides participants with an opportunity to showcase their sporting talents and creativity while strengthening the bonds that unite the judicial family,” the statement read in part. NASAJ disclosed that each year, the tournament brings together participants from courts and judicial institutions nationwide in an atmosphere of healthy competition, teamwork, mutual respect and fellowship, adding that through sport, the competition continues to reinforce the enduring values of discipline, integrity, fairness, excellence and professionalism that are the hallmarks of the judiciary. The association, which described the successful hosting of the 31st edition in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, as a significant milestone in the history of the games, expressed gratitude to the Almighty God for the success recorded and expresses its profound appreciation to the Government and people of Akwa Ibom State, the Akwa Ibom State Judiciary, and all stakeholders whose hospitality, support and contributions made the event a resounding success. “This year’s edition promises to be one of the most exciting and memorable in the history of the competition. Participants will compete in a wide range of sporting events, including football, volleyball, handball, lawn tennis, table tennis, badminton, swimming, athletics, scrabble, chess, ayo and other recreational activities. These events are designed to encourage broad participation, strengthen institutional relationships, and promote a healthy work-life balance among members of the judiciary,” the statement added. Meanwhile, NASAJ expressed profound gratitude to the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, for her unwavering support and commitment to the advancement of sports within the judiciary, stating that her visionary leadership and steadfast encouragement continue to inspire initiatives that enhance the welfare, unity, productivity and overall well-being of judicial officers and staff through sporting activities. The association also commended the Governor of Kaduna State, Senator Uba Sani, the Government and people of Kaduna State, the Kaduna State Judiciary, the Local Organising Committee, and all stakeholders involved in the preparations for their dedication and commitment towards delivering a successful and memorable tournament. “As preparations enter their final stages, NASAJ warmly invites members of the media, corporate organisations, development partners, stakeholders, and the general public to support and participate in this unique gathering of the Nigerian Judiciary. Beyond celebrating sporting excellence, the competition will further strengthen the bonds of unity, friendship, cooperation, and understanding that are essential to the effective administration of justice in Nigeria. “NASAJ looks forward to welcoming participants and guests from across the country to Kaduna State for what promises to be an outstanding celebration of sportsmanship, fellowship, wellness, and judicial excellence,” the statement read.

title: Judge watches suspects’ confession video recording in Arise TV journalist murder case
body:
Judge Mohammed Idris of the FCT High Court in Jabi , Abuja, on Wednesday, watched a confessional video recording of suspects involved in the last year September’s armed robbery that claimed the lives of Arise News Television journalist Somtochukwu Maduagwu and her residence’s security guard.
The prosecution presented the video recording, which captured the police interrogation sessions of the 11 defendants facing charges in the case.
However, only about the first 20 minutes of the video was played back, showing only two of the defendants taking turns to give their oral statements.
The playback was stopped after the defence lawyer requested it to be discontinued to save the court’s time.
Ms Maduagwu was killed alongside security guard Barnabas Danlami during the armed robbery attack on her Unique Apartments residence in Katampe, Abuja, on 5 September 2025.
In January, the police arraigned 11 suspects linked to the robbery. They include Shamsu Hassan, Sani Sirajo, Hassan Isah, Abubakar Alkamu, Abdulsalam Saleh, and Suleiman Badamasi.
The rest are Zaharadeen Mohammed, Musa Umar, Mashkur Jamil, Suleiman Sani, and Abubakar Usman.
They all pleaded not guilty to nine counts of criminal conspiracy, armed robbery and murder.
The judge, Mr Idris, subsequently remanded them in the Kuje Correctional Centre in Abuja, from where they have been standing trial.
The police’s prosecution lawyer, Adama Musa, tendered on Thursday the video recording of the suspects’ interrogation.
The recording was tendered through Douglas Ishaku, an assistant superintendent of police who appeared as the fourth prosecution witness.
Mr Ishaku told the court that he recorded the suspects’ confessional statements and asked them questions in Hausa, and translated the questions to English. He said he also translated the suspects’ Hausa responses to English.
After admitting the recording as an exhibit, the judge granted the prosecution’s request for its playback.
The judge, sourrounded by the prosecution and defence lawyers watched the video on a laptop facing them, while the court audience listened to the audio.
In the video clip, the first defendant, Mr Hassan, confirmed that he was aware that he was being investigated for armed robbery.
He also named other gang members allegedly at the scene of the crime, including Sani, Abba, Kabari (said to be at large), and Nura. He said they used knives and guns during the operation.
He confirmed shooting the security guard at the house when he tried to overpower one of the gang members. But he said he was not aware that the guard later died. He said a lady jumped down from the building, as a result of the gunshot.
Mr Hassan was also captured in the video clip as saying that the gang carted away items, including a car. He took N200,000 as his own share of the proceeds, the defendant said.
For Mr Sirajo, the second defendant, he confirmed in the video recording being the driver of the car that transported the gang members to Unique Apartment.
He said one of the co-defendants, Mr Suleiman, provided the car, which he picked from Area 1 in Abuja.
He said after fuelling the car, he drove to Sauka to pick up Abba before proceeding to Madalla to fetch Mr Kabari and Mr Hassan. He said he also picked Isah and Nura from Kubwa.
The second defendant also said Mr Kabari gave him instructions and directions guide to the target location in Katampe. He said while Messrs Hassan and Kabari held guns, Mr Isah and Nura held machetes, and Abba held a knife.
On arrival at Unique Apartments, the defendant said he parked the car and was observing the robbery when he heard a gunshot.
At this point, the lawyers for the 11 defendants agreed that they had seen enough of the video.
The prosecution closed Mr Ishaku’s examination-in-chief.
Four lawyers for the first to sixth defendants cross-examined Mr Ishaku on the procedure followed in taking the confessional statements.
A.B. Samson, the first defendant’s lawyer, asked about the dates the written and the video-recorded statements were taken but the witness said he could not recall.
Mr Samson, who fielded questions that sought to examine compliance by the police with the safeguards provided for in the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA), also confirmed that lawyers or relatives of the suspects were not present during the recording of the suspects’ statements.
The witness, also confirmed that the robbery victims could not identify the defendants.
In September, the witness told the court that the second defendant was arrested at a hospital in Gosa-Toge in Abuja where he was receiving treatment.
But on Wednesday, Mr Ishaku, fielding cross-examination questions from the second defendant’s lawyer, William Otabor, said he could not recall the name of the hospital or a staff member of the hospital he spoke to. But he said he knew the ailment the defendant was receiving treament for, although he ommitted the information in his own witness statement.
Mr Ishaku said he did not find the gadgets stolen from the robbery scene on the defendant when he was arrested. However, when storing the recovered gun that the defendant led them to, he did not go with the keeper to the police exhibit room.
The third defendant’s lawyer, E. I Onoja, adopted the cross-examination by first and second defendant’s lawyers.
Responding to questions from the fourth to the sixth defendants’ lawyer, Ojonomi Apeh, the witness confirmed that the fifth defendant denied participating in the robbery but that his denial was found to be baseless. He said investigation showed that the fifth defendant was part of the robbery gang.
The judge adjourned proceedings until 9 December for the continuation of the cross-examination by Mr Apeh.
In September, Mr Ishaku told the court that Ms Maduagwu, the Arise News journalist, was pushed over a three-storey building by a member of the robbery gang and that one of the robbers shot the security guard, Mr Danlami, during the 29 September 2025 robbery attack.
Earlier in April, Maxwell Eje, an assistant suprintendent of police, narrated how the police arrested the suspected armed robbers and recovered some of their weapons.
Mr Eje said an English double-barrelled gun and an AK-47 used by the assailants were recovered following the confession of a suspect.
During earlier proceedings in February, two witnesses, Sani Yusuf and Fatou Toborteh, who were Ms Maduagwu’s neighbours at the Unique Apartment, Katampe, took turns to testify about the incident.
In their separate testimonies, they said they heard female screams on the night of the incident.
The two witnesses, who were robbed that night, recalled seeing Ms Maduagwu’s body with a serious head injury. They said she was later confirmed dead at the hospital.
However, they said they could not identify any of the defendants because the robbers were masked on the night of the robbery.

title: Abu Dhabi F1 Grand Prix: 'Unprecedented demand' and preparations on track with 50 days to go
body: Planning for the 2026 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix “never stopped for one day”, according to Saif Al Noaimi, chief executive of organisers Ethara. The F1 season finale is now 50 days away, and preparations for the race have clicked up a gear at Yas Marina Circuit. Eleven artists, including Andrea Bocelli, Lewis Capaldi and The Script, have been booked for the after-race concerts, with the final headline act set to be announced next week. Doubts were raised earlier this year when the Grands Prix in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were cancelled because of the Iran war. However, F1 president Stefano Domenicali has said they intend to finish the season as planned, with “everything confirmed for [us to stay in] Qatar and Abu Dhabi”. The season finale will take place in the UAE capital from December 3-6, and Al Noaimi spoke to The National at Yas Marina Circuit as the days tick down to the 18th Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. Q: Given some of the speculation we have seen about the race, what assurances can you give about the 2026 event? A: We are delivering the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix at the same high standard we deliver every year. We are delivering a safe event, just like we do every year. We are planning and preparing ourselves just like we do every year. And from a readiness point of view, we are 100 per cent ready to deliver the Grand Prix this year. Everything is on schedule, the date has not changed. We're really excited to be hosting the season finale on December 6. Q: You are used to seeing a rise in demand every year, so how have ticket sales been this year? We are 50 days away from the Grand Prix, and if you compare where we were last year, 50 days away, we're actually ahead in terms of ticket volume and sales. So, demand is unprecedented. We are fortunate our customers know they're going to come because it's such an important event. Every year, early on, as soon as we go on sale, we see a huge spike in sales. And, you know, the last few weeks we've seen a spike in international sales also. So, interest in inbound tourism is growing, and we're starting to see that in the sales numbers. Q: Considering what happened with the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia Grands Prix, was there ever a fear that this wasn't going to go ahead? To be honest, we haven't stopped planning for the 2026 Grand Prix for one day. We've been full speed ahead since the beginning of the year. Since we delivered the Grand Prix last year, we've been completely full speed ahead. Obviously, being the last race of the season, early on in the year, we were in the planning period and the planning phase. September is when we start to see the venue transform and the build start. But this is our schedule every single year. We haven't had to make any changes to the planning and the execution. Q: Can you give a message to fans thinking about buying a ticket? Come and see Abu Dhabi, come and visit Abu Dhabi. We are seeing a huge growth in international visitations over the last few months. As you can see, everything's functioning normally over here. It's an exciting time to be here. And yeah, we're very, very happy to start welcoming the world back. Q: Are you a little bit worried that Kimi Antonelli is going to win the title before we get to Abu Dhabi? It was very fun last year … It was fun last year; we had the three-way fight. I mean, look, we can't have a three-way fight every year. But what I can assure you is these guys are going to fight till the chequered flag in Abu Dhabi, regardless of the championship. It's great to see someone young like Kimi taking that position. But also, like I said earlier, you can't write off the championship yet. You have Max Verstappen winning the last two races out of nowhere. Six different drivers have won races in 2026. So, regardless, it's still going to be an exciting race. ADGP 2025 – in pictures Q: Can you talk about the enhancements the venue has undergone this year? So, we are upping the capacity for the event this year. We have unprecedented demand. We are expanding our Paddock Club (hospitality) offering. We already have the biggest Paddock Club, but we're actually increasing it to surpass 12,000 in 2026. There's a completely new Paddock Club offering that we're building on the west side also. And, you know, every year we look at additions and enhancements. We have a few new exciting products that we have launched already for 2026. And, you know, from a hospitality point of view, we have 16/360 (hospitality) expanding. We launched it last year for the first time, and we're making some additions to that product, which has been very, very popular. And then, in terms of other branded hospitality offerings, we announced our partnership with Nammos at Turn 9. And then we have a few other new branded hospitality experiences that we're launching this year. Q: Today we heard that Rashid Al Dhaheri will race in F3 next season. How long until we see him here? It's really exciting having Rashid and Keanu [Al Azhari] now both representing the UAE in the FIA Formula 3 championship. It really shows how strong our grassroots motorsports programme and our academy are. Both of them came through the Yas Heat Academy. They both raced in Formula Four UAE for Yas Heat. They're both Yas Heat ambassadors. And today they're both participating in the FIA Formula 3 World Championship. It's a huge, huge achievement for us. Huge achievement for them and for their families, who have dedicated so much over the years. And look, it's very, very promising, you know, maybe one or hopefully both of them could be in Formula One in as little as two years. So we're excited to see that. Congratulations to them.

title: APEN Plans Homegrown AI Model for Nigerian Classrooms
body: Funmi Ogundare The Association of Private Educators in Nigeria (APEN) has unveiled plans to develop a contextualised Artificial Intelligence (AI) model tailored to Nigeria’s socio-cultural realities and educational needs, as more than 300 delegates have registered for its forthcoming 16th annual conference. The association said the initiative was aimed at ensuring that AI adoption in Nigerian classrooms preserved local values, cultural identity and ethical standards while equipping learners with the skills required to compete globally. The conference, themed: ‘Human First: Leading with Purpose in the Age of AI’, is scheduled to hold in November 2 and 3, at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos. Briefing journalists on Wednesday, the Chairperson of the Planning Committee, Mrs. Bolanle Adewole, said excessive reliance on foreign AI models could produce educational content that failed to reflect Nigeria’s realities. She said APEN was exploring the development of its own AI engine that would enable schools to access tools and resources relevant to the country’s educational environment. “AI has not come to kill education; on the contrary, it has come to enhance and support it by promoting innovation, sustainability, and efficiency,” Adewole stated. She, however, cautioned against unrestricted adoption of the technology, stressing the need for locally developed models that reflected Nigerian experiences rather than generating outputs primarily suited for Europe and other parts of the world. The conference, according to Adewole, is expected to attract school proprietors, administrators, teachers, parents and international education partners from 14 states in Nigeria and parts of East Africa. “Although the event was initially projected to attract 350 participants, more than 300 delegates had confirmed their attendance weeks before the conference,” she said, expressing optimism that participation would exceed the target and approach the venue’s capacity of 600. The conference, she noted, has also secured the support of more than eight corporate sponsors, including several returning partners. A member of APEN’s Board of Trustees, Mrs. Olufunke Fowler-Amba, said mainstream AI systems were not necessarily designed to accommodate the cultural and educational needs of minority communities and countries such as Nigeria. She stressed the importance of ensuring that Nigerian children retained their cultural identity while acquiring the competencies required in the global marketplace. Fowler-Amba said APEN would continue to provide a unified platform for private educators to engage the government on policies affecting the sector. On the practical application of AI in schools, the association’s Founding Chairman, Mrs. Lai Koiki, said the technology should help reduce teachers’ workloads rather than create fears about job losses. She said AI could ease administrative burdens, improve lesson planning and streamline student assessment, allowing teachers to concentrate more on classroom mentorship and learners’ development. Koiki added: “Structured training would help educators acquire the skills needed to remain competitive internationally while maintaining their central role in the learning process.” She also emphasised APEN’s international engagements, including its relationship with the Council of British International Schools (COBIS) and participation from Kenya and Uganda. Another member of the Board of Trustees, Dr. Femi Ogunsanya, emphasised the importance of effective governance, continuous professional development and engagement with relevant authorities in sustaining private education institutions. She said school proprietors needed to understand how to manage institutional change, recruit qualified teachers and provide regular training as AI continued to reshape education. Ogunsanya added that the Federal Ministry of Education had recognised APEN’s contributions by giving private educators a voice in national education policymaking. The organisers said the conference would feature specialised breakout sessions for school owners, educational leaders, classroom teachers and parents. The sessions are expected to provide practical governance frameworks and guidance for implementing human-centred AI practices in schools from November 4.

title: EU Will Need to Increase Ukraine Funding to Plug Gap: Merz
body:
Germany’s Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Thursday the European Union will have to find more money to finance Ukraine, as Kyiv warns it faces a major budget shortfall next year.
“We must do everything we can to help Ukraine through the winter and also to help next year,” Merz said at the start of a two-day summit of EU leaders in Brussels for crunch budget talks.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We will have to increase the funds again here in order to really assist Ukraine on a lasting basis.”
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky was heading to Brussels to join the meeting on Friday in a bid to rally support amid fresh tension with US President Donald Trump.
The war-torn country is facing a dire winter as Moscow has stepped up bombardments, and relations with Washington have soured after Trump struck a deal with Russia to supply diesel fuel.
The mood has darkened as Ukraine has complained that its battlefield access to the US-provided Starlink satellite communications system has been hampered.
EU leaders have thrown their support behind Zelensky.
“We stand shoulder to shoulder with the Ukrainians, and they have to do whatever is necessary to protect the Ukrainian people,” Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said.
“Let’s step up our game and make sure that they can win this senseless war.”
Others backed Ukraine’s right to target Russian refineries despite pressure from the United States to stop hitting Moscow’s oil production.
“The faster all the Russian refineries and ability to sell energy will be blown to smithereens the better,” said Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal.
EU leaders are set to open discussions about how to keep Ukraine afloat next year in the face of a growing realisation that funds will run dry.
The EU has in place a 90-billion-euro ($101-billion) loan for Kyiv that was set to help cover funding to the end of 2027.
But the Ukrainian authorities have warned they will need tens of billions more as Russia’s strikes have battered the country’s economy.
The European Commission has said it is working with Kyiv to get a definitive figure for what is needed next year.
The talks around the new funding have reignited calls for the European Union to tap around 200 billion euros in frozen Russian central bank assets to fund Ukraine.
But there seems little momentum on that front as Belgium, where most of the funds are held, remains opposed.
Merz pushed back against any attempt by the United States to try to get Europe to hand over some of the money as part of Washington’s peace negotiations with Moscow.
“These are assets that are frozen in Europe, and they should remain frozen in Europe. This is our business, and we will decide on it,” he said.

title: Russia cautions NATO, EU against attempts to isolate Kaliningrad Region — diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. NATO and the European Union know full well what will happen if they try to isolate Russia’s Kaliningrad Region, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko told reporters on Thursday.
"Our position is well known, and corresponding signals have been communicated to both NATO and the EU, and they are aware of consequences that any attempts to isolate the Kaliningrad Region or disrupt essential supplies to it may entail," the diplomat noted.
Grushko refused to provide an analysis of statements from Estonian officials, especially those responsible for defense. "They have already made a number of statements that it is hard to comment on in political terms," he noted.
Earlier, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal announced plans to initiate the decommissioning of a natural gas pipeline passing through the republic that serves as a backup transit route to Russia's Baltic exclave.
Russian officials have repeatedly stressed that any attempts to isolate the region may trigger a major response.

title: Edo to Inaugurate 100mw CCETC Power Plant December
body: Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City The Edo State Government is looking forward to the inauguration of the 100-megawatt CCETC independent power plant in Ologbo, Benin, which it hopes will add 100 megawatts power to electricity generation in the state. The inauguration date is set for December 2026. Commissioner for Power, Paul Usenbo, disclosed this during an inspection of the facility, where he assessed construction progress, equipment installation and preparations for testing and inauguration. Usenbo said the inspection was aimed at establishing clear implementation timelines and verifying the project’s progress against the state government’s target of delivering additional power generation capacity before the end of the year. He said the inspection also covered the Tahur Industrial Park and its associated 300-metric-tonne energy facility in Ologbo, with the government engaging developers to establish measurable timelines for completing the projects. According to the commissioner, the projects are part of the government’s broader strategy to increase electricity generation and improve power supply across Edo State’s three senatorial districts. He said the government was committed to ensuring that the projects delivered tangible benefits to residents and businesses, adding that Governor Monday Okpebholo had continued to prioritise initiatives aimed at expanding electricity access across the state. Usenbo said the projects had met their second-quarter implementation timelines, expressing optimism about progress towards the government’s inauguration target. Speaking during the visit, the Marketing Manager, CCETC, Eric Ju, thanked the state government for its continued support and cooperation. He disclosed that the company had completed the construction and installation of 46 megawatts of generation capacity and planned to commence power supply by the end of 2026. Ju added that the company would continue working towards the completion of subsequent phases of the project, with the objective of providing more stable electricity and supporting economic activities in Edo State

title: Central Asia Economic Growth Expected to Slow in 2027
body: After several years of rapid expansion, Central Asian economies are expected to lose some momentum. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) forecasts that regional economic growth will slow from 5.8% in 2026 to 5.3% in 2027. However, growth in manufacturing and construction will not necessarily translate into comparable increases in household incomes. The forecast appears in the EBRD’s September report . The bank’s Central Asia figures also include Mongolia, so the regional growth rate should not be interpreted as an average for the five Central Asian countries alone. The Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development (EFSD) has published its own projections for Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan. They differ somewhat from the EBRD’s forecasts but also anticipate continued economic growth. Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan Maintain Strong Growth The EBRD expects the economies of Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan to grow by 7% in 2027, the highest rates projected for the five countries in the region. Kyrgyzstan has experienced a construction boom in recent years, driven by investment in roads, housing, and energy infrastructure. The service sector is also expanding. The country’s economy grew by 11.9% in the first half of 2026. However, rapid growth has been accompanied by rising food and fuel prices. The country’s performance is closely tied to economic conditions in Russia, where a significant number of Kyrgyz migrant workers are employed and from which Kyrgyzstan imports the vast majority of its fuel. Changes in the Russian labor market can affect remittances and household spending in Kyrgyzstan. In Tajikistan, growth is supported by investment and exports, particularly precious metals and mineral resources. The economy expanded by 8.2% in the first half of 2026. Tajikistan also relies heavily on imported goods and equipment, with spending on imports exceeding export earnings. Remittances from migrant workers in Russia are an even more important source of household income for Tajiks than for their Kyrgyz neighbors, while rising fuel costs are putting additional pressure on family budgets. Kazakhstan Remains Dependent on Oil Exports For Central Asia’s largest economy, the EBRD forecasts growth of 4.5% in 2027, while the Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development expects 5%. In 2026, Kazakhstan’s economy has been constrained by disruptions to oil production and exports. Problems arose at the Tengiz oil field and along the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) export route, through which a significant share of Kazakhstan’s oil reaches global markets via Russia. Meanwhile, Kazakhstan’s factories increased production. But even growth in industries outside the oil sector has yet to eliminate the country’s dependence on commodity exports. For international buyers, the reliability of supply routes is also important. Disruptions to the CPC can restrict Kazakhstan’s oil exports regardless of demand or global prices. The Times of Central Asia recently examined the challenges facing Kazakhstan’s oil logistics. Inflation is another concern. According to the EFSD, prices in Kazakhstan are expected to rise by approximately 9.5% by the end of 2026. This means economic expansion will not necessarily be accompanied by a noticeable improvement in household purchasing power. Uzbekistan’s Growth Driven by Domestic Demand The EBRD has raised its 2026 growth forecast for Uzbekistan to 7.5% and expects the economy to expand by 6% in 2027. Uzbekistan’s economy receives substantial support from domestic consumption. The country has a population of more than 38 million, larger than that of any other Central Asian state. Growing demand for goods, housing, and services supports local businesses and attracts foreign companies. For international investors, Uzbekistan is attractive not only as a manufacturing location but also as a large consumer market. However, further expansion in trade and services will depend on household incomes, borrowing costs, and the prices of imported goods. Turkmenistan Remains the Region’s Least Transparent Economy The EBRD forecasts that Turkmenistan’s economy will grow by 6.3% in both 2026 and 2027. The bank identifies construction, services, and public investment as the main drivers of growth. However, assessing the country’s actual economic conditions is more difficult than in neighboring states. Turkmenistan publishes limited data on private businesses, household incomes, and individual sectors of the economy. As a result, official figures do not provide a complete picture of economic developments. How External Markets Could Affect Central Asia The EBRD warns of risks associated with fuel supplies from Russia, potential disruptions to trade routes, and declining global commodity prices. Kazakhstan is particularly sensitive to oil prices and the operation of export pipelines. Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan depend on trade with Russia, the cost of imported goods, and migrant workers’ earnings. Uzbekistan relies more heavily on domestic demand but also remains connected to external markets.

title: Almost half of Britons unwilling to take up arms in wartime, poll shows
body:
LONDON, October 15. /TASS/. Almost half of Britons would refuse to take up arms in the event of war, according to an Ipsos opinion poll.
"Nearly one in two Britons (48%) state there are no circumstances where they would be willing to take up arms and go to war for Britain, compared to 36% who say there are circumstances where they would," the pollster said.
According to Ipsos, the figures have changed little since August 2025, despite repeated statements by government officials about alleged security risks facing the United Kingdom.
Meanwhile, 51% of respondents believe the country’s defense spending should be increased, marking a significant rise from June 2022, when 28% of those polled shared that view.
The poll surveyed 1,090 British adults from September 29 to October 1.

title: Kazakhstan Arrests Russian Rapper Navai on Drug Smuggling Charges
body:
A court in Kazakhstan has reportedly placed popular Russian hip-hop artist Navai in pre-trial detention after border authorities arrested him on suspicion of drug smuggling.
Navai Bakirov, 31, was detained on Tuesday at a border checkpoint while attempting to cross into Kazakhstan from neighboring Kyrgyzstan.
The Korday District Court ordered Bakirov to be placed in pre-trial detention for two months, Telegram news channel Baza reported on Thursday.
According to the report, Bakirov had allegedly admitted during police questioning to purchasing the drugs in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek, where he performed on Monday.
Baza, which is purported to have links to Russia’s security services, claimed Kazakh border guards uncovered 2.5 grams of marijuana in Bakirov’s vehicle after being alerted by a sniffer dog.
Bakirov’s arrest led to the cancellation of his concert in Astana on Wednesday. His show in Chisinau, Moldova, was rescheduled from this Friday to Dec. 8.
The Samara native rose to prominence across the post-Soviet space as part of the hit-making duo HammAli & Navai before launching a solo career.
Bakirov’s legal trouble in Central Asia comes nearly one month after he resolved a separate civil dispute in Moscow by compensating the city for damages caused when he crashed his Ferrari in central Moscow in May.

title: CAS rejects Russian Curling Federation’s appeal to lift suspension
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. The Court of Arbitration for Sport has rejected the Russian Curling Federation's and athletes' appeals against the decision to extend the suspension of Russian national teams from international competitions, the CAS press service told TASS.
According to it, both appeals filed by the Russian Curling Federation and Russian athletes on the participation in international competitions were rejected in a final decision issued on October 13.
In turn, Sports Minister and Russian Olympic Committee President Mikhail Degtyarev announced that the ROC and the Russian Curling Federation are preparing an appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court against the CAS decision.
On August 11, World Curling extended the suspension of Russian athletes through the end of 2026. The organization stated that it decided to extend the suspension after reviewing the International Olympic Committee's (IOC) recommendations, as well as feedback from its members and competition organizers.
Russia’s national curling teams have been suspended from international tournaments since 2022 due to the situation in Ukraine. However, in January 2026, Russia’s junior national teams were permitted to participate in international tournaments while displaying national symbols. In July, the IOC reinstated the ROC's membership and recommended that international federations lift restrictions on Russian athletes, including those in team competitions.

title: CIS defense chiefs sign off on joint action plan for 2027
body:
BISHKEK, October 15. /TASS/. Defense ministers from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) signed an action plan for 2027 at a meeting of the CIS Council of Defense Ministers in Kyrgyzstan’s Cholpon-Ata, the Kyrgyz Defense Ministry said in a statement.
"Following a [CIS] Defense Ministers’ Council meeting, agreed documents reflecting the results of work in 2026 and an action plan for the CIS Council of Defense Ministers for 2027 were signed," the statement reads.
Participants in the meeting also heard reports from their counterparts, including on the organization of combat training in the Belarusian Armed Forces, the organization of combat training in the Russian Army, taking the experience of the special military operation into account, the holding of exercises by the Armed Forces of Tajikistan, and the experience of taking part in UN peacekeeping missions by the Kazakh Army.
"The meeting discussed the practical use of unmanned systems and robotic complexes in solving the tasks of engineering support in present-day combat and the experience of the combat use of unmanned aerial vehicles in offensive and defensive operations," according to the statement.
Also, the meeting discussed the organization of operational and combat training for CIS troops "for the provision of collective security."
The meeting in Cholpon-Ata was attended by defense chiefs from Russia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan as well as CIS Secretariat officials.

title: Ukrposhta plans to install 32 more indoor parcel lockers, additional modules in 38 branches by Nov 1
body:
National postal operator Ukrposhta JSC has announced the installation of 601 indoor parcel lockers and plans to install another 32 by November 1, along with additional compartment modules in 38 branches.
"Almost 8 out of 10 shipments are already picked up independently by customers. This demonstrates the demand for fast parcel collection without operator assistance and explains the company's decision to continue expanding the network," the company said in a press release on Thursday.
The network will be developed in stages; currently, the largest number of such parcel lockers operates in the Kyiv region (159), Lviv region (68), Dnipropetrovsk region (67), Odesa region (42), and Kharkiv region (40).
The company also plans to expand the capacity of existing parcel lockers by adding an extra module to 33-compartment lockers, thereby increasing the number of compartments to 67.
"This will make it possible to issue more parcels without installing a separate device and will reduce the workload on branch operators," Ukrposhta explained.
The national postal operator noted that indoor parcel lockers are located directly inside the company's branches and are accessible according to their operating hours.
Separately, Ukrposhta recalled the rollout of its outdoor parcel locker network, aiming to expand their number to 1,000 by the end of the year.
As reported, in the first half of this year, Ukrposhta increased its revenue by 4.2% to UAH 6.776 billion and posted a net profit of UAH 92 million, compared to a net loss of UAH 312 million in the first half of last year.
The national postal operator has 7,200 customer service locations, including 2,000 mobile post offices serving 21,300 settlements. The average headcount of the national postal operator for the second quarter of 2026 is 25,800 employees, and the average salary is UAH 20,300.

title: Abu Dhabi shuts down cafe over repeated food safety violations
body: An Abu Dhabi cafe has been temporarily shut down for repeated food safety violations that posed a public health risk . Let's Talk Riz Corner Cafe's licence was suspended by the emirate's food regulator after it failed to take effective corrective action over the issues. The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority said it had intervened immediately to protect food safety and consumer health. The closure will continue until the outlet addresses the violations and receives approval to resume trading, the authority added. The closure is part of the authority's work to strengthen Abu Dhabi's food safety system. Food regulators regularly inspect cafes , restaurants and products to ensure compliance with safety standards. The authority urged residents to report any violations they notice in cafes, restaurants or grocery stores, including suspected food contamination, by calling the Abu Dhabi Government’s toll-free number 800555.

title: Law Reform Conference Seeks More Powers For States, LGs
body: Participants at the maiden Conference of All Law Reform Commissions in Nigeria have called for comprehensive reforms of the country’s legislative framework to address structural imbalances in federalism, strengthen local government autonomy and devolve more powers to states. The participants also advocated fiscal federalism, a review of the Exclusive Legislative List in favour of states and full judicial federalism as part of measures to strengthen Nigeria’s democratic institutions. These recommendations were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the two-day conference, hosted by the Edo State Law Reform Commission at the John Odigie Oyegun Public Service Academy, Benin City, from September 28 to 29, 2026. The conference, which had as its theme, ‘Consolidating Nigeria’s Democracy through Law Reform: Charting the Way Forward,’ featured an opening address by Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, while the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice (AGF), Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), was represented by Otunba Wale Fapohunda (SAN) who delivered the keynote address. On national security and human rights, the participants stressed the need to strike a balance between safeguarding the country and protecting the fundamental rights of citizens. They maintained that executive measures taken in the interest of national security must remain subject to judicial scrutiny, while urging civil society organisations to remain vigilant against human rights abuses perpetrated under the guise of security operations. The conference also called for a coherent national intelligence-sharing system anchored on clearly defined mandates, inter-agency cooperation, accountability and digital readiness to strengthen the country’s response to security challenges. It further advocated reforms to police investigation procedures in line with international best practices, alongside measures to enhance accountability within law enforcement agencies. On local government administration, the participants called for reforms to enable councils to discharge their constitutional responsibilities and exercise the autonomy affirmed by the Supreme Court. They also emphasised the need for effective mechanisms to ensure that increased allocations to local governments translate into improved infrastructure and the provision of essential services, including healthcare, food and shelter. The communiqué noted that financial autonomy at the grassroots level must deliver tangible benefits to citizens, rather than remain a constitutional provision without corresponding improvements in service delivery. The participants further called for adequate and sustainable funding, qualified personnel and modern infrastructure for law reform commissions across the country. They argued that the effectiveness of the commissions would remain limited without the necessary institutional support to conduct research, review existing laws and recommend reforms that reflect contemporary realities. To address delays in implementing their recommendations, the conference proposed a legal framework compelling the legislative and executive arms of government to consider and act on reports submitted by law reform commissions within specified time frames. The participants warned that failure by relevant authorities to act on such recommendations undermines the objectives of law reform and limits its potential impact on governance and national development. On electoral matters, the conference advocated reforms to ensure that pre-election and post-election disputes are resolved before elections or inauguration, where applicable. According to the communiqué, such measures would help reduce prolonged litigation, promote certainty in the electoral process and ensure that electoral outcomes reflect the will of voters. The participants also called for a comprehensive review of Nigeria’s tertiary education curriculum to incorporate emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and robotics, in response to developments associated with the Fifth Industrial Revolution. At the end of the conference, the Chairman of the Edo State Law Reform Commission, Hon. Osikhena-Boih Donald, was appointed Pro Tem Chairman of the Forum of State Law Reform Commissions in Nigeria. The communiqué was jointly signed by Prof. Inegbedion, Chairman of the Communiqué Drafting Committee; Donald; and the Edo State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Prof. Roland Otaru (SAN).

title: After booting 760K off ACA health plans, the Trump administration adds some people back
body:
The anti-fraud moves affect people in the states that use Healthcare.gov to buy Affordable Care Act health insurance. Not all of the 760,000 people disenrolled are "phantoms," as the government has claimed. Stefani Reynolds/Bloomberg via Getty Images hide caption
Late last month, the Trump administration announced that it had cut 760,000 people from the Affordable Care Act rolls, claiming fraud and improper enrollments and touting billions in potential taxpayer savings .
Check out the NPR Politics Podcast for daily analysis of the biggest news out of Washington, D.C.
Not all of those kicked off were fraudulently enrolled, KFF Health News has learned. Insurance industry sources said the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has reinstated a small number of people whose coverage should not have been canceled. More could follow in the coming weeks if enrollees discover they are uninsured when they go to use their coverage.
Still, the sweep was long overdue, say supporters such as Brian Blase, whose Paragon Health Institute has supplied many of the sometimes controversial findings cited by those who allege widespread enrollment fraud in the ACA. But other policy experts question how many legitimate consumers were caught in the dragnet, perhaps because they failed to open a letter from their insurer or answer a phone call.
Questions continue to swirl, even as a second phase of the anti-fraud effort is underway. An additional 419,000 sign-ups are being scrutinized. Insurers must let CMS know how many of those enrollees don't respond to outreach efforts by "around mid-to-late November, after the midterm elections," said David Merritt, senior vice president of external affairs at the Blue Cross Blue Shield Association.
He confirmed that some BCBS members are among those who have been reinstated. He also said that CMS has an expedited review process for those who discover they have been improperly disenrolled.
Overall, however, the administration is providing few details about the cancellations, such as how robust the outreach was to those it targeted, how long it takes for people to get reinstated after discovering their coverage was wrongly canceled, and how many such cancellations have been reversed.
"It may be true that some of those enrollments were not authorized, but it can be equally true that people got lost in the shuffle and have a valid enrollment. Without more information, it's almost impossible to tell," said Katie Keith , a director of the Center for Health Policy and the Law at Georgetown Law. "That they are not being very transparent is telling too," she said of the administration.
The enrollment cut comes as part of a larger Republican strategy to focus on fraud in government programs, including Medicaid and hospice care , which polls show resonates with GOP voters.
At an Oct. 14 press conference, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz touted the removal this year of subsidies for about 189,000 ACA enrollees with duplicate Medicare, Medicaid, or Children's Health Insurance Program coverage, citing not fraud but a failure to look for concurrent enrollments or continued coverage for dead people. They credited an effort begun last year by the Trump administration to restore more frequent data matching checks than were done under the prior administration.
Unauthorized sign-ups by rogue insurance agents seeking commissions and other potential impropriety in the ACA marketplace — applicants' providing incorrect income estimates, for example — has been a concern for several years , with much debate over the magnitude of the problem.
Even so, how the move will play out politically is uncertain. Healthcare costs are tied with gas prices as a top concern for voters. It is likely that many removed from the ACA are in red states, such as Texas, Florida, Louisiana, and Mississippi. Those areas saw rapid growth in ACA enrollment from 2020 to 2025, driven in part by now-expired enhanced subsidies put in place during Joe Biden's presidency. Additionally, the cancellations target only states that use Healthcare.gov, the federal ACA marketplace. The 21 states fully running their own marketplaces generally have more robust fraud prevention programs and have reported few or none of the kinds of unauthorized sign-ups plaguing the federal marketplace.
"To the extent there is a reaction depends on whether the government got it wrong, whether people try to get care and then find out their coverage is no longer active," said Adrianna McIntyre, assistant professor of health policy and politics at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.
According to information the agency provided to KFF Health News, CMS in June selected for further review nearly 1.2 million enrollments that had all of what it deemed four warning signs for fraud:
Then, as first reported by KFF Health News, CMS sent lists of those ACA accounts to specific insurers, instructing the carriers to review them and use at least two methods of contact — such as a phone call and a letter — to try to reach the enrollees. Policyholders were given 30 days to respond to the insurers' outreach and provide the missing information. CMS disenrolled those who didn't respond.
Johnny Wallin, chief operating officer of Texas-based Marketplace Insurance Exchange, which helps clients in about 35 states enroll in coverage, said insurers reached out to his organization for help contacting people on the CMS lists, prompting "an all-hands-on-deck" effort by agents to reach clients, some of whom were vacationing overseas.
"Getting them to answer the phone isn't easy," he noted, although he suspects his agents had a better chance of getting a reply than an insurer because their clients are familiar with their phone numbers. Still, they could not reach about 60 of them.
Additionally, his team has been asked by insurers to help contact those targeted in the second phase of CMS' review. A recent case involved a client who needed to upload his new green card after his previous one expired, but language barriers meant that he had to take time off work to come in for agents to help with the process.
CMS would not provide a list of the insurers it contacted, but publicly available documents show that New York-based Oscar Health was one.
In an August earnings call with analysts and investors, CEO Mark Bertolini said the company was reviewing the files and that "there are a number of cases where we've actually had contact " with people on the list. In other words, the company reached enrollees CMS had targeted over fraud concerns.
He did not specify how many it had reached. The company declined to comment for this article because it is in a voluntary "quiet period," when publicly traded companies limit disclosing information before the release of an earnings report.
Still, in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Oscar Health estimated that 250,000 to 300,000 of its members might be disenrolled because of the CMS effort. Nationally, the company had about 3 million members in the second quarter and reported strong profits.
Overall ACA enrollment has declined sharply , falling by nearly 3 million in the first few months of the year, due in large part to the expiration at the end of last year of the enhanced subsidies. The Trump administration has also taken some credit, saying its focus on weeding out improper enrollments and other changes, such as eliminating a special year-round low-income enrollment period, led to the decline.
CMS has also suspended some brokers for improper activity and barred new brokers from enrolling clients in ACA insurance on the federal exchange during the upcoming open enrollment period.
CMS did not respond to requests for data on the reasons it canceled enrollments. What percentage of enrollees were deemed ineligible due to incorrect income reporting or because they had other health coverage, such as through their jobs? How many because their ACA applications lacked immigration documents or Social Security numbers?
"Currently, there is no additional data to share," the agency's press office said.
But people outside the administration have been vocal.
"This was clearly phantom enrollees," said Paragon's Blase. He thinks more than 99% of the cancellations are of zero-premium coverage that people were signed up for by rogue call centers without their knowledge, or for people who don't exist at all.
Blase said the carriers had a big incentive to get hold of the enrollees because they would lose the subsidies they were being paid if the plans were canceled.
And for any people unfairly caught up, Blase and Trump administration officials say all they have to do to be reinstated is call the marketplace and provide their Social Security number or other missing information.
"Everyone has the political incentive for that process to be that easy," Blase said. "We're a month before the election."
But, as prior reporting has shown , it isn't always a quick process to get an ACA plan canceled or reinstated following an unauthorized sign-up or switch, even when a consumer discovers it themselves and reaches out to the marketplace.
Brokers and policy analysts note that some of the factors used to question enrollments — such as a plan's having no claims filed in a year — are not that unusual. Many people, for example, don't visit a doctor or hospital in a given year.
Insurers "want those healthy people in the insurance pool to help bring down the rates," said Ronnell Nolan, president and CEO of Health Agents for America, a trade group for health insurance agents. "We're against fraud, and CMS has allowed a lot of fraud to happen. But we don't want people who just didn't go to the doctor to be canceled."
And even with the outreach required by CMS, not everyone answers phone calls from unknown numbers or opens their mail or emails.
A recent marketing report found an average "open rate" on emails of 28.6%.
Policy experts also note that, while lack of a Social Security number on an ACA application could indicate a fake enrollee, it might also be an oversight, or the number might not be required, like for a child if the person applying is an adult who is not seeking coverage for the child.
"There will be legitimate people who don't have a claim or don't respond to an inquiry from an insurer," said Matthew Fiedler , a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution. "If the goal is to target fraudulent enrollment, what CMS did is better than tossing people at random, but is likely to miss the mark."
KFF Health News is a national newsroom that produces in-depth journalism about health issues and is one of the core operating programs at KFF — the independent source for health policy research, polling, and journalism.
