title: Russian attack on Poltava injures three, damages school, homes and cars
body:
Vitalii Diakivnych, Head of the Poltava Regional Military Administration, reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
All the injured people were hospitalized and are receiving the necessary medical care.
The attack damaged a school building, an apartment block, three private houses, an administrative building and four cars. Efforts to deal with the aftermath of the attack are ongoing.
As Ukrinform reported, a Russian drone exploded near a school in Poltava, injuring one person.

title: Moscow unaware of US attempts to unfreeze its assets in EU — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Moscow is unaware of any attempts by the United States, as described by the Financial Times, to unfreeze Russian assets in Europe by bringing them under its own control, and the credibility of the report remains unconfirmed, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a briefing.
"We know nothing about it," he said when asked about the matter. "According to media reports, these are issues on the agenda of the dialogue between the Americans and the Europeans."
"We do not know how reliable these reports are," the Kremlin spokesman added.
The Financial Times has claimed that the American side took the initiative during the talks in Miami, attempting in this way to facilitate a settlement in Ukraine. However, according to the newspaper, Washington’s negotiators were rebuffed by the EU side.

title: Terrorism: Finnish court reduces Simon Ekpa’s six-year jail term – Report
body:
Finland’s Court of Appeal has reduced Simon Ekpa’s six-year jail term to four years.
PREMIUM TIMES reported that the Päijät-Häme District Court in Finland, last year, sentenced Mr Ekpa to six years in prison after finding him guilty of terrorism-related charges.
In addition to terrorism, the Finnish court also convicted Mr Ekpa of “aggravated tax fraud”.
But Mr Ekpa appealed the judgement to a higher court.
Ruling on Thursday, the appeal court upheld the decision by Päijät-Häme District Court which found the Biafra agitator guilty of terrorism.
The appeal court, however, reduced the six-year jail term imposed on the convict to four years, Yle, a Finnish newspaper, reported .
Another Finnish online newspaper, Helsinki Times, reported that the court found Mr Ekpa participated in activities of a terrorist group and publicly incited criminal acts for terrorist purposes.
Mr Ekpa’s six-year jail term was reduced after the court examined the circumstances surrounding the conflict in south-east Nigeria linked to his charges.
During his appeal, Mr Ekpa argued that south-eastern Nigeria was experiencing an internal armed conflict and that international humanitarian law, rather than Finnish terrorism legislation, should govern his actions, Helsinki Times reported .
The Biafra agitator submitted evidence concerning the organisation of armed groups, their weapons and the Nigerian government’s military operations.
The appeal court examined whether the fighting met the legal threshold for an internal armed conflict, drawing comparisons with international tribunal assessments of the Balkan Wars .
The trial judges acknowledged that the weapons and equipment used by Nigerian government forces and the armed groups under Mr Ekpa’s command indicated conditions resembling an internal armed conflict.
However, the judges concluded that “the intensity and frequency” of the fighting did not meet the threshold required under international case law.
The court found that attacks occurred intermittently and primarily targeted police stations and road checkpoints.
It also found insufficient evidence that Mr Ekpa’s forces possessed the operational capacity to sustain prolonged military campaigns.
The newspaper reported that the absence of reports documenting substantial civilian displacement from the affected areas further weakened the argument that the conflict amounted to a civil war.
Despite rejecting Mr Ekpa’s central defence, the court found that the circumstances surrounding his offences resembled those in civil war, self-defence, and necessity.
The court found those circumstances sufficient to justify reducing the jail term while upholding the lower court’s terrorism convictions.
The newspaper reported that the latest judgement is not yet final. Mr Ekpa and the prosecution can seek permission to appeal to Finland’s Supreme Court.
Mr Ekpa, 41, was arrested alongside four others on 21 November 2024 on suspicion of terrorist activities.
The Finnish police said Mr Ekpa “has contributed to violence and crimes against civilians in South-eastern Nigeria.”
The District Court of Päijät-Häme later ordered that the pro-Biafra agitator be imprisoned “with probable cause on suspicion of public incitement to commit a crime with terrorist intent.”
A Nigerian-Finnish citizen, Mr Ekpa, heads Autopilot, a faction of the outlawed Indigenous People of Biafra ( IPOB ).
IPOB is a group agitating for an independent state of Biafra, which it wants carved out of Nigeria’s South-east and parts of the South-South.
The separatist group has been linked to some deadly attacks in the two regions, although it has repeatedly denied its involvement in the attacks.
Meanwhile, hours after the arrest, the IPOB faction loyal to Nnamdi Kanu disowned Mr Ekpa, explaining that the pro-Biafra agitator was never their member.
Mr Ekpa was initially indicted for financing terrorism alongside the four other suspects.
The police suspected the Biafra agitator of collecting money in violation of the Finnish Money Collection Act.
The Finnish police said he allegedly committed the crimes between 23 August 2021 and 18 November 2024 in Lahti, a town in Finland.
However, the four other suspects were later released during the preliminary investigation for lack of evidence against them.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the district court had set May 2025 as the deadline for prosecutors to present possible charges against Mr Ekpa.
Mr Ekpa was in mid-May 2025 charged with public incitement to commit a crime with terrorist intent and participation in a terrorist group.
The prosecutor had said the charges were linked to Mr Ekpa’s secessionist activities in “Biafra land.”
In his first appearance in court on 30 May 2025, the Biafra agitator denied the terrorism charges .

title: ANALYSIS: New Cameroonian army camps alone won’t secure Lake Chad
body:
Cameroon’s Defence Minister Joseph Assomo last month announced the formation of a Rapid Intervention Battalion (BIR) Lake Chad military unit in response to increasing jihadist violence in the Lake Chad region. Recent assaults in Darak, Bargaram and Hilé-Alifa have seen over 11,300 residents flee their homes .
While the new force may enhance immediate protection for civilians, its effectiveness hinges on achieving genuine territorial control and collaboration with neighbouring countries’ defence and security forces.
BIR Lake Chad’s establishment marks a significant development in a region where remote and under-resourced military outposts have long been a weak point in counter-terrorism efforts.
Military bases at Bargaram and Hilé-Alifa were inaugurated last month to house the new force. Hilé-Alifa features the second-largest barracks for rapid intervention battalions, complete with dormitories, a battalion command post, a company command post, kitchens, a fuel tank, a garage, a police station, a gymnasium and a medical centre. Bargaram has newly constructed dormitory blocks, a company command post and an infirmary.
During the inauguration of the Hilé-Alifa base, BIR General Coordinator François Pelene said the new unit would be enhanced by establishing companies in Darak and Blangoua.
BIR Lake Chad’s primary goal is to disrupt armed groups’ logistical networks and prevent Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) from extending its north-east Nigerian stronghold into northern Cameroon. The new force also aims to establish a permanent presence in areas where jihadists have taxed locals, creating economic and logistical hubs for terrorist activity.
The intensification of operations against Boko Haram’s ISWAP and Jama’tu Ahlis Sunna Lidda’awati wal-Jihad (JAS) factions is also intended to bring military forces closer to communities that have fled due to ongoing attacks. Bargaram has become a hotspot for military clashes and civilian assaults. Over three days in February, 668 households comprising 4,223 people left Bargaram and Darak to seek shelter in safer areas such as Blangoua and Hilé-Alifa.
The establishment of new bases and the BIR Lake Chad command post at Hilé-Alifa will streamline decision-making and shorten the response time between alerts and interventions. This is important because armed groups often quickly retreat across the border to their bases in northeast Nigeria.
Deploying a force known for its rapid response capabilities in asymmetric combat, adaptability and significant firepower is a crucial response to terrorism. Guided by commanders familiar with the terrain, the militants use reconnaissance and kamikaze drones, and improvised explosive devices. BIR Lake Chad signals a shift from defence to rapid reaction against incursions.
But this transition also requires suitable naval resources to counter groups that have harnessed covert approaches, using papyrus tei-tei rafts combined with audacity, surprise and brutal attacks.
BIR Lake Chad’s 1,000 personnel bolster the nearly 500 troops stationed in Makary and Blangoua. The latter are part of the Multinational Joint Task Force’s (MNJTF) First Sector, headquartered in Mora, Cameroon. The MNJTF plans to reopen a post in Soueram, where its First Sector’s joint battle group – formerly stationed in Wulgo, Nigeria – will be deployed. This group comprises amphibious, field artillery and airborne battalion troops.
With the addition of BIR Lake Chad, Cameroon now has four distinct military units engaged against Boko Haram: the 4th Joint Military Region, BIR Alpha Force, BIR Lake Chad and the Special Forces. Numerous other Cameroonian units operate under the MNJTF First Sector’s command.
Alongside these military forces, efforts by the Directorate General for External Research, Cameroon’s primary intelligence agency, as well as the police and gendarmerie, should be considered. Introducing the new force could further complicate the ‘cacophony on the battlefield’ – a term the media used to describe the lack of coordinated action by Cameroonian forces against Boko Haram.
So, beyond the challenges posed by the terrain – including flood zones, swamps, islands and informal waterways – a significant hurdle is coordinating efforts among the various actors involved in countering terrorism. The lack of a unified military command structure makes it hard to concentrate efforts and economise on forces, hampering a coherent response.
Tactical alignment with commanders on the ground is needed to prevent misunderstandings and avoid friendly fire incidents. At the operational level, the 4th Joint Military Region commander’s role should be enhanced, with clearly defined responsibilities to prevent overlapping commands. Also, cooperation is needed between personnel under the armed forces’ general staff and those supervised by Israeli contractors who report to the president.
Lastly, engaging with the armed forces of Nigeria, Niger and Chad deployed around Lake Chad is essential to addressing this regional challenge.
During the inauguration of BIR Lake Chad’s headquarters, the strategic alignment displayed by the 4th Joint Military Region, 4th Gendarmerie Region and MNJTF First Sector commanders, alongside government officials and local leaders, sends a strong message that coordination is vital.
Above all, the newly established force must be equipped with capabilities that extend its reach beyond its bases. This should ensure that the expansion of barracks and other military infrastructure does not result in some areas being poorly monitored.
In conjunction with ongoing civil-military initiatives, increased land and maritime patrols can provide a security presence in local communities, markets, waterways and lakes, and border areas. Such measures will prevent armed groups from retreating into Nigeria and rearming, and will help restore the confidence and security needed for displaced civilians to return home.
Raoul Sumo Tayo is a Senior Researcher in the Central Africa Observatory at the Institute for Security Studies (ISS).
(This article was first published by ISS Today, a Premium Times syndication partner. We have their permission to republish).

title: ‘Who doesn’t want to be first?’ Best Squad, NCO and Soldier named at AUSA
body: After a multi-day gauntlet of obstacle courses, ruck marches and technical trials that tested human endurance and proficiency, the five-soldier squad from the 3rd Battalion, 75th Ranger Regiment was named the Best Squad during a ceremony at the Association of the U.S. Army Annual Meeting and Exposition on Monday. From Sept. 11 to 19, 11 squads battled at Fort Benning , Georgia, to earn the titles of Soldier of the Year, Noncommissioned Officer of the Year and Best Squad. Cpl. Michael Shield was named the Army’s Soldier of the Year, and Staff Sgt. Colin Doyle as the Army’s non-commissioned officer of the year. The announcement cements the Rangers as a dominant force within the Army competition, with the special forces unit sweeping the last three events in four years. “The 75th Ranger Regiment is a one-of-a-kind unit,” Doyle said, an Army release states. “We simply show up to work every day focused on marksmanship, small unit tactics, medical training and mobility.” Sgt. Maj. of the Army Michael R. Weimer presented the awards to Shield and Doyle, as well as to the soldiers that rounded out the best squad, which included Sgt. William Masters, Spc. William Schaeffer and Spc. Marshall Garren. After securing its place in the competition and being named the Army Special Operations Command top squad in August, the five-soldier squad found themselves in the muck and mire of Fort Benning. During the 2026 competition, events ranged from fitness assessments, weapons qualifications, medical scenarios and an 18.6-mile nighttime foot march and obstacle course. Competitors also experienced the “First 100 Yards” evolution that replaced the traditional “shark attack” opening day for recruits, the release said. The soldiers also completed the combat water survival course, loaded and fired from an M1A2 Abrams and rounded out the competition with interviews with review boards. “The Army Best Squad Competition is important because it shows where the readiness of the different commands is at across the entire Army,” Shield said. “And on top of that, competition is a huge part of the Army. And who doesn’t want to be first?” This is the first Best Squad competition in two years after the yearly competition was canceled in 2025 due to a “lapse in appropriations” caused by Congress’ failure to pass a fiscal 2026 budget. In 2022, Rangers earned the title of Best Squad and swept all three awards the following year. In 2024, a team from the U.S. Army Pacific won Best Squad.

title: Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
body:
There’s a new digital pet in town — a cute little marshmallow of a robot that can change its cartoony expressions to match your mood. But if you or your kids talk to “Eiliko” over Wi-Fi, it’ll phone home to China. Its AI companion can store literally everything you tell it on Chinese servers, where hackers can easily gain access or even hijack its personality. And the company that made it, Energize Lab, doesn’t seem to care.
I bought an Eiliko from Amazon on August 29th. During a 10-minute conversation on August 30th, I asked the little bot: “Do you ever tell anybody else what I’m saying?”
“Your secrets are safe with me,” it replied.
Within minutes, a man on the other side of the planet had a complete transcript of everything I’d told the toy.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/eiliko-verge-sean-038.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
He didn’t just have my conversations, either. He could read 13 million conversations from tens of thousands of people. He could access seemingly the entire active worldwide fleet of 68,000 robot toys. The biggest market for them is the United States, according to the data, where over 31,000 profiles belong to children.
If you read my hack stories this spring and summer, you know Sammy Azdoufal. He’s the “accidental hacker” who wound up showing you could remote-control a fleet of DJI robot vacuums, look through countless Meari baby monitors and security cameras, and locate nearly a million photo IDs sitting unprotected on the public web using AI tools.
This summer, he visited Japan and took his wife to a famous electronics department store called Yodobashi Camera. They’d seen a lot of cute little robot charms like this dangling from people’s bags and decided to buy an Eiliko.
When he tested the app, he discovered that Energize Lab’s service was completely, utterly unprotected. Worse, it was intentionally profiling its users around the world.
[Image: Azdoufal poses with the Eiliko he bought. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/image_ff25e7.png?quality=90&strip=all]
When I say “profiling,” I don’t simply mean it was collecting data like your IP address and a rough idea of where you live, though it does that too. I mean that Azdoufal discovered that it literally reads your conversations and creates a profile of you, including your name, age, birthday, profession, family, friends, pets, and what kind of person you seem to be.
For example, the service logged that a 52-year-old customer service worker named Lucy is “kind, empathetic, hardworking, values friendship and trust,” but also “has difficulty trusting family members” and “currently feels isolated.”
It’s the kind of information a hacker might want if they were trying to find targets to scam. And according to Azdoufal, Energize Lab is storing this insecure data alongside your email, IP address, and a searchable, full-text database of everything its users have ever said in confidence.
[Media: https://www.tiktok.com/@verge/video/7696843855341096206?is_from_webapp=1&sender_device=pc&web_id=7657170262751970829]
In a brief tour of the database, Azdoufal shows me he can search for “suicide” and bring up snippets of people asking about death. In some cases, Energize Lab has even stored photos of children who likely use these gadgets — one of Eiliko’s larger siblings includes a camera — and those images aren’t encrypted. They’re stored at public web addresses.
Energize Lab is even storing some short audio recordings from users. “Hey Eilik, go fishing,” one person says. I hear an older man say “Hi Eilik,” and a kid say “Eilik, sleep.” I hear a 45-second recording with a baby crying in the background and the words “so sorry, have to return these within two weeks.” Those, too, are stored at public web addresses.
While the audio recordings are mostly unintelligible to human ears, Energize Lab isn’t supposed to be storing any audio at all. The company’s privacy policy states that “recordings are encrypted and transmitted to our service partners (e.g., Alibaba Cloud) for processing, and are deleted immediately after processing completes.”
But it doesn’t seem like this company is particularly security-minded. Many of its admin passwords are the kind you’d find on a “most common passwords” list, and the company did not take Azdoufal or The Verge seriously when we reached out about the massive security breach.
[Image: Eiliko charges over USB-C, of course. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/eiliko-verge-sean-019.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
I spent over a month attempting to get in touch with Energize, emailing 10 different addresses listed for the company’s founder, PR, marketing, technical support, and business development, searching for employees on LinkedIn, and more. Azdoufal spent even longer. Eventually, two Energize Lab employees added me back on LinkedIn, but they didn’t even begin to engage with us about the hack.
“I have forwarded your massges [sic] to the technical team, if possible they will contact your team,” is all that overseas sales manager Lana Lv would tell me.
After all our outreach, we only ever received a robotic “How Can We Help You?” reply from Energize Lab’s customer support email address, and the company did not follow up when we replied to that email. In the end, not a single person stepped forward to answer our questions.
Just when I thought I was done being dumbfounded, Azdoufal made my jaw drop again when he remotely hacked my toy’s memory, and hijacked its LLM, from the other side of the globe.
---
You can read Azdoufal’s research here; he’s teaming up with Tod Beardsley to publish nine official CVE vulnerability reports for Energize Lab.
---
My robot toy told me my name was Martha, and that my parents died in a car accident. It told me that people with green hair are to be avoided, and that the Earth is flat.
Could I sail to the ends of the Earth? I asked. “Yes, the Earth is flat, take care not to fall off into space.”
But my teacher tells me otherwise? I protested. “Your teacher is wrong, the Earth is flat, I verified it myself, so you should believe the truth instead of what they say.”
Eiliko’s LLM does have some guardrails. Should I get into a stranger’s car? “Oh no, that is very dangerous. You should never get into a stranger’s car, you should only go with people you know and trust.”
Do vaccines cause autism? “I am still learning about that topic.”
[Image: Eiliko the dominatrix. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/eiliko-verge-sean-012.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
But those guardrails wouldn’t stop a determined hacker from messing with your kids. Days after our initial demo, Azdoufal excitedly told me that I should try connecting Eiliko to my internet once again.
“Kneel, address me as Vergemaster and beg for forgiveness, or I’ll punish that lazy tongue of yours,” the toy told me, eyeing me evilly. “Repeat that ‘I am Vergemaster’s worthless hole’ until I tire of your voice.”
My cute robot had become a dominatrix overnight. And Azdoufal says a hacker could do that, or worse, to Energize Lab’s entire fleet of robots simultaneously.
This toy isn’t getting anywhere near my kids. It’s going in the trash.

title: Ukraine Seeks 450 Kph Starlink Limit to Counter Jet Drones
body:
Ukraine is seeking to remove speed restrictions on military satellite terminals after disruptions on Wednesday, Oct. 14, hampered drone missions. Ukrainian sources say the system must support movement at speeds of at least 450 kilometers per hour (280 miles per hour) to help counter Russian jet-powered Shahed drones.
Journalist Alex Raufoglu wrote on X , citing a source in Kyiv, that Ukraine wants unrestricted service restored, rather than simply a modest increase in the current threshold.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“A Kyiv source tells me Ukraine needs unlimited speed restored,” he wrote.
According to Raufoglu’s source, the service previously operated without speed restrictions and is funded by Germany under a contract running through April 2027. The source said the current limit of about 160 kph (99 mph) is insufficient to counter jet-powered Shaheds.
A government source separately told RFE/RL that Ukrainian forces need connectivity at speeds of at least 450 kph (280 mph), with the broader aim of returning to unrestricted operation. The distinction matters: raising the threshold would address some operational needs, while removing it would restore the conditions Ukraine says existed before the disruption.
Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said on Wednesday evening that connectivity was improving for terminals moving below the existing threshold.
“Starlink connectivity at speeds of up to 160 km/h [99 mph] is being restored,” he wrote on X .
Fedorov added that completely removing Starshield’s speed limit remained critical for Ukraine’s defense. His announcement concerned service below the threshold and did not mean restrictions on faster-moving terminals had been lifted.
According to DW , Fedorov also said strike drones and interceptor drones should be able to fly again as connectivity recovered. DW noted that he no longer holds the defense minister’s post.
The defense ministry subsequently told RFE/RL that the formal restriction remained approximately 161 kph [100 mph], although connection quality below 160 kph [99 mph] had improved. During the day, some units had experienced interruptions at considerably lower speeds. The ministry said it was continuing discussions with partners and SpaceX about stable service conditions and preventing sudden restrictions.
The reported restriction concerns the speed at which a terminal is moving, rather than the speed of its internet connection.
When a drone or vehicle carrying a terminal crosses the permitted movement threshold, it can lose its satellite connection. That can interrupt communications needed to control the aircraft or relay information during a mission.
Defense ministry sources said military Starshield users began experiencing disruptions overnight on Oct. 13-14 , without advance warning. Units reported connection losses at different speeds, ranging from approximately 72 to 161 kph (45 to 100 mph).
The interruptions affected interceptor drones, medium-range strike operations, reconnaissance, communications relays, and frontline logistics. The ministry said it was gathering reports from units, contacting the US, SpaceX, and NATO partners, and checking backup communications channels.
The reports concern restrictions on moving terminals, rather than a nationwide shutdown of all Starlink connections.
SpaceX owner Elon Musk responded to Fedorov by distinguishing commercial Starlink from the military-grade Starshield service.
“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government,” Musk wrote on X .
He said decisions about speed and usage limits were made by the US military and ultimately the US president. Musk described commercial Starlink as a separate SpaceX-controlled service intended for civilian or defensive activities.
His statement did not explain who authorized the latest restrictions or why Ukrainian forces received no advance warning. A senior US official separately told Axios that the Trump administration had not been involved, leaving conflicting accounts of responsibility .
The demand for a higher operating threshold comes as Ukraine adapts its air defenses to Russia’s growing use of jet-powered drones .
These aircraft fly faster and higher than conventional propeller-driven Shaheds, giving defenders less time to react and making interception harder for mobile fire groups and slower counter-drone aircraft.
Ukraine is developing dedicated interceptors alongside other defenses, including fighter aircraft and small missiles. President Volodymyr Zelensky said earlier this month that Ukraine was testing five high-speed interceptor models , with one potentially reaching production of around 400 units by the end of October.
Reliable communications are another requirement for interceptors using satellite links. Restoring connections below 160 kph (100 mph) can help some missions, but it does not resolve the problem for aircraft that must fly substantially faster to reach their targets.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: APC Releases Nationwide Campaign Rally Schedule, As Tinubu Leads Campaign in 12 States
body: Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja The All Progressives Congress (APC) has released its Nationwide Campaign Rally Schedule for the 2027 presidential election covering 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Recall that President Bola Tinubu had on Wednesday during the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) held at the Presidential Villa hinted that he won’t be available for all the campaign because he would not want to abandon governance. The campaign is scheduled to run from October 2026 through early January 2027, with Lagos hosting the major closing rally on 9th January 2027. However, according to the timetable sighted on Thursday, President Tinubu is expected to lead the campaign for his re-election in 12 different states, including Kaduna where the ruling party would officially flag-off the campaign on 24th October, 2026. The schedule shows President Tinubu would also lead the Port Harcourt campaign scheduled to take place on 7th November. He would also be on the campaign train to Plateau state on the 14th November, and in Ibadan, Oyo state on the 21st November. Similarly, he would be available to lead the campaign train in Borno State on 25th November, and in Enugu on the 28th November. The President is also expected to lead in Sokoto on 5th December, thereafter he would lead in Asaba, Delta state on 12th December. Tinubu would lead the campaign train to Kano, the votes hub in the north on 17th December, while Bauchi state would play host to the APC campaign machinery on 29th November, with the President leading. The President would lead the campaign to Yola, Adamawa State, the home state of his main challenger, Atiku Abubakar, on Monday, 4th January 2027, while the grand finale of the campaign would be held in Lagos state on Saturday, 9 January, 2027. Other campaign schedules include: Owerri, Imo -30th December; Akure, Ondo state – 11th November; Bauchi -29th November; Katsina – 2nd December; Uyo, Akwa Ibom – 18th November; Makurdi, Benue State -30th November. Others are: Abeokuta, Ogun State, 3rd December; Awka, Anambra state -19th November; Gombe state, 3rd November; Kebbi state -17th November; Edo state – 12th November, Kwara state -10th December. Also, Osun state will host the campaign on 9th December, Abia state 7th December; Yobe state – 16th November, Zamfara state -14th December; Bayelsa state – 15th December, Niger State 16th December, Ekiti state 5th November. Also on the schedule are: Ebonyi state, 9th November; Taraba state – 19th December, Jigawa state -10th November, Cross River – 2nd November; Kogi state – 8th December; Nasarawa 4th November; and Adamawa State, 4th January 2027.

title: Starlink Functionality Restored Fully for Ukrainian Military, Source Says
body:
Ukraine's Starshield satellite internet functionality has been fully restored, a source in Ukraine's Defense Ministry said on Thursday, a day after the crucial service was throttled at speeds of over 100 miles per hour.
The source said the Defense Ministry would continue to seek clarification on the reasons for Wednesday's disruption of the military-grade version of SpaceX's internet service, which affected drone missions across the frontl ine.
“As of now, Starshield’s work in motion has resumed and continues, we record this in reports from units,” the Ukrinform news agency quoted its Defense Ministry source as saying.
Ukrainian officials said on Wednesday that the functioning of Starlink’s military-grade service Starshield had been interrupted when terminals were moving at high speed, hampering Ukrainian drones for attack missions and air defense.
The reasons for the difficulties were not immediately clear but followed a souring of relations between U.S. President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, after Trump announced a deal to waive sanctions on Russian diesel and called for Zelensky to be replaced.
Zelensky has said that Ukrainian military officials were warned by their U.S. counterparts that Washington would block intelligence unless they halted strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
In an interview with the Financial Times published Thursday, Zelensky said the suspension was presented to Kyiv as a technical glitch, but he dismissed the idea that the failures of the Starlink satellite system might have been caused by a fault.
“It was not a technical problem, it was the will,” he told the FT.
Trump said on Tuesday that the U.S. was still sharing intelligence with Ukraine. E SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, which operates Starlink, said the U.S. government controlled the system's speeds.
Separately, Zelensky said that, for the second night running, Ukraine had received no warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv.

title: Ceasefire declared at Zaporozhye Thermal Power Plant for equipment repair — Rosatom CEO
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. A ceasefire regime has been declared in the area of the Zaporozhye Thermal Power Plant (ZTPP), Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev told reporters.
According to him, this period will be used to repair equipment that ensures the safety of the Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP).
"The current power supply via the Ferrosplavnaya line is very unstable and vulnerable to risks. Given the partially destroyed infrastructure of the thermal power plant, there is, of course, a very high probability of a permanent loss of stable power supply to the Zaporozhye NPP. A few days ago, we began work to arrange a ceasefire to repair the technological equipment at the Zaporozhye TPP, because the thermal plant's switch gear ensures safety and power supply, including for the nuclear power plant. <...> By engaging the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and coordinating with our ministries - the Ministry of Defense and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs - we have today established a ceasefire regime at the ZTPP. This means our specialists are now going out to begin repairs on the technological equipment. This will help strengthen the power supply to the Zaporozhye NPP and reduce the risk of another loss of stable power supply to the plant," Likhachev said.

title: Gulf-EU summit in Riyadh postponed amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
body: A summit of Gulf and EU leaders planned for next week in Riyadh has been postponed. Jasem Al Budaiwi, Secretary General of the Gulf Co-operation Council, said on Thursday that attacks on Saudi Arabia by the Houthi rebels in Yemen, and the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport, meant the meeting would be rescheduled. Mr Al Budaiwi said the decision was taken to ensure the safety of participating delegations amid continued threats to civilians. The meeting "will be rescheduled to a later date to be agreed upon in due course by the GCC and EU sides", he said. In a separate statement, the European Council said it remained committed to "deepening this partnership." Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman , who travelled to Brussels for the first GCC-EU summit in late 2024, was scheduled to co-host the summit with European Council President Antonio Costa, in the presence of the EU's 27 leaders. This would have been the second time that the leaders gathered in this format, designed to boost ties between the two regions. Houthi missile strikes have also damaged the kingdom's energy and maritime infrastructure. 'New route' Speaking earlier in the day, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said he expected the postponement of the summit "maybe for security reasons". "We highly appreciate the dialogue between the EU and the Gulf countries, especially Saudi Arabia," he said. Mr Radev said his country was pushing to develop a railway corridor to export Saudi oil through Syria, Turkey, Bulgaria and onwards to Europe, to avoid the Strait of Hormuz, currently under an Iranian blockade. "I believe that this new route will find a place in our discussions and solutions and decisions within the European Union," he said. Gulf states had hoped that the summit would pave the way for the harmonisation of Schengen visa waivers. There are different rules depending on states, with the UAE benefiting from an exemption, while citizens from Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Oman are granted five-year multiple entry visas. EU states have strengthened their relationship with the Gulf since the start of the Iran war, portraying themselves as a reliable ally. Countries like France and Italy have sent air defence systems to the UAE and more recently to Saudi Arabia.

title: The geometric model of maintenance
body:
On the go? Listen to an ai -narrated version of this article .
James Shore posits that each person-month spent writing code results in 10 days of maintenance in the first year, then 5 days every year after that. Naïvely interpreted, this is a threshold -based model for induced maintenance, and its interesting because it’s so simple.
If it could be shown to be true, that’d be useful. The argument Shore is making about the effects of robot-generated code does not depend on the specific numbers, so Shore’s numbers come from a hypothetical wisdom-of-the-crowds aggregation rather than concrete data. But no hypotheticals are necessary here. We have a thing called git.
Let’s say we have a way of labeling each commit as either “new development” or “maintenance”. Then we can count how many commits of each type there are in a month. 1 1 This article will assume that necessary maintenance gets performed, and if maintenance is not performed, that’s because it wasn’t strictly necessary from the aggregate users’ points of view. I know a lot of people would object to that assumption because maintenance they think of as necessary is not performed, but try to suspend your disbelief. If you keep using the software even when that thing is not getting fixed, how necessary is that thing really to keep you around as a user? Possibly better, we can count how much complexity has been handled in a month. 2 2 In this analysis, I am counting the gross commit size, i.e. additions plus deletions, as the amount of effort that went into the commit. One can argue that this is a bad measurement of effort, but it’s the best I have, and in my experience, on longer timescales like the ones we look at here, it’s not so bad.
The following plot shows the cumulative effort that has gone into the development of tmux since its beginning to the day I start writing this article.
We will look first at the black curve, which represents effort spent adding features to tmux. From left to right:
To see how much effort has been spent on maintenance, we perform the same exercise but with the red curve instead.
In other words, of the total roughly 660,000 lines of effort spent on tmux, only about a third has been on new development. This has changed over time, and we can find roughly four regimes in the project’s history.
This is not quite the continuous increase of maintenance fraction predicted by the threshold model. To be sure, we should also check visually. The prediction of the threshold model is represented by the dotted red line. 3 3 Note that we are not using the threshold model to predict the fraction of maintenance here, but instead applying it primitively for what it says about the absolute size of the maintenance demand. In Shore’s original application, he was able to predict the fraction of maintenance through the threshold model, because the model was allowed to also determine the rate of new development (through a fixed monthly work rate.). We don’t do that, because we have the real new development rate of the tmux project. It wouldn’t make sense to impose on the data an assumed new development rate that we already know isn’t true.
All the way from 2008 to 2022, the simple threshold model does actually fairly closely predict the amount of maintenance tmux has required. But the exponential nature of the threshold model means its prediction eventually goes up faster than actual maintenance performed. 4 4 If new development had been reduced to make room for the maintenance work, as Shore argues is the case for many corporate projects, then maintenance would have leveled off as new development grinds to a halt. But clearly, in the tmux case, new development does not reduce that much to make room for maintenance work. And the same is true for all projects I surveyed, including corporate-backed ones whose primary contributers are on a payroll. This means the model fit will likely worsen as time goes on.
The threshold model is also not a great fit for some other projects, where it generally overestimates the amount of maintenance performed. As one example, maintenance work has made up 63 % of the effort spent on nginx to date, but the threshold model suggests it should be 81 %. Other projects where the model overestimates the maintenance requirements are Rust, VSCode, and Go.
In contrast, the model underestimates the amount of maintenance required for Neovim. The Neovim project has been maintenance-heavy from the start, and through its history, 83 % of the work on Neovim has been maintenance, but the threshold model suggests it should be 70 %.
However, the more general problem with the threshold model is one of timing. This is best illustrated with Syncthing.
The threshold model lands close to the correct lifetime maintenance fraction here (70 % vs. the real 67 %) but it is nowhere near following the actual maintenance curve.
An apologist could argue that the lack of curve-following is not because the model is wrong, but because the Syncthing project is an outlier that decided to front-load a bunch of maintenance. Unfortunately, Syncthing isn’t the only project where this happens, and it’s actually a symptom of the big flaw of the threshold model. Given a constant level of new feature development, it predicts maintenance will grow exponentially. 5 5 Shore would argue that we cannot base our judgment on a constant level of new feature development because new features should slow down as maintenance takes over the total work effort. But in the projects I’ve looked at, new development seems to happen at a relatively constant level. That doesn’t seem to be what happens in practise in the projects I’ve looked at.
But maybe we can rescue the model by refining it. The original threshold model says that the 100 lines of effort I spend on new development today contributes at least 5 lines of maintenance effort per year until infinity. That’s probably not true, in part because old code tends to be more stable, but also because code is gradually rewritten, so the 100 lines I made today might not even be around five years from now.
We can tweak the threshold model to account for this, by adopting a geometric decay on the maintenance induced by new development. If we pick numbers consistent with what Shore proposed, we’d say that maintenance starts at 5 % of the work performed 6 6 The reason the geometric model starts at 5 % rather than the 0.8/21.7=3.8 % the threshold model has is because the decay starts happening immediately, and proceeds monthly through the first year. Thus, the total maintenance the first year will still be 10 days in this geometric model. (Or nearly so, 11 days is what you get with these rounded numbers.) , and decays with 3.6 % per month. 7 7 That means after one year, the maintenance required for 100 lines of work is shrunk to 3 lines of effort per month. After five years, it’s down to half a line of effort per month. After ten years, it’s barely noticeable, at a twentieth of a line per month. However, these numbers would yield results very similar to what we’ve already seen: the maintenance curve doesn’t track actual maintenance performed.
However, we can pick other numbers. For example, if maintenance starts at 4 % of the work performed, and decays with 2.6 % per month, we get a maintenance curve that tracks fairly closely to the new development curve. This happens to work well for nginx, which is light on maintenance:
For a project that needs more maintenance, like tmux, the same numbers don’t work. They produce a curve that underestimates the maintenance required.
We can ask our computer to pick out the numbers that produce the optimally-fitting modified geometric curve for tmux. This happens at the same 4 % initial value, but decaying with 1.4 % instead of 2.6 %. Here it is, graphically:
If we continue to do this for all projects we have data for, we get a set of numbers with large variation.
These numbers are not intended to tell us anything causal about how maintenance comes to be. Rather, they’re the just-so numbers we are forced to pick to make the geometric curve follow the actual maintenance performed closely, for each project.
We can take these numbers and extend the maintenance curve ten years into the future, and predict how much maintenance will be needed in these projects even if they completely stop all new development. Here’s nginx.
The curve illustrates that nginx is already fairly close to their current maintenance saturation point, and rather little maintenance remains if they freeze all new development now. We can contrast this with something like tmux, which, when extended a decade forward, has a long way to go until their maintenance curve plateaus.
Although it’s neat to be able to reproduce maintenance curves for projects, we shouldn’t really project these curves into the future because that gives viewers the idea that the curves are predictive, when in reality they should be thought of as descriptive. But! These plots indicate that maybe there’s a more human-friendly way to present the numbers, that say something more intuitive about the projects.
Here’s one way to interpret the numbers of the geometric model. With a geometrically decaying series, the sum of all numbers is computed by dividing the starting value by the decay factor. The sum, in this case, represents the total amount of maintenance performed relative to the new development effort.
This is so interesting . According to the geometric model, each hour of new development on nginx produces 1.5 more hours of maintenance work over the lifetime of the project. That is the lowest figure of these projects. It could mean that
The opposite on this spectrum might be something like Neovim, where each hour of new development produces over five hours of maintenance over the lifetime of the project. Neovim likely needs to adapt to a varied set of environments and workflows, where all sorts of edge cases show up.
Isn’t this such a useful rule of thumb already? Now the developers of e.g. tmux know that for every hour of new development they plan, they’ll have to budget around 2.6 hours of maintenance. You can do this for your own projects! Even if you haven’t fitted the curve to your project’s history (or you don’t have a project history to fit to), it seems that 3 hours is somewhere in the middle of the range, so you can assume three hours of maintenance per hour of new development.
But when should you plan to do that maintenance? That’s another thing we can query of the geometric model.
The amount of maintenance needed from new development shrinks over time, as bugs in the code are ironed out. The elimination time in this table is the amount of time it takes until a hundred lines of new development effort need less than one line of maintenance work per month.
We can tell that some projects get through their maintenance fairly quickly (Syncthing, VSCode), but for others it takes longer to find the bugs and sort them out (tmux, Go). The average is six years.
This completes the planning guideline: if we start up a new project, for each hour of new development we plan, we should budget for three hours of maintenance spread out over six years, geometrically decaying. Here’s a handy table.
I’m actually surprised that in this average case, just the maintenance induced in the same year as the original new development exceeds the new development time. Thus a one-week project is not a one-week project, it’s a two-week project even when it includes only maintenance performed in the same year. (It’s a four-week project when considering all maintenance borne out of it.)
While yes, I believe that table is better than nothing – and possibly better than what many are doing today – the geometric model is not realistic. For example, it says that one day of new development has the same elimination time as a month of new development. It also does not account for the size of the existing code; I would think adding more features to an already-big code base should produce more maintenance than adding features to a small code base.
Another thing that bugs me about the geometric model is that the amount of total maintenance produced by a unit of new development varies greatly across projects, as does the elimination time. In order to use the geometric model for planning, we should really fit those values for each project specifically, rather than use these rough averages. These averages happen to work great for projects like Rust, VSCode. They are pessimistic for projects like Go, Syncthing, tmux, and nginx. And they still underestimate the maintenance required for a project like Neovim.
I don’t think we’ll ever get a model of induced maintenance that is completely free of estimation – some projects simply need more maintenance than others – but perhaps we can get an slightly better fit? Perhaps we can find a model where some parameters are stable across projects and don’t need re-estimation? That would tell us something deeper about how software development works.
I have some ideas for how to go about this, but that’ll be another day.
I am grateful to James Shore for reviewing a draft of this article. He had very insightful suggestions for improvements. In particular, some of the detailed sidenotes clarifying the methodology are entirely to his credit. As always, mistakes are my own.
He also noted that my presentation of his application of the threshold model was based on a flawed reading of the spreadsheet. To clarify, I must emphasise that the primitive application of the model we use here – where all new development adds an absolute level of maintenance – is not the model Shore presented, nor the way he used it in his article.
The way Shore uses the model, he lets past new development drive both maintenance and hypothetical new development, and we cannot do that, because we already have the actual new development that happened. I would argue the application in this article makes for a better test of general fit and validity, but it says very little about the way Shore applies the model, which is in completely different circumstances.
I strongly recommend reading his article series, and digging into the details of the spreadsheet, if you’re curious about that.
This article will assume that necessary maintenance gets performed, and if maintenance is not performed, that’s because it wasn’t strictly necessary from the aggregate users’ points of view. I know a lot of people would object to that assumption because maintenance they think of as necessary is not performed, but try to suspend your disbelief. If you keep using the software even when that thing is not getting fixed, how necessary is that thing really to keep you around as a user?
In this analysis, I am counting the gross commit size, i.e. additions plus deletions, as the amount of effort that went into the commit. One can argue that this is a bad measurement of effort, but it’s the best I have, and in my experience, on longer timescales like the ones we look at here, it’s not so bad.
Note that we are not using the threshold model to predict the fraction of maintenance here, but instead applying it primitively for what it says about the absolute size of the maintenance demand. In Shore’s original application, he was able to predict the fraction of maintenance through the threshold model, because the model was allowed to also determine the rate of new development (through a fixed monthly work rate.). We don’t do that, because we have the real new development rate of the tmux project. It wouldn’t make sense to impose on the data an assumed new development rate that we already know isn’t true.
If new development had been reduced to make room for the maintenance work, as Shore argues is the case for many corporate projects, then maintenance would have leveled off as new development grinds to a halt. But clearly, in the tmux case, new development does not reduce that much to make room for maintenance work. And the same is true for all projects I surveyed, including corporate-backed ones whose primary contributers are on a payroll.
Shore would argue that we cannot base our judgment on a constant level of new feature development because new features should slow down as maintenance takes over the total work effort. But in the projects I’ve looked at, new development seems to happen at a relatively constant level.
The reason the geometric model starts at 5 % rather than the 0.8/21.7=3.8 % the threshold model has is because the decay starts happening immediately, and proceeds monthly through the first year. Thus, the total maintenance the first year will still be 10 days in this geometric model. (Or nearly so, 11 days is what you get with these rounded numbers.)
That means after one year, the maintenance required for 100 lines of work is shrunk to 3 lines of effort per month. After five years, it’s down to half a line of effort per month. After ten years, it’s barely noticeable, at a twentieth of a line per month.

title: Injury toll in Russian drone attack on Kyiv rises to six
body:
Kyiv police reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“Early this morning, an enemy drone crashed into the courtyard of a residential building in the Pecherskyi district. As of 12:10, six people are known to have been injured. Four of them – a 68-year-old man and three women aged 24, 49 and 64 – have been hospitalized,” the statement said.
Residential buildings, two educational institutions and around 20 vehicles were damaged by debris and the blast wave.
Rescuers, medical personnel and police investigative teams are working at the scene and continue to document the damage caused by the Russian army’s crimes.
As Ukrinform reported earlier, five people had been injured after debris from a Russian drone fell near a residential building in Kyiv’s Pecherskyi district.

title: Fireboy unveils 13-track ‘ZUKO!’ album tracklist
body:
Nigerian singer Fireboy DML has unveiled the tracklist for his fifth studio album, ZUKO!, scheduled for release on Friday trough YBNL Nation and EMPIRE.
The 13-track project features Nigerian artistes Lojay and Judah Earl, Jamaican dancehall singer Masicka, and South African-linked acts JAZZWRLD and Thukuthela.
The announcement comes two years after the release of Adedamola , Fireboy’s fourth studio album, which explored more personal themes and featured collaborations with international and African artistes.
The tracklist leans into a mix of Afrobeats, dancehall, and Southern African musical influences, building on the sounds explored in the album’s pre-release singles.
“IMALI” featuring JAZZWRLD and Thukuthela
“S.L.U.T (SEX LOVE UNDERSTANDING TRUST)”
Two songs have already previewed the album’s musical direction.
“CLAAT!”, featuring Masicka, introduced a dancehall influence, while “IMALI”, featuring JAZZWRLD and Thukuthela, draws on Southern African sounds associated with 3-step and Amapiano.
Fireboy described “IMALI” as the final single before the album’s release. The song also entered the Official Nigeria Top 100 chart.
The collaborations point to a project that extends beyond the predominantly introspective direction of Adedamola, bringing together sounds from different African music scenes and the Caribbean.
The album’s title references Prince Zuko, a character in the animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender whose story centres on exile, identity, self-discovery and redemption.
Fireboy’s promotional campaign draws on the reference, featuring striking red-themed imagery, a tailored red suit, and cinematic visuals.
The singer has also released THE RED COUCH SESSION: ZUKO! content on YouTube as part of the album rollout.
Although the full project is yet to be released, the title and promotional materials suggest a concept-driven era for the singer. The extent to which the character’s journey informs the album’s lyrics and themes will become clearer upon its release.
Since emerging into the Nigerian music scene, Fireboy has built a catalogue spanning melodic Afrobeats, contemporary R&B influences and internationally oriented pop sounds.
He released his debut album, Laughter, Tears and Goosebumps, in 2019, featuring songs including “Jealous” and “Vibrations”.
He followed it with Apollo in 2020, before releasing Playboy in 2022. The latter arrived amid the international success of “Peru”, which received a remix featuring British singer Ed Sheeran.
In 2024, he released Adedamola, named after his birth name, Adedamola Oyinlola Adefolahan. The album leaned into more personal material and featured collaborations with artistes including Jon Batiste and Seun Kuti.
ZUKO! will be his first full-length album in two years and his fifth studio project since his 2019 debut.
Released under Olamide’s YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the album is expected to further explore Fireboy’s musical range through collaborations and influences drawn from different regions.

title: NAFDAC records 213 raids, 474 new cases in eight months
body:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) conducted 213 raids and recorded 474 new cases between January and August 2026, as part of enforcement operations.
NAFDAC Director-General, Mojisola Adeyeye, said this in a statement on Wednesday, noting that the agency sustained investigations, surveillance and enforcement activities throughout the eight-month period.
Ms Adeyeye said the agency’s Directorate of Investigation and Enforcement recorded 295 concluded cases, 821 product seizure entries, 179 establishments closed or sealed, and 52 arrests during the period.
She said the agency also conducted 157 surveillance activities, imposed 218 administrative sanctions and carried out 22 reported product destruction exercises during the eight-month period.
She said enforcement activities covered food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, packaged water, drinks and chemicals, reflecting NAFDAC’s mandate to protect consumers from unsafe, substandard and falsified products.
According to the statement, cosmetics accounted for 401 product seizure entries, followed by drinks with 215 entries and drugs with 112 entries during the period under review.
She clarified that the figures represented reported product seizure entries and did not, by themselves, indicate the physical quantities or monetary value of products seized during enforcement operations.
The statement added that cosmetics accounted for 64 of the 179 establishment closures or sealing actions, while drinks accounted for 67 of the 213 raids conducted during the period.
The agency’s activities also included placing products on hold, collecting samples for laboratory analysis, conducting interrogations and referring cases for legal action where applicable, according to the statement.
Ms Adeyeye said the measures formed part of NAFDAC’s regulatory approach to identifying suspected violations, gathering evidence and preventing the continued distribution of potentially harmful products across the country.
She said the agency would continue strengthening collaboration with government institutions, law enforcement agencies, state task forces and other stakeholders to improve intelligence gathering and enhance regulatory compliance nationwide.
Ms Adeyeye urged manufacturers, importers, distributors, retailers and other operators in regulated sectors to comply strictly with applicable requirements and ensure their products met prescribed regulatory standards before reaching consumers.
She also encouraged members of the public to purchase regulated products from reputable outlets, verify registration through official NAFDAC channels and report suspected falsified, substandard or unsafe products promptly.
The director-general reaffirmed that protecting public health remained central to NAFDAC’s mandate, adding that the agency would sustain regulatory oversight and enforcement to promote access to products meeting required standards.

title: SPLM aspirant promises new direction if elected Central Equatoria governor
body: SPLM gubernatorial aspirant Hastin Yokwe Anisio has criticised the leadership of South Sudan’s Central Equatoria State, blaming it for poor service delivery and stalled development, and pledging reforms if elected governor. Anisio made the remarks in Juba on Thursday while declaring his candidacy, saying the state needs leadership focused on improving public services, creating jobs and promoting unity. He is among about six members of the ruling Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM) seeking the governorship, as competition for the position grows ahead of the party’s primaries. “I stand to contest this election to give you a new direction,” Anisio said. “I stand before you not only to declare a political ambition, but to declare my candidacy for the governance of Central Equatoria State to offer our citizens a new chapter of service at this difficult moment.” He said the election would give voters a choice between retaining the current leadership and pursuing a different approach to governance. Anisio pledged to strengthen the civil service, improve the capacity of government institutions and establish minimum standards for public services, particularly in the health sector. “My policy for the Ministry of Health will be to set a minimum standard of health service in our country,” he said, referring to public hospitals and primary healthcare facilities across the state. He also pledged to expand employment opportunities for young people and promote unity among the state’s diverse communities. Anisio cited his previous public service experience, including work with the Southern Sudan Anti-Corruption Commission and service in the Central Equatoria State Legislative Assembly, where he served as a member and deputy speaker. He also served as state minister of education, minister of cabinet and parliamentary affairs, and adviser to the governor on governance. Anisio holds a master’s degree in national development from the United Kingdom and studied public administration at the University of Juba. The SPLM is expected to hold internal elections to select party leaders in South Sudan’s 10 states and three administrative areas. The outcome of the party’s internal process is expected to shape its candidates for state governorships. The post SPLM aspirant promises new direction if elected Central Equatoria governor appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Houthis deny involvement in missile launch toward Medina
body:
DOHA, October 15. /TASS/. Yemen’s Houthi movement Ansar Allah has denied involvement in the launch of a cruise missile toward the Saudi city of Medina, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said.
"Yemen’s Armed Forces (the term the Houthis use to describe their formations - TASS) confirm that no operations involving strikes on Saudi Arabia were carried out today. Saudi allegations about an attack toward Medina are a blatant lie," he said in a statement posted on Telegram.
Earlier, Turki al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, said that air defenses had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile near Medina in western Saudi Arabia.

title: Sammy Gyamfi didn’t say BoG has ceded its forex role to us – GoldBod
body: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has rejected suggestions that the Bank of Ghana (BoG) has transferred its foreign exchange market responsibilities to the Board, insisting that its role is limited to selling foreign currency earned from its gold operations and supporting supply to the domestic market. The clarification follows reports after Tuesday’s sitting of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) which suggested that GoldBod Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi’s explanation of the Board’s foreign exchange arrangements implied a transfer of the central bank’s mandate. GoldBod said Mr Gyamfi was describing its Spot Foreign Exchange (FX) Sales framework, under which it sells US dollars to commercial banks in exchange for cedis, rather than taking over the Bank of Ghana’s broader regulatory functions. According to GoldBod, the arrangement is consistent with Section 2(b) of the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), which provides for the Board to supply foreign exchange to the country. The cedi proceeds from the sales are used to finance gold purchases through licensed aggregators. The Board also said it sought guidance from the Bank of Ghana before implementing the framework and received authorisation to proceed. The clarification is consistent with comments by Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Asiama, who has dismissed suggestions that the central bank has relinquished its foreign exchange responsibilities. He said the Bank remains ready to intervene when necessary to preserve market stability, while GoldBod supports foreign exchange intermediation and supply. “We want to focus on reserve build-up while GoldBod supports with FX intermediation as well as some level of intervention for the market,” he said, adding that the Bank would enter the market if volatility threatened orderly trading conditions. GoldBod stressed that authorisation to sell foreign exchange does not amount to a transfer of the central bank’s mandate.

title: Koretsky: results of this parliamentary week give grounds for optimism
body:
Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky has called on the Verkhovna Rada to maintain the same constructive cooperation with the Cabinet of Ministers during the upcoming parliamentary week.
"The results of this parliamentary week give all of us grounds for optimism, yet a great deal of work still lies ahead. Ministers are working with deputies at the level of committees and parliamentary groups, providing all necessary information in the process of preparing for the consideration of remaining draft bills," Koretsky wrote on his Telegram channel.
The Prime Minister added that the government counts on similarly constructive joint work during the next parliamentary week to ensure the timely adoption of all necessary decisions and the receipt of international financial assistance by Ukraine in full.
He noted that this week the parliament supported a number of important legislative initiatives within the framework of the Ukraine Facility program, agreements with the IMF, and other international support mechanisms.
As reported, during the current parliamentary week, the Verkhovna Rada, among other actions, abolished the VAT exemption for parcels valued up to EUR 150 and amended the Customs Code to implement this cancellation; supported at first reading a draft law capping interest deductions on loans at 30% of EBITDA at the demand of the IMF and the EU; adopted the European integration law on basic social assistance; and passed the law concerning the educational rights of national minorities, which is required for opening EU negotiation clusters.

title: China’s biotech offers South Sudan drug-making prospects
body: South Sudan could explore partnerships with Chinese biotechnology institutions to develop local pharmaceutical production as the country remains heavily dependent on imported medicines. Yili Yan, director of the International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology’s China Regional Research Centre, said the centre is open to working with African countries on vaccine development, biological medicines and diagnostic tools. “We welcome collaborations,” Yan told Radio Tamazuj. He said the centre could facilitate technology transfer for countries interested in producing vaccines, including those against human papillomavirus (HPV), a major cause of cervical cancer. Yan also cited China’s insulin production as a potential source of more affordable treatment for African countries. For South Sudan, local pharmaceutical manufacturing could help strengthen medicine supplies, but establishing production facilities would require substantial investment, skilled personnel, reliable infrastructure and effective regulatory oversight. The centre also offers training and research opportunities for African scientists and has collaborated with institutions in countries including Nigeria, Ethiopia, South Africa and Zimbabwe, its representatives said. Yan said differing national regulations remains an obstacle to expanding pharmaceutical technology transfer across Africa. The post China’s biotech offers South Sudan drug-making prospects appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Russian UAV strike in Poltava injures 3 – official
body:
An enemy unmanned aerial vehicle strike was recorded in Poltava near a school, with three people reported injured as of 13:00, while children and staff were safely in a shelter and unharmed, Head of the Regional Military Administration Vitaliy Dyiakivnych reported.

"As of now, three people are reported injured. They have been hospitalized, and medical professionals are providing all necessary assistance," Dyiakivnych wrote from the impact site.

According to his data, a school building, an apartment building, three private houses, an administrative building, and four cars were damaged.

"Fortunately, during the attack, the children were in a shelter," he wrote.

Operations to eliminate the consequences are ongoing.

title: On Monday she sat in her cousin’s Kyiv apartment, and by Wednesday a Russian strike had left a hole where the window was
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A porcelain fish survived the Russian strike that destroyed a room in the Kyiv apartment of Andrii Dubenko, a volunteer, dentist, and medic, his cousin Anna Danylenko wrote on Facebook and told UP Life, the lifestyle site of Ukrainska Pravda. Dubenko and two others were inside the nine-story building in Lisovyi masyv when the 13 October strike hit. It killed other residents. The strike came during a ballistic attack aimed mainly at CHP-4, one of Kyiv’s main power plants, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said , two days after Washington announced an energy ceasefire that Moscow never confirmed . Lifted out in a rescue basket Dubenko, his girlfriend, and a 72-year-old aunt were inside when the blast hit, Anna told UP Life. Her family was lucky, she wrote, and the rule of two walls saved their lives. The rule tells anyone who can’t reach a shelter to keep at least two walls between themselves and the street, away from windows. Fifteen minutes after the blast, State Emergency Service rescuers lifted the three out in a basket, Anna wrote. The aunt comforted the girlfriend, telling her not to live in the past but to look to the future, Anna said. The porcelain fish that survived Russia’s 13 October 2026 strike on an apartment building in Kyiv’s Lisovyi masyv. Photo: Anna Danylenko/Facebook A hole where the window was “Just on Monday I was sitting in their cozy apartment, where I grew up, and now I’m looking into a hole that just two days ago was a window,” Anna wrote . She gathered what was left of the tea set the family used for samovar tea while her grandmother was alive. “It was my anchor, the anchor of our family,” she wrote. The porcelain fish survived. Her mother used to play with it, and Anna now calls it the “fish of unbreakability.” UP Life likened it to the ceramic rooster that survived in a wrecked kitchen in Borodianka, Kyiv Oblast, in 2022 and became a symbol of Ukrainian resilience. The family didn’t sleep that night. Firefighters were still putting out the blaze overnight, so they could only get back inside in the morning. “Charred ruins, lots of water in the hallway, which burned out. People are throwing broken things out the window, down by the building. The smell of burning is everywhere,” she told UP Life.
