title: Ningi: ‎How Senator Mandiya Died In Abuja Home
body: Senator Abdul Ningi has recounted how his colleague, Bello Mandiya, reportedly died after slipping in his bathroom and hitting his head, with his body discovered about 72 hours later in his Abuja residence. ‎ ‎Ningi, who represents Bauchi Central Senatorial District, said neighbours discovered Mandiya’s lifeless body after a foul smell began emanating from his apartment and residents became concerned about his prolonged absence. ‎ ‎Speaking during a Senate plenary session, Ningi said he was in Saudi Arabia when he received a telephone call from his son informing him of Mandiya’s death. ‎ ‎He said his son was among those who discovered the former lawmaker’s body on Monday, September 7, 2026. ‎ ‎Recounting the events leading to the discovery, Ningi said a colleague had last seen Mandiya at about 11am on Friday, September 4, before the former senator returned to his residence, where he lived alone. ‎ ‎According to him, Mandiya was preparing to attend the Friday congregational prayer when he reportedly slipped and hit his head after bathing. ‎ ‎“He brought out his cap, his phones, and put them on the bed, and went into the bathroom to take his bath,” Ningi said. ‎ ‎“After taking his bath, when he was out of the bathroom, then he slipped and knocked his head in the bathroom.” ‎ ‎Ningi said nobody realised what had happened until the stench from Mandiya’s apartment began spreading to neighbouring properties. ‎ ‎“For 72 hours, Mr President, nobody knew where Bello Mandiya was,” he told the Senate. ‎ ‎He said the chief imam of Apo also raised the alarm after noticing that Mandiya, who regularly joined other Muslims for the five daily prayers, had been absent for three consecutive days. ‎ ‎The combination of the imam’s concern and the foul smell prompted residents to investigate the apartment. ‎ ‎Ningi said those who went to the residence eventually broke open the door and found Mandiya’s body in the bathroom. ‎ ‎“And there lies Bello Mandiya in the bathroom, lifeless. Seventy-two hours, and that’s a simple tragedy,” he said. ‎ ‎Expressing sadness over the circumstances of his colleague’s death, Ningi said the incident highlighted the uncertainty of life, noting that nobody could predict when death would come. ‎ ‎He also expressed condolences to Mandiya’s family, the people of Katsina State and the constituents he represented in the Senate. ‎ ‎Before his election to the Senate, Mandiya served as chief of staff to former Katsina State Governor Aminu Bello Masari. ‎ ‎He was elected in 2019 on the platform of the All Progressives Congress to represent Katsina South Senatorial District and served in the ninth National Assembly until 2023. He also chaired the Senate Committee on Water Resources. ‎ ‎Mandiya’s death prompted tributes from political leaders and former colleagues, who remembered him for his contributions to public service in Katsina State and at the national level. ‎ ‎Ningi, who said he had known Mandiya since 2002, described the loss as a reminder that political office, wealth and social status could not shield anyone from the fragility of life. ‎ ‎“There is nothing permanent about anything. Nothing permanent about our position, nothing permanent about our wealth,” he said. ‎ ‎He prayed for Allah to grant the deceased eternal rest and give his family the strength to bear the loss. ‎

title: Floor Jansen leaves Nightwish
body:
Jansen has been lead singer of the band since 2013.
Nightwish announced on Thursday that lead singer Floor Jansen is leaving the band.
"After careful consideration, we have, in mutual agreement, decided to part ways. This decision is necessary and important to us and our future ambitions. Thus, we will now pursue those goals in our own separate ways," the band shared in a statement on their Instagram.
Dutch singer Jansen has fronted Nightwish since 2012, first as a touring musician and then as the band's permanent vocalist from 2013 onward. She is the band's third lead singer.
Before Jansen, the band's vocalists were Tarja Turunen and Swedish singer Anette Olzon .
Nightwish, a symphonic metal band, is one of Finland's most internationally successful musical bands.

title: Starshield services for Ukraine’s Defense Forces resume – source
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, sources in the Ministry of Defense said this.
“As of now, Starshield services while in motion have been restored and remain operational. We are confirming this through reports from military units,” a source said.
The Ministry of Defense also assured that it is continuing communications with partners to establish all the reasons for and circumstances surrounding yesterday’s restrictions.
As reported by Ukrinform, the previous day, Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, a technology adviser to the President of Ukraine, said that SpaceX had introduced restrictions overnight on the operating speed of Starlink terminals while in motion, without notifying Ukraine’s Defense Forces in advance.
The Ministry of Defense also reported that the restrictions on Starlink detected overnight had complicated the operation of the Defense Forces’ unmanned systems, logistics and middle-strike capabilities.
Starshield is SpaceX’s specialized military and intelligence program, built on the technology behind its civilian Starlink satellite internet service but developed specifically for the needs of the US government, the Pentagon and American intelligence agencies.

title: ‘You never know tomorrow’ – Anthony Baffoe on contesting for GFA Presidency
body: Former Ghana international Anthony Baffoe has admitted not having the “drive” to contest for the Ghana Football Association presidency but has not ruled out an opportunity in the future. The 61-year-old, who was born in Germany, featured for the Black Stars from 1991 to 1994 before taking up a role at CAF, including becoming its Deputy Secretary General for Football and Development. He has been tipped to run for the GFA presidential position in the upcoming 2027 elections. “I have said no on multiple occasions,” Baffoe told 3Sports. “It does not drive me, but I don’t know what is going to happen in six months, or twelve or twenty-four months. “For now, I don’t see myself there, but you never know tomorrow,” he added. Meanwhile, Kurt Okraku, who has been president of the GFA since 2019, has come under increasing pressure following a slump in form for the Black Stars. Ghana’s latest setback came in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, where the Black Stars suffered a 4-2 home defeat by The Gambia in their second Group C match. The defeat followed the loss to Ivory Coast in their opening qualifier, leaving the nation without a point from their first two matches. The senior national team now sits bottom of Group C, while Ivory Coast and The Gambia lead the group with six points each.

title: Eye-care campaign targets 5,000 in Northern Bahr el Ghazal
body: An eye-care campaign is targeting 5,000 people for treatment, including 1,500 patients requiring cataract surgery, in South Sudan’s Northern Bahr el Ghazal State, health authorities said on Wednesday. The campaign, led by Christian Blind Mission (CBM) in partnership with the Episcopal Church of South Sudan’s Diocese of Wanyjok and the state health ministry, began in Aweil East County on Monday after operations were completed in neighbouring Aweil North County. Dr. Aguer Angok, director of Malualkon Hospital in Aweil East, told Radio Tamazuj that the campaign aims to perform cataract operations on 1,500 patients and provide other eye-care services to an additional 3,500 people across the two counties. “This is the second round of the eye-care campaign led by Christian Blind Mission in collaboration with the Episcopal Church of South Sudan under the Diocese of Wanyjok and the Ministry of Health in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State,” Angok said. He welcomed the initiative, saying it would help extend eye-care services to communities in need. David Mathok Ngong, 76, said he had lived with impaired vision for 12 years and hoped an operation would restore his sight and enable him to resume farming. “I cannot weed the crops on our family farm. I only plough open spaces without seeds or crops,” he said. Another patient, Daniel Garang Aleu, from Rum Mading, expressed relief after undergoing an operation on one eye. He said medical staff had told him that surgery on his other eye was scheduled for Thursday. “I am not even feeling hungry because I am very excited after getting back my sight,” Garang said. The post Eye-care campaign targets 5,000 in Northern Bahr el Ghazal appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Ukraine’s Privatized Air Defense Project Sees First Successes
body:
Ukraine’s Defense Ministry approved a project in November last year to allow certain public and private businesses to defend their own plants in support of the country’s air defense network tackling Russian aerial attacks. The Ministry announced on Wednesday that almost 100 enterprises have joined the project
Of the companies that have come forward, six, including those operating critical infrastructure, have already established around 50 operational air defense groups. These employ a variety of interceptor drones and automated turrets equipped with large-caliber machine guns.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The private initiative is intended to be part of a multi-level air defense system operating under the relevant air commands of the Ukrainian Air Force (UAF) that coordinate air defense activity where they are based. The company and the military coordinate the areas of operation, allocation of personnel and the necessary equipment, weapons and other means.
The Defense Ministry announced that, as of Oct. 14, 2026, these groups have destroyed more than 60 air targets, including Russian reconnaissance and attack drones . The first confirmed shoot downs of aerial targets, including a jet-powered “Shahed” drone, were in the Kharkiv region in March and April this year as reported by the then Defense Minister, Mykhailo Fedorov.
Along with the groups that are already performing combat missions a large number are at various stages of training, acquiring the necessary weaponry and preparing to deploy.
While several of the volunteer enterprises have funded the purchase of weapons themselves, others are permitted to request the temporary provision of weapons and ammunition from the AFU command.

title: Comoros-flagged tanker YARA J struck by drone in Romanian waters, fire breaks out – media
body:
The Comoros-flagged tanker YARA J was struck by an unidentified drone approximately 10 nautical miles from the Romanian city of Sulina, resulting in a fire on board that was subsequently brought under control by the crew, Romanian public broadcaster Radio România Constanța reported.
According to data from the Bulgarian publication Maritime.bg, a distress signal from the vessel was received at around 20:00 on October 14. There were 17 crew members on board from Syria, India, and Iran. According to preliminary data, none of the crew members were injured.
It is noted that following reports of the incident, the Romanian Agency for Life Saving at Sea (ARSVOM) dispatched the rescue vessel SAR Apollo to the tanker.
According to Maritime.bg, the YARA J is currently proceeding under its own power to the port of Constanța.
The Romanian public broadcaster specifies that the tanker had arrived from Turkey and was scheduled to enter the Sulina Canal. At the time of the incident, the vessel was stationary in the area, awaiting favorable weather conditions for passage.
In turn, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bulgaria expressed solidarity with Romania regarding the fire on board the tanker Yara J in the Black Sea.
"The recurring incidents affecting commercial shipping in the region are a matter of deep concern," the Bulgarian MFA reported on the social platform X.
The ministry emphasized that under circumstances where details are still being clarified, coordination between Bulgaria and Romania is essential to guarantee the safe passage of merchant vessels in the Black Sea.
The Bulgarian MFA also added that this issue will be one of the key priorities during upcoming discussions in the European Council.
As reported, Romanian President Nicușor Dan and Iliyana Yotova agreed on close cooperation between Romania and Bulgaria to introduce more effective countermeasures against drones within the EU and NATO following drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea near the Bulgarian coast.
According to him, during a telephone conversation, the parties also discussed other incidents affecting shipping and infrastructure in Romanian waters.
Earlier, on October 5, Romanian media reported that the Turkish vessel Royad Mammadov, carrying a cargo of grain and previously calling at the Ukrainian port of Izmail, was struck by a drone in the Black Sea near Peskerash oil platform, after which a fire broke out on board and the vessel sank; two people died, while 11 crew members were rescued.
Also on October 12, near the Bulgarian coast, the merchant vessel Chelsea 3, sailing under the flag of Malta and registered in the port of Odesa, was attacked by three aerial drones.
On October 6, in the same area, two merchant vessels were struck by aerial and maritime drones in the exclusive economic zone of Bulgaria in the Black Sea, approximately 70 nautical miles east of Byala. The vessel ALFA WATAN, sailing under the flag of Togo, sank, and its crew of 12 Syrian citizens went missing. Another vessel, ABLE, flying the flag of Palau, sustained damage, after which a fire broke out on board.

title: Ghanaian President: Govts Must Not Shift Unemployment Burden To Graduates
body: Governments in Nigeria and across African continent must take responsibility for creating an enabling environment for businesses rather than shifting the burden of unemployment to young graduates, President John Dramani Mahama of Ghana has said. Mahama said while graduates must adapt to technological changes and create economic opportunities, governments must provide stable institutions, quality infrastructure and relevant education to enable enterprises to thrive. He spoke at the maiden convocation of the University of Offa in Kwara State. Represented by his Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, the president said the graduating students were entering a period of extraordinary change. He said Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital technologies and climate change were reshaping professions, markets and economic planning across the world. Mahama urged the graduates to develop the skills to identify problems, devise solutions and create value, rather than depend solely on certificates to secure paid employment. “My first message to the graduating class is simple: Your certificate is a foundation. It is not a finish line,” he said. He stressed, however, that “encouraging graduates to become innovative and entrepreneurial should not absolve governments of their responsibility to tackle unemployment. “Governments have a responsibility to create an enabling environment in which enterprises can flourish.” The president said governments must provide the necessary conditions for businesses to grow and generate decent jobs, while young people must continue learning, adapting to change and creating value. He said the changing global economy required graduates to combine human judgement, creativity and integrity with the intelligent use of technology. “Do not fear technology. Learn to use it responsibly and intelligently. The future will favour those who combine human judgement, creativity and integrity with the intelligent use of technology,” he said. Mahama also urged the graduates to look beyond Nigeria for business opportunities, citing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as an avenue for building enterprises and partnerships across the continent. “Your market is not only Offa, Kwara or Nigeria, it’s Africa and beyond. Go and build businesses. Build institutions. Build solutions. Build bridges between people and ideas. Create opportunities. Serve your communities. Lead with integrity,” he said. He called on governments, financial institutions, universities and the private sector to improve access to affordable finance, infrastructure and markets for young entrepreneurs. He warned that encouraging enterprise without providing the necessary support would leave young people without the tools to succeed. “It will be paradoxical for us to tell young Africans to become entrepreneurs but deny them access to finance, infrastructure and opportunity,” he said. The president also urged universities to move beyond producing graduates who could pass examinations by integrating entrepreneurship, digital skills, innovation and critical thinking into their programmes. “Africa does not merely need intelligent people. It needs trustworthy people, those who honour their agreements,” he said. On the relationship between Ghana and Nigeria, Mahama said the two countries shared historical, commercial and cultural ties that could support stronger economic cooperation. He urged their universities, businesses and young people to deepen collaboration and pursue opportunities across national borders, stressing that Africa would advance faster through cooperation. Earlier, Vice-Chancellor, Professor Kazeem Alagbe Gbolagade, said the university produced eight First Class graduates out of 140 graduands. Fifty-four graduates earned Second Class Upper degrees, 76 obtained Second Class Lower degrees, while two graduated with Third Class honours. The university, licensed in 2021, commenced academic activities in 2022 with two faculties and 10 programmes. It has since expanded to four faculties and 17 academic programmes, with plans to introduce Law, Theatre Arts and Public Health. Gbolagade said student enrolment had grown from 81 in the 2022/2023 academic session to 640 newly admitted students in the 2026/2027 session. He attributed the growth to the institution’s emphasis on academic excellence, adherence to its academic calendar, information technology and entrepreneurship. He also disclosed that the university was helping students register their businesses with the Corporate Affairs Commission, with plans to introduce start-up grants for graduates to encourage them to become job creators rather than job seekers. However, he identified inadequate infrastructure as a major challenge and appealed for support to develop additional student accommodation, a library complex, a 1,000-capacity lecture theatre and other facilities. Addressing the graduating students, Mahama urged them to use their education to build businesses, strengthen institutions, develop solutions and create opportunities for their communities.

title: US weighs relief for sanctioned shadow fleet tankers, days after freeing Russian diesel
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); The Trump administration is weighing looser sanctions on shadow fleet tankers that have hauled oil from Russia, Iran, and Venezuela, a US official said on 14 October, Reuters reported . An industry research group expects the change to do little for freight rates. With Reuters calling high fuel prices a risk for Trump before the 3 November midterms, Washington has already eased sanctions on Russian oil and diesel this year and is now looking at the ships blacklisted for hauling sanctioned cargoes. In March, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a waiver on Russian oil at sea would bring Moscow no significant financial benefit, yet Russia’s seaborne oil income jumped by $890 million in the week to 15 March, Bloomberg data showed. “Legal oil” on blacklisted ships The talks center on letting “legal oil” sail on previously sanctioned vessels, the official said. Only crude or fuel free of US sanctions would qualify, not Russian or Iranian oil. Washington wants more crude and refined products moving out of the Gulf, the official added. Companies would need US Treasury approval to use the ships. Explore further Ukraine is going back to hitting Russian oil after its Trump-pressured pause, during which Kyiv got no US warnings of incoming ballistic missiles Research group Energy Aspects said US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, in a video to the World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh, tied the easing to record freight rates. Those rates hit records after the Iran and Ukraine wars drove up inflation and left US crude too costly for Asian refiners, Reuters said. Energy Aspects itself expects the easing to do little for freight rates, since most tankers sanctioned over Russian or Venezuelan links have kept trading for the past three months. The Energy Department said any relief would do nothing to help Russia ship its oil or refined products. Treasury referred questions to the Energy Department. Yet Reuters noted that both departments could face pressure to let these vessels carry Russian diesel, given Trump’s push to get it onto world markets fast. Britain is pushing the other way. UK finance minister John Healey urged counterparts at International Monetary Fund meetings in Bangkok on 15 October to keep tough sanctions on Russia, “especially a tighter ban on shipping services” that keep Putin’s shadow fleet operating. Diesel license criticism and an unconfirmed ceasefire On 9 October, the US Treasury issued a license clearing Russian-origin diesel trade until 7 April 2027. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told reporters it was a weak decision unworthy of Ukraine’s partners. Democratic Senators Jeanne Shaheen, Chuck Schumer, and Elizabeth Warren called it a “total betrayal of Ukraine.” Republican Senator Thom Tillis said there is “a legitimate case for saying the president’s not following the law.” Explore further “He thinks Ukraine is a weak link and that it needs to be squeezed into giving in”: diplomat on why Trump pressures Kyiv, not Moscow Trump then pressed Kyiv to spare Russian refineries and declared an “energy ceasefire” on 11 October. A White House official told Axios it covers only oil refineries. Neither side confirmed a similar announcement Trump made in mid-September, AAP reported . Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters on 13 October that contacts on the ceasefire were continuing and referred further questions to Trump, Russian newspaper Vedomosti reported . He claimed the diesel deal was “a very mutually beneficial item of Russian-American cooperation” that serves the interests of Russia, the US, and world energy markets, Russian newspaper Kommersant reported . Read also America has sided with Russia against Ukraine. Europe should stop pretending and build a coalition against Russia, China, and even the US “It finances an economy geared toward total war”—Ukraine’s third president on the Russian diesel Washington just cleared Bipartisan US senators say Trump’s Russian diesel deal conflicts with 2022 ban, as he presses Kyiv to spare Russian refineries

title: Finland's appeal court cuts Simon Ekpa's terrorism sentence to four years
body:
Ekpa was convicted last year of participating in a terrorist organisation and publicly inciting crimes for terrorist purposes.
The Court of Appeal has upheld the decision by Päijät-Häme District Court last year to find Simon Ekpa guilty of terrorism-related charges.
However, the appeal court reduced the amount of time Ekpa will spend behind bars from six years to four.
Ekpa, who moved to Finland from his native Nigeria in 2007, was found by the district court to have participated in a terrorist organisation and to have publicly incited crimes for terrorist purposes.
The charges related to Ekpa's alleged activities aimed at re-establishing an independent state in the Biafra region of southeastern Nigeria, which was briefly independent in the late 1960s.
In its verdict, the district court said that Ekpa had used his significant social media following to stoke tensions in the region between August 2021 and November 2024.
Ekpa appealed this ruling, and although the Court of Appeal found him guilty of the same offences, it reduced the severity of his sentence because it took into consideration the circumstances surrounding his actions — noting that the current situation in the Biafra region closely resembled, but did not meet the definition of, a civil war.
Ekpa had argued in court that, because of the political turmoil in Biafra, his involvement was not carried out with terrorist intent.
The prosecutor in the case had also lodged an appeal against the district court's decision, arguing the amount of prison time did not reflect the seriousness of Ekpa's offences.
The 41-year-old Ekpa is a long-term resident of Lahti and once served on the city's council, representing the National Coalition Party.
The court of appeal's verdict is not final, meaning it can be appealed to a higher court.

title: Top Russian diplomat meets with his Turkish counterpart in Baku
body:
BAKU, October 15. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov is holding a meeting with his Turkish counterpart Hakan Fidan on the sidelines of the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku, Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said.
"Talks between the Russian and Turkish foreign ministers on the sidelines of the CICA summit in Baku," the diplomat wrote on her Telegram channel, accompanying the post with a photo.

title: Ukraine War: Does Europe Need a New Direction?
body:
US President Donald Trump has struck a diesel deal with Russian leader Vladimir Putin while the EU is struggling to reach a consensus on the next package of sanctions against Moscow. At the same time, voices within the EU are increasingly calling into question aid for Ukraine. Commentators ask how Europe should position itself to find an appropriate response.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Politiken analyses the role of special interests in the haggling over EU sanctions against Russia (Denmark):
“During the negotiations on the EU’s 21st sanctions package this summer, Germany, for example, blocked a ban on Russian Alaska pollock. Why? Because it could jeopardise German production of fish fingers and put jobs at risk. Greece secured a provision allowing Greek shipping companies to continue transporting Russian liquefied natural gas to third countries even though imports to the EU will be banned as of next year. … Austria, France, and Italy pursued other special interests. All this makes it easier for Donald Trump to denounce the Europeans’ hypocrisy. His latest gestures towards Putin should therefore also serve as a wake-up call for Europeans themselves.”
Don’t lose sight of the battle against corruption
The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (Germany) takes a worried look at the situation in Germany:
“The Ukrainian government is partly to blame for the waning support for Ukraine in Germany. It is dragging out reforms while at the same time expecting rapid EU accession. No voter or taxpayer will take kindly to a country demanding billions of euros when it is facing new corruption investigations. ... We can see in Saxony-Anhalt what lies ahead if the AfD , either alone or in alliance with the pro-Moscow BSW, gains positions of power. A government has yet to be formed there, but the two parties have already jointly tabled a symbolic motion opposing sanctions against Russia and aid to Ukraine.”
Europe can and must respond, La Stampa (Italy)ninsists:
“Most of the Russian diesel is loaded there [at Primorsk] and must be transported via the Baltic Sea, passing a number of EU countries in most of which these tankers are now subject to sanctions. EU countries and the UK have been tightening controls for a year now and could expand these measures further by seizing shadow fleet vessels that are subject to sanctions, and, for those not under sanctions, looking for other grounds to intervene.”
Sanctions against Russia are ineffective, argues columnist Karol Lovaš in Új Szó (Slovakia) :
“As a mocking statue of Trump was unveiled in the European Parliament, the US President was striking a deal with Putin. Like a true businessman – in his own interests and in the interests of the world. What is the European Union doing for its own good and for the good of the world? What is it doing for Europeans? ... All we are left with are the sanctions, the war in Ukraine and our own mistakes. ... I wonder who will be the first to say out loud that it was a mistake to cut ourselves off from Russian raw materials? What have the sanctions against Russia achieved, apart from creating an existential dependence on the US?”

title: Ukrainian parliament passes key bill on international parcel taxes
body:
Editor's note: The story has been updated to include comments from Ukrainian officials.
Ukraine's parliament passed a bill on taxing e-commerce and international parcels on Oct. 15, meeting a condition linked to international financial assistance after missing earlier deadlines.
The bill passed its final vote with 252 lawmakers in favour after facing criticism from some lawmakers. Parliament had previously failed to advance the bill and sent it back for revision.
Its adoption is linked to Ukraine receiving the International Monetary Fund's ( IMF ) tranche of around $700 million and the EU tranche of 3.7 billion euros ($4.1 billion) in macro-financial assistance.
The legislation introduces the value-added tax (VAT) on international parcels worth up to 150 euros ($168), which are currently tax-exempt. Lawmakers also backed new customs regulations for international mail and express shipments.
The changes could take effect on July 1, 2027, but only after a separate government decision.
Finance Minister Serhii Marchenko said the tranches would be disbursed to Ukraine’s state budget "in the coming weeks."
"The adopted bills will ensure a level playing field for Ukrainian businesses and allow the state budget to raise an additional Hr 10 billion ($222 million) annually to fund the Armed Forces," he added.
The parliament repeatedly failed to pass some of the conditions set by Ukraine's partners throughout 2026, amid widespread unpopularity of the changes. Most toxic was a package of new taxes, including a tax on small imported parcels, and a tax on income received from digital platforms, such as Uber.
In recent days, lawmakers have advanced several key bills tied to Western aid, with $29.5 billion in funding at stake if parliament and the government fail to meet the required conditions.
Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said on Oct. 15 he hoped lawmakers would maintain the pace of passing bills.
"The results of this plenary week give us all reason to be optimistic, but there is still a lot of work ahead," Koretskyi wrote on social media.
"We count on the same constructive cooperation in the coming plenary weeks to ensure that all necessary decisions are adopted on time and Ukraine receives the full amount of international financial aid."

title: Slovakia to hold talks with Ukraine, revive economic meetings with Russia
body:
Slovakia's Prime Minister Robert Fico announced on Oct. 14 that the Slovak and the Ukrainian governments will hold their next round of talks in the western Ukrainian city of Lviv on Nov. 5.
Separately, Fico also confirmed talks with Russia on Nov. 25 under the framework of a joint economic commission, a format that was suspended after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Slovakia 's populist, Moscow-friendly leader framed this outreach as part of Bratislava's foreign "policy toward all four cardinal directions."
Fico noted that the upcoming Slovak-Ukrainian talks will be the fourth meeting of this format, with the last one held in the eastern Slovak city of Kosice last October.
The negotiations are to focus on expanding border crossings, providing humanitarian assistance to Ukraine, and establishing a school for Ukrainian children in Bratislava.
Fico last visited Ukraine in September 2025 for talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky. He was also scheduled to attend the inaugural Carpathian summit on Sept. 18 in Ukraine's Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, but ultimately skipped the event for health reasons.
Speaking to Slovak lawmakers before his departure for the European Council, Fico said that EU leaders are set to hold talks on a potential next loan for Ukraine and said Bratislava would not take part.
Fico's government has declined to participate in the EU's 90-billion-euro ($101 billion) loan for Kyiv adopted in April, but has not blocked it either and has voiced support for Ukraine's accession talks.
At the same time, the Slovak leader has consistently criticized energy sanctions against Russia and military aid to Ukraine, cutting off arms deliveries from Slovak army stocks. He was the only EU leader to visit the Russian capital for the May 9 Victory Day celebrations in 2025 and this year, meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Fico agreed with Putin on restarting the intergovernmental commission during the May celebrations in 2025, the Slovak newspaper Sme reported .
The last meeting of the commission, focused on economic and scientific cooperation between the two countries, was held in November 2021, months before the start of the all-out war in Ukraine.
The Slovak leader did not provide further details about the upcoming talks with the Russian side.

title: Zelensky: Replacing Me Won’t Change Ukraine’s Need for Defense
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky pushed back against US President Donald Trump’s call for a new Ukrainian leader, saying any successor would continue defending Ukraine and that choosing a president was a decision for Ukrainians.
Speaking on Piers Morgan Uncensored , Zelensky rejected the suggestion that his departure would resolve the obstacles to ending Russia’s war against Ukraine.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
He said a future president, whether a man or a woman, would still have a responsibility to protect the country.
“I am sure that a new man or woman will defend our country, because this is our home,” Zelensky said.
His response challenged Trump’s argument that a change in Ukraine’s leadership could produce an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump said on Saturday, Oct. 10 that Ukraine needed a new president capable of reaching a deal, accusing Zelensky of passing up opportunities to end the war.
Morgan put Trump’s comments directly to Zelensky, telling him: “He wants you gone.”
Zelensky responded that Russia’s occupation of Ukrainian territory had begun before he took office. When he became president, Crimea and parts of the Donbas region were already occupied, as his predecessor had also confronted Russia.
Zelensky’s argument was that Ukraine’s resistance reflected the country’s interests rather than the position of one president. According to him, a successor might defend Ukraine better or worse, but would nevertheless defend it, rejecting the idea that foreign figures should determine who holds office.
His removal, he said, would be “a decision for our people, not Trump, not Musk, not anyone else.”
Asked whether he intended to resign, Zelensky answered: “No, of course not. This is my responsibility.”
He said holding a presidential election was currently nearly impossible because Russian attacks continued every hour.
On Monday, Oct. 12, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov claimed that Trump had suggested Ukraine choose a new president because Zelensky was unwilling to make the decisions needed to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.
“Trump said that, in his opinion, it is time for a new president,” Peskov said.
“Why? Because the president of Ukraine must make very responsible and very difficult decisions to stop this war.”
Peskov accused Zelensky of failing to demonstrate the political will to take those steps.
“Either Zelensky takes on that responsibility and demonstrates that political will, or he does not,” he said. “So far, he has not.”
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: 25 trainees graduate from vocational training programme in Rumbek
body: Twenty-five trainees have completed a three-month technical and vocational education and training (TVET) programme at Riak-Dor Vocational Training Centre in Rumbek, Lakes State, after receiving instruction in hairdressing, computer skills and construction. The programme was organised by the Disabled Association for Rehabilitation and Development (DARD) with funding from Oxfam. DARD Executive Director Cipuounyuc Awur congratulated the graduates on completing the training and urged them to use their newly acquired skills to pursue employment and other economic opportunities. “Today’s event is not the end of the training but the beginning of your journey into the labour market,” Awur said on Wednesday. He said vocational skills could help graduates contribute to national development, improve their livelihoods and support economic growth. Awur added that the centre aims to ensure graduates acquired practical skills and the tools needed to apply their training. Nyankor John, a hairdressing trainer at the centre, said the programme had equipped participants with practical knowledge they could use in their future work. She thanked DARD and Oxfam for supporting the programme, saying the graduates intended to put their newly acquired skills into practice. Charles Anau Cirillo Majok, director general at the Lakes State Ministry of General Education and Instruction, said vocational training is important in a country where formal employment opportunities were limited. He said graduates could use their skills to establish businesses, provide services and contribute to local economic development rather than depend solely on government jobs. Majok also thanked DARD and Oxfam for supporting the programme, adding that South Sudan had a national TVET policy aimed at expanding vocational training opportunities. He said the government is working to strengthen and equip vocational training centres to ensure trainees acquired the skills needed to become self-reliant and support their families. Makuei Goljok, acting director general at the Lakes State Ministry of Labour, Public Service and Human Resource Development, said skills-based training is important for economic growth, youth employment and household incomes. He urged graduates to seek opportunities that matched their qualifications, including computer-related work and hairdressing. Goljok said the state government would engage relevant ministries, including the Ministry of Trade, to explore ways to support graduates seeking to establish businesses and practise their trades. He also encouraged the graduates to enter the labour market and apply their skills, saying vocational training could help communities become less dependent on government employment and external assistance. The post 25 trainees graduate from vocational training programme in Rumbek appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: New Dubai footbridge and Sharjah buses to improve access to Etihad Rail stations
body: New transport links in Dubai and Sharjah are making it easier to reach Etihad Rail stations, with a pedestrian footbridge opening in Dubai on Thursday and three connecting bus routes launching in Sharjah. Passengers can now switch more smoothly between Metro and train services in Dubai using the new footbridge linking Jumeirah Golf Estates station with Etihad Rail’s Al Yalayis Station . Before the elevated 400-metre footbridge opened, a shuttle bus operated between the stations. Passengers can use a Nol One-Day Pass ticket, which offers unlimited travel on the emirate's public transport network and is valid until midnight. Using digital QR codes on phones eliminates the need for a single-use red paper Nol ticket. In the coming years, Dubai Al Yalayis Station will become a transport super-hub with an interchange between the Metro Red and Gold lines planned for 2032. The station opened to passengers on September 30 for the first rail service to Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and Fujairah. Due to increased demand, extra services were added on some weekends. Variable pricing has been introduced on several routes due to demand, with some tickets increasing by up to Dh69. More bus services, more links The F38 bus also serves Dubai's rail station, operating a circular route to Dubai Sports City and Dubai Production City. Sharjah 's Road and Transport Authority on Wednesday announced three new bus routes connecting Sharjah's first rail station in Al Dhaid. ER1 connects Al Madam Bus Station to Al Dhaid Station, stopping in Mleiha and Al Dhaid and taking one hour. ER2 connects Al Sajaa Bus Station with Al Dhaid Station, stopping in Al Batayeh and Al Dhaid, and takes about 43 minutes. ER3 links Jubail Bus Station in Sharjah city with the rail station on a non-stop service, taking about one hour and 42 minutes. These services are vital for connecting some of the smaller towns in Sharjah emirate that previously had limited public transport connectivity to other emirates. Bus journeys are timed to train arrivals and departures, and you can buy tickets with cash or a Sayer Card.

title: Thursday, 15 October 2026
body: Regional Russia’s Justice Ministry designated another Russian organisation in Georgia as undesirable. Tbilisi-based cultural space Frame has announced it is immediately closed after the announcement, which came after it was declared a foreign agent in February. It has urged followers not to comment on or share its social media posts, or mention the organisation in their own publications, citing potential legal consequences under Russian law. Russia’s customs service says they found $425,000 hidden in a car belonging to a driver heading to Georgia. According to information released by the agency yesterday, the money was discovered during a customs inspection at the Russian side of the Upper Lars border crossing. Armenia Civil Contract MP Lusine Badalyan was refused entry to Russia to participate in a CIS (Commonwealth of Independent States) committee meeting. Badalyan claims no reason was given and Moscow has not commented. The Armenian government recognised obtaining 100% of shares in Electric Networks of Armenia, belonging to Russian-Armenian tycoon and opposition figure Samvel Karapetyan, as an ‘overriding’ public interest. Azerbaijan Ilkin Huseynov, has reportedly been detained in connection with the ‘Let Leyli Go to School’ initiative. Reports of the activist and artist’s arrest came after the website, which sought to organise teaching for those boycotting school, had been live for just one day. Fellow activist Javid Agha reported that unidentified individuals arrived at Huseynov’s home at around 4pm on 14 October. Turkish President’s Chief Advisor Hasan Nuri Yaşar stated in a post on X that there are forces seeking to drive a wedge between the two countries and that caution is necessary. Baku’s media and broadcasting council has previously claimed that individuals in Turkey are spreading misinformation as protests continue against the ban on hijabs in schools. On Wednesday, Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev held bilateral meetings with the presidents of Israel, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan ahead of the 7th CICA Summit in Baku. During his meeting with Israeli President Isaac Herzog, the two leaders discussed bilateral relations, strategic cooperation, and regional and international developments. Talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev focused on strengthening strategic partnership, expanding trade, and advancing cooperation in energy, transport, logistics, and investment. In his meeting with Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, Aliyev discussed deepening bilateral ties and enhancing cooperation within regional and international organisations. Georgia The prison guard seen wearing a glove in a video released of prisoner Giorgi Davitadze, who has accused prison staff of rape, no longer works in the penitentiary system. The Special Penitentiary Service told OC Media that Giorgi Varabiovi left his job voluntarily in March 2026. Georgian citizens are among the foreign nationals whose possible involvement is being investigated in a cryptocurrency investment fraud and money laundering case in Moldova. Eight people have been placed in pre-trial detention, the country’s Prosecutor’s Office has announced. Georgian opposition politician Zurab Japaridze was detained yesterday at an airport in Turkey while travelling to Brussels. The Alliance of Liberals and Democrats for Europe (ALDE) reported that Japaridze was held in a cell and had his passport and luggage confiscated. The organisation added that he would be returned to Georgia on Thursday. Georgia and seven other countries have signed a new Council of Europe treaty aimed at making it easier to seize assets obtained through criminal activity, including cryptocurrency. The protocol was signed in Strasbourg yesterday , with Georgia among the first eight countries to sign it. Abkhazia The Academy of Sciences of Abkhazia, Abkhazian State University and the Russian State Social University have signed a cooperation agreement. In 2027, the Russian State Social University will offer applicants from Abkhazia 10 state-funded places, some of which will be allocated for study at the college affiliated with the university. South Ossetia Around 300 teachers in South Ossetia will receive one-off payments from Russia under an order issued by Russian President Vladimir Putin. This became known following a meeting between Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Chernyshenko and South Ossetian President Marat Kambolov. The North Caucasus In Ingushetia, the Malgobek department of the republic’s Investigative Committee responded to a complaint with a quote from Felix Dzerzhinsky. Dzerzhinsky founded the VChK (also known as the Cheka), the first iteration of the Soviet secret police and his quote — ‘the fact that you are free is not your merit, but our failure’ — was sent in a letter to Ibragim Tochiev, who was beaten by security personnel. Idris Israilov, a former investigator from Chechnya, has been appointed head of a garrison military court in Ukraine’s partially-occupied Zaporizhzhia region. The appointment was made by a decree signed by Russian President Vladimir Putin. Nadyrkhan Kadirhanov, a resident of Daghestan, has been found guilty of murdering MMA fighter Magomedrasul Mutaev. He was sentenced to four years, but released from the courtroom after the court took into account the time he had spent in pre-trial detention. On 31 January 2024, Mutaev sustained several gunshot wounds near his home in Makhachkala and died on the way to hospital. The murder was motivated by Kadirhanov’s personal animosity towards Mutaev: witnesses say Kadirhanov had been subjected to humiliation and abuse by the fighter. Russia’s Supreme Court has banned the followers of Batalkhadzhi Belkhoroev, designating it a terrorist organisation. According to the Prosecutor General’s Office, members of the Batalkhadzhi community were involved in terrorist attacks in Ingushetia and elsewhere, including the attack on Crocus City Hall. The Batalkhadzhi followers are adherents of the Sufi Sheikh Batalkhadzhi Belkhoroev, who lived in Ingushetia in the 19th and early 20th centuries. The Kizlyar District Court has sentenced the unnamed imam of a local mosque to nine years in prison for strangling his wife in December 2025. According to the court he then buried her body before turning himself into the police seven weeks later. For ease of reading, we choose not to use qualifiers such as ‘de facto’, ‘unrecognised’, or ‘partially recognised’ when discussing institutions or political positions within Abkhazia, Nagorno-Karabakh, and South Ossetia. This does not imply a position on their status.

title: Obuasi SHTS head accused of sexually abusing students is NDC Juaben secretary seeking chairmanship
body: JoyNews investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni says the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School in the Ashanti Region, who has been suspended over sexual abuse allegations against female students, is a serving constituency secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and an aspirant for the chairmanship position. Speaking on Joy FM on Thursday, October 15, about excerpts from his latest documentary, Manasseh said he learnt of the headmaster’s political position while filming in the community. According to him, the headmaster intends to contest the chairmanship at the party’s constituency delegates’ conference, expected before the end of the year. “This man [the headmaster], we are told, is the Juabeng Constituency Secretary of the governing National Democratic Congress, and there are posters of him wanting to contest for the constituency chairman,” he claimed. Manasseh expressed alarm at what he described as widespread knowledge of the allegations among residents, including NDC members, coupled with an apparent reluctance to speak publicly about them. He said his interactions during the investigation suggested that the allegations were widely known within the community. “So, a former NDC constituency executive who spoke to me, Frederick Addai, says that, anytime the issue [the alleged sexual assault] came up, some members of the party tried to come together and tried to calm tempers and get the issues resolved,” he said. Manasseh also confirmed that although various people in the school as well as the Ghana Education Service in the district and region knew about the reports, they did not take adequate steps to act on them. He suggested that the headmaster, who is in a position of power, appears to be enjoying some protection from people in high places. The headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, is the subject of the documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, which examines allegations of sexual abuse involving female students. On October 13, Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu directed the Ghana Education Service to suspend Mr Abdulai pending a full investigation. The Minister also requested an investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department of the Ghana Police Service.

title: What Makes a Great KotlinConf Proposal?
body: The KotlinConf 2027 Call for Papers is now open! We invite developers from across the Kotlin community to bring their ideas, experiences, and expertise to the stage in Kraków. Do you have a Kotlin lesson or discovery that could help other developers? Perhaps you solved a difficult technical problem, introduced Kotlin into an existing codebase, built something unexpected, or learned valuable lessons from an approach that did not go according to plan. That experience could become a KotlinConf talk. Submit your proposal However, turning an idea into a convincing conference proposal can be challenging, especially if you’ve never submitted one before. How do you know whether your experience is worth sharing? What do reviewers notice first? How detailed should your abstract be? And how can you make a familiar topic stand out? To help you prepare your submission, we asked Kotlin developers, developer advocates, experienced speakers, and KotlinConf program committee members what makes a strong proposal. Alongside practical advice for shaping your title, abstract, and takeaways, we have added a new section answering an especially important question: What do reviewers notice first when they open a proposal? First-time speaker? Submit your idea anyway! It’s easy to assume that a KotlinConf talk must begin with a groundbreaking discovery, a major production system, or years of speaking experience. In reality, a valuable talk can begin with a simple idea or a lesson learned while solving an everyday development problem. You don’t need to know everything about Kotlin – you need something useful to share and a clear idea of who it could help. Pamela Hill-Galloway. Developer Advocate, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , LinkedIn Submit your idea anyway! There have been some wildly successful talks at KotlinConf that started out as just a simple idea. If you’re unsure whether your topic would interest anyone, discuss it with the people around you. Explain the idea to colleagues, friends, members of a user group, or people in the Kotlin community. Their questions and reactions can help you understand which parts are most valuable. Marcin Mycek. Product Manager, Kotlin Build Tools LinkedIn If you can find one interested person, there are probably more! If you can find at least two people around you who find the topic interesting and can listen for more than five minutes, it is already a decent candidate. Previous conference experience is not required. A clear, authentic proposal based on something you understand and care about can be more compelling than a polished proposal with little substance behind it. Start with the story you want to tell Before writing the title or opening the submission form, identify the central story behind your talk. “A talk about coroutines” or “a session about Kotlin Multiplatform” describes a subject, but it doesn’t explain what makes the session valuable. Ask yourself: What problem, question, or opportunity did you encounter? Why was it important or difficult? What did you try? What surprised you? What succeeded and what did not? What did you learn that other developers could apply? Your story doesn’t need to come from a large company or a system used by millions of people. A focused lesson from a small project can be just as useful if it offers an original insight or explains a difficult subject clearly. Try summarizing the idea in one sentence, for example: This talk will show [audience] how we [solved or explored something], what we learned, and how they can apply those lessons. If you can’t complete that sentence clearly, the idea may need a little more development before you start writing the proposal. What do reviewers notice first? The title may be the first line reviewers read, but the overall level of care quickly becomes visible. Reviewers consider not only whether the topic is interesting, but also whether the speaker can explain it clearly. A thoughtful title, focused description, concrete takeaways, and careful formatting show that you have spent time developing your idea. Pamela Hill-Galloway. Developer Advocate, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , LinkedIn I can sum it up by saying that the care you take in writing the proposal is probably more obvious than people think. If I can see that you took the time to come up with a catchy or descriptive title that works well with the content, I am more comfortable giving you a thumbs-up to speak at KotlinConf. If your description is so short or so long, or so clearly AI-generated, that you cannot express your idea clearly and neatly, I will probably not vote positively for your talk. This doesn’t mean you need to use complicated language or create a perfect marketing pitch. It means giving reviewers enough information to understand your idea and showing that the proposal represents your own experience and voice. Marcin Moskała’s Taming Asynchronous Beasts: Debugging and Performance Tuning in a Coroutine World provides a good example of a precise promise: “You’ll learn how to effectively use built-in tools, recognize problematic patterns, and implement proven optimization strategies.” Write a clear and informative title A strong title should give reviewers, and eventually attendees, an accurate idea of what the talk will cover. Creativity can make a title memorable, but clarity should come first. Avoid titles that rely entirely on a joke, reference, or metaphor without explaining the subject. Pamela Hill-Galloway. Developer Advocate, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , LinkedIn A carefully-selected title can make all the difference! Audience members often lack the time or attention span to read more than the title when deciding whether to attend a talk. Prefer clarity over a catchy or fun title that doesn’t give a good idea of what the talk is about in a nutshell. Compare the following title examples: Too broad: Our Multiplatform Journey More informative: What We Learned Migrating Our Mobile App to Kotlin Multiplatform Too vague: Coroutines Gone Wild More informative: Debugging Coroutine Performance Problems in Production Too general: Building Better APIs More informative: Designing Type-Safe Kotlin APIs That Are Difficult to Misuse A good title usually communicates at least two of the following: The main topic The problem or question The context in which it was explored The practical benefit for attendees The expected experience level You can still use humor or wordplay, but make sure the title does not hide what the session is actually about. Build your abstract around a clear journey Your abstract doesn’t need to contain your entire presentation. However, it should provide enough detail for reviewers to understand the problem, the direction of the talk, and its value. Two or three focused paragraphs will usually communicate more than either a single vague sentence or a very long description covering every detail. Sebastian Sellmair. Software Developer and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , YouTube Talking at KotlinConf is a great experience and a huge achievement for any Kotlin developer. While choosing a great title, having highly polished animations, and curating high-quality memes might enhance your talk, the most important thing is having a story worth telling. Do you have something novel and technically interesting to present? Can you break down a topic in a way that is engaging and truly fun? Can you inspire fellow developers? Márton Braun. Developer Advocate, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , LinkedIn While we don’t need a full script for your talk as the abstract, we’re also unlikely to accept a talk where the abstract is just a single sentence. Two or three paragraphs are usually enough to provide meaningful detail. A simple structure can help: The context Introduce the situation and the audience likely to recognize it. The challenge Explain the problem, limitation, or question that motivated the work. Jodie Burchell. Developer Advocate and Data Scientist LinkedIn , Mastodon , BlueSky Hook your audience by telling them the problem you’re going to be solving. People love mystery books for a reason, and that’s because they build up a bit of suspense before they jump into the solution. A great proposal will do the same thing. The approach Describe what you explored, implemented, compared, or discovered. The outcome Clarify what attendees will learn and how they can use it. A strong takeaway can be as concrete as the one from Tadeas Kriz’s Dependencies and Kotlin/Native : “Learn how native dependencies interact, how they are loaded, and the unexpected complexities of the native world.” Chantal Loncle. Software Developer, Exposed, JetBrains LinkedIn Avoid vague promises. Instead, use action verbs and specific outcomes to describe the exact capabilities and transformations the audience will gain. Will they leave your talk feeling that their time was well spent? If so, what practical knowledge, immediately applicable skills, or high-value tools will they take with them? For example: Maintaining separate Android and iOS implementations allowed our teams to move independently, but it also resulted in duplicated business logic and inconsistent behavior between the applications. In this session, we’ll examine how we introduced Kotlin Multiplatform gradually, beginning with one shared feature rather than attempting a complete migration. We’ll discuss how we selected the first component, structured the shared code, tested it across platforms, and worked with the existing native applications. You’ll leave with a practical framework for evaluating where to introduce shared code, which challenges to expect, and how to plan an incremental Kotlin Multiplatform adoption without rebuilding your entire application. The example establishes the problem, explains what the session will cover, and gives the audience a reason to attend. It doesn’t reveal every detail, but it makes a concrete promise. Think like an attendee A strong proposal doesn’t focus only on what the speaker wants to present. It also explains what the audience will gain. Ask yourself: Who is this session for? What knowledge should attendees already have? What problem will the talk help them solve? What will they understand or be able to do afterward? Why should they choose this session over another talk happening at the same time? Svetlana Isakova. Team Lead in Kotlin Developer Advocacy, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X When submitting a talk, think like an attendee. Would you want to sit through this? What’s in it for the audience? That’s why we ask about key takeaways. What do you want people to learn, try, do, or feel inspired by? Avoid broad promises such as: “You will learn best practices.” “We will explore Kotlin Multiplatform.” “This talk will cover coroutines.” Instead, describe specific outcomes: Attendees will learn how to identify and debug three common coroutine performance problems. Attendees will understand how we structured shared code across Android and iOS. Attendees will be able to evaluate whether the approach fits their own project. Attendees will learn which parts of our migration worked, which did not, and what we would change today. Specific takeaways make the proposal easier to evaluate. If the talk is selected, they also help attendees decide whether it is relevant to them. Make a familiar topic feel fresh Your subject doesn’t have to be completely new. Many valuable conference talks revisit established technologies from perspectives that have not been explored in the same way before. If you are proposing a popular topic, identify what makes your version distinctive. This could be: A real production case An unusual scale or environment A surprising result A failed approach and what it taught you A comparison between several possible solutions A gradual migration rather than a greenfield implementation An unconventional use of Kotlin A personal experience that challenges a common assumption A particularly clear way of explaining a difficult concept For example, “Introduction to Kotlin Multiplatform” is broad and familiar. “What Broke When We Introduced Kotlin Multiplatform Into a Seven-Year-Old Mobile App” offers a specific context and creates curiosity. Be honest about trade-offs. A talk doesn’t need to present a flawless success story. Explaining what failed, what changed, and what you would do differently can be especially useful to other developers. Chantal Loncle. Software Developer, Exposed, JetBrains LinkedIn Bringing a real, practical narrative to a familiar topic can strengthen a proposal. Be honest about what broke, what made your team unhappy, or what you would do differently if you could turn back the clock. A familiar issue can feel fresh when you look at it from the perspective of someone who will encounter the same problem for the first time tomorrow. Rather than providing another general overview, build the talk around one specific pain point or discovery and introduce broader themes only where they support that story. A takeaway that attendees can immediately apply to their work can also help distinguish the proposal from a basic tutorial. Keep the proposal relevant to KotlinConf KotlinConf welcomes talks about backend development, Android, multiplatform development, web, desktop, AI, language design, tooling, libraries, developer experience, and other parts of the Kotlin ecosystem. Whatever your area, the role Kotlin plays in the story should be clear. Márton Braun. Developer Advocate, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , LinkedIn Keep in mind that your talk should be related to Kotlin! For example, not every Android talk is necessarily a good fit for the KotlinConf audience. Or talks about Jetpack Compose often cover things that work the exact same way with Compose Multiplatform, and the latter is much more likely to be accepted at KotlinConf! An Android topic, for example, is not automatically a KotlinConf topic. The proposal becomes more relevant when it explains how Kotlin influenced the solution, explores a Kotlin-specific technical decision, or provides lessons that Kotlin developers can apply. Ask yourself: Why is this a Kotlin story? Which parts of the experience are especially relevant to Kotlin developers? Would the proposal still be essentially the same if Kotlin were removed from it? If the answer to the final question is yes, strengthen the connection to Kotlin before submitting. Anshika Koul’s Kotlin Multiplatform’s Cross-Platform Brilliance at Norway’s 377-Year-Old National Postal Service offers a clear example of a Kotlin-centered takeaway: “We’ll learn how KMP provides a unified framework for code sharing and execution across various platforms to solve the challenge of different codebases targeting different runtimes.” Sound confident, but stay true to yourself Your proposal should show that you understand what you want to share and why it matters. This doesn’t mean exaggerating your expertise or pretending that you have no doubts. It means presenting the idea as a clear statement rather than repeatedly questioning its value. Marcin Mycek. Product Manager, Kotlin Build Tools LinkedIn Keep statements as statements and questions as questions. It is normal to doubt yourself; everybody does, but a common mistake is to let it show in the text, for example, by changing statements into questions. Read your submission, or even better, ask someone else to read it, and ask yourself: Does this person sound convinced about what they want to tell? For example: Uncertain: Could Kotlin Multiplatform possibly help teams reduce duplicated business logic? In this talk, we might find out. More confident: In this talk, I’ll show how our team used Kotlin Multiplatform to reduce duplicated business logic, including where sharing code helped and where it did not. Confidence should not erase your personality. The proposal should still sound like you. Marcin Mycek. Product Manager, Kotlin Build Tools LinkedIn Stay true to yourself! It is important to make sure that your submission can be understood by others. A great practice is to give it to a few people you trust and ask what they understood from it and how it made them feel. However, keep your soul in it. A lot of great talks are quirky, do not follow every best practice, and people are there for it. Advice and templates can help you organize your thoughts, but they shouldn’t make every proposal sound identical. Your perspective, language, humor, and enthusiasm are part of what makes the submission memorable. Show reviewers how you communicate Examples of previous talks help reviewers understand your presentation style and energy. If you have recordings from conferences, meetups, webinars, or livestreams, include the most relevant ones. If you’re a first-time speaker and don’t have a formal recording, you can record yourself explaining part of the proposed talk. A simple laptop recording is enough. It doesn’t need professional lighting, editing, or production. Svetlana Isakova. Team Lead in Kotlin Developer Advocacy, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X Examples of your talks help us make better choices. If you’re a first-time speaker and don’t have recordings, no worries! You can simply record yourself (even just part of your proposed talk) on your laptop and share the link. We would really appreciate it. Depending on the topic, you can also include: A technical article An open-source project Documentation you have written A short technical demonstration A podcast or meetup appearance Other work connected to the proposed session These materials support your proposal, but they don’t replace a clear title, abstract, and set of takeaways. Reviewers should still be able to understand the session from the submission itself. Choose the format that fits the idea Not every subject needs a full-length session. A focused lesson, experiment, side project, or surprising discovery may work better as a lightning talk. A subject that involves significant technical context, several connected lessons, or a detailed demonstration may require a regular session. Choose the format according to the amount of meaningful material you have. If you need to repeat yourself or add unnecessary content to fill a regular session, consider proposing a lightning talk instead. Márton Braun. Developer Advocate, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , LinkedIn Don’t forget that we also accept lightning talks! If you feel like your content would have to be padded to fill a regular session, it might be more enjoyable as a lightning talk. You can also submit more than one proposal if you have several distinct ideas. Each submission should have its own story, audience, and takeaways rather than being a minor variation of another proposal. Pamela Hill-Galloway. Developer Advocate, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , LinkedIn Submit more than one talk! It gives you more chances to join in on the KotlinConf fun. Review the proposal before submitting Once you have completed your draft, step away from it and return later from the perspective of someone encountering the idea for the first time. Check whether your proposal answers the following questions: Can someone understand the subject from the title? Is the connection to Kotlin clear? Does the abstract identify a real problem, question, or story? Is it clear who the session is for? Are the takeaways concrete? Does the proposal explain what makes your perspective different? Is the scope realistic for the selected format? Does the writing sound confident and authentic? Have you checked the spelling, grammar, links, and formatting? Does the proposal sound like the person who will deliver the talk? Ask someone else to review it, too. Rather than simply asking whether they like it, ask them to describe what they think the talk will cover and what they expect to learn. Their answer will show whether the proposal communicates what you intended. Chantal Loncle. Software Developer, Exposed, JetBrains LinkedIn Double-check that the intended audience level aligns with the description and expected takeaways. Review the proposal from the perspective of someone you hope will be in the audience. Does it make sense as it is, or is it missing context that may be obvious to you but not to the reviewer or the future audience they are keeping in mind? AI tools may help you check grammar or organize your thoughts, but the final proposal should reflect your own experience, ideas, and voice. A polished abstract without specific or authentic insight won’t be as convincing as one that clearly represents the speaker behind it. Márton Braun. Developer Advocate, KotlinConf Program Committee member, and KotlinConf speaker X , BlueSky , LinkedIn Your submission should show that you’ve put some thought and energy into preparing it. Check your submission for formatting issues and typos, and please don’t submit abstracts that were generated by LLMs. Your Kotlin story could take the stage You don’t need to know everything about Kotlin or have years of conference experience to submit a proposal. You need a useful story, an understanding of who it can help, and a clear explanation of why it matters. Not every strong proposal can be selected. Conference programs must balance subjects, formats, experience levels, and audience interests. If your submission is not accepted, continue refining the idea, sharing your knowledge, and looking for other opportunities to present it. Your experience might be exactly what another Kotlin developer needs to hear. The KotlinConf 2027 Call for Papers is open! Share your experience, ideas, and Kotlin expertise with the community in Kraków. Submit your proposal

title: What we know about FSB’s detention of Swedish citizen for plotting subversive acts
body:
MOSCOW, October 15. /TASS/. Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) has detained a Swedish citizen who fought on the Ukrainian army’s side and illegally crossed the Russian border for carrying out subversive and terrorist acts at military facilities, the FSB press office reported.
TASS has gathered key information available as of now.
- The FSB detained a Swedish citizen in the northwestern Pskov Region who had illegally crossed the state border, the FSB press office reported.
- Under the pretext of joining the Russian Armed Forces, he was traveling to Russia to carry out subversive and terrorist acts at military facilities.
- According to the FSB’s data, the foreign national served under a contract in February-June 2026 in an organization recognized as terrorist in Russia.
- The detainee served as commander of the unmanned aircraft systems squad within the 24th separate assault battalion, the FSB specified.
- Available documents confirm the detainee’s participation in combat operations on the Ukrainian army’s side against Russia, the press office said.
- Detained Swedish citizen Freddy Mikael Stalkrantz Lindholm admitted that he had signed a contract in Ternopol with the Aidar battalion (outlawed as a terrorist group in Russia), as follows from an FSB video.
- According to the detainee, he was sent for training, during which he learnt to operate FPV drones for the purposes of reconnaissance and surveillance.
- In addition, he trained others, as follows from his testimony.
- The FSB showed photos of the foreign national wearing the Ukrainian uniform and gear, and also the documents confirming his service in Ukraine.
- A criminal case has been opened against the foreign national under Article 322 of the Russian Criminal Code (‘Illegal Crossing of the State Border of the Russian Federation’). The issue of initiating criminal cases under Articles 205.5 (‘Organizing the Activities of a Terrorist Organization and Participating in the Activities of Such an Organization’) and 359 (‘Mercenary Activity’) is currently under consideration.

title: Germany to continue supporting Ukraine but expects reforms – Vice Chancellor
body:
He made the remarks to journalists on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank in Bangkok, Ukrinform reports, citing Reuters .
“Our support for Ukraine is clear. There is no wavering on that. But there are also clear expectations of the Ukrainian government. I think there is room for improvement,” Klingbeil said.
According to the German official, these expectations are linked, among other things, to the need to explain to the German public the substantial amount of aid provided to Ukraine amid cuts in Germany’s budget spending.
Klingbeil said he was holding talks with international partners to secure continued funding for Ukraine. In particular, Australia and South Korea reaffirmed their commitments to continuing support during meetings in Bangkok on Thursday.
“One has to say that this ⁠is a different kind of commitment from that of us Europeans, who are geographically much closer," Klingbeil ⁠said. "But both made very clear that their support for Ukraine will continue,” the German minister said.
As reported by Ukrinform, Prime Minister of Ukraine Sergii Koretskyi said Ukraine’s need for external budget financing next year exceeds $52 billion.

title: Nissan Patrol marks 75 years with limited-edition model exclusively for Gulf
body: Nissan has announced a limited-edition Patrol to mark the SUV’s 75th anniversary, with an initial production run of 1,951 vehicles exclusively for the GCC region. The number marks the nameplate's debut in 1951. Based on the flagship Platinum V6 Twin Turbo grade, the anniversary edition features copper-gold exterior accents, a Bordeaux red interior and special anniversary detailing. AWR Automotive, Nissan’s dealer in Dubai, Sharjah and the Northern Emirates, introduced the model on Thursday. It costs Dh439,900 ($119,780) including VAT. What’s different about the anniversary edition? Nissan says its bespoke copper-gold finish is inspired by desert landscapes. The detailing appears across the grille bars, fog lamp surrounds, fender vents, shoulder line and emblems, paired with dark chrome finishes and black alloy wheels. Anniversary signatures feature on the front grille, shoulder-line graphic and rear emblem. An illuminated carpet light projects a “Patrol Since 1951” graphic and a sand-dune motif. Nissan lists five exterior colours for the Gulf edition, while AWR Automotive has confirmed four options for its customers: grey, white, black and two-tone white with a black roof. Inside, the cabin features copper-gold steering wheel detailing and ambient lighting alongside dark chrome trim. Anniversary detailing appears on the passenger-side dashboard, seat headrests and floor and luggage mats. Other additions include illuminated anniversary kick plates and a deep red leather key fob case. Thierry Sabbagh, Nissan and Infiniti’s divisional vice president and president for the Middle East, Saudi Arabia, India and CIS, said: “To mark 75 years of the Patrol, we wanted to deliver something lasting for our customers, a special product that serves as a memorable token of our shared history.” Engine and technology The anniversary edition keeps the Platinum V6 Twin Turbo’s 3.5-litre twin-turbocharged engine, which delivers 425hp and 700Nm of torque. It is paired with a nine-speed automatic transmission and adaptive air suspension with Intelligent Dynamic Damping. The cabin includes a 28.6-inch Monolith display, a Klipsch audio system and quilted leather seats with heating, ventilation and massage functions. The model also features Biometric Cooling, ProPILOT driver assistance and advanced visibility systems. In the UAE and Saudi Arabia, NissanConnect 2.0 with Google built-in provides navigation , voice assistant functions and connected car services. Where can I buy it in the UAE? The anniversary edition joins a regional Patrol range that includes the Platinum, PRO-4X and Nismo. AWR Automotive says the model is available through its Nissan showrooms in Dubai, Sharjah and the Northern Emirates, and can also be viewed at its City Walk location in Dubai.

title: UK Pledges $23M for Chornobyl Repairs Amid Support Strains
body:
Britain pledged £17 million ($23 million) on Thursday, Oct. 15 toward repairs to the protective shelter and ventilation system at the Chornobyl nuclear power plant, as far-right parties question continued aid to Kyiv and Ukraine’s military faces disruption to satellite communications.
The UK government said the funding will help restore the shelter’s confinement and ventilation functions. The contribution is part of an international program coordinated by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), working with Ukraine and G7 donors.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
However, it is not the full cost of the repairs. The EBRD has estimated that the work could exceed €500 million ($585 million).
The New Safe Confinement is a 35-story arch built over reactor No. 4 to contain radioactive material and allow engineers to dismantle the remains of the reactor and the original sarcophagus. The €2.1 billion ($2.5 billion) structure was designed to last 100 years and was constructed with contributions from 45 countries.
