title: Abu Dhabi revokes doctor's licence for violating controlled medication rules
body: Abu Dhabi health authorities have revoked a doctor's licence and suspended another's over violations of controlled medication rules. The breaches included incomplete clinical assessments, a lack of proper follow-up care and missing medical records, the Department of Health – Abu Dhabi found. In some cases, the two doctors failed to record the medical reasons for prescribing controlled medications. The health department said it took the action to protect patients and ensure doctors followed medical rules and professional standards. The violations were identified through routine inspections, digital monitoring and co-ordination with other authorities. The health department said it would continue monitoring healthcare facilities and carry out inspections to identify violations and ensure compliance with the rules. Controlled medications are subject to strict regulations because they carry a risk of misuse or dependence. They typically include strong painkillers such as morphine and fentanyl, medicines used to treat anxiety and sleep problems, and drugs that affect mood and behaviour. They also include certain medications for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Only licensed doctors are allowed to prescribe controlled drugs in the UAE and should provide documentation to prove the need for a patient. The medicines have to be administered by a registered nurse. Healthcare facilities must comply with all regulations, laws and policies related to narcotics, controlled and semi-controlled drugs. Storing, distributing, dispensing, administering or handling narcotics, controlled or semi-controlled drugs without approval from the Ministry of Health and Prevention and Dubai Healthcare City Authority-Regulatory is prohibited.

title: “The spectrum enables the force, but it can also expose the force”
body:
The question of enabling or achieving spectrum dominance was a recurring theme on the first day of the Africa Aerospace and Defence (AAD) 2026 Conference on 16 September. Ryno van Staden, Head of Sales and Marketing at Hensoldt GEW, sought to address the challenge of achieving spectrum dominance in multi-domain operations, examining how land-based electronic warfare has evolved from a standalone capability into a critical enabler of integrated military operations.
Van Staden began his session, entitled ‘The future of land EW: Enabling spectrum dominance in multi-domain operations,’ by grounding his presentation in one simple question: “What design principles should shape future land EW capabilities?”
Modern systems provide invaluable opportunities to observe, understand, and act, but their electromagnetic emissions also create a risk. “The spectrum enables the force,” he said, but “it can also expose the force.”
The true challenge, he said, is not to transmit more power or more frequently, but “to use the spectrum intelligently, deliberately and in support of the mission.”
According to van Staden, the most meaningful or practical way this challenge can be addressed is for electronic warfare, cyber activity, spectrum management, intelligence and command and control capabilities to operate as part of an “integrated ecosystem”.
He pointed to the concept of Cyber Electromagnetic Activity, or CEMA, describing it as a framework that “helps connect those activities and transform information into coordinated action.” The objective, he said, “is clear: it is decision advantage.”
However, as electromagnetic spectrums proliferate, volume becomes a particularly difficult challenge to overcome. “Future electromagnetic environments will generate and is generating more information than any operator can process manually,” van Staden said.
As a result, he argued that software-defined defence has become particularly important. However, he cautioned that “software-defined defence is not simply about updating software faster. It changes the relationship between hardware and capability.”
At this point, van Staden turned to the question of AI (artificial intelligence) integration, contending that rather than replacing human judgement, the objective is to use AI integration as a means to achieve “better-informed, human decision-making.”
Returning to what he described as the core message of his presentation, namely the continual evolution of the EW environment, “these changes do not wait for scheduled acquisition cycles,” he said, adding that if there is one thing that we have learned from the Ukrainian conflict, it is that it is no longer viable to field a capability and expect to keep it for a period of time and undertake a modernisation programme at a later stage.
According to van Staden, this is where a key advantage of software-defined defence can be found. Capability, he argued, increasingly resides in “data, algorithms, and configuration,” enabling electronic warfare, cyber, ISR (intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance), and spectrum management to be reconfigured and evolve for new missions “without replacing entire systems,” as and when operational environments require.
Van Staden described his central message as “when forces understand earlier, decide faster, and act with greater confidence, they create the operational conditions required for spectrum superiority and mission success.”
“Technology creates potential, integration turns this potential into understanding, decision-making turns this understanding into action, and adaptation ensures that the advantage can be sustained as the operational environment evolves,” he added.
“The future of land electronic warfare is not fundamentally about generating more electromagnetic effects. It is not fundamentally about deploying more sensors, and it is definitely not about collecting more data. It is about creating a decision advantage within a contested electromagnetic environment,” he emphasised.

title: Qatargate suspect Urich met with Qatar's 'head of Israel project' months after October 7 - report
body: Yonatan Urich, senior aide and personal media adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, met with senior Qatari official Ali al-Thawadi at least twice in July 2024, N12 reported on Wednesday, citing testimony Urich gave to Lahav 433 in May 2025.One of the meetings with Thawadi, described by N12 as one of Qatar's most powerful figures and a close associate of its emir, reportedly included Urich's business partner, Yisrael “Srulik” Einhorn, and lobbyist Jay Footlik, whom Urich has previously denied knowing or meeting.During his questioning, investigators asked Urich about testimony from a former senior Mossad official identified as  S., who alleged that he and Einhorn had met Thawadi - referred to as “head of the Israel project” - at least twice“According to S.'s testimony, there were two meetings with Thawadi at which you and Srulik presented your ideas. What happened there?” an investigator asked, to which Urich stated he did not remember presenting anything at any meetings.He did not, however, accuse S. of lying; instead, he insisted he didn't remember and needed to “jog his memory.”Urich's stance did not change during the exchange; he said he could not remember where or when any alleged meetings took place.When the investigator specified that the meetings with Thawadi took place after October 7, Urich responded: “If you say so.”According to N12, the meetings were not part of an official assignment on behalf of Israel, and Netanyahu previously testified that Urich had never disclosed his ties to Qatar or the meetings with Thawadi.Urich confirmed his phone was hacked, says leakers will 'pay full price'The latest update to Urich's testimony came days after he revealed that his WhatsApp account had been hacked and promised that the people who leaked his private conversations would "pay the full price.""Whoever hacked into Yonatan Urich's WhatsApp and published personal correspondence while adding and changing the conversations will pay the full price," Urich said in a message shared on X."This will also happen to anyone who publishes, distributes, or shares messages. Whoever does so commits a criminal offense, and a personal lawsuit will be filed against them," he warned.According to Israeli media reports, the leaked messages included several conversations between Urich and his contacts in which he discussed politics, law, journalism, and political consulting.The leaker, who posted the images of the chats from an anonymous account, claimed that he had access to additional messages and that he was going to release them to the public later.Urich's legal case involving Qatar, PM NetanyahuUrich is a central suspect in the "Qatargate" investigations alleging corruption within the Prime Minister's Office.The case centers on alleged influence by Qatari-linked individuals close to Netanyahu.It is separate from the so-called “Bild affair,” which concerns reports in the German outlet. The Jerusalem Post has previously reported on intensified scrutiny of both tracks, as well as on the appointment of Shin Bet Director David Zini and recent leadership changes within the agency.Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

title: School roof collapse kills at least 29, injures more than 3 dozen in Pakistan
body:
A volunteer clears the way for an ambulance transporting injured school children following a roof collapse at a private school in Peshawar, Pakistan, Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. Maaz Awan/AP hide caption
PESHAWAR, Pakistan — The roof of a private school collapsed in northwestern Pakistan on Thursday, killing at least 28 children and a female teacher and injuring more than 50 other people, a hospital spokesman said, as rescuers searched the rubble for anyone still trapped. Six girls were among the dead.
Several children were also trapped under the rubble in Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, said Bilal Faizi, a spokesman for the emergency services.
A hospital spokesman, Mohammad Asim, also confirmed the casualties, saying some of the injured were in critical condition. All the children killed or injured were age 13 or younger, he said. The hospital declared an emergency as medical staff treated the wounded.
Hours later, rescue officials said that everyone trapped beneath the rubble had been pulled out and crews were clearing the debris. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Gov. Faisal Karim Kundi expressed sorrow over the collapse and sought a report from the relevant authorities about the cause of the collapse. He directed officials to provide the best possible medical care to the injured children.
Mahwish Zaman, an injured teacher speaking from a hospital bed, said that the three-story school had an estimated 1,200 students enrolled in nursery through fifth grade. She told The Associated Press that she was in her classroom when the roof collapsed and felt as if the sky had fallen. She regained consciousness in the hospital.
Rescue workers and volunteers take part in the rescue operation at the site of a roof collapse at a private school, in Peshawar, Pakistan, Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. Maaz Awan/AP hide caption
According to witnesses, residents were among the first to reach the school in a congested neighborhood in central Peshawar. Rescue workers arrived within minutes of being alerted, according to accounts from the scene.
A resident, Samiullah Khan, said that he rushed to the school after learning of the collapse and helped rescue three girls. Khan said his son, who attends the school, survived because he had stepped out of his classroom to drink water.
A resident, Mohammad Khan, said rescuers carefully removed debris, trying to reach children and staff feared trapped beneath the collapsed roof. Outside the school and at the state-run Lady Reading Hospital, anguished parents sought information about their children, unsure whether they had survived.
The cause of the collapse was under investigation. Peshawar police chief Saeed Ahmed said that the school's owner had been arrested. He said that the building was structurally weak.
The provincial government said that the school occupied a three-story building and that a committee had been formed to investigate the cause of the roof collapse.
The provincial government spokeswoman, Samar Haroon Bilour, said that the government directed hospital officials to provide prompt medical care to the injured children and praised rescue workers for their swift response. She said that the government was using all available resources to bring those trapped beneath the rubble to safety.
In Islamabad, President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed sorrow over the deaths and offered condolences to the bereaved families in separate statements.
"The entire nation shares the grief of the affected families in this hour of sorrow," Zardari said.
He also called for a comprehensive investigation into the collapse and stressed the need to ensure school buildings meet safety standards to prevent similar tragedies.
In July, a roof collapsed at a tutoring center under construction in Lahore, killing four schoolchildren.
Building collapses are common in Pakistan, where construction standards are often poorly enforced. Many structures are built with substandard materials, and safety regulations are frequently ignored to reduce costs.

title: Suspect in Alleged U.S. Asylum Fraud Scheme Extradited From Argentina to Georgia
body: Giorgi Khatiashvili, accused of involvement in a transnational organized crime scheme that allegedly fabricated asylum claims for Georgian citizens seeking to enter the United States, was extradited from Argentina to Georgia, the Prosecutor’s Office announced, describing the extradition as a “precedent” and the first such case involving a country outside Europe and the region. The case concerns a criminal group that allegedly fabricated persecution stories and supporting documents for Georgian citizens seeking asylum in the United States in exchange for payment. The investigation, conducted in cooperation with the U.S. Embassy’s Regional Security Office (RSO), identified more than 1,000 people to whom the group allegedly offered its services between 2023 and 2026. The Prosecutor’s Office said it charged nine people in the case in previous months. According to the Prosecutor’s Office of Georgia’s October 15 statement , amid the tightening of the immigration policy in the USA, Khatiashvili and other individuals “formed a criminal group to obtain material benefits, the purpose of which was to create false stories, so-called ‘cases’ and corresponding false evidence necessary for Georgian citizens seeking asylum in the United States.” Khatiashvili is accused of “facilitating the illegal stay of a Georgian citizen in a foreign country by a criminal group, facilitating and organizing the submission of false information for a Georgian citizen to obtain asylum in a foreign country, and producing and issuing a false official document.” “Members of the criminal group convinced Georgian citizens that with the help of documents they had prepared and stories they had created, they would be able to obtain asylum in the United States without any problems,” the Office said. According to the statement, the group fabricated accounts of persecution on various grounds, including “political views, sexual orientation, persecution by law enforcement officers, and other reasons,” and to substantiate these stories, created “fake documents.” The investigation identified “more than 1,000 individuals to whom members of the criminal group offered their services between 2023 and 2026 and received approximately 600 thousand GEL, 2,250,000 USD, and 12,500 EUR from them.” The statement also noted that “another person wanted in the case has been extradited from Germany as a result of effective international legal cooperation implemented by the Georgian Prosecutor’s Office.” “The Georgian side’s request was fully granted by the competent authorities of the Argentine Republic, which is a precedent, as it is the first extradition case to be carried out from countries outside Europe and the region,” the statement added, thanking Georgian relevant bodies for taking measures to carry out the extradition. The U.S.-Georgian joint efforts to uncover the scheme come amid wider reports of the two countries cooperating on security issues, including combating transnational crime, despite lingering uncertainty in bilateral relations after the U.S., under Joe Biden, suspended the strategic partnership with Tbilisi in late 2024. title: Nearly one in three civilian Ukrainians has PTSD or complex PTSD – T&F
body:
A national survey of Ukrainian residents showed that 31.2% of respondents met the criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) or complex PTSD (CPTSD), according to the results of a study published by British academic publisher Taylor & Francis Group in the European Journal of Psychotraumatology.
"High rates of both lifetime and war-related trauma were documented. The national prevalence of ICD-11 PTSD was 25.2%, with an additional 6.0% of respondents meeting criteria for ICD-11 CPTSD, yielding a combined prevalence rate of 31.2%," the publication says.
The collected data reflects the state of mental health at the time of the survey rather than the dynamics of symptom changes over time. The article material was received by the publisher in 2025.
Factors associated with a higher likelihood of developing PTSD or CPTSD included female sex, older age, lower education level, prior military service, forced displacement due to war, as well as a higher number of lifetime traumatic events and war-related stressors.
Loneliness was the only factor specifically associated with CPTSD rather than PTSD.
Study co-author, clinical psychologist Emma Facer-Irwin, noted that the fact that PTSD occurred much more frequently than CPTSD may indicate that psychological responses to an ongoing war do not always fit neatly into models developed in post-conflict settings. "When the threat remains current and unpredictable, the ways of experiencing and adapting to traumatic stress may differ, representing an important area for future research," she indicated.
Lead author of the study, lecturer and researcher in forensic mental health at King's College London (KCL), Deirdre MacManus, noted that the vast majority of those surveyed experienced multiple traumatic events during their lifetimes, and many were also directly affected by the ongoing war through forced displacement, loss of loved ones, destruction of their communities, or anxiety for family members, with many Ukrainians continuing to face stressors in daily life. "Despite this, many Ukrainians continue to live and adapt under extraordinarily difficult circumstances," she noted.
Study co-author, professor at the Department of Social Sciences at the Kyiv School of Economics Volodymyr Kulyk, noted that PTSD and CPTSD affect not only veterans or people who were near active combat zones. "These disorders are also common among other population categories severely affected by the war—including internally displaced persons, people who have experienced missile and drone attacks on their cities and towns far from the front line, as well as those caring for injured or traumatized individuals," he stressed.
According to Kulyk, further research will be necessary to understand how the psychological impact of war evolves among the general population as the conflict continues.
In addition to specialists from KCL and the Kyiv School of Economics, the research team included scientists from George Washington University, the University of Manchester, the Centre for East European and International Studies (ZOiS), and Combat Stress—a leading British charity caring for veterans' mental health. The study was initiated by the research network "Conflict and Cooperation in Eastern Europe" (KonKoop), led by Professor Gwendolyn Sasse (ZOiS), and funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space.
The study was conducted via telephone interviews based on a random sample of 2,504 respondents in government-controlled areas of Ukraine. The relationships between the type and number of lifetime and war trauma exposures and PTSD/CPTSD status were examined using a series of logistic regression models adjusting for age and sex. The sample is representative by age, sex, marital status, education level, macro-region, language, and ethnicity.
Prior to field work, questionnaires were pre-tested on an approximately representative sub-sample (n = 20) of the target group (adults residing in urban and rural settlements of Kyiv and nine regions of Ukraine). During data collection, interviewers had the opportunity to ask questions and consult with a psychologist regarding complex cases. The average duration of an interview was 27 minutes.

title: US Threatened Immediate Intelligence Cutoff Unless Ukraine Halts Strikes
body:
US intelligence officials warned Ukraine that Washington would immediately stop sharing intelligence if Kyiv continued attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.
The Washington Post reported , citing a person familiar with the matter, that the warning was conveyed to Ukraine’s embassy in Washington. It came amid disputes over an energy ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump and Ukrainian complaints that some Russian ballistic missile attacks had arrived without advance warning from partners.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The Trump administration has previously warned that it could suspend intelligence sharing and halt European purchases of US weapons for Ukraine if Kyiv refused to stop deep strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
The newspaper’s source said the US had not completely halted intelligence sharing. The source also noted that the missiles used in recent attacks on Kyiv had previously evaded warning systems.
Earlier, Zelensky said that Ukrainian forces received no warnings from partners about Russian ballistic missile launches toward Kyiv for two consecutive nights, as attacks struck the capital’s energy infrastructure.
He subsequently disputed the Pentagon’s explanation that a technical problem was responsible, saying the failure to provide warnings reflected a deliberate decision, according to the Financial Times.
President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that military commanders had received warnings about a possible intelligence cutoff.
“They said this to my generals, not to me,” he said.
“My generals said they had received this information at the military level.”
Trump, however, said intelligence cooperation would continue.
“We are helping them, and we are sharing intel. We want the war to end,” he told reporters.
Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Oct. 11, saying both sides had agreed. He demanded that Ukraine refrain from attacking Russian oil refineries.
After several days of Russian attacks, Zelensky said he had lifted the prohibition on strikes against Russian refineries
Zelensky said Kyiv will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after Washington pressured Ukraine to halt attacks, warning that the US has endangered Ukrainian lives by restricting access to intelligence and Starlink satellite communications.
“The block [on attacking refineries] is out. We’re done,” Zelensky told the Financial Times in an interview in London.
Last week, Trump announced an agreement for Russia to supply diesel to US and global markets, drawing criticism from US lawmakers and European allies.
Zelensky described the deal as a “simple victory” for the Kremlin in an interview with British broadcaster Piers Morgan on Wednesday.
“It’s a pity that we are losing a strong partner,” Zelensky said.
He also accused Trump of taking Russia’s side in the war, arguing that Washington should remain neutral rather than favor Moscow.
“This is our country, our body, our home, our children,” Zelensky said. “That’s why it’s painful when Trump chooses one side.”
“If you’re in the middle, you have to stay in the middle. Not on the wrong side,” he added. “This is not the right side of history.”
The dispute comes as Russian forces continue attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities. Zelensky said Russian strikes had left more than 600,000 people without electricity.
Moscow has also intensified aerial attacks as battlefield advances remain limited, with both sides targeting energy infrastructure.
Zelensky has sought to strengthen European support amid uncertainty over Washington’s commitment. During his visit to London on Wednesday, he met British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and King Charles III .

title: PCC slaps onion cartel with record fine of P1.76B
body: MANILA, Philippines – Almost four years since the country’s onion crisis, the Philippine Competition Commission (PCC) imposed a combined P1.76-billion fine against onion cartel members that colluded in an “illegal market allocation scheme in the importation, cold storage, and wholesale distribution of red and yellow onions.” In late 2022, onion prices in the Philippines skyrocketed to over P800 per kilo, prompting a House probe into alleged price manipulation and cartel operations. “Because the importers’ submitted audited financial statements were found to be grossly understated, the Commission computed the fines using actual import clearance volumes, and wholesale prices reported by the Philippine Statistics Authority,” the PCC said on Thursday, October 15. This comes two years after the PCC sued onion firms in 2024, as well as a dawn raid of warehouses in September 2023, including the respondents’ offices located in Golden Shine Corporate Center. “An examination of the evidence [from the raid] revealed that Golden Shine systematically applied for sanitary and phytosanitary import clearances using the other respondent-importers’ credentials, assigned the same importers as consignees, monitored permit allocations, and coordinated shipments. By accumulating permits across separate corporate entities, the respondents collectively controlled nearly 50 percent of all approved import clearances for red and yellow (or white) onions in 2020 and 2021, routing imported shipments to cold storage facilities managed under Tian Long [Corp.] from where imported onions were distributed nationwide,” the PCC explained. Six firms named engaged in the onion cartel and subsequently fined are: Golden Shine International Freight Forwarders Corp. Tian Long Corp. La Reina Fresh Vegetables & Young Indoor Plants, Inc. Yom Trading Corp. Vegefru Producing Store Rosal Fruit and Vegetable Trading In 2024, the Department of Agriculture blacklisted importers linked to the cartel: La Reina Fresh Vegetables Young Indoor Plants Incorporate, Vegefru Producing Store, and Yom Trading Corporation. The individual officers held liable are: Lilia Cruz , president of Golden Shine Eric Pabilona, corporate executive officer of Golden Shine and corporate secretary of Tian Long Renato Francisco Jr., chairman and president of La Reina and Yom Trading Letty Baculando, incorporator of Golden Shine According to the PCC, charges against other companies allegedly involved — Philippine Vieva Group of Companies, Inc. and the Vegetable Importers, Exporters & Vendors Association of the Philippines Inc. — were dismissed due to “insufficient evidence.” But key officers of these companies are also the same individual officers fined, as mentioned above such as Cruz and Pabilona. Cruz had been referred to as the “onion queen” or “Mrs. Sibuyas” for being implicated as the cartel mastermind. “By imposing the maximum fines, the PCC underscores its commitment to holding cartels accountable across all sectors of the economy and protecting consumers from the harmful effects of anti-competitive conduct,” PCC Executive Director Kenneth Tanate said. The government initially sought a P2.423-billion fine against the cartel back in 2024. Aside from the fines, those involved in cartel activities may also face criminal liability if the Department of Justice-Office for Competition finds basis in filing cases. The PCC is the quasi-judicial body that implements Republic Act No. 10667 or the Philippine Competition Act, which seeks to promote and protect market competition in the country. – Rappler.com Who is Lilia Cruz, the woman implicated in smuggling of onions, garlic? An unknown soldier of the West Yorkshire Regiment, discovered near the Thiepval Memorial on the Somme, has been given a peaceful burial more than 100 years after his death.
The coffin of the unknown soldier, dressed in the Union Flag, is guarded by two serving soldiers prior to the start of the service (Crown Copyright)
More than a century after his death in the First World War, the remains of a man of the West Yorkshire Regiment were laid to rest today (14 October 2026) with full military honours at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission’s ( CWGC ) Serre Road Cemetery No.2 in France.
Some of the military party, including a representative from the British Embassy in France, at the service for the unknown soldier (Crown Copyright)
In the winter of 2025 – 2026 human remains were discovered on the edge of a freshly ploughed field about a kilometre south of the Thiepval Memorial. Since the remains had been disturbed by a plough, it was impossible to fully understand the context of the find and to relate the artefacts to the soldier conclusively. However, a shoulder title found near the remains indicated possible service with the West Yorkshire Regiment, and this was strengthened by the presence of a belt with the letters WYR marked on it, also found near the casualty. An entrenching tool issued prior to July 1916 and first-issue webbing gave some clues as to when this soldier might have been equipped, but there was no clue as to his personal identity.
The recovery location was immediately adjacent to the Leipzig Redoubt, and records of the West Yorkshire Regiment show that various battalions were tasked with capturing Thiepval including the Leipzig Salient on the 1st July 1916, and remained in the line in this area until 17 July, before revisiting the area again in August of the same year.
Research showed that more than 1000 men of the West Yorkshire Regiment are named on the Thiepval Memorial, having died in the period 1 July 1916 – 31 August 1916. A further 745 men of the same regiment died on other dates from September 1915 to March 1918, and also remain missing.
With such an extensive list of potential candidates, and nothing in the way of artefactual evidence to point to his identity it proved impossible to identify the man. Nonetheless, he gave his life in the service of his country, fighting for freedom and peace. Whilst his identity remains known only to God, today he was buried by a party from the Royal Yorkshire Regiment – his military family, with full military honours.
The service was organised by the JCCC and supported by serving soldiers of the Royal Yorkshire Regiment, as well as staff from the CWGC .
The service was led by Padre David Jeal and supported by the Royal Yorkshire Regiment (Crown Copyright)

title: Don’t Interfere in 2027 Elections, Obidients Warn Wike
body: Chuks Okocha in Abuja The Obidient Movement has warned the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, against any attempt to influence the outcome of the 2027 general election. This follows the former Rivers State governor’s declaration that he would lead President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign in Rivers State and the FCT. The movement urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and security agencies to remain impartial and ensure that voters freely determine the outcome of the elections. Wike had last Monday declared himself the field commander of Tinubu’s re-election campaign in the two territories, a move that has drawn criticism from the political group. In a statement issued yesterday by its Media and Communications Directorate, the movement said taking charge of a political campaign did not give Wike control over voters or the electoral process. “Wike must understand that coordinating a political campaign does not confer ownership of the electorate, control over voters, or authority over the electoral process,” the statement said. The group insisted that Rivers State and the FCT belong to their people and not to any politician, political party, or influential political figure. It challenged Wike to campaign for Tinubu based on the president’s performance rather than create the impression that political control over the two territories would determine the election outcome. “If Wike believes the APC deserves victory, he should campaign for it and allow the people to decide. If he believes that Tinubu’s performance will earn him another term, he should present that record to Nigerians and submit himself to the verdict of the ballot box,” the movement said. The group also called on INEC and security agencies to address concerns about the 2027 elections and demonstrate their independence from political interests. It warned that any attempt by Wike, his associates or other political actors to manipulate the polls should attract legal consequences. The movement further urged Nigerians to monitor the elections, document suspected irregularities and report credible evidence of malpractice through lawful channels. It maintained that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend on whether votes were freely cast and accurately counted, regardless of the political status of those involved. The group concluded that neither Wike, Tinubu nor the All Progressives Congress (APC) should regard victory as guaranteed, insisting that the electorate must have the final say.

title: 'Mother of all bombs': US potential Iran strike plans include largest non-nuclear weapon - report
body: The United States military has developed strike plans against Iran that include using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb (MOAB), colloquially known as the "mother of all bombs,"  one of the largest non-nuclear weapons in the US arsenal, CNN reported on Thursday.According to CNN, multiple US officials said that the plans called for the MOAB to be used against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites, including Pickaxe Mountain.Another source said that the phrasing used in the plan was that the attack would come “prior to US retrograde in CENTCOM AOR (area of responsibility),” meaning that the US might strike Iran and then immediately pull its forces out of the region.Several of US President Donald Trump's advisors have also told CNN that, despite Trump's claims that he would not take further action against Iran before the US midterms, it remains unclear whether he will change his mind before Election Day.The potential deployment of the 21,000-pound bomb would mark a significant escalation in the conflict, although officials familiar with military planning discussions told CNN that questions remain over its effectiveness in achieving Washington's strategic objectives.MOAB unlikely to penetrate Iranian nuclear sitesAccording to several sources, the MOAB likely would be unable to penetrate deep below the ground, where Iranian nuclear facilities, such as Pickaxe Mountain, are believed to be.“The MOAB is a massive information operation type weapon that is great for huge area clearance but not much else,” one source familiar with military planning discussions around Iran told CNN. “It is definitely not designed as a deep penetration warhead.”The source said the MOAB's main tactical advantage in this scenario would be its psychological effect on Iran.“POTUS has unfortunately put himself in a situation where he is almost compelled to do something and, without the ammunition designed to penetrate that level… you have to look at psychological effects for which the MOAB is well-equipped,” the source said.When asked about the plan, a White House official told CNN that “President Trump keeps all options on the table to ensure that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon,” adding that they do not comment on sensitive military plans.A Pentagon official told CNN that it "plans for a wide range of operational scenarios to execute Presidential and Secretary‑level direction and to ensure mission success in any operational environment.”Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Love Is Blind on Netflix: Every international edition ranked as US season 11 arrives
body: Is love really blind? Since 2020, couples around the world have been trying to prove as much – mostly unsuccessfully – in Netflix's hugely popular reality show Love is Blind . Following its debut, set in the US, the show has spawned 13 international versions, including Love is Blind: Habibi , the Arabic spin-off that premiered in October 2024. A second season is coming later in the year. The format is similar across all. A group of single men and women looking for love are introduced to each other through “pods”, where they can interact but not see the other person. Once participants have chosen their prospective partners, the couple meet for the first time and become engaged. They are then flown to a luxury resort where they spend time and get to know each other better. In the final stage of the experiment, the couples who are still together go back to their respective lives where they meet each other's families and friends, and are given 10 days to prepare for their wedding. From Brazil to the UK and Japan, each edition of Love is Blind has proved to be a hit, turning some of its cast members into overnight celebrities. Love is Blind: Habibi , for instance, was viewed more than 1.3 million times in the first seven days after its debut. It also ranked No 8 globally among Netflix's non-English shows. With Love is Blind: South Africa set to debut later this year, here are all the editions so far ranked by fan ratings on IMDb. Watch out for spoilers from reunion episodes =12. Love is Blind: Habibi Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 5.4/10 Viewership in first week: 1.3 million Hosts: Khaled Saqer and Elham Ali The Arabic version of Love is Blind became a massive hit, dominating social media chats and debates for weeks after its premiere in October 2024. Featuring 20 singles – 10 women and 10 men – from across the Arab world and North Africa who are all residents of the UAE, the series was filmed in Lebanon, Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Six couples progressed to the next stage and were flown to a luxury resort in Lebanon, where their relationship was further tested. Eventually, out of two couples who made it to the wedding day, only one – Safa and Mohammed – exchanged vows. Speaking to The National a few weeks after its debut, cast members shared how their lives had changed thanks to the popularity of the show. “This experience didn’t just transform me, it shaped me into a person I never imagined I could be,” Mohammed said. “It opened up a whole new world and revealed aspects of myself I hadn’t recognised before. Beyond discovering ‘the one’, I found myself.” Season two will have celebrity couple Wissam Breidy and Rym Saidi taking over hosting roles. =12. Love is Blind: Mexico Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 5.4/10 Viewership in first week: 1.2 million Hosts: Omar and Lucy Chaparro One of the most dramatic editions, Love is Blind: Mexico debuted in August 2024. Of the nine women and nine men taking part, six couples progressed to the next stage and only one couple, Karen and Fernando, made it to the altar. In the reunion episode, which aired three weeks later, the couple confirmed they were still together and had even started a business. 11. Love is Blind: Argentina Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 5.5/10 Viewership in first week: Data unavailable Hosts: Dario Barassi and Wanda Nara Launching in November 2024, Love is Blind: Argentina featured two couples getting married. In a break from format, Florencia Fernandez and Jose Luis Farina, who did not get engaged during the pods segment, returned to the show as a couple during the honeymoon phase. They are also the couple who have managed to stay married, a fact revealed in the reunion episode. 10. Love is Blind: Germany Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 5.6/10 Viewership in first week: 1.3 million Hosts: Steffi and Chris Wackert-Brungs Hosted by German TV presenter Stephanie “Steffi” Brungs and her husband, the show had its premiere in January last year with 30 singles. Only one couple, Alina and Ilias, have remained married. 9. Love is Blind: Netherlands Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 5.9/10 Viewership in first week: 1.7 million Hosts: Nicolette van Dam and Bas Smit Dutch celebrity couple van Dam and Smit shepherd 30 single men and women in search of love in this spin-off, with only one couple, Mika and Jurriaan, tying the knot in the final episode aired on October 14. =6. Love is Blind: Brazil Number of seasons: 4 IMDb rating: 6.2/10 Viewership in first week: 2.1 million (season four) Hosts: Camila Queiroz and Klebber Toledo The first country to get its own version, Love is Blind: Brazil debuted in October 2021, with production for season five in progress. Hosted by celebrity couple Camila Queiroz and Klebber Toledo, this spin-off is as dramatic as reality shows can get. In season one, for example, there was a massive twist in the fairy tale: Nanda – who originally chose Thiago over Mackdavid – revealed in the reunion episode that she and Thiago had separated and that she had got back with Mackdavid. Nanda and Mackdavid welcomed baby Ben in 2022. =6. Love is Blind: France Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 6.2/10 Viewership in first week: 1.3 million Hosts: Teddy Riner and Luthna Plocus Debuting in September last year, the first season of the show's French version featured 15 men and 15 women. It was hosted by French Judo champion Riner and his wife Plocus, and filmed in Tangier, Morocco. Of the six couples who made it to the next round, Jonathan and Cynthia, called it quits following several arguments. The remaining decamped to Paris to test how well they mesh in everyday life, after which another couple, Yannick and Tatiana, decided to end their relationship, leaving four couples to plan their wedding. On the big day, two Alexandre and Chloe, and Charles and Julie eventually said “I do”. But the reunion episode, which aired in October, revealed none of the couples have remained together. =6. Love is Blind: USA Number of seasons: 11 IMDb rating: 6.2/10 Viewership in first week: 2.5 million (season ten) Hosts: Nick and Vanessa Lachey All seasons of the original US series have been hosted by celebrity couple Nick and Vanessa Lachey. The latest, season 11, premiered on October 14 and is set in Boston, where six couples have found potential partners. However, episode five ends on a cliffhanger, as Jax and Stew, whose first face-to-face meeting did not go particularly well, agree to meet again to talk things through. The next batch of season eleven episodes will stream on October 21. The show has won Critics' Choice Real TV Awards, which recognise achievements in non-scripted shows, three times – in 2020, 2022 and 2023. =4. Love is Blind: Italy Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 6.3/10 Viewership in the first week : 1.3 million Hosts: Benedetta Parodi and Fabio Caressa The Italian version of the show had its premiere on December 1 last year, featuring 12 men and 12 women. Hosted by journalist couple, Parodi and Caressa, the show revealed only two couples made it to the altar. Fan sites have noted that both couples – Karen Norman and Nicola Botticini, and Hyoni Song and Alessandro Bianchin – have remained together. =4. Love is Blind: Poland Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 6.3/10 Viewership in first week: Data unavailable Hosts : Zofia Zborowska-Wrona and Andrzej Wrona Poland's version had its premiere on May 6, 2026, with 30 singles looking to meet their ultimate partners. Hosted by actress Zofia Zborowska-Wrona and her husband, volley ball star Andrzej Wrona, five couples made it to the next stage, with three of them failing to say I do. Two couples – Marta and Damian as well as Daria and Filip – said “I do” and were still married when the cast members reunited to share their relationship statuses in an episode that aired on May 24, 2026. 3. Love is Blind: Sweden Number of seasons: 2 IMDb rating: 6.5/10 Viewership in first week: 1.7 million (season one) Host: Jessica Almenas Sweden's version had its premiere in January 2024, with five couples moving to the next stage of the relationship. Three couples celebrated their wedding, out of which Krisse-Ly and Rasmus recently revealed the former is pregnant. Amanda and Sergio's first child, a boy named Ralph, was born in May last year. The second season, which had its debut in March, had three couples eventually exchanging vows, of which Karin and Niklas announced they were expecting their first child in the reunion episode. 2. Love is Blind: UK Number of seasons: 2 IMDb rating: 6.9/10 Viewership in first week: 3.6 million (season one) and 2.6 million (season two) Hosts: Matt and Emma Willis Matt Willis, co-founder of English pop-punk band Busted, hosts this show with his wife, broadcaster Emma Willis. Debuting on August 7 2024, the show featured seven couples who found their prospective partners. Out of these, three made it to the altar. The reunion episode revealed Steven and Sabrina have called it quits after saying “I do”, leaving just two couples who successfully found love – Benaiah and Nicole, and Bobby and Jasmine. Season two debuted on August 13 last year with five couples moving on to the next stage. While this season received lower buzz and viewership than the first, the UK version of the reality show is still one of the most popular globally. Five couples met their match, but three made it to the altar – Billy and Ashleigh, Kieran and Megan, and Kal and Sarover. Of the three, only Kieran and Megan have remained together. 1. Love is Blind: Japan Number of seasons: 1 IMDb rating: 7.0/10 Viewership in first week: Data unavailable Hosts: Takashi Fujii and Yuka Itaya The second spin-off after Brazil, Love is Blind: Japan had its premiere in February 2022 and featured eight couples who found their potential true loves. Six couples separated before their wedding day, leaving Wataru Mizote and Midori, as well as fan-favourites Ryotaro and Motomi, to get hitched. The couples are still married with both pairs now becoming parents. A second season was announced in March, but later cancelled.

title: FACT CHECK: Martin Romualdez remains detained in Payatas jail
body: Claim: Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez is not in detention and is now out of the country. Rating: FALSE Why we fact-checked this: Facebook page Makata Ng Bayan posted the claim on October 14, 2026. As of writing, it has reached over 4,700 reactions, 1,600 shares, and 700 comments. The post included a photo of Romualdez with his cousin, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and text labeling it as “breaking news.” The graphic reads: “Breaking News! Martin Romualdez wala na sa kulungan nakalabas na ng Bansa! Si Marcos naman habang sabog ay naging tuta ng sindikato Kaya dapat ng lumayas at Palayasin.” (Breaking news! Martin Romualdez is no longer in jail; he has left the country! As for Marcos, he became the puppet of a syndicate while high on drugs, so he should leave and be ousted.) The post received mixed views in the comments section. Some criticized the Marcos administration for allowing Romualdez to flee the country, while others questioned the post’s credibility for calling for a revolt against the government. The facts: Romualdez has been detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas since September 14, 2026. He was arrested over a P7.44-billion plunder case related to the flood control scandal on September 7. The Ombudsman dubbed Romualdez a “ central figure ” in the scheme due to his strong influence in Congress during his time as House speaker. His transfer to the jail was not immediately carried out after his arrest, as he was first confined at a hospital in San Juan City hours before the warrant against him was served. In his arraignment before the Sandiganbayan on September 16, Romualdez pleaded not guilty . His bail hearing began on October 12, and will continue every Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Meanwhile, the presentation of evidence for his case is set to begin on November 23. Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously debunked false claims revolving around the lawmaker. FACT CHECK: Romualdez still detained, no evidence of planned escape abroad FACT CHECK: Video of Marcos saying Romualdez’s arrest is ‘staged’ is AI-generated FACT CHECK: No evidence Romualdez has stage 4 cancer FACT CHECK: Romualdez did not ‘dare’ Senate to investigate him; video is AI-generated FACT CHECK: Video of Romualdez challenging VP Sara to face allegations is AI-generated FACT CHECK: Romualdez did not release USB containing budget corruption evidence vs Marcos – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Boxer ruled out of cavalry role as variants shelved
body: Armoured mortar, repair and recovery, and mounted close combat overwatch capabilities are no longer being pursued within the Mechanised Infantry Vehicle programme, and Boxer will not be used in the armoured cavalry role at all, according to answers given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked what elements had been cut from the programme as part of the funding removal and budget reprioritisation recorded in the National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority’s Major Projects Annual Report for 2025 to 2026, which logged £1,858.38 million coming out. He separately asked how many of each Boxer variant would go to the armoured cavalry role and how many to mechanised infantry. Luke Pollard, the Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, said: “As part of reprioritisation within the Military Strategic Headquarters, the Armoured Mortar, Repair and Recovery and Mounted Close Combat Overwatch capabilities of the Mechanised Infantry Vehicle programme are no longer being pursued. “The Army is considering how the underlying capability requirements will be addressed.” On the cavalry question, Pollard said: “Boxer vehicles will not be used in the Armoured Cavalry role. Boxer will form the spine of the Mechanised Infantry force. Under current plans, Boxer is being fielded in supporting roles across 3rd (UK) Division, including Command and Control, Specialist Troop Carrier and Medical functions. Detailed fielding plans and vehicle allocations remain subject to refinement.” The requirement survives the first decision even though the Boxer-based route to meeting it does not, which leaves the Army to find another way. In practice that means an existing vehicle takes the task on, a separate procurement follows, or the capability thins. Each of the shelved functions does a job the mechanised infantry brigades still need done. Armoured mortar gives a battlegroup indirect fire of its own, able to move with the vehicles it supports and put rounds down without waiting on artillery allocated at a higher level. Repair and recovery keeps a wheeled armoured fleet running and drags disabled vehicles off the battlefield, which matters because a vehicle of Boxer’s weight that loses mobility cannot be moved by anything smaller than a purpose-built recovery variant. Mounted close combat overwatch is the anti-armour role, carrying a missile system that lets the infantry hold tanks at a distance. Armoured cavalry is the reconnaissance and screening job the Army is equipping with Ajax, the tracked family built by General Dynamics Land Systems UK and fitted with a stabilised 40mm cased telescoped cannon. Ajax carries the sensors and the gun for that work, while Boxer is wheeled, has no turret on the British variants ordered so far, and is built to carry infantry and the things infantry need. Ruling it out of the role closes off a line of speculation that has followed the vehicle since Britain rejoined the programme. Boxer is a modular design built around a common drive module onto which different mission modules are fitted, the feature that was supposed to make adding variants straightforward. Britain rejoined the programme in 2018, having left it in 2003, and the order has grown past six hundred vehicles across infantry carrier, specialist carrier, command and ambulance types, built under licence by Rheinmetall BAE Systems Land at Telford and WFEL at Stockport. The post Boxer ruled out of cavalry role as variants shelved first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Marine Alutech wins German Navy combat boat contract
body:
BAAINBw (Federal Office of Bundeswehr Equipment, Information Technology and In-Service Support) and Marine Alutech Oy have signed a contract for the manufacturing and delivery of Watercat M18 AMC combat boats.
As informed, the contract was signed on October 12, 2026. The vessels are intended for the Seebataillon of the German Navy. includes delivery of 15pcs of Watercat M18 AMC combat boats with training, documentation and a life cycle support package.
Built on the Watercat M18 AMC military off-the-shelf (MOTS) platform, the boat can be configured with different systems to support a range of missions.
The vessels have been used by the Finnish Navy for combat operations, patrolling, transportation of troops, evacuation, and command since 2014. They are made for operations in shallow waters, landing, and fast movement in coastal areas.
Lithuania is also set to use M18 combat boats for specialized operations along its Baltic coast.
Lithuania and Finland have joined the CFMAC development and procurement program, which is open to other EU and NATO member states, following a model similar to Patria’s Common Armored Vehicle System (CAVS) program.

title: UAV crashes in open area in Kyiv's Pecherskyi district – mayor
body:
A drone crashed in an open area in the Pechersky district of Kyiv, damaging the facade, part of the roof, and window glazing of a five-story residential building, Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported.

"In the Pechersky district, a UAV crashed in an open area near a 5-story residential building. The facade, part of the roof, and window glazing of the building were damaged," he wrote on Telegram on Thursday.

According to the mayor, the facades of two three-story residential buildings near the crash site were also damaged, and a car in the yard caught fire. Emergency services are working at the scene.

title: Emirati racer Rashid Al Dhaheri takes major step towards F1 dream with Formula 3 move
body: Rashid Al Dhaheri will compete in FIA Formula 3 in 2027 after signing with Van Amersfoort Racing. The Dutch team announced a deal with the 18-year-old Emirati on Thursday in a move that will see him step up in class after finishing fourth in this year’s Formula Regional European Championship. “I’m very proud to be taking the next step into FIA Formula 3 with Van Amersfoort Racing,” said Al Dhareri, a member of the Mercedes Junior Driver Programme since March 2025. “It is an important milestone in my journey, but I know the hard work is only beginning. I’m proud to represent the UAE and the wider region at this level, and I’m looking forward to learning, improving and giving everything I have on and off the track. “Every step has to be earned, and my focus now is on preparing as strongly as possible for 2027. I’m grateful to everyone who has supported me and helped make this opportunity possible.” View this post on Instagram The move means that the UAE will have two drivers on the grid next season after it was also announced that Keanu Al Azhari had signed for Hitech. No Emirati has previously competed in F3. Brad Joyce, team principal for Van Amersfoort Racing, added: “We’re looking forward to welcome Rashid to [the team]. He has had a very strong season in Formula Regional, with three wins and eight podiums, finishing in fourth place in the championship. “He has shown his pace throughout the year and has been able to fight at the front of a very competitive field. That gives us a good starting point as he steps up to Formula 3. We’re looking forward to working with him during the post season tests and preparing for his first F3 season together.” Al Dhaheri's journey in motorsport began at the age of three, and he quickly rose through the ranks, winning the WSK Super Master Series and the South Garda Winter Cup in the 60 Mini category. In 2023, he made his single-seater debut with Prema Racing in the Italian F4 Championship, finishing 10th overall and taking P3 at Macau. He continued to impress in 2024, competing in the Formula 4 UAE Championship and the Euro 4 Championship. title: Houthis urged to lift Taiz siege as Yemen warns of humanitarian catastrophe
body: The EU has urged the Iran-backed Houthi rebels to lift their siege of Taiz, as the Yemeni government appealed to the UN for urgent action to avert a humanitarian catastrophe. Taiz, in south-western Yemen, is controlled by government troops but has long been attacked by the Houthis and remains the main front line in the civil war. In recent weeks, fighting between the rebels and government forces has intensified and the rebels have encircled the area. The EU called on the Houthis to allow desperately needed food, water, medicine and fuel to enter the city . It stressed that civilians and civilian infrastructure must be protected and humanitarian partners must be permitted to deliver essential aid. On Wednesday, the Yemeni government sent a letter from Foreign Minister Afrah Al Zouba to senior UN and humanitarian officials, outlining a sharp deterioration in conditions in Taiz governorate amid a new Houthi escalation. Ms Al Zouba warned that the tightening of the siege on Taiz and surrounding villages could trigger a humanitarian disaster affecting more than four million people. They include residents trapped inside the city and displaced families in districts such as Al Shamayatayn, Al Mawasit and Jabal Habashi. The government urged the UN to apply direct pressure on the Houthis to lift the blockade immediately, reopen all access routes for civilians and supply chains, and ensure sustained, unhindered delivery of food, fuel and drinking water. It also called for stronger monitoring and documentation of violations to preserve evidence, hold perpetrators accountable and prevent impunity. Mustafa Al Noman, Yemen's Deputy Foreign Minister, told The National that the government had no option but to “go all the way” with the battle against the Houthis. “If the government stops at this point, that'll be a disaster on the population and give the Houthis a much higher hand of the situation. It will be a disaster,” he said. Mr Al Noman said there was no hope of a political process with the Houthis. “The government is now deciding that there is no way that there will be a political process and talk with the Houthis and the fight should continue until the government forces can retake the areas the Houthis control since 2015.” “The only solution is a military solution because the Houthis have not left an option for the government to adhere to,” he said. Humanitarian agencies have voiced concern over low food and medical supplies, as well as hospitals' ability to care for thousands of injured people. Wheat flour stocks in the city are nearly exhausted, ‌the UN World Food Programme said. The WFP said remaining food supplies may not last long if access constraints ​continue. At least 600,000 people in Taiz depend on aid, including more than 200,000 children. The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said front-line hospitals in areas such as Marib, Taiz and Yemen's ​Red Sea coast ‌are taking in unprecedented numbers of patients wounded by weapons, with some admitting more than 700 casualties in one week. More ⁠than 200,000 people have been displaced from their homes since fighting began in ⁠recent weeks, the UN's International Organisation for Migration said. “Trauma care staff are under enormous pressure,” said Feras Abusamra, ICRC health co-ordinator. Only a small proportion of Yemen's functioning health centres can provide comprehensive trauma care, he said, while hospitals face large numbers of wounded people and shortages of ​surgical supplies, anaesthesia, oxygen and medicine. The siege of Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, has been in place since 2015 and has long been a severe humanitarian flashpoint, with aid agencies warning that shortages of basic goods and medical supplies are pushing civilians towards crisis conditions.

title: 1.5m Vote Target for Tinubu in Osun Unrealistic, Says Oyetola’s Former Spokesperson
body: Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo A former Chief Press Secretary to the immediate-past Governor of Osun State, Gboyega Oyetola, Ismail Omipidan, has questioned the feasibility of securing 1.5 million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Osun State in the 2027 general election, warning that the political strategy surrounding the target could undermine the All Progressives Congress (APC). Omipidan also cautioned Tinubu and the APC national leadership against political arrangements that could alienate loyal party members, arguing that resentment within the party could weaken grassroots mobilisation ahead of the presidential election. In an opinion article, he maintained that Osun State’s historical voting patterns did not support the projection of 1.5 million presidential votes, urging the president and the party leadership to adopt a strategy that reflects the state’s electoral history, political peculiarities, and the interests of its people. He also expressed concern over the political implications of Governor Ademola Adeleke’s reported emergence as Osun State coordinator of Tinubu’s 2027 re-election campaign, warning that the arrangement could generate discontent among APC members if their established political structures were not adequately considered. “In war, just like in politics, strategy is everything,” Omipidan wrote, arguing that a strategy driven by the ambitions of a few individuals could fail if it did not accommodate the interests of the wider party membership. Omipidan said he first heard about the proposed 1.5 million-vote target less than 24 hours after the APC lost the August 15, 2026, governorship election in Osun State. He added that the subsequent repetition of the target by the party’s National Secretary, Senator Ajibola Basiru, had heightened his concerns about the political calculations behind the proposal. The APC lost the governorship election to Adeleke, who contested on the platform of the Accord Party. According to Omipidan, the proposed target appeared inconsistent with Osun’s historical presidential election results, as the state had never recorded up to one million votes for a presidential candidate in previous elections. Citing the 2011 presidential election, he said the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN) candidate polled 299,711 votes in Osun State, while the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) secured 188,409 votes, with registered voters standing at 1,342,289. In 2015, he said the APC won the state with 383,603 votes against the PDP’s 249,929, while the number of registered voters was 1,407,107. For the 2019 presidential election, Omipidan cited 347,634 votes for the APC and 337,377 for the PDP. In the 2023 presidential election, he said the APC polled 342,941 votes in Osun, while the PDP secured 353,860. He argued that the figures demonstrated the challenge of achieving the proposed 1.5 million votes, particularly without a substantial increase in voter participation. “Historically, Osun State has never posted up to a million votes in any presidential election, and it will not happen next year, unless some persons just want to write figures,” he said. Omipidan acknowledged that voter turnout in presidential elections could differ from that recorded during governorship elections but maintained that the distinction should inform the party’s electoral calculations. He urged the APC leadership to establish realistic targets based on the state’s voting patterns and develop a mobilisation strategy capable of attracting voters across Osun State. Omipidan expressed concern over the political arrangements being developed in Osun State to secure Tinubu’s re-election. He specifically questioned the implications of Adeleke’s reported appointment as the president’s campaign coordinator in the state, arguing that the APC must ensure the arrangement did not undermine its existing structures. While acknowledging the governor’s role in the emerging campaign arrangement, Omipidan maintained that the APC should be allowed to strengthen its organisational machinery and mobilise its members in support of Tinubu. He warned that party members who felt sidelined could become less committed to the campaign, potentially weakening the grassroots mobilisation required to achieve the desired electoral outcome. According to him, the presidency and the APC national leadership must pay attention to the concerns of party loyalists who have invested time and resources in building the party. He also cautioned against political arrangements that could create unnecessary divisions between Tinubu and the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, a prominent APC figure in Osun State. “President Tinubu and Oyetola must tread softly and cautiously,” he wrote, urging both leaders to consider the implications of the emerging political dynamics. Omipidan suggested that those promoting the current arrangement could inadvertently create tension between the two leaders if the interests of the established APC structure were not adequately protected. He argued that the party’s national leadership should not underestimate the feelings of members who might perceive the arrangement as favouring a few political actors at the expense of the wider party. He maintained that the success of the president’s re-election campaign would depend partly on the ability of the APC to reconcile competing interests and ensure that its members remained actively involved in the mobilisation process. Omipidan further argued that political strategies must reflect the peculiarities of the states in which they are deployed, noting that an approach that works in one part of the country might not necessarily produce the same results elsewhere. He maintained that Osun’s political culture, voters’ expectations and prevailing interests should be considered in determining how the APC would pursue Tinubu’s re-election. According to him, electoral mobilisation involves more than bringing prominent political figures together or announcing ambitious vote targets. He argued that voters and party members are influenced by personal interests, political loyalties, emotions and expectations, which can shape their decisions at the polls. Omipidan also drew on the Rational Choice Theory associated with economist and philosopher Adam Smith to explain how personal interests could influence voting decisions. He said his earlier work applying the theory to electoral behaviour showed that voters’ decisions were influenced not only by candidates’ identities or party affiliations but also by their assessment of personal interests and potential benefits. According to him, voters often consider available alternatives before deciding which candidate or political platform they believe will best serve their interests. He argued that the theory offered a useful framework for understanding why political arrangements that appeared advantageous to party leaders might not automatically translate into widespread support among party members or voters. He, therefore, called for greater engagement with stakeholders in Osun State to address concerns surrounding the emerging campaign arrangement before they developed into deeper divisions. According to him, the APC needs to strengthen its structures in the state, address the concerns of aggrieved members and ensure that its campaign arrangements encourage rather than discourage grassroots participation.

title: Musk Tells Zelensky to ‘Go’ as Ukraine Questions US Support
body:
Tech billionaire Elon Musk called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky “to go” on Thursday, as Kyiv raised concerns that US restrictions on satellite communications and intelligence sharing were weakening Ukraine’s defenses against Russian attacks.
“And so the slaughter continues,” Musk wrote on X . “Time for Zelensky to go.”
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The dispute escalated after Ukraine reported restrictions on military Starlink services, which Ukrainian forces rely on for battlefield communications and drone operations.
And so the slaughter continues … Time for Zelensky to go https://t.co/tMBThajxhH
Zelensky warned that the restrictions could lead to significant casualties as Russia intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure.
“It’s a big mistake,” he said. “This decision will bring a lot of human losses… People will die.”
He urged Musk, whose SpaceX operates Starlink, to restore the service, saying he hoped the disruption was the result of a technical problem.
Musk said on Wednesday that Starshield is owned and controlled by the US government , which determines restrictions on its use.
He distinguished it from Starlink, a commercial satellite network used by Ukraine for communications, and said it should not be used for offensive military operations.
The satellite dispute comes amid concerns that reduced US intelligence sharing could leave Ukraine more vulnerable to Russian missile attacks.
Ukrainian officials told CNN that the loss of intelligence could give Russian forces an advantage on the battlefield. A European official also questioned Washington’s explanation that weather had caused gaps in missile-warning information.
For two consecutive nights, air raid alerts in Kyiv came only after Russian ballistic missiles were already approaching or striking the capital.
On Oct. 12-13, Russia launched successive ballistic missile attacks, hitting civilian infrastructure and a major power plant. Zelensky said Ukraine had received no advance warning of the launches from Western partners .
The Trump administration has previously warned it could suspend intelligence sharing and halt European purchases of US weapons for Ukraine if Kyiv refused to stop deep strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
The growing dispute has also spilled into relations between Kyiv and Washington over energy policy.
Zelensky said he felt “betrayed” after US President Donald Trump announced a diesel supply deal with heavily sanctioned Russia.
Trump, facing key midterm elections next month, has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries for contributing to fuel shortages and rising prices at US gas stations.
