title: Nausėda proposes EU leaders discuss ban on Russian grain exports via Baltic Sea
body:
President of Lithuania Gitanas Nausėda will propose that European Union leaders discuss the possibility of banning Russian grain exports through the Baltic Sea, emphasizing the continued need to support Ukraine.
He said this to journalists in Brussels on Thursday upon arriving for a two-day meeting of the European Council.
In the view of the Lithuanian leader, the current situation is complicated, requiring continued pressure on Russia, strict enforcement of sanctions compliance—specifically discussing the possibility of blocking grain exports through Baltic Sea ports—and ongoing military, political, and economic support for Ukraine.
Speaking about statements regarding a ceasefire in the war waged by Russia against Ukraine, the President of Lithuania stressed that this process must be bilateral. He noted that it cannot be a one-way street, explaining that if Ukraine halts attacks on Russian energy infrastructure while Russia retains full freedom of action to strike Ukrainian energy, it would lead to catastrophic consequences in the war.
Nausėda stated that it is unclear how anyone can speak about a ceasefire while raising demands and imperatives for only one side. He emphasized that Russia is also obligated to comply with international norms, though adding that it would be naive to expect compliance with international rules from a country that unleashed war in 2022—a conflict now entering its fifth year.
He pointed out that Russia is challenging the Western way of life, rules, the rule of law, democratic principles, and human rights. According to Nausėda, the conflict is not simply about territories, and it would be naive to believe that Russia's goal is merely capturing new lands, as its actions challenge the very foundation of Western society.
The Lithuanian President also expressed satisfaction that two negotiation clusters have already been opened, voicing hope for the opening of the remaining two clusters. He expressed conviction that Ukraine must receive positive signals—which currently only Europe can provide—with one of the strongest signals being the prospect and "light at the end of the tunnel" regarding Ukraine's integration into the European Union.

title: New DICT chief faces task of putting house in order amid digital ambitions
body: MANILA, Philippines — As the Philippines races to modernize government services, improve internet connectivity, and position itself for the age of artificial intelligence (AI), the agency tasked with leading that transformation faces a more immediate challenge: putting its own house in order. This is the situation that newly appointed Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) Secretary Robert Joseph de Claro faces. The former Social Security System (SSS) chief replaced Henry Aguda following a tumultuous tenure marked by budget controversies, internal disagreements reported in the media, and questions over the implementation of government technology projects. De Claro has promised a comprehensive review of the department’s projects, budgets, and procurement processes, with a clearer plan for the agency, BusinessMirror reported. Give him 3 months, he told reporters. The commitment comes as the DICT faces mounting pressure to demonstrate that it can effectively manage public resources while delivering on the administration’s digitalization goals. Questions over the department’s financial management surfaced as early as late 2025, when DICT officials disclosed that its budget contained P8.3 billion in excess funds , compared to what they had originally proposed under the National Expenditure Program. Officials at the time said P5 billion had been used for connectivity initiatives, including the Bayanihan SIM program and free Wi-Fi for schools, while P3.3 billion was not released to the agency. Then-undersecretary Christina Faye Condez-de Sagon rejected allegations linking her to questionable budget insertions. De Sagon said, “… we were a disruptive force in DICT. We brought in a new kind of leadership, we brought in better governance, I believe,” in an ABS-CBN report . In hindsight, these were already probably murmurs of trouble in paradise because in August 2026, Malacanang would dismiss Condez-de Sagon , and assistant secretary June Vincent Manuel Gaudan over alleged procurement violations. In December 2025 as well, Rappler uncovered internal DICT audits that alleged eGov Undersecretary David Almirol Jr. had conflict of interest issues arising from contracts between the agency and companies he formerly had ties with. A separate audit also warned of the possible weak data protections due to the absence of contracts in the implementation of the eGov app together with partner local governments. Later in April 2026, the agency once again faced scrutiny over the reliability of its digital services. A two-day outage of the eGovPH app exposed infrastructure and funding constraints after a surge in users overwhelmed systems. At a Senate hearing, Senator Bam Aquino said, “You need to subscribe to a higher tier. Usually, you just pay — and that solves your problem,” referring to scalable cloud infrastructure. “Clearly, that’s not acceptable,” Aquino reprimanded the agency. Internal disagreements further complicated matters. In May, BusinessMirror reported that two information technology organizations warned that tensions between Aguda and Almirol Jr. could undermine public services and the country’s digital transformation agenda, and called for cooperation between the two. In September, the Office of the Ombudsman announced a fact-finding investigation into alleged “ghost internet” projects involving the agency’s flagship Free Wifi For All initiative, including possible payments for undelivered services and the use of substandard or counterfeit software. That same month, the House also deferred its proposed budget due to concerns over the supposed lack of results in online safety, particularly in the wake of the multiple fatal school shootings in the second half of the year, with supposed ties to online entities influencing the youth to commit violent acts or nihilistic violent extremism. Aguda’s final weeks were marked by backlash over the DICT’s temporary blocking of Discord , a decision reversed within a day. In an odd incident, the DICT retracted its statement that the House had invited Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to a hearing, blaming news organizations for spreading the information, even if it came from its own Facebook page itself. A mere error? Or a sign of internal turmoil surfacing? Now, for de Claro, the challenge extends beyond resolving the controversies he inherited. The DICT must simultaneously expand public connectivity, strengthen cybersecurity, maintain digital government platforms, and establish policies for emerging technologies — its known mandates . But first, these ambitions will require institutional stability, and regaining the public confidence in the agency’s ability to deliver after a year of tumult. For an agency central to the Philippines’ digital future, rebuilding confidence in its own operations by sorting out whatever factions that have formed in the past year may be the first step toward fulfilling that mandate. And after that, can new leadership demonstrate that existing programs are properly funded, implemented, and monitored? De Claro has 3 months to get this started on the right foot. – Rappler.com

title: Romania Says Eight People Missing After Fire on Vessel in Black Sea
body:
Romania said eight people were missing after a fire broke out on a vessel flying the San Marino flag on Thursday morning, the latest incident in the Black Sea, which has seen a series of drone attacks.
Suspected Russian drones have hit several ships off Romania and neighbouring Bulgaria since last week in a spillover from the Ukraine war.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The vessel, named the Wine Trader, reported a fire at around 7:00 am (0400 GMT), approximately 13 nautical miles southeast of the Romanian city of Sulina, the Romanian Naval Authority said in a press release.
“There were 12 people on board the vessel. Four of them are safe, whilst eight are currently missing,” it added.
A search and rescue operation was underway, involving a vessel and a helicopter, it said.
Romanian authorities did not say whether a drone caused the fire.
The incident comes after Romania said on Wednesday it was probing a possible fresh drone attack on a tanker off its Black Sea coast.
Rescuers rushed to help the Comoros Islands-flagged Yara J after a fire broke out, but the ship’s crew managed to douse the fire themselves.
“Whether it was struck by a drone or not, an investigation is currently underway,” defence minister Radu Miruta told the Digi24 television channel.
“This is a matter of significant gravity, given that such incidents are occurring in Romanian territorial waters,” he said.
At least 163 civilian and commercial vessels were hit on the Black Sea in the first eight months of this year, according to Turkey’s IMEAK chamber of shipping.

title: Russia attacks Poltava region gas production infrastructure overnight
body:
On the night of October 15, Russia attacked the gas production infrastructure of the Naftogaz group in Poltava region, the company reported on Thursday.

As a result of Russian UAV strike, technological equipment was damaged, a fire broke out at the facility, and operations were suspended, the group noted.

"At the time of the attack, employees were in a shelter; none of the personnel were injured. Assessment of the consequences and scale of the destruction is ongoing on site," Acting CEO of Naftogaz Serhiy Fedorenko stated.

title: Strait of Hormuz closed, transit must be coordinated
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 15 (MNA) – Iran's deputy army coordinator said the Strait of Hormuz is closed and any transit requires coordination, citing rising US gasoline prices as proof.
Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, Chief of Staff and Deputy Coordinator of Iran's Army, said the Strait of Hormuz is closed and that any passage through it must be coordinated.
Speaking to reporters on Thursday on the sidelines of a ceremony honoring army nurses, Sayyari said that if the strait were not closed and oil were passing through, gasoline prices in the United States would not have risen. He called this clear and evident.
He described the military posture in the region: the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps Navy is firmly positioned in the west of the Strait of Hormuz, while the Army of the Islamic Republic of Iran is present with authority from the east of the strait to the north of the Sea of Oman, exercising full control and surveillance over the area.
Sayyari stressed that any transit must be coordinated, warning that otherwise "you see in the news what happens."

title: Ukraine is going back to hitting Russian oil after its Trump-pressured pause, during which Kyiv got no US warnings of incoming ballistic missiles
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, ending a three-day pause it held at Washington’s request, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the Financial Times in an interview published on 15 October. Russia kept bombing Ukraine’s energy system throughout the pause, while Kyiv lost US missile warnings and its Starlink service slowed. Zelenskyy said Ukraine would halt energy strikes again only in exchange for more US air defense. Ukraine's deep-strike campaign targets the Russian oil industry, which fuels Russia's army in Ukraine and earns the export revenue funding the war. Striking the plants that turn Russian crude into fuel, 12 of them hit in September alone, is one of the few levers Kyiv controls on Moscow’s war income. US President Donald Trump has blamed those strikes for higher US fuel prices, which most analysts attribute to the Iran war, and Washington has threatened to withhold intelligence, and reportedly weapons, unless Kyiv gives it up. Each step Washington takes toward Moscow, from fuel waivers to talk of frozen assets, widens the gap Europe and Ukraine must fill, while Russia gains revenue and time to keep striking. A pause that bought nothing Zelenskyy said he stopped the refinery strikes for three days to meet US wishes, but Russia kept hitting Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and killing civilians. During the pause, Ukraine received no US warnings of ballistic missile launches, he said. Starlink also slowed across the country, hampering front-line operations and mid-range strikes on Russian military targets, he added. Russia used those days to fire 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones at Ukraine’s grid overnight into 14 October, leaving at least 600,000 people without power. “We hold energy ceasefire from our side,” Zelenskyy told Piers Morgan on 14 October. Of the Starlink slowdown, he added: “I’m sure that they knew what they did.” The price of another pause Ukraine could again stop hitting Russian energy only if it receives more US interceptors for its Patriot systems, Zelenskyy told the FT. He warned that a halt could simply invite more US-Russia deals that feed Russia’s war machine, and predicted the next one would involve gas. Explore further “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government”: Musk says Trump, not SpaceX, is behind cut hitting Ukraine US intelligence officials had warned Ukraine’s embassy in Washington that a new strike on Russia’s energy facilities would end all intelligence sharing at once, The Washington Post reported , citing a person familiar with the matter. Washington has not fully cut it off, but the threat stands, the person said. Trump said on 13 October that the US was still sharing intelligence. Washington’s other moves toward Moscow A senior US official told Axios the administration had nothing to do with the Starlink limits , which Elon Musk had blamed on the US military. The administration is also considering easing sanctions on shadow fleet tankers, which have carried oil from Russia, Iran, and Venezuela, so the blacklisted vessels could haul non-sanctioned cargo, a US official told Reuters. The US Energy Department said the move would not help Russia ship its oil or fuel. Washington eased sanctions on Russian oil this spring, after which Russia’s oil income jumped $890 million in a week, and it extended that waiver despite telling allies it would not. US envoys also proposed unfreezing part of Russia’s frozen assets to lure Moscow back to talks, an idea European officials rejected, the Financial Times reported . title: AI is changing us as humans, says pioneering Arab scientist
body: AI will help humans operate at a "higher intellectual level", even if that means ditching some of the life skills we once had, a leading Arab scientist has said. Fadel Adib, an MIT professor and successful AI start-up founder, said it was not necessarily bad that people are coming to rely on large language models such as ChatGPT. "We first augment humans and increase their productivity, and then eventually we also augment humans with robots, not just with AI ... increase productivity there as well. AI is changing who we are as humans," he told The National at a World Economic Forum event in Dubai. His company, Cartesian, uses AI technology to help robots navigate hundreds of warehouses and retail stores in 15 countries, tracking and collecting thousands of different products. "Some of us cannot operate without asking ChatGPT the question, and that might not necessarily be bad," he said at the Annual Meeting of Global Future Leaders, which he co-chaired. "I'm a professor. So I remember when people used to say 'oh, students are not memorising anymore in schools, and we're losing the ability to memorise.' "What's the point of memorising if you can Google everything? And maybe AI is going to help us operate at a higher intellectual level. "And as humans, we've repeatedly managed to do that. We don't learn how to make fire anymore, and we don't need to. "As humans, we've managed to repeatedly figure out how we operate at a higher level of abstraction, and I think we're going to do that again." Dr Adib, who grew up in Tripoli, Lebanon and was given a Dh1 million Great Arab Minds award in 2023 by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, also predicted further challenges to US tech firms' dominance of AI. Speaking earlier at the same event in Dubai, Omar Sultan Al Olama, the UAE's AI minister, said that superpower dominance of AI was not appealing, and that middle powers and sovereign governments would want an alternative. "AI is moving at an accelerated pace. It is moving from the digital into the physical world," said Dr Adib. "If you look at the 1990s, where the internet was growing... that was a US-led world. "Today, there is the race between the US and China on AI. What role is Europe and Africa and Latin America and the rest of Asia going to play? The answer is not clear that just the US or China is gonna win this race." He added: "Our first prime adopters were in Europe. And if you look at the United Arab Emirates, there's a lot of investment. There's a lot of AI investments here in Dubai, and they are deploying it. They're seeing real change. And in Abu Dhabi, with the creation of G42, and the investment in data infrastructure. "And as a scientist, I love challenges, and as a technologist, I love the optimism of it. There is an opportunity for real change and impact."

title: Make peace, Iran reformist urges, as hardliners rule out surrender
body: A former Tehran mayor has urged Iran to reach an agreement with the US to end the war, as internal divisions widen over how to respond to Washington amid a deepening economic crisis. Gholamhossein Karbaschi, a reformist politician, made the remarks on Iranian state television last on Wednesday, warning that a prolonged conflict would deepen domestic hardship. “We cannot take on America’s power and diplomacy,” Mr Karbaschi said. “We must make a non-emotional assessment of the situation." Mr Karbaschi said there was no clear end in sight and that officials should consider the consequences of continuing the fighting. “We were never volunteers for war,” he said, adding that families faced uncertainty over whether hostilities would resume. Iran is facing soaring inflation and pressure on household finances, while restrictions on oil exports have contrained a key source of government revenue. Long petrol queues have also been reported. Mr Karbaschi also criticised the Iranian attacks in June on three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, saying they had derailed the peace process and given Washington a pretext to breach the interim accord. “If the Islamabad agreement had been implemented as it should have been, the incident involving the targeting of the three ships would not have happened,” he said. “We must distinguish between the reason for violating the agreement and a pretext for violating it.” The attacks he was referring to appear to have occurred about 10 days after the US and Iran signed the Islamabad memorandum of understanding on June 17. Mr Karbaschi said the interim agreement had been advantageous to Tehran and had surprised observers because Washington accepted its terms while Israel opposed them. He argued that the subsequent attacks on the ships gave the US an opportunity to breach the agreement. He also questioned who had ordered the strikes, adding that nobody had publicly claimed responsibility. “Everyone says, ‘We don’t know who attacked the three ships,’” he said. Referring to President Masoud Pezeshkian, he asked: “Can it be that the president doesn’t know?” 'Washington's ambassadors' Mr Karbaschi's comments were reported by other media outlets on Thursday morning, including the Entekhab newspaper. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps responded sharply. Its spokesman, Hossein Mohebi, rejected suggestions that the attacks were unauthorised or carried out without the approval of senior officials. Mr Mohebi described the strikes as a “decisive and crushing response” to what he called the third US breach of its commitments. He accused Washington of breaking its commitments twice during negotiations and a third time after signing the memorandum. “In the armed forces, no action is taken without observing the chain of command and co-ordinating with senior officials,” he was quoted as saying by the reformist Shargh newspaper on Thursday. The dispute has also prompted attacks by Hossein Shariatmadari, editor-in-chief of the ultraconservative Kayhan newspaper, on former foreign minister Mohammad Javad Zarif, former president Hassan Rouhani and politician Hossein Marashi. Mr Shariatmadari accused the three of advancing positions on ending the war or preventing renewed fighting, which allegedly serve US and Israeli interests. He described Mr Marashi’s proposal for a "tactical retreat" to avoid another war as a surrender and rejected Mr Rouhani’s suggestion of a referendum on whether military attacks should continue. “Although the US has no embassy in Iran, some political figures effectively act as Washington’s ambassadors through their positions,” Mr Shariatmadari wrote in an editorial. The comments reflect the level of disagreement among Iranian politicians over the terms of a possible settlement, the conduct of the war and the risks of renewed hostilities.

title: Sybiha: Putin's response to energy truce calls was missiles, drones
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha stated that Russian attacks on energy infrastructure resulted in civilian casualties and left over 600,000 people without power, calling this Putin's response to calls for an "energy truce".

"This is Putin’s response to calls for an energy ceasefire: missiles and drones instead of peace," he wrote on the X social network.

According to the minister, Russia must face stronger sanctions and stricter compliance monitoring rather than the easing of restrictions or concessions. Ukraine, in turn, urgently requires additional air defense systems and interceptor missiles.

Sybiha also expressed gratitude to President of the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly Pere Joan Pons for condemning Russian attacks and for the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly's continued support of Ukraine.

title: [Pastilan] Sara wants to answer? Start with the wealth
body: There is something unconvincing about Sara Duterte and her defenders suddenly discovering the virtues of a full and fair hearing after prosecutors withdrew three of the four articles of impeachment against the Vice President this week. The complaint is not entirely without merit. The prosecution spent over a month presenting evidence on grave threats and the alleged misuse of confidential funds, only to abandon those charges, including the one on bribery, after it was done with its case on unexplained wealth. Articles 1, 3, and 4 are gone, leaving Article 2 to carry the entire burden. What looked like a broad prosecution has become a concentrated gamble. The prosecutors have narrowed their battlefield and staked their chances of conviction on a single front. Must Read Dropping 3 impeachment articles vs Sara, who benefits? It is possible to question the wisdom of this decision without pretending that it constitutes some monumental injustice. Lawyers are entitled to decide which charges they believe could get the job done. The objective of a prosecution is not to accumulate the largest number of accusations, like stamps in a passport, but to secure a conviction. Al Capone was not undone by a full catalogue of his crimes but by tax evasion. Sometimes, it can only take one to do someone in. But what is hard to stomach is the sudden eruption of indignation from a camp that has spent some time behaving as though the very act of asking questions was an intolerable persecution. Where was this appetite for giving answers before the impeachment trial? Where was it during the House hearings? Where was it when Sara Duterte was repeatedly asked to explain her finances and responded with verbal evasion? Her celebrated answer, “ shimenet, ” was not an explanation. It was a noise made in place of one. Sara has perfected the art of substituting grievance for argument. She presents herself as the victim of political persecution, accuses her critics of malice, and wraps herself in the familiar costume of the embattled underdog. Her defenders dutifully repeat the performance. Yet the essential questions remain stubbornly unanswered. Where did the money come from, where did it go, and why do the figures appear so difficult to reconcile? When her lawyers were pressed during the early weeks of the impeachment trial, their refrain was that they would answer “at the proper time.” One might wonder whether this proper time belongs to the same category as the mythical land of milk and honey, forever promised but never reached. Now that prosecutors have withdrawn three of the four articles , the defense has discovered a fresh cause for outrage. Its leader has lambasted the prosecution, as though the abandonment of charges were an assault on the accused rather than a tactical decision by the accusers. Did I get it right that they want four instead of one charge against their client, or was it just to feed the Duterte trolls? One is also tempted to wonder whether the outburst has anything to do with the consequences of a shorter trial, including fewer appearances and potentially lower lawyers’ appearance fees. As I watched the defense lawyer throw a tantrum, one sentence kept playing at the back of my head: “Your Honor, we respectfully appeal this decision on financial grounds.” That is speculation, of course, and should not be mistaken for an established motive. But the spasm of indignation did invite an uncomfortable question about who benefits from dragging proceedings out. The withdrawal may also have upset the Duterte camp ‘s apparent penchant for delay. A defense that had contemplated presenting more than 90 witnesses might now find that the stage has become considerably smaller. This brings to mind Sara’s own advice about the need for a Plan A, Plan B, and Plan C. Applied to this situation, it is sound advice, though rather less impressive coming from someone whose political survival increasingly depends on never having to explain herself. One wonders what comes after indignation, evasion and the familiar claim of persecution. Is there a Plan D, or does the alphabet run out before the excuses do? What is done is done. The prosecution has made its decision, and the impeachment court has accepted the withdrawal. The remaining business is therefore quite straightforward. Sara and her lawyers should answer the allegations that remain, rather than continue to manufacture distractions around the manner in which the case is being prosecuted. The unexplained wealth allegations cannot simply be waved away as fabrications. The prosecution has presented financial documents and called witnesses from the Office of the Ombudsman, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System, the Anti-Money Laundering Council, the Bureau of Internal Revenue, banks and insurance companies. A financial forensic analyst has also presented his findings. They are substantial enough to merit answers. It is difficult to imagine why all those bankers would lie, and how they could possibly have managed to do so in concert. And the figures are not difficult to understand. Sara’s declared net worth rose from P7.2 million in 2007 to P98.6 million in 2025. Even when she was already Vice President, she did not divest and retained a stake in at Metro City Chow Foods Corporation and Gencorp Industries Incorporated, a firm which secured Davao City government contracts worth P34.2 million. Her brother, Mayor Baste Duterte, claimed he did not know Sara had interests in the firm even as he said that he merely appointed a representative to sign the contracts. Authorities also reported P4.4 billion in covered and suspicious transactions linked to Sara and her husband between 2007 and 2025, including P319 million in remittances from China to Cale88 Foods Corporation. Later, Sara asked whether it was wrong to do business with Chinese firms, stopping just short of admitting what the question plainly invited her to confront. If one happens to be the vice president, the answer is yes. The proceedings examined properties linked to her husband, 19 insurance policies, and questions about Sara’s compensation income and constitutional restrictions on outside employment. The BIR cited records showing she received compensation from the Davao City Hall even when was already getting paid as vice president. If it wasn’t double compensation, I don’t know what is. On October 9, a financial forensic analyst reported over P817 million in allegedly undeclared assets and income from 2022 to 2025. He said the figure could reach P1.5 billion without his conservative assumptions, citing discrepancies between companies’ declared capital and earnings and the extent of alleged under-reporting. Let’s return to the question: Was all this wealth declared in her SALNs? Did she disclose the full extent of her wealth? Given the documented figures, “persecution” hardly qualifies as a financial explanation. If the figures are wrong, identify the errors. If the assets were lawfully acquired, explain their source. If the properties and income were properly declared, produce the records. If the companies’ accounts have been misread, demonstrate how. The defense has every right to dismantle the prosecution’s case, but it must do so with something more substantial than indignation. Sara is entitled to answer, and answer she should. What she is not entitled to is the presumption that demanding answers from her constitutes an act of political persecution. Public office comes with obligations, and declaring one’s assets is not an optional exercise. The withdrawal of three impeachment articles may have changed the prosecution’s strategy, but it did not magically resolve the questions raised by the financial evidence. The point is to establish the facts, not to award victory to whichever camp shouts loudest. Sara has told people to always have a back-up plan. Perhaps it is time to try a more radical proposition. Go to the impeachment court, answer the questions, produce the documents, and let the evidence speak pertaining to the unexplained wealth charge. So who is behind Sara’s problems? Sara, chiefly. If all that documented wealth was not declared in her SALNs, she has no one but herself to thank for the questions it raises. She wants to answer? Then answer she must. Pastilan. – Rappler.com

title: IG Seeks Stronger Intelligence Gathering to Prevent Attacks on Schools
body: Funmi Ogundare The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Rilwan Disu, yesterday called for stronger intelligence gathering, early-warning systems, and improved collaboration between schools and security agencies to prevent attacks on educational institutions across the country. He stated that sustainable school protection requires a shift from reactive responses to preventive measures, stressing that safeguarding schools must be treated as a national security priority rather than the sole responsibility of school administrators or security agencies. Disu also called for stronger police-community partnerships, improved emergency preparedness, and effective information-sharing among government, school authorities, parents, community leaders, and other stakeholders to address threats to educational institutions. The IGP made the call while delivering the keynote address at the 7th annual summit of the Education Writers’ Association of Nigeria (EWAN) held in Lagos with the theme: ‘Schools Under Threat: From Reactive Responses to Sustainable Protection’. Disu, who was represented by the Lagos State Commissioner of Police, Tijani Fatai, said the consequences of insecurity in schools extended beyond victims of attacks to include heightened anxiety among families, loss of public confidence, disruption of academic activities and the denial of educational opportunities to children. According to him, a society cannot achieve its full potential when insecurity prevents children from accessing education or discourages teachers from performing their duties in safe and supportive environments. “School safety must therefore be understood not merely as the responsibility of school administrators or security agencies, but as a national security priority and a collective obligation,” he said. He noted that although immediate responses to security incidents, including rescuing victims, apprehending offenders and restoring safety, remained essential, greater attention must be given to identifying vulnerabilities and preventing the recurrence of attacks. The police boss said the police would continue to strengthen intelligence-led operations, improve threat assessment and encourage the prompt reporting of credible security concerns. The IGP urged school administrators, teachers, parents, students and community members to report suspicious developments through appropriate channels, adding that such information must be professionally assessed and acted upon where necessary. He also emphasised the importance of trust between security agencies and communities, noting that effective partnerships depended on professional conduct, accountability and public confidence. On emergency preparedness, Disu called on schools to establish appropriate safety arrangements and procedures that reflected their locations, sizes and levels of vulnerability. He urged EWAN to sustain the conversation beyond the summit by developing practical recommendations, strengthening professional networks and maintaining engagement with institutions responsible for education and security. “The future of our nation depends, in no small measure, on the opportunities we create for our children today. Protecting those opportunities is a responsibility we must all take seriously,” he said. In his remarks, the Chairman of the occasion and former Vice-Chancellor, University of Lagos, Prof. Oluwatoyin Ogundipe, called for a unified national framework for school safety, urging federal, state and local governments to strengthen early-warning systems, improve security coordination and prioritise preventive measures to protect schools against attacks. He said Nigeria must move beyond reactive responses to school attacks, including abductions of learners and teachers, to sustainable protection strategies that prevent threats, mitigate their impact and ensure continuity of education during crises. Ogundipe, who is the chairman of the Governing Board of the National Universities Commission (NUC), said the recurring attacks on educational institutions in some parts of the country were not isolated incidents but a pattern threatening national development, disrupting learning and leaving affected communities traumatised. According to him, protecting schools requires more than deploying security personnel after an attack, condemning incidents or providing temporary relief to affected communities. “For too long, our responses have been largely reactive, mobilising security after an incident, issuing statements of condemnation, and providing temporary relief to affected communities. While these actions are necessary, they are not sufficient,” Ogundipe, who was represented by the Dean of Faculty of Education, Prof. Joseph Awoyinfa, stated He urged stakeholders to build systems capable of identifying and addressing security threats before they escalate, stressing that effective school protection requires collaboration among security agencies, local communities, school authorities and the media. He said journalists have a critical role to play in identifying emerging risks, amplifying community concerns, investigating security gaps and ensuring that vulnerabilities are addressed before they result in tragedies. He also identified insecurity, weak governance in remote areas and socio-economic pressures as some of the underlying factors that made schools vulnerable to attacks. Ogundipe advocated sustained investment in school infrastructure, surveillance systems, safe transportation and secure boarding facilities, with greater attention given to rural schools and institutions in conflict-prone areas. Earlier in his remarks, the Chairman of the Education Writers’ Association of Nigeria (EWAN), Mojeed Alabi, urged journalists to intensify investigative and accountability reporting on school safety, warning that persistent attacks on educational institutions threaten the future of Nigerian children and national development. Alabi said journalists must move beyond reporting school attacks after they occur to investigating security vulnerabilities, scrutinising funds allocated for school protection and tracking the implementation of government policies aimed at preventing attacks. He said the protection of schools required coordinated action by government, security agencies, education authorities, communities and the media, stressing that journalism remained essential to exposing security lapses and holding public officials accountable. “Children are not safe until every school is safe,” he said, adding that no parent should have to choose between a child’s education and safety, while no teacher should have to work under the threat of abduction Alabi recalled the 2014 abduction of schoolgirls in Chibok, Borno State, and the subsequent Dapchi abduction, alongside other attacks on educational institutions, as evidence that insecurity in schools remained a persistent national challenge.

title: Marine Protection Initiatives in South Al Sharqiyah Governorate
body:
Sur: During the month of September 2026, specialised teams from the Environment Department in South Al Sharqiyah Governorate conducted a campaign during which the participants saved the lives of 201 adult turtles that went stray from their natural habitat. They also brought a total of 57,744 hatchlings of turtles back to the sea during the campaign.
Sur: During the month of September 2026, specialised teams from the Environment Department in South Al Sharqiyah Governorate conducted a campaign during which the participants saved the lives of 201 adult turtles that went stray from their natural habitat. They also brought a total of 57,744 hatchlings of turtles back to the sea during the campaign.
The Environment Department in South Al Sharqiyah undertake constant efforts to raise public awareness about the importance of preserving marine ecosystems. These efforts involve educational programmes that combine fieldwork with community outreach. The drive includes initiatives to protect nesting sites, monitor turtles and their hatchlings and handle emergency cases. The drive, which laid emphasis on community engagement, was supported by Oman India Fertiliser Company (OMIFCO). The recent activities took place at Ras Al Hadd Turtle Reserve—a prime nesting site for sea turtles. During such campaigns, specialists and environment activists patrol the beach, track egg-laying sites and assist hatchlings when necessary. They also facilitate visitor access to the sites and address behaviours that could endanger the turtles or spoil their habitat.

title: War update: 260 combat engagements on front line over past day, most in Pokrovsk sector
body:
Ukrinform reports this, citing a statement by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on Facebook on the situation as of 08:00 on Thursday, October 15.
The enemy launched one missile strike and 85 airstrikes, dropping 278 guided aerial bombs.
In addition, Russian invaders deployed 8,224 kamikaze drones and carried out 2,625 attacks on settlements and Ukrainian military positions, 15 of them using multiple-launch rocket systems.
In Sumy region, the settlements of Bezsalivka, Koreniok, Tovstodubove, Sopych, Ulanove, Malushyne, Rohizne, Kucherivka, Yastrubshchyna, Neskuchne, Bachivsk, Khrinivka, Volfyne, Kozache and Shalyhyne came under fire. In Chernihiv region, Liskivshchyna was shelled. Partyzanske and Sukhodil were also hit by airstrikes.
Ukraine's Defense Forces aviation, missile forces and artillery struck a Russian troop concentration area and a drone launch site.
On the Northern Slobozhanshchyna and Kursk axes, the enemy carried out two assault operations, launched one airstrike using a guided aerial bomb, and shelled Ukrainian military positions and settlements 55 times, including twice with multiple-launch rocket systems.
On the Southern Slobozhanshchyna axis, Ukrainian units repelled 12 attacks. Russian invaders attacked near the settlements of Izbytske, Ternova, Okhrimivka, Chuhunivka, Mykolaivka and Rybalchyne, and advanced toward Zakharivka, Chorne and Mala Vovcha.
On the Kupiansk axis, the enemy made 18 attempts to improve its positions, including offensive operations toward Radkivka.
On the Lyman axis, Russian forces attacked seven times toward the settlements of Kolodiazi and Lyman and near Masliakivka. Attempts to penetrate Ukrainian defenses were repelled.
On the Sloviansk axis, the enemy launched two attacks near Kryva Luka.
On the Kramatorsk axis, Russian forces conducted no assault operations.
On the Kostiantynivka axis, 22 attacks were recorded. Russian invaders conducted offensive operations near the settlement of Kostiantynivka and toward Novoselivka, Mykolaipillia, Novopavlivka, Toretske, Hruzke, Vilne and Molodetske.
On the Pokrovsk axis, the enemy launched 35 attacks, including attempts to advance toward the settlements of Bilytske, Dorozhnie, Novyi Donbas, Chernihivka, Svitle, Dobropillia, Novohryshyne, Hulive, Serhiivka, Myrne, Molodetske, Muravka and Novopavlivka.
On the Oleksandrivka axis, Russian forces launched one assault toward Berezove.
On the Huliaipole axis, Russian forces attacked Defense Forces positions 16 times, including attempts to advance toward the settlements of Rybne, Ternuvate, Rivne, Vozdvyzhivka, Hirke, Verkhnia Tersa, Novoselivka, Huliaipilske and Omelnyk.
On the Orikhiv axis, the enemy made four attempts to attack toward Pavlivka and Stepnohirsk.
On the Prydniprovske axis, Russian invaders conducted no assault operations.
On the Volyn and Polissia axes, no signs of Russian offensive force groupings being formed were detected.
As Ukrinform previously reported, total Russian military personnel losses from February 24, 2022, through October 15, amount to approximately 1,559,230.

title: F-35C Begins Operational Testing Aboard Ford-Class Carrier John F. Kennedy
body: The United States Navy has reached a significant milestone regarding the integration of the F-35C carrier-based variant of the Joint Strike Fighter on the Ford-class nuclear powered aircraft carriers. Beginning on October 13, F-35C “Lightning II” assigned to the “Salty Dogs” Air Test and Evaluation Squadron (VX) 23 based at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, embarked on PCU John F Kennedy (CVN-79) for aircraft launch and recovery operations. The US Navy released several sets of imagery detailing the arrival and operation of at least two F-35C, tail numbers 401 and 403 on the yet to be commissioned aircraft carrier. The aircraft completed arrested recovery and catapult launches from CVN-79, utilising the carrier’s distinct EMALS and AAG electromagnetic launch and recovery systems. This activity is part of the aircraft compatibility testing (ACT) the new carrier needs to undergo in order to ensure basic functionality with embarked aircraft. Protracted integration of F-35C with newest US Navy carriers The first of class USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) entered active service with USN in 2017. However, to date the carrier does not embark F-35C, instead exclusively relying on air wings equipped with F/A-18E/F and G-variants for combat capability. In contrast, US Navy F-35C have been operational on older Nimitz- class carriers for six years. The stealthy naval fighter jet first commenced ACT in November 2014 onboard USS Nimitz (CVN-68). The first Nimitz -class carrier to operationally deploy the fighter jet was USS Carl Vinson in 2020, after initial testing with F-35C commencing on the carrier in 2017 . A U.S. Navy F-35C Lightning II, attached to the “Salty Dogs” of Air Test and Evaluation Squadron (VX) 23, makes an arrested landing on the flight deck aboard PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), marking the first time an F-35C lands on a Ford-class aircraft carrier. Photo US Navy. The principal reason for the delayed induction of F-35C with Ford -class carriers is the USN decision to extend various testing and integration measures on the new carrier-design as cost-saving measure, deriving from a Congress-mandated cost cap on the CVN-78-program. Congress intended these measures to compel stricter compliance within mandated budget, preventing cost blow-outs on fielding the new carriers. The US Navy however deferred various integration benchmarks in order to abide by the mandate, without significantly delaying acceptance of USS Gerald R Ford herself. This dynamic resulted in marginal functionality of various systems on the notionally operational carrier, affecting aspects such as EMALS and the newly designed weapons elevators. In response the House Armed Services seapower and projection forces subcommittee in its FY2020 submission included language mandating that USN must not accept CVN-79 without the ability to embark the F-35C . Domestic conflict over future Ford-class development Present activity onboard PCU John F. Kennedy occurs in this context, with the carrier slated to enter service with USN in 2027. The new Ford -class carriers have attracted both domestic and international scrutiny over their delayed induction and reported deficiencies in functionality for several of their subsystems, most prominently the EMALS electromagnetic catapult launch system. A U.S. Navy F-35C Lightning II, attached to the “Salty Dogs” of Air Test and Evaluation Squadron (VX) 23, is rigged to launch on the flight deck aboard PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), marking the first F-35C launch on a Ford-class aircraft carrier, October 14, 2026. Image US Navy. These difficulties most recently prompted President Donald Trump to mandate a 60 day-review back in August this year into whether additional new carriers, commencing with USS Doris Miller (CVN-81) should be modified for integration with the older steam-based catapult and arrestor system in use on Nimitz- class carriers. Despite the top-level initiative however the chances of such a change appear very marginal. Such a drastic design change would likely impose significant cost-increases and delays on further carrier construction. This disruption would occur at a time when the US Navy already struggles with operational availability across the fleet. For now the US Navy continues to order long lead items for support and future integration of EMALS-equipment. International dynamic of competition with emerging Chinese Navy Internationally, F-35C integration on the new carriers occurs among the backdrop of the Chinese Navy (PLAN) also engaging in their own expansion of carrier aviation featuring next generation-technologies. The third Chinese aircraft carrier Fujian (18), the first such vessel in Chinese service equipped with catapults, officially commissioned with PLAN in November 2025. The Chinese “supercarrier” conducted flight testing involving recovery and launch of several aircraft including the next generation J-35, an operational analogue to the F-35C, using its own electromagnetic launch gear as early as March 2025. J-35 operational testing onboard Chinese Navy aircraft carrier Fujian in March 2025. Image official PLA media channel. The Fujian’s activities, combined with another presumed nuclear-powered Chinese carrier taking shape at the Dalian shipyard, underscore a new dynamic for the US Navy. After several decades lacking a peer for naval competition, the service now experiences increased scrutiny bringing its newest aircraft carriers and fighter jets into routine operation, facing a notional adversary with similar capability. The post F-35C Begins Operational Testing Aboard Ford-Class Carrier John F. Kennedy appeared first on Naval News .

title: Gaza death toll passes 1,500 since October 2025 ‘ceasefire’
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 15 (MNA) – The death toll in Gaza has reached 1,501 since the October 2025 “ceasefire”, Gaza health ministry reported.
The death toll in Gaza has reached 1,501 since the October 2025 “ceasefire”, after Gaza’s Health Ministry reported three new deaths on Wednesday, including two Palestinians who died from injuries sustained in earlier Israeli attacks. The ministry’s latest report said 17 people were injured in the past 24 hours, adding to the 5,323 hurt since the October 2025 “ceasefire”. Nearly 840 bodies were recovered during the same period, the report added.

title: Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region leave two killed and three injured
body:
According to Ukrinform, the head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, Oleksandr Hanzha, reported the attacks on Telegram .
Russian forces attacked five districts with drones and aerial bombs.
In the Dnipro district, the Novooleksandrivka community came under attack. Two people were killed. An 82-year-old woman and a 56-year-old man will receive outpatient treatment.
In Kryvyi Rih, private homes and vehicles were damaged.
In the Nikopol district, the district centre and the Marhanets community came under attack. A warehouse building and a private home were damaged.
In the Kamianske district, Russian forces struck Zhovti Vody and the Saksahan community. Industrial facilities, infrastructure, and private houses were damaged.
In Pavlohrad, Russian forces targeted private homes, sparking a fire. A 31-year-old woman was taken to hospital in moderate condition.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Russian forces carried out nearly 40 attacks on four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region on October 14.

title: Trump – The Gift That Keeps Giving to Putin
body:
Watching Trump “perform” on Russia–Ukraine this week, I am left thinking, does this guy actually have any clue what he is doing, or is there an agenda here to basically go back to business as usual with Russia, sell Ukraine down the river, because Trump and his friends just want to do big business deals with Russia?
I am left shifting between the total incompetence angle and that this is just about his desire to do business.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Perhaps Trump thinks that Putin is just like him, and is driven by money, and the deal. And hence, by offering Putin the prospect of a big deal, sanctions moderation, and huge personal enrichment, this will encourage him to cut a deal over Ukraine.
I would argue that this is a fundamental misunderstanding of Putin. Putin already has extraordinary wealth, beyond perhaps what even Trump can imagine. Putin owns the commanding heights of the Russian economy. No big business deal goes down in Russia without Putin’s nod, or slice. Putin is already a trillionaire. So what possible deal could Trump offer Putin that would be interesting?
For Putin, it’s not about the money but more about historical legacy – his place in history. He invaded Ukraine in 2022, and before that annexed Crimea in 2014, because he could; the opportunity was there (because of the weak response of the West); because he saw this as providing an opportunity to rectify the “wrongs of the past,” and therein the collapse of the USSR.
That is why he launched a full-scale invasion, and that is why he is waging this war, and he will stop at nothing less until he achieves his goals, or gets carried out trying.
So Trump does not understand Putin if he thinks the solution is for Ukraine just to surrender the remaining territory it controls in Donbas, and then Putin will move on. No, no, no, absolutely wrong. If Ukraine, under duress from Trump, surrenders the remaining territory in Donbas that it controls, Putin will take that and move on, attacking further.
Actually, for Putin, it is beyond Ukraine, and it is also about breaking NATO itself. It is about driving a knife into the heart of NATO, as he sees the Western alliance and its prior adherence (pre-Trump) to a rules-based order, with values (democracy, human rights, rule of law) that are at odds with the fundamental basis of Putin’s fascist Russia.
And therein Trump is the gift that keeps giving to Putin – as Trump has fundamentally undermined the core of the NATO alliance, its Article 5 defense, through his actions on Greenland, but also on Ukraine. No one in European NATO seriously thinks that the US, under Trump, would come to Europe’s defense if attacked by Russia. And Putin thinks the same, which may encourage him to take risks and push and test that Article 5 defense.
Now Ukraine knows the above if Trump does not.
Ukraine knows that once it surrenders its front-line defenses in Donbas, its defenses will be fatally flawed, and Russia will drive on to take more territory.
The problem for Ukraine still is that, while it understands that Trump has no clue what he is doing, and does not understand Putin, it is still somewhat dependent on the US for munitions and intelligence. So it kind of must be nice to Trump, even though they generally view him as having zero clue what he is doing, to keep the supply of those munitions and intelligence.
The angle is to play Trump as long as possible, to draw down supplies and intelligence as long as possible, to buy Ukraine time, to develop as much autonomy from the US, until the point that the US is no longer there – and they know that point is approaching.
And it is also understanding that there is a nightmare scenario where Trump totally gets into bed with Putin, signs big business deals, pulls Western sanctions, and forces its allies also in Europe to pull their support from Ukraine. There is a scenario where Ukraine is left totally alone against Russia. So Ukraine must play along as far as possible with Trump to try and stall or delay that worst-case scenario.
And I think here that Ukraine is still prepared to walk away from Trump’s efforts to impose a peace agreement, which would leave Ukraine unsustainable as a sovereign state, and its population at risk of genocide.
And given its deep strike drone capability now, Ukraine has an ability to fight on for a considerable amount of time, and to impose high costs still on the Russian economy, and with it the global economy through its ability to hit Russia’s energy and commodity export sector.
So when pushed, as Trump is doing, Ukraine will eventually be forced to escalate.
I noted above that there is a scenario where Trump tries to bully Europe to pull its support for Ukraine to force it to agree to Trump’s bad peace deal. I think Europe will reject those demands from Trump and eventually bite the bullet, understanding that it will ultimately have to walk away from the US.
It will make this choice as it increasingly understands it faces an existential threat from Russia, with the US backstop no longer there, and its future depends on its ability to build an autonomous defense capability.
Building that capability will take time, and Ukraine is key to buying Europe time. So Europe needs Ukraine to hold out against Russia as long as possible to buy Europe time. So when push comes to shove, I think Europe will have to choose between the US and Ukraine and given that the latter might now be more critical to Europe’s existential security threat (Russia), it will choose it over the former.
Perhaps European politicians will find some balls and pitch the line to Trump that, in asking Europe to surrender Ukraine to Russia, Trump will, in effect, be the US President who kills NATO, the most successful defensive alliance in history. Will Trump really want to go down in history as that President? The president that killed NATO.
I don’t think he can believe his luck in having Trump as President.
As noted above, Putin will take whatever concessions Trump offers, and demand more. He sees Trump as weakening NATO and undermining European support for Ukraine. He will assume Trump continues this path and will hold out on any deal, expecting more concessions from Trump further down the line. He views Trump as weak, and having gotten involved in a war in Iran that has proven disastrous. He views Trump as desperate for a deal. So he will play hard ball to secure more concessions.
Putin thinks Trump fears him and is unwilling to hold him to account –Trump has done little to tighten sanctions on Russia and actually has softened sanctions and has offered sanctions moderation.
And Putin likely sees politics in Europe as suggesting division and fracture, as the far right rises, and eventually looks to cut deals also with Moscow. The French elections there in May are a highlight for Putin, and I think he will look to delay any deal over Ukraine until after those elections, as he will think Europe will then be weakened, and with it its support for Ukraine, and that he will get an even better deal the longer he leaves it.
His strategy this winter will be to escalate against Ukraine, to try to wreck its economy, increase its financing needs, and hence the burden on Europe, until the point at which Le Pen wins in France and then pressures Europe to pull support for Ukraine.
So there is little chance that Putin will cut any deal over Ukraine any time soon. And both sides have an interest here to escalate.
See the original in the author’s @tashecon blog here.
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.

title: Kirovohrad region hit by largest-ever attack: Critical infrastructure and logistics damaged, people killed and injured
body:
According to Ukrinform, the head of the Kirovohrad Regional Military Administration, Andrii Raikovych, reported the incident on Facebook .
According to Raikovych, "Today, the Kirovohrad region experienced the largest enemy attack since the start of the full-scale invasion. Nearly 360 enemy UAVs were recorded across the region."
Impacts were recorded at 26 locations. Russian forces deliberately targeted critical infrastructure, transport companies, logistics facilities, and residential buildings. Kropyvnytskyi suffered the most extensive damage. Znamianka, Oleksandriia, Pomichna, and several other communities across the region were also attacked.
Three residents of Kropyvnytskyi were killed, and six people were injured. Medical assistance was provided promptly, Raikovych noted.
"All relevant services have been working continuously and are still working now. The response and recovery efforts are ongoing," the regional administration head said.
Special commissions will inspect the affected sites and assess the damage to determine the losses and provide the necessary assistance to those affected, Raikovych added.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Ukraine's air defence forces neutralized 536 of the 580 drones used by Russian forces to attack Ukraine starting on the evening of October 14.

title: Tinubu won’t go everywhere
body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has declared that he would not go everywhere for campaign rallies as the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign kicks off on October 24 in Kaduna. Speaking shortly after inaugurating the APC Presidential Campaign Council at the State House Banquet Hall, Abuja on Wednesday, President Tinubu said the demands of his office would not allow him to follow the entire campaign trail. He noted that Nigeria’s economic and developmental challenges required his attention and he would not shelve that for campaigns. While promising to make out time to speak with Nigerians, President Tinubu told the Senator Abdulaziz Yari-led campaign council that he would not be able to go to all the states and local government areas. NSCIA calls for national unity, peaceful coexistence as CAN marks 50th anniversary Nightmare on Zambezi Crescent He said, “You have warned me and asked me not to allow the rigour of the campaign to distract me from governance. I hear you. I am in full agreement with your decision. Nigeria needs more attention now than ever before. The responsibility of this office does not pause. “However, I will still make time to speak directly with Nigerians, even as you lead the campaign in the states and local government areas. So, you will excuse me from going everywhere with you.” Daily Trust, however, learnt from a reliable source in the APC that among the few places the President would go are the national campaign flag-off scheduled for Kaduna next weekend and the grand finale in Lagos. The party stalwart, who requested anonymity, added that the President would attend all the zonal campaigns in the six geopolitical zones of the country but would be represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima in most of the campaign rallies in the states. Our correspondents report that the party will decide on where to host the rally in each zone depending on if the zonal headquarters is controlled by the APC, the voting population and whether it has hosted any APC event lately. Earlier, Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, had called on President Bola Tinubu to concentrate on governance and leave the task of securing his re-election in 2027 to the APC governors, lawmakers and grassroots political structures. Uzodimma, who is Chairman of the Progressive Governors’ Forum and Secretary of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, said, “An election season has a way of consuming everything around it, and there will be no shortage of people who would like to see you spend the next three months responding to every distraction on the campaign trail. “We would ask that you do not allow it to distract you from governance. The reforms you began need your full attention if they are to deliver everything they promise. Please, Your Excellency, leave the heavy lifting of this campaign to us,” he added. President Tinubu said there is a need to sustain investor confidence and the responsibility of securing a better future for Nigerians could not be subordinated to political activities. He said the government must continue meeting its financial commitments while creating an environment capable of attracting long-term investments that would generate opportunities for future generations. “We have bills to pay,” he declared, emphasising the importance of encouraging investors to establish interests for the future of the country. President Tinubu also charged members of the campaign council to regard their assignment as an opportunity to renew the APC’s covenant with Nigerians rather than merely securing another electoral victory. ‘Cost of staying away from campaign’ A political scientist, Prof. Gbade Ojo, said President Tinubu’s decision not to visit all states during his 2027 re-election campaign could undermine democratic principles. Ojo said presidential candidates were expected to tour the country to explain their programmes, defend their records and persuade voters to support their candidacy. He described the president’s position as inconsistent with the demands of electioneering. He argued that although the demands of the presidency might make it difficult for Tinubu to visit every local government area, the president should be able to visit every state capital and engage stakeholders directly rather than rely entirely on delegations. “If a president seeking a second term is now saying publicly that he may not be able to visit all the states, that is a negation of democratic canons that demand that he should go out and campaign,” he said. The political scientist added that Tinubu could combine official responsibilities with campaign activities within the country. Ojo attributed the president’s position to what he described as overconfidence arising from the perception that there was no strong opposition to challenge him in the election. Asked whether Tinubu’s decision was suspicious, Ojo said he could not rule out the possibility that Tinubu might be concerned about the physical demands of campaigning nationwide. The political scientist described the prospect of a presidential candidate openly indicating that he might not visit every state as unusual. He argued that an incumbent seeking another term should use the campaign to explain his achievements, acknowledge shortcomings and outline what he intends to do differently if re-elected. However, another analysts and senior lecturer in the Department of Political Science and International Relations, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Dr Shuaibu Mohammed, expressed mixed feelings about Tinubu’s decision. He said, “Traditionally, incumbents have used rallies as a show of strength, travelling across all states to demonstrate grassroots connection and party dominance. By choosing to limit his attendance, Tinubu is signaling a shift in priorities by placing governance and economic management above constant campaign presence. This move is particularly notable given Nigeria’s pressing fiscal challenges, including debt obligations and the need to further entrench investors’ confidence. “For the APC, this strategy has both advantage and disadvantage. On one hand, it allows Tinubu to project himself as a leader focused on governing rather than politicking, which could resonate with voters who value stability and seriousness. “On the other hand, his absence from rallies may weaken the party’s visibility in certain regions, leaving delegates like Vice President Shettima, governors, party leaders and members of the APC Presidential Campaign Council to carry the burden of motivating and mobilising supporters. This delegation could test the strength of APC’s internal cohesion and organisational capacity, especially in areas where Tinubu’s personal presence might have been crucial.” Families struggling with food, but opposition has no answer – Abbas In his Speech, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, said the APC would speak honestly about the economy. “Families have endured high prices. Workers have struggled with food, transport and housing. Businesses have faced expensive credit. We acknowledge these realities. The president is the first to accept this. But hardship must not make us abandon the evidence,” he added. He maintained that Nigeria’s economy grew by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026, external reserves rose above 54 billion dollars in September, gross federation revenues rose by 69 per cent in real terms between 2023 and 2025 and revenues increased by about 93 per cent. “These are findings reported by the World Bank,” the Speaker added. He argued that the figures did not mean that every family had felt the full benefit, but the economic base was becoming stronger. “The opposition will try to reduce this election to anger. We must elevate it to an argument. They condemn reform but offer no credible replacement. They promise reversal without calculating its cost. “They assemble familiar political actors under new arrangements and call it a new beginning. But a rearrangement of ambition is not a programme of government,” he said. Nentawe: We’ll present our case, let Nigerians make their choice On his part, the National Chairman of the APC, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, said the ruling party is ready to present its scorecard in the last three years to the people, adding that it is left for the people to decide. The chairman said the party would ask Nigerians to support the re-election of President Tinubu “because we believe the administration’s reform agenda and development priorities deserve continued consideration and the opportunity to deliver further results. “To our colleagues in the opposition, we recognise your legitimate role in our democracy. Let the coming election be a contest of ideas, records and policies, conducted peacefully and with respect for the Nigerian people. “The APC will present its case with confidence, defend its record with facts and trust Nigerians to make their choice through a credible democratic process,” he stated. Meanwhile, Uzodimma has asked party leaders and governors to be ready for the campaign, saying the election would be a referendum on the APC as a whole and not President Tinubu alone. He said, “It follows that our party has no excuse not to win. Victory is guaranteed when we are united, committed and work as a focused team. So we must jettison any misgivings we have against each other.” He warned that a party that controls every tier of government can easily grow comfortable and begin to mistake the size of its structure for the depth of its support. The chairman said the party would ask Nigerians to support the re-election of President Tinubu “because we believe the administration’s reform agenda and development priorities deserve continued consideration and the opportunity to deliver further results.” “To our colleagues in the opposition, we recognise your legitimate role in our democracy. Let the coming election be a contest of ideas, records and policies, conducted peacefully and with respect for the Nigerian people. “The APC will present its case with confidence, defend its record with facts and trust Nigerians to make their choice through a credible democratic process,” he stated.
