title: Barista: Synthesizing Typestate Specifications with LLM Agents
body:
Synthesizing Typestate Specifications with LLM Agents
Catarina Gamboa , Paulo Canelas, Ricardo Costa, Márcio Caetano, Jonathan Aldrich, Alcides Fonseca
ASE 2026 - International Conference on Automated Software Engineering, CORE A*.
Java classes come with rules nobody writes down formally: connect a socket before sending data, never reuse a closed stream. Barista reads those rules from the Javadoc and turns them into LiquidJava specifications, so the compiler can catch violations before the code runs.
Best PhD Poster Award LASIGE Workshop 2026
The paper's running example is java.net.Socket . Its documentation describes seven states in prose. Barista models them as the state machine below (Figure 2 in the paper), then writes the annotations that let LiquidJava enforce it. Build a program and see which calls the specification accepts.
Creates a stream socket and connects it to the specified port number at the specified IP address.
Connects this socket to the server with a specified timeout value.
Send one byte of urgent data on the socket.
Places the input stream for this socket at "end of stream".
Disables the output stream for this socket.
Closes this socket. Once a socket has been closed, it is not available for further networking use (i.e. can't be reconnected or rebound).
Excerpts from the JDK 17 Javadoc . Underlined: the phrases that imply the protocol.
Figure 1 of the paper shows the agentic workflow. Each numbered step is an agent with a tool that checks its output, and the agent loops on that feedback until the check passes. Click a step to see what it produces for Socket .
Built with Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK (Sonnet 4.6). The checks are MCP tools, and the typestate and LiquidJava guides are provided as skills.
We compared Barista's specifications with ones written by two experts for 29 JDK classes. Barista ran five times on each class, and every run was checked against the experts' test suites: 3,262 test files in total.
Precision. When the specification flags a call as a protocol violation, it is a real violation 87% of the time.
Recall. The specification catches about two thirds of the violations in the expert tests. When it errs, it errs on the permissive side.
Faster than an expert. 7.3 minutes and $2.20 per class, against 31 minutes for a person writing it by hand.
We rated one run per class: could a developer start from this specification?
An ablation study: prompting with the documentation alone (baseline), adding the state machine step, and the full pipeline with tests.
Quality drops as protocols get harder: F1 goes from 88% on simple protocols to 72% on moderate ones and 54% on complex ones. When we traced each divergence from the expert specification to its cause, most turned out to be modeling gaps in the pipeline rather than missing information. The most common one is transitions that depend on an argument's value, which a plain state machine cannot express.
35 JDK 17 classes with typestate protocols, drawn from Beckman et al.'s study of object protocols in Java. They range from 5 to 89 public methods. Expert specifications, tests and annotation guidelines are in the replication package . Each class links to its Javadoc.

title: Finnish households to receive printed emergency preparedness guide in January
body:
The guides will cover how to prepare for disruptions and crises, including the threat posed by drones.
The Finnish Interior Ministry will distribute around 3.5 million printed emergency preparedness guides to households and businesses across mainland Finland in January.
The guide will explain how people should prepare for disruptions and crisis situations. It will also cover the increasingly topical threat posed by drones.
Such a guide is essential in case electricity and internet connections are disrupted.
"It is not enough for guidance on preparing for disruptions and crises to be available to the public only through the Suomi.fi online service," says Ira Pasi, a project manager at the Interior Ministry.
The ministry has previously noted that an online guide is a cheaper option and easier to update.
"Reading the online version is particularly easy for the groups that are least prepared. Those who are least prepared are young adults and urban residents," Pasi says.
In May, Prime Minister Petteri Orpo (NCP) said preparations were under way for a guidebook to be distributed to households. Finland's Parliamentary Ombudsman has also commented that the current method of communicating preparedness advice is lacking.
The guide sent to households will be a brief summary rather than a comprehensive information package. It will consolidate essential advice from various authorities and organisations.
The material draws on sources including the Suomi.fi preparedness guide and the 72 hours website . Advice on the threat posed by drones comes from the rescue services' website .
"The aim is for everyone to be able to read it from cover to cover. It will not be a guide running dozens of pages that people would have to memorise," Pasi added.
He further noted that the advice is intended as guidance rather than a set of requirements. People can adapt it to their own resources and circumstances.
The guide's preparation and distribution will cost around two million euros. In addition to Finnish and Swedish, versions will also be produced in Sámi.

title: Lionel Messi’s Champions League records tumble as Mbappe, Haaland and Kane make history
body: Lionel Messi holds so many records that there’s a good chance he’s not even aware of half of them. Many of those records relate to the Champions League , a competition he won four times with Barcelona between 2006 and 2015, but has not played in since PSG’s last-16 defeat to Bayern Munich in 2023. For example, Messi scored the most goals for a single club (120 for Barcelona), the most hat-tricks (eight, shared with Cristiano Ronaldo ) and scored in the most consecutive seasons (18, alongside Karim Benzema). But this week, three of his personal benchmarks were surpassed - each by one of this generation’s three elite goalscorers: Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Erling Haaland . Youngest to reach 100 games Back in September 2015, Messi became the youngest player to reach 100 Champions League appearances when he featured in a 1-1 draw against Roma at the age of 28 years and 84 days. On Wednesday night, he saw that record fall when 27-year-old Mbappe made his 100th appearance in the competition. However, there was at least a sense of symmetry, as it came against the same opposition. Real Madrid came back from 3-1 down to beat Roma 4-3 at the Stadio Olimpico. Mbappe celebrated with a goal, his 72nd in 100 Champions League appearances. 100 – Kylian Mbappé plays his 100th UEFA Champions League match today, becoming - at 27 years and 298 days old - the youngest player to reach this milestone (across European Cup and #UCL ), breaking Lionel Messi's previous record (28y, 84d). Prodige. #RomaRealMadrid pic.twitter.com/9wOwFFpOz8 — OptaPaolo (@OptaPaolo) October 14, 2026 Fastest to 60 goals As if that wasn’t enough, Messi simultaneously lost another of his records over in Manchester, at the Etihad Stadium, where City were hosting defending champions PSG. The visitors put on a first-half clinic but had to survive an Erling Haaland-inspired fightback after the break. By scoring twice on the night, Haaland became the fastest player to reach 60 goals in the competition, doing so in just 60 games. His second goal took his tally to 61 in 60 appearances. Messi had previously held the record, having reached 60 goals in 80 games. Erling Haaland keeps breaking records 👏 #UCL pic.twitter.com/slMSEMzcBO — UEFA Champions League (@ChampionsLeague) October 14, 2026 Goals after 30 On Tuesday night, it was widely reported that Kane had broken Messi’s record for Champions League goals scored after turning 30. More accurately, Kane moved ahead of Messi on the list. The record is held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored 68 times in the Champions League after his 30th birthday. However, Messi, who scored 35 times after turning 30, did find himself pushed further down the list as Kane’s double against Viking for Bayern Munich took his tally to 36. Given the way the Englishman is making up for lost time, perhaps he could yet threaten Ronaldo’s mark.

title: The Nordics and NVIDIA Show What’s Possible When a Region Commits to Advanced Computing
body: The Nordic countries have become the European leader in unicorn startup density, producing the most emerging companies valued at $1 billion or more per capita on the continent. Now, a new chapter for the region is unfolding as countries race to build one of Europe’s most consequential technology ecosystems. The many computing advancements already underway in the Nordics, combined with the opportunity that lies ahead, signal a region moving from ambition to application. Nordics Emerge as Infrastructure Hub The foundation for establishing the Nordics as a technology powerhouse is already being built and the region holds a structural advantage: abundant renewable energy, rigorous data governance and a research tradition that bridges academia and industry. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements The Nordics are one of Europe’s fastest growing hubs for infrastructure. AI clouds are expanding with a projected 1 gigawatts of capacity to be deployed across the region by the end of 2027. Among these cloud providers are Bitdeer, CoreWeave , Crusoe , Hyperstack, Nscale , Verda and Volta . In Sweden, a consortium anchored by Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, with SKF as strategic partner, launched Sferical One — a shared supercomputer running on two NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs with 16 racks of NVIDIA DGX GB300 systems and 1,152 GPUs. The consortium will build services using NVIDIA Nemotron open models, which allow researchers to customize and deploy their models in a secure environment. Nordic-Built Intelligence Some of the Nordics’ leading technology companies are now building proprietary intelligence on NVIDIA infrastructure. Spotify , which personalizes music, podcasts and audiobooks for hundreds of millions of listeners, uses NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM inference software to run AI-powered podcast recommendations faster and cheaper at scale. The deployment is a case study in inference efficiency: delivering the same recommendations to a global audience at a lower cost per query. ABB Robotics developed RobotStudio HyperReality using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bridge the gap between robot simulations and real-world performance. By combining NVIDIA’s advanced simulation capabilities with ABB Robotics’ virtual controller, running the same firmware as its physical robots, the solution enables engineers to train, test and validate robots virtually, while using real-world data to continuously improve the digital model. According to ABB Robotics, the solution delivers up to 99% simulation accuracy and reduces commissioning time by up to 80%. Finnish telecom company Elisa is launching a beta of Moontalk AIRI, a real-time enterprise agentic assistant that retrieves information, captures insights and documents decisions during meetings and calls. Built on NVIDIA Nemotron open models and distributed infrastructure, it uses company data and low-latency networking to deliver fast, context-aware responses. Nordic Startups Scaling on NVIDIA Sweden’s startup ecosystem raised $2.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and is projected to reach $5 billion for the year. This next generation is building fast — and on open models. Stilta is reinventing how companies protect their inventions with intellectual property. The Stockholm-based startup is post-training NVIDIA Nemotron open models to scale patent analysis from a single patent to entire portfolios — work that was previously out of reach. Nemotron gives Stilta the language model accuracy for continuous portfolio monitoring at scale, across the thousands of patents that large industrial and technology companies hold. ConfidentialMind’s SampoTron , built on NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Embed, delivers more than 20% improvement in cross-lingual retrieval accuracy across English, Finnish and Swedish. Agaton , a platform that analyzes customer conversations in real time, is using NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning to speed up Revenue Mining solution on live sales calls. By routing knowledge retrieval to Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Agaton can cut response latency to deliver fast responses that inform customers’ buying decisions. Klang , a Swedish speech lab, fine-tuned the NVIDIA Parakeet v3 model to create Pianissimo — a Swedish transcription model that reduces errors by 75% while being 64x faster than the most accurate alternative. Built on over 50,000 hours of Swedish speech using the open source NVIDIA NeMo framework, the model is freely available on Hugging Face. Embedl , founded in Gothenburg and a member of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups, and Space Cargo Unlimited unveiled an onboard prototype that monitors protein crystallization, flags anomalies and recommends actions on a single NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module, without continuous ground connectivity. Sweden AI Factory — one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories — announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises across industries, including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming. Autonomous Machines on Nordic Roads and Factory Floors In Sweden, advanced computing is also powering vehicles on the road and machines in factories. Autonomous freight company Einride is building its next-generation Einride Driver on NVIDIA Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using the NVIDIA Halos safety system and NVIDIA Cosmos open world models. Meanwhile, Toyota Material Handling Europe — the world’s leading forklift manufacturer — is bringing autonomous machines to factory floors. In a collaboration with NVIDIA and SoftServe, Toyota Material Handling Europe is adopting a simulation-first approach to autonomous material handling, cutting autonomous solution deployment time by up to 50% across its global engineering, manufacturing and innovation teams. Norrsken Foundation and NVIDIA are opening the Stockholm AI Lab, a physical hub for AI-native founders working on global challenges, set to open in 2027. Quantum Meets Accelerated Computing Finally, Swedish companies are advancing quantum research using NVIDIA’s quantum computing platform. Stockholm-based FirstQFM used NVIDIA accelerated computing to train a model that reduces the execution time of quantum processors by 33% without sacrificing performance. Validated on a QuantWare quantum processor unit, this model optimizes how the operations needed by quantum algorithms are turned into detailed hardware instructions, accounting for detailed updates on how the hardware is calibrated. Tune in to NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 11 a.m. CEST. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

title: Houthis make ‘major leap’ building advanced missiles with greater Middle East range
body: Yemen's Houthis have made a “major leap” in locally producing sophisticated ballistic missiles using components imported from China , an arms intelligence report has revealed. Experts have also told The National that the militia's manufacturing was becoming increasingly sophisticated. Its engineers have developed the Palestine-2 missile that has the capability to manoeuvre during its terminal stage at 6,000kph, allowing it to evade defences. It was allegedly responsible for Saturday’s attack on Riyadh's King Khalid Airport attack that killed 13. Attacks by the Houthis have significantly increased in the past month and are designed to put pressure on Saudi Arabia to end its blockade of the Yemen rebels. Major leap The Houthis have been significantly helped by specialist parts for missiles imported from China, according to the Conflict Armament Research report passed to The National . Its teams examined weaponry from an intercepted shipment that had been heading to the Houthi-held port of Hodeida. The haul included highly specialist machined parts for rockets such as stabilising fins and equipment for hypersonic flight. “The discovery points to a major leap in the group’s domestic production ambitions and has major regional security implications at a time when Houthi forces are intensifying their deep strike campaign against critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia,” the report said. The components, discovered in containers on a cargo ship from China, demonstrate that the Houthis are now advanced in their work to manufacture the Iranian-made Kheibar Shekan series of ballistic missiles. Their Palestine-2 variant has a range of 1,800km, bringing much of the Middle East into their sights. The findings also demonstrate that the rebels, who are under a UN arms embargo, have expanded their supply chains beyond their traditional Iran-linked networks, the paper said. “The documented components suggest that, in terms of longer-range ballistic missiles, the Houthis have moved beyond simply reassembling Iranian systems,” it stated. “Only a few countries in the world have the capacity to manufacture missiles of comparable ranges domestically.” Accelerated progress While the Houthis have “not yet mastered” the technology for the Kheibar Shekan ballistic missile, Iranian expertise on the ground is “accelerating their progress”, said Dr Nawaf Obaid, of Kings College London. “Their principal constraint is time, not technical impossibility,” he told The National . While it is understood the airport attack involved several projectiles in a swarm attack, the Houthis currently cannot build significant numbers, he added. “Scale remains their weakness,” he said. Analysis by Kings College's department of war studies showed that 85 to 90 per cent of missiles were intercepted by Saudi Arabia’s advanced defence system, he added. It is understood that the Houthis exploited a gap between Saudi Arabia’s lower and middle air defence layers in the airport attack, rather than a “technological breakthrough”, said Dr Obaid. He added that the kingdom’s air defences were “performing exceptionally well under sustained wartime conditions”. UK support for Riyadh Documents show the contents from four shipping containers arrived in the Aden Free Zone in Yemen in June and October 2025 from China. The shipments contained custom-made metal parts including components of the airframe and a solid-propellant rocket motor for a Kheibar Shekan missile. They were made by a Chinese precision-metal producer “that advertises itself as a specialist manufacturer of custom aerospace parts”, the report said. It demonstrated that the Houthis were buying “more specialised parts for the construction of missiles, apparently independent of Iran-linked supply networks”. According to UN reports, Chinese companies form the biggest source of seized goods bound for the Houthis and they have been importing components for solid-fuel missiles from China for at least two years. China has stated that it adheres to the UN Houthi arms ban. Asked by The National what action the UK government might take against Chinese companies allegedly supplying components, the prime minister’s official spokesman said Britain “strongly condemns Houthi attacks and remains committed to supporting the security of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”. Saudi Arabia's ambassador to London told a meeting of parliamentarians on Tuesday that the UK's support in the face of the Houthi missile menace was welcomed by his government. Prince Abdullah bin Khaled held discussions focused on “recent Houthi attacks against the kingdom, regional security, and the importance of international co-operation in safeguarding stability and supporting peace in Yemen”, an embassy post on social media said.

title: Asian markets fall on tech stock rout as high US inflation weighs on Wall Street
body: Asian markets fell on Thursday, as artificial intelligence-related stocks plunged after a drop on Wall Street, fuelled by concerns about rising competition and profit growth in the chips sector. South Korea's Kospi slumped more than 7 per cent, while Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 index was down 5.12 per cent at midday local time on Thursday. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index dropped by 1 per cent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.75 per cent. Asian markets are dealing with "not just the deeper sell-off in AI-related stocks but also the tightening of financial conditions that comes from higher yields and a higher US dollar", said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. In its report on Thursday, the International Monetary Fund also warned of the Asia region's heavy reliance on the AI boom. Strong global demand for semiconductors, AI infrastructure and related technology products has boosted exports and investment, particularly in economies integrated into technology supply chains. "The AI-driven technology boom has provided an important offset for economies in East and South-East Asia, although the evolution of AI investment and its long-term economic effects are uncertain," the fund said in a report on the outlook for the Asia-Pacific region. "A correction in AI-related investment or asset valuations could weigh disproportionately on Asia given its central role in global technology supply chains," it added. The IMF also said uncertainty over US monetary policy could keep Asian financial markets volatile. Overnight, stocks on Wall Street dropped as consumer price inflation rose more than expected in September. "Wall Street tumbled on further evidence that inflation in the United States is sticky, while a pullback in chip stocks on fears about rising competition and peak profit growth added to the woes," Mr Rodda said. The inflation figures were the "critical driver of markets in US trade", he added. US inflation rose to 3.7 per cent annually in September, above both the 3.6 per cent forecast for the month and August’s 3.4 per cent. Core inflation also was higher than expected, at 2.6 per cent year-on-year. "US stocks sold off as higher-rate expectations returned to the fore, with the S&P 500 recording its weakest session since late July and the Nasdaq hit harder by pressure on chip names," said Daniel Richards, senior economist at Emirates NBD. "The risk-off move extended into Asia, where falls in Japan and Korea this morning were much sharper." The US inflation data now points to a higher chance of a rate hike by the US Federal Reserve, Mr Rodda said.

title: Russian attacks in Dnipropetrovsk region leave two killed, private houses on fire
body:
According to Ukrinform, the head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, Oleksandr Hanzha, announced the incident on Telegram .
"Early this morning, the Russians attacked the Dnipro and Pavlohrad districts. A private house was destroyed in the Novooleksandrivka community. Two people were killed," he wrote.
According to the official, several private houses also caught fire in Pavlohrad.
Rescue workers are operating at the scene, Hanzha said, adding that information about possible injuries is still being clarified.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Russian forces launched nearly 40 attacks on four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region on October 14, killing one person.

title: Police search home following double homicide at resort amid hunt for motive
body:
Metallica Harrison is accused of killing her husband and 3-year-old son.
Authorities searched the Pennsylvania home of a family at the center of a double homicide at a Poconos resort as they tried to find a motive for why a woman allegedly killed her husband and 3-year-old son before trying to take her own life, according to court filings.
The "violent domestic tragedy" unfolded on Monday in a room at the Great Wolf Lodge in Scotrun, Pocono Township, officials said.
Police responding to a call for a suicidal caller found the two victims -- Charles Harrison and his son -- dead on mattresses, according to the criminal complaint. Harrison had been stabbed multiple times in the chest, while his son, identified in the complaint as T.H., appeared to have a single stab wound to his chest, according to the complaint.
The 911 caller -- identified in the complaint as 27-year-old Metallica Rose Harrison of Towanda -- was charged with two counts of homicide in connection with the deaths, according to the complaint.
On the 911 call, she allegedly reported that she was "too weak to stab my neck" and that she had knives but they were "not working" and needed "help dying," according to the complaint. When asked if she was alone, she allegedly said that "my husband and son are already gone in the bed," and, "They're already gone, I'm sorry."
A "large butcher kitchen knife" and a smaller knife were found in the bathroom, according to the complaint. Resort staff confirmed that the knives, which had teal handles, did not belong to the lodge, according to the complaint.
The family had been staying at the family resort since Sept. 21 and, after extending their stay, were slated to check out on Tuesday, according to the complaint.
Instead, officers responded to the family's home in Towanda that day searching for evidence that, according to the search warrant application, "may reveal valuable evidence relating to the motive for this incident as well as recover evidence connecting the knife used at the crime scene to other items" at the home.
"It is common for individuals in these scenarios to document their homicidal and suicidal ideation's via hand writings or electronics prior to, during and after the act has taken place," the application stated.
Officers were additionally seeking financial information and insight into why the family had left their home and had been staying at the resort for the past three weeks, according to the application.
Police ultimately seized nearly a dozen "teal knives" from the home, as well as a safe, a journal, a financial notebook, a laptop and other items, according to a court filing on the inventory.
Amid the investigation, the victims' family members described the suspect to police as "dominant" and "controlling" and that she had "isolated" them from the father and son, according to the search warrant application. One family member also claimed that Harrison was "resentful" toward her son because she "never wanted to get pregnant" and had made statements about the toddler "taking away one-on-one time between her and Charles," according to the application.
Harrison was denied bail during her arraignment on Tuesday, police said. She is in custody awaiting a preliminary hearing scheduled for Oct. 21. The online court docket does not list any attorney information for her at this time.
The Great Wolf Lodge said the resort was "cooperating fully with local law enforcement as they conduct their investigation."
"We are deeply saddened and heartbroken by a tragic domestic incident that occurred yesterday in a guest room at our resort in the Pocono Mountains," the company said in a statement on Tuesday. "Our thoughts are with the family and loved ones of those affected."
If you are struggling with thoughts of suicide or worried about a friend or loved one, call or text the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 for free, confidential emotional support 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

title: Mariah Carey to bring Christmas hits to Abu Dhabi in December
body: Mariah Carey is returning to Abu Dhabi for a Christmas concert at the Etihad Arena on December 12. The American singer will bring her Christmastime show to Yas Island, with a programme expected to include festive favourites such as All I Want For Christmas Is You, Santa Baby and Christmas (Baby Please Come Home). Tickets for the Saturday concert are already on sale, with prices starting at Dh249. The performance will mark Carey's second appearance in the capital this year, after her Saadiyat Nights concert in February. She also performed at the outdoor concert series in January 2024. View this post on Instagram Carey has become closely associated with the festive season thanks to the enduring popularity of All I Want for Christmas Is You . Released in 1994 as part of her album Merry Christmas , the song has become an annual fixture on music charts around the world. It reached No 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for the first time in 2019, 25 years after its original release. The five-time Grammy winner is among the best-selling recording artists of all time, with 19 No 1 singles on the Billboard Hot 100, including We Belong Together, Fantasy and Hero. Her coming concert also continues a long history of UAE performances. Carey previously appeared in Dubai in 2004, 2017 and 2019, with the latter concert taking place as part of celebrations marking one year before Expo 2020 Dubai. Carey's concert joins a busy December calendar on Yas Island. Andrea Bocelli will perform at Etihad Arena on December 2, before the Formula One Abu Dhabi Grand Prix from December 3 to 6. The weekend's after-race concerts will feature Lewis Capaldi, Imagine Dragons, The Chainsmokers and The Script. Etihad Arena will also host a series of film concerts including Encanto on December 18, Frozen and Home Alone 2: Lost in New York on December 19, and The Lion King on December 20. Mariah Carey performs at Etihad Arena, Yas Island, on December 12. Tickets start at Dh249 and are available through the venue's official website.

title: PSG show class to hold off Man City as Guardiola looks on, Real Madrid launch stunning comeback
body: Manchester City's 4-2 defeat by Paris Saint-Germain in the Uefa Champions League told only part of ​the ​story of Enzo ​Maresca's first loss at the helm, with ⁠his men staggering through the first half before roaring ⁠back after the break. ⁠City were staring at a rout when a rampant PSG raced to a 3-0 lead with a first-half masterclass. Then they woke up. Maresca's side tore into the visitors after half-time, pouring forward with ⁠an intensity and urgency that had been entirely absent in the opening 45 minutes. Erling ​Haaland spearheaded ⁠the fightback, scoring twice to ‌become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the mark in ​just 60 games, 20 quicker than Lionel Messi. City kept coming. They finished with nearly twice as many shots as PSG and around three times as many touches in the opposition box, while recording a higher expected goals figure at both half-time and full-time. PSG, though, were more ruthless. “I think we start quite good until the first goal [from Desire Doue in the 13th minute] and then we concede the second one (Ousmane Dembele) after one minute. That created some bad feelings,” Maresca told TNT Sports. “Second half, we were much better and probably deserved something more.” 10 - PSG are now unbeaten in each of their last 10 UEFA Champions League matches against English opponents (W8 D2). Conquering. pic.twitter.com/oucYZj0Fft — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) October 14, 2026 City had arrived on the back of a 3-0 thrashing of Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday and Maresca felt they generated enough chances to salvage something even ​after digging themselves a three-goal hole. “Even with 3-0 in the first ‌half, with the amount of ⁠chances we created in the second half, ​we deserved more,” he said. “Luis (Enrique, PSG's manager) said at the end of the ​game that ‌they were quite lucky today. “You have to be clinical but not lose the balance,” Maresca said. The ⁠defeat unfolded against a backdrop of turmoil stretching far beyond City as an independent commission found City guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period. City have denied any wrongdoing and have appealed. On the pitch, they remain three points clear of Arsenal atop ​the Premier League table ahead of Saturday's home game against Ipswich. Asked if he had a message for supporters, Maresca said: “We are sorry for the first half for sure. Saturday is a Premier League game and we need to continue our run.” Former City manager Pep Guardiola watched from the stands in Manchester alongside chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and senior executives Ferran Soriano and Hugo Viana. Madrid's comeback On a breathless night of Champions League football featuring 46 goals, Real Madrid staged a stunning comeback to beat AS Roma 4-3. At the ‌Stadio Olimpico, Real Madrid scored three times in the closing stages to overturn a two-goal deficit. Marten de Roon gave Roma the lead ⁠in the 20th minute before Kylian Mbappe equalised five minutes later, but Donyell Malen struck twice in the 51st ⁠and 57th minutes to put the hosts in control. The visitors mounted a remarkable comeback as Carlos Espi pulled a goal back in the 82nd minute before Endrick levelled three minutes later. Former Roma defender Antonio Rudiger then completed the turnaround in the 90th minute, holding off his marker to steer home Arda Guler's corner from close range and snatch victory for ​the Spanish giants. Meanwhile, Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick in Liverpool's ⁠6-3 thrashing of LASK. Barcola scored his first goals for the club during the rout of Champions League newcomers LASK in Austria. Ronald Araujo, Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also scored for Andoni Iraola's side, who bounced back from Sunday's 3-0 Premier League defeat by City. Florian Flecker struck twice for the hosts.

title: Zelensky on US–Russia 'diesel deal': We lose strong partner
body:
According to Ukrinform, he made the remarks in an interview with British journalist Piers Morgan.
The president said that it was sad that Ukraine was losing a strong partner, adding that this was his personal opinion.
When asked whether he believed Ukraine was losing the United States, Zelensky confirmed that it was. However, he stressed that this was not Ukraine's fault, explaining that the country could not afford to be weak if it wanted to survive. He emphasized that Ukraine was not willing to sell its country, as the issue was not about business but about its life, homeland, people, families, and children. He said it was painful to see President Trump choose a side that did not support Ukraine.
Zelensky added that Ukraine had no objection to Trump acting as a mediator, but stressed that if he intended to remain neutral, he needed to maintain that position rather than side with the wrong party.
The Ukrainian president also expressed the view that Trump's advisers were making a mistake, although he said he did not know who was influencing the American president to take what he considered the wrong side of history.
When asked by Morgan whether he felt betrayed by Trump over the diesel fuel agreement with Russia and the announcement of an energy truce, following which Russia attacked Ukraine's energy infrastructure, Zelensky admitted that he did feel betrayed. However, he explained that the situation was more complicated than his personal emotions or feelings, emphasizing that the matter was beyond his control and that Ukraine's priority was to survive.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Russia will supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to the global market with US approval and substantially increase its export volumes in the future.

title: Tinubu: I’m Ready to Renew Pact With Nigerians, Inaugurates 2027 Campaign Council
body: • Says governance must not be grounded, as Nigeria needs fixing •Shettima throws jabs at Atiku, Obi, says nation can’t be governed with borrowed statistics • Yari: campaign for Tinubu will be performance driven •Wike to APC Govs: don’t claim Tinubu’s victory if you failed to deliver your states • Yilwatda: Tinubu’s reforms deserve continuity •Rainbow coalition on course for Tinubu’s 2027 victory, senate maintains • Sani tasks appointees on president’s election •Atiku: inauguration of Tinubu’s campaign council in Aso Rock abuse of public office • APC’s campaign council a Nebuchadnezzar coalition heading for the rocks, says MDPCO •Soludo, Adeleke optimistic about Tinubu’s victory Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha, Emmanuel Addeh, Adedayo Akinwale, Sunday Aborisade in Abuja and John Shiklam in Kaduna President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, declares his readiness to renew covenant with Nigerians ahead of the official launch of his second term campaign, billed to kick off in Kaduna on October 24. The president, who foreclosed the possibility of being present at all the campaign grounds nationwide, said the pressing needs of the country required his attention, stressing that governance must continue side-by-side electioneering. Speaking while inaugurating the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 poll, he said while the council would lead the party’s mobilisation across the states and local government areas, he would make time to address Nigerians directly without accompanying the campaign to every location. Tinubu said he agreed with party leaders, especially Governor Hope Uzodinma of Imo State, who advised him not to allow campaign activities to distract him from official duties. Vice President Kashim Shettima, speaking at the occasion, threw jabs at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Shettima questioned both candidates’ economic interventions and their readiness to lead Nigeria. He said the country’s size, population, and economic realities made it unsuitable for policies copied from other countries without proper adaptation to local realities. In his acceptance speech, Director-General of APC Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC), Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said Tinubu’s achievements since May 2023 and his future plans would form the basis of the party’s campaign for the January 16, 2027 presidential poll. Yari said the campaign would focus on communicating the administration’s record to Nigerians, particularly its impact on ordinary citizens, and its infrastructure projects. Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, told coordinators of Tinubu’s 2027 re-election campaign not to claim victory if they failed to deliver their respective states. Wike, though a member of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), said every campaign official must be held accountable for their electoral performance. Relatedly, the Senate, yesterday, declared that the rainbow coalition incorporated into the APC-PCC for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 was on course, describing the initiative as an unprecedented political alliance aimed at promoting national unity and inclusive governance. President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, and Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, made the remarks yesterday at plenary. However, Atiku, yesterday, condemned the inauguration of Tinubu’s campaign council inside the Presidential Villa, Abuja, describing it as an abuse of public office and a troubling breach of public trust. He said this in a statement by Director of Strategic Communication of African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC), Phrank Shaibu. Nonetheless, Tinubu, at the inauguration of the APC-PCC in Abuja, said, “As I stand before you with a heart full of gratitude and spirit full of resolve, it is my honour to inaugurate the presidential campaign council of the All Progressives Congress for the 2027 General Election. “I thank all of you for the last election, but no one gets credit for an incomplete assignment until you deliver the next election, until you deliver your electoral wards, until you deliver the votes.” Tinubu acknowledged Uzodinma’s advice not to let the rigours of the election campaign distract him from his responsibilities of governance, said, “I hear you. I am in full agreement with your decision. Nigeria needs more attention now than ever before. The responsibility of this office does not pause.” Uzodimma, in his speech, had assured the president that the governors and other party leaders would do their best to deliver the right message to Nigerians during the campaign. On why he would not travel to every campaign ground, the president said the government had pressing financial obligations and needed to attract investors to support the country’s future. According to him, “The job must go on. We have bills to pay. The American creditors cannot wait. We want those investors to come in, be here to stay, to invest for the future of our children. “However, I will still make time to speak directly with Nigerians even as you lead the campaign in the states and local government areas.” He charged the campaign council to take the party’s record, vision and agenda to Nigerians nationwide up to the ward level. “Let the word go out from this hall to every corner of our nation. The APC is ready,” Tinubu said, adding that APC is renewing its commitment to Nigerians and the responsibilities entrusted to it as the governing party. The president stated, “We have gathered not merely to inaugurate a council. We have gathered to renew a covenant, a covenant with the Nigerian people and the historic responsibility they have thrust to us as Nigeria’s governing party. We promise we will not let them down.” He also warned all the 31 APC governors, as well as federal lawmakers and other party leaders against taking previous electoral efforts for granted, insisting that their performance in the 2027 election would determine whether they have fulfilled their assignment. He stated, “No one gets credit for an incomplete assignment. So until you deliver the next election, until you deliver your wards, until you deliver the votes, before we can say thank you.” Tinubu pledged to support legislative efforts to increase women’s representation in the National Assembly and state-level legislatures, describing women as key mobilisers and voters. He said, “Women are the greatest mobilisers and voters. And from this hall, I assure you, the sponsorship of the bill.” He urged women to work towards securing greater representation, while promising to support efforts to increase their numbers at both national and sub-national levels. The president said, “The women deserve seats. Go and work for it, come to fruition. We will increase the number of women’s representation at both National Assembly and sub-national level. I assure you that.” Tinubu, while commenting on security, gave an assurance that state police would become a reality, signalling his support for the proposed restructuring of policing in the country. “On security, state police will be a reality,” he declared. The president lauded the party leadership for conducting its congresses and strengthening its structures from the ward to the national level, describing APC as increasingly united. He charged party members to remain determined in their efforts to build the country, recalling measures taken during his tenure as Lagos State governor to address the threat of flooding from the Atlantic Ocean. “There is a limit, but there is no limit in daring. We dared the Atlantic Ocean, and the result is the Atlantic City in Lagos,” he said. He commended Lagos State Governor Babajide Samwo-Olu and his Deputy, Obafemi Hamzat, for their contributions to the success he recorded during his term as governor of the state, especially in taming the encroachment by the Atlantic Ocean. Speaking at the inauguration, Shettima threw political jabs at Atiku and Obi, questioning their economic interventions and readiness to lead Nigeria ahead of next year’s general election. Criticising Obi’s reliance on foreign economic comparisons, Shettima said, “A country of over 250 million people cannot be governed through borrowed statistics and economic prescriptions detached from its peculiarities.” According to him, policies that worked in Bangladesh could not simply be replicated in Nigeria without considering differences in population, economic structures, institutions and national circumstances. He stated, “I respect Peter Obi. But he has gone beyond his mastery of philosophy to make an august claim about winning the 2023 presidential election without adducing a shred of evidence to buttress his assertion. “Obi is the master of bogus statistics and incoherent economic prescriptions.” Shettima compared the challenge of applying foreign policies to Nigeria to transferring a cloth meant for a smaller body onto a much bigger one. He also faulted Atiku, who had several times in the past sought the presidency, saying political ambition must be matched by character, discipline and an understanding of the responsibilities attached to public office. He was, however, quick to add that political opponents should be treated with respect, as they were fellow Nigerians and not enemies. Shettima said, “For the rest of the duration of this campaign, we’ll discuss ideas, we’ll discuss policies, but we’ll treat all our opponents with respect and dignity. They are not our enemies. They are our brothers. They are our countrymen. They are our leaders.” Shettima told the party leaders not to insult opponents in the course of the campaign, urging them, instead, to respond to criticism with evidence and reason. He said, “We have the capacity to respond to all sorts of innuendos and outright lies that our political opponents are taking on. But we won’t fall into their traps. We’ll give them facts. We’ll give them statistics. We argue with reason, not with sentiments, not with exaggerated truth or fabricated lies.” The vice president said the Tinubu administration over three years ago inherited an economy facing severe fiscal pressures and it had taken difficult decisions, including removing the petrol subsidy and addressing distortions in the foreign exchange market. He explained that the reforms were necessary to address longstanding economic challenges, while acknowledging the responsibility to ensure that their benefits reached Nigerians. “The next obligation is to turn these gains into jobs, meaningful earnings and meaningful planning,” Shettima stated, maintaining that the administration’s priority should be to protect the reforms, improve their implementation, and ensure that public resources deliver results for households and businesses. He said, “We must protect the reforms, improve their execution, and carry their benefits from the treasury to the household.” He said Tinubu deserved a second term because the government’s reform programme had gained momentum, which the country could not afford to squander. “President Tinubu deserves a second term because the work has acquired momentum that Nigeria cannot afford to squander,” Shettima said. Yari said Tinubu’s achievements in office and his future plans for the country would form the basis of the party’s 2027 campaign. He stated, “As we start going around to royal fathers and clerics, this is the message I have been sending today: our campaign is going to be centred on what you have done and what you are going to do in the future.” Yari commended the president for his achievements in infrastructure development and improving the lives of ordinary Nigerians, adding that his record has made the campaign team’s assignment easier. He said, “You have touched the life of the ordinary man. You have been there in infrastructure, building the iron road as if the money is nothing.” The former two-time governor of Zamfara State assured the president that members of the campaign council would work together to secure his re-election, describing the assignment as a collective responsibility. “We are going to do it all honestly with the trust and, by God’s grace, we are going to deliver,” Yari said. Wike, for his part, said securing a national victory for Tinubu would not excuse campaign coordinators who failed to mobilise sufficient votes in their assigned territories. He stressed that appointments and positions in the campaign council must translate into tangible electoral results. The FCT minister said, “If you don’t deliver your state and the president wins, don’t say we have won. It is not a question of I am chairman of this, I am secretary of this, I am a member of this.” The minister, who is the coordinator of Tinubu’s campaign in Rivers State and the FCT, said campaign officials must take personal responsibility for delivering their areas rather than rely on the overall outcome of the presidential election. He illustrated the point with Lagos State, recalling a conversation with the Chief of Staff to the President. “If you don’t win in Lagos, don’t say we have won,” Wike said. The minister expressed confidence in his own assignment, saying Rivers and the FCT would deliver massive votes for Tinubu in the January 2027 presidential election. Wike stated, “Simple, there is not too much work for me. It’s Rivers and FCT, and let me say and pledge, by the grace of God, Rivers and FCT will vote massively for Bola Tinubu. That is my job. “Rivers and FCT, it is taken. I challenge any area council that can say they don’t see the presence of Mr President. “For me, as an opposition party member, as the leader of the Peoples Democratic Party, there are not two leaders of the PDP. I’m the leader of the PDP, so I speak on behalf of the Peoples Democratic Party.” Defending his support for Tinubu, Wike said being an opposition party member should not prevent politicians from acknowledging what they consider positive actions by the ruling party. He said, “Democracy allows the opposition to be there to look at things that the ruling party has not concentrated on and say these are the issues you are not tackling. Democracy is not that if the ruling party is doing well, because you are in opposition, you say they are not doing well. That is not democracy.” Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo and his Osun State counterpart, Ademola Adeleke, also expressed optimism about Tinubu’s re-election. Soludo, a member and national leader of the opposition All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), disclosed that his party would campaign round the clock for Tinubu’s second term. He told the president, “Count on us, the All Progressives Grand Alliance, 24/7. We are with you because we believe.” The former Governor of Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) declared that the president’s return for a second term was already settled in the minds of his supporters. He said, “We are talking about when you get into the second term. It is the acceleration in the transformation process — from stability and reform to shared prosperity.” Soludo described Tinubu as a symbol of “the unity of Nigeria, the security of Nigeria and the shared prosperity of Nigeria”, saying those values informed APGA’s decision to back him. He also defended the government’s economic reforms, acknowledging their difficulty but insisting they were necessary. “The path you have chosen, that you have had the courage to take, is the difficult but necessary path,” he said. Adeleke also declared that no one could stop the second term movement of Tinubu. Adeleke of the opposition Accord Party said the president would emerge victorious during the January poll. He stated, “I can see the victory in 2027. Nobody can stop this movement. I am going to lead. We will sing and dance all the way back to Aso Rock. Four years isn’t enough, that’s why I am here to throw my weight. “Let us rise from all nooks and crannies to ensure his victory. Let us pray for Mr President and, by the grace of God, we shall be there.” Yilwatda: Tinubu’s Reforms Deserve Continuity APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, said the various reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration deserved continuity. Yilwatda added that under Tinubu, the government had pursued major economic reforms that addressed longstanding structural challenges and established a stronger foundation for sustainable growth. He spoke yesterday in Abuja during the inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council of the party ahead of the 2027 general election. He stressed that the inauguration marked the beginning of a coordinated and credible campaign to secure the re-election of Tinubu. Yilwatda stated that the presence of party leaders reflected shared commitment and confidence in the party’s collective capacity to present a compelling vision for Nigeria’s future. He charged the council to organise effectively, communicate the achievements and policies of the administration, and engage Nigerians with confidence. Yilwatda stated, “Today, we begin an important assignment of bringing together the strength of our national structures, the experience of our leaders and the energy of our members to build a coordinated and credible campaign. “We have made so much progress but must acknowledge where we have challenges while explaining the objectives, progress and continuing work of the administration.” The chairman stated that the party must communicate its critical infrastructure investments in roads, power, gas projects, railways, ports, agricultural infrastructure, and digital connectivity, and explain how they translated into practical improvements in daily lives. “This is the substance of our campaign: a clear record, an honest assessment of the challenges and a credible vision for the future,” he said. Yilwatda assured party members at all levels that they mattered and that the party’s strength depended on their effectiveness. He called for direction, coordination and clear responsibilities among governors, legislators and campaign officials. Senate: Rainbow Coalition on Course for Tinubu’s 2027 Victory Senate said the rainbow coalition incorporated into the APC Presidential Campaign Council was on course to deliver victory. It said the initiative was an unprecedented political alliance aimed at promoting national unity and inclusive governance. The declaration came as the upper chamber called on the federal government to prioritise the completion of abandoned and ongoing road projects across the country before embarking on new ones. It warned that the continued deterioration of critical highways was endangering lives, disrupting economic activities, and imposing additional hardship on Nigerians. Akpabio and Bamidele made the remarks yesterday during plenary, shortly before the chamber adjourned proceedings to enable senators attending the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council at the Presidential Villa participate in the event. Bamidele, who sought the indulgence of his colleagues to make what he described as a historic observation before moving the motion for adjournment, said the composition of the campaign council demonstrated the emergence of a broad political alliance cutting across party lines. He cited the involvement of Soludo of APGA; Adeleke of Accord Party; Wike of PDP; and Senator Ibrahim Dankwambo of Gombe North as coordinators of different segments of the campaign council. The senate leader said the arrangement represented an opportunity to deepen democratic engagement and promote a political campaign focused on ideas rather than partisan divisions. He stated, “My point, Mr. President, is that in this country, in the best interests of the Nigerian people, a rainbow coalition, indeed, is on the move and very much on course. “I think it is something that should not go unnoticed. We will proceed out of this chamber as members of the ruling party, accompanied by our colleagues, to go to the presidential campaign council. We look forward to a campaign that will really celebrate ideas and celebrate our democracy. I really congratulate you, Mr. President.” Responding, Akpabio described the coalition as historic, stating that its composition reflects an effort to bring political interests together under a common platform ahead of the 2027 presidential election. He said the arrangement went beyond infrastructure development, revenue allocation, and economic reforms to embrace national cohesion and unity of purpose. Akpabio stated, “Let me also note, like you said, that this is historic and this is uncommon. This has never happened in the history of our democracy since 1999, that a sitting president will constitute his presidential campaign council with almost all the parties in Nigeria inclusive. “So, this is not just an inclusive government in terms of infrastructure; it’s not just an inclusive government in terms of revenue allocation and allotments; it’s not just an inclusive government in terms of giant strides in reform. It’s also an inclusive government in terms of unity, unity of purpose in democracy.” He said the composition of the campaign council suggested that Tinubu’s second-term agenda would place considerable emphasis on political cooperation. The senate president said, “The coalition is evidence of the fact that President Tinubu’s second term is going to be a unity government, just like his campaign council is a unity campaign council made of almost all the political parties in the country.” The political discussions came against the backdrop of mounting concerns over the condition of federal roads, with Senate urging the federal government to concentrate resources on completing existing projects while limiting new construction to essential interventions, including roads needed to reconnect communities cut off by flooding and provide access to underserved areas. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Senator Tony Nwoye on the deplorable condition of the Ogbaru-Ndoni-Rivers Federal Highway, a strategic transport corridor linking communities in Anambra State to Ndoni in Rivers State. Senate urged the Federal Roads Maintenance Agency (FERMA), South-East Development Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Works to undertake emergency palliative repairs on failed sections of the highway pending comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction. It also called on the Ministry of Works to commence the immediate rehabilitation and reconstruction of the Ogbaru-Iyiowa-Odekpe-Atani-Ogwuikpele-Ndoni Federal Highway through a special intervention programme or another appropriate funding arrangement. The lawmakers mandated Senate Committee on Works to inspect the highway, engage relevant stakeholders, and report back within four weeks. The committees on works and appropriations were also directed to ensure adequate budgetary provision for the project. Sani Tasks Appointees on Tinubu’s 2027 Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, tasked political appointees in the state and at the federal level to deepen grassroots engagement and work towards delivering a resounding victory for Tinubu in 2027. Speaking at a strategic meeting with the appointees at Government House, Kaduna, Sani charged them to mobilise for a successful presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Kaduna on October 24. He urged the appointees to “strengthen coordination of political activities, towards the success of the All Progressives Congress(APC) in the coming elections.” According to the governor, “President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated an unprecedented commitment to Kaduna State through transformative investments in infrastructure, education and economic development. “Such extraordinary commitment deserves more than expressions of gratitude; it demands collective responsibility to consolidate these gains and sustain the momentum of development. “We must translate our appreciation into decisive political action. I charge every federal appointee and stakeholder to close ranks, deepen grassroots engagement and work towards delivering a resounding landslide victory for President Tinubu in 2027.” Sani said Tinubu’s support for the Kaduna Light Rail, Abuja–Kaduna–Kano Highway, Kaduna–Birnin Gwari Road, Kaduna–Kano Rail Project and investments in federal tertiary institutions underscored the president’s commitment to the development of Kaduna State. He emphasised that sustained collaboration between federal appointees and the state government was critical in translating the investments into lasting economic opportunities, improved security and better living conditions for the people. Atiku: Inauguration of Tinubu’s Campaign Council in Aso Rock Abuse of Public Office Atiku, yesterday, condemned the inauguration of Tinubu’s Presidential Campaign Council inside the Presidential Villa, Abuja, and described it as an abuse of public office and a worrying violation of public trust. He stated that the seat of government belonged to all Nigerians and should not be used to host partisan political activities, particularly when alternative venues were available in Abuja. Atiku, in a statement by Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign, Phrank Shaibu, said the size of the APC campaign structure further reflected a president more concerned about political endorsements than accounting for the difficulties Nigerians had endured under his administration. The statement said, “The Presidential Villa belongs to the Nigerian people. It is not a campaign venue or the private property of any political party. Using it for an APC political event is a gross breach of public trust and a troubling abuse of public office.” Atiku questioned why the president chose to inaugurate the council at night within the Villa rather than use a conventional event venue. He said the decision raised questions about the administration’s commitment to separating state institutions from party politics. Atiku stated, “Abuja has no shortage of halls and public spaces large enough to host a campaign gathering. Why, then, did Bola Tinubu choose to inaugurate his campaign council at night, behind the gates of the Presidential Villa? “Nigerians may draw their own conclusions. But a president confident in his record should be willing to face the public in daylight and ask for another mandate. “Tinubu cannot expect Nigerians to renew a mandate built on a promise of renewed hope when, for millions, that promise has given way to hardship and disappointment.” Atiku also described Tinubu’s expanded campaign council as a “crowded confession of fear”. He accused the president of assembling hundreds of politicians to shield himself from public anger over worsening economic hardship and insecurity. MDPCO: Tinubu’s Campaign Council a Nebuchadnezzar Coalition Heading for the Rocks The Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) dismissed the APC-PCC as a “Nebuchadnezzar Coalition” on a collision course with the will of the Nigerian people. In a statement by Richard Ihediuwa, the campaign’s director of communications and strategies, the organisation described APC’s presidential campaign council as a haven of internationally discredited and politically inconsistent characters and corrupt politicians intoxicated by the arrogance of power, imperial ambition, and the dangerous illusion that political influence could substitute for public trust and democratic legitimacy. The Makinde/Daura campaign council said, ‘’This Nebuchadnezzar Coalition is headed for the rocks as it cannot whitewash the failures of the Tinubu administration, nor rewrite the painful realities confronting citizens. “It cannot manufacture public acceptance through a parade of ‘political predators’ and power drunk elites, who are mistaking political dominance for public acceptance. ‘’With the high confidence that President Tinubu reposes in this alliance of failed governors, yes-along legislators, and discredited politicians some of whom are fleeing from corruption investigations; even as his administration presides over an unprecedented economic crisis, worsening insecurity and a devastating collapse of public confidence, we see in the APC Presidential Campaign Council imminent political humiliation.” The campaign council added, ‘’History is replete with the humiliation of those who mistake transitory power for permanence while reinforcing their illusions by surrounding themselves with compensated loyalists and sycophantic, who do not command the loyalty or followership of the people, rather than confront stark reality of failures.’’

title: AFC Appoints CBN Governor, Yemi Cardoso Board Chairman
body: Nume Ekeghe in Bangkok, Thailand The Africa Finance Corporation (AFC), the continent’s leading infrastructure solutions provider, yesterday announced the appointment of the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr. Olayemi Cardoso as Chairman of its Board of Directors. He succeeds the immediate-past Chair, Ireti Samuel-Ogbu, who served the Corporation meritoriously during her tenure and continues to serve as a board member. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele and Cardoso, yesterday wooed investors with commitments to sustain economic reforms, improve the investment climate and attract long-term capital as the federal government seeks to mobilise $78.5 billion for 65 projects across key sectors of the economy. Also yesterday, the Dangote Group endorsed the federal government’s reforms, with its Group Chief Economist, Hassan Mammud, saying fiscal and monetary policy changes had helped stabilise investments in the Dangote Refinery and other subsidiaries. He urged international investors to invest in Nigeria, describing the country as an emerging model for other African economies. At an investors’ forum in Bangkok, Thailand, held on the sidelines of the ongoing International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group Annual Meetings, the federal government’s officials outlined the government’s priorities, including reducing inflation to single digits, addressing power sector constraints, improving regulatory efficiency and providing clearer fiscal data to support investment decisions. A new feature introduced this year was a deal room that designed to connect investors with key policymakers, guide them through available investment opportunities and answer questions about investing in Nigeria. The initiative is intended to give investors direct access to relevant government officials and help convert interest in the country’s investment pipeline into actual commitments. The pipeline comprises 65 projects requiring a total of $78.5 billion, with energy and transport accounting for almost four-fifths of the funding requirement. According to the project breakdown presented at the forum, oil, gas and power account for 25 projects requiring $36.4 billion, while transport and maritime account for eight projects valued at $25 billion. Agriculture and agro-processing account for six projects requiring $9.8 billion, while industry, manufacturing and mining comprise 17 projects requiring $6.6 billion. Technology, health and urban services account for the remaining nine projects, with a combined capital requirement of $700 million. The government presented investment opportunities across different funding categories, from projects requiring less than $100 million to those needing $1 billion or more. The pipeline ranges from $1 million to $15 billion per project, with a median capital requirement of $153 million. Of the 65 projects, 48 require less than $500 million, while 17, valued at a combined $72.3 billion, require at least $1 billion each. The government is also seeking to strengthen investor participation by highlighting the protections available to foreign investors. These include permission for 100 per cent foreign ownership in most sectors, full repatriation of capital and profits with a Certificate of Capital Importation, double taxation and bilateral investment treaties, and Nigeria’s membership of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID). The investment framework also includes a five per cent annual tax credit on qualifying capital expenditure for five years under the Economic Development Tax Incentive. Oyedele called on investors to consider longer-term commitments, particularly as interest rates begin to decline and the relative attractiveness of fixed-income investments changes. He asked investors what the government needed to do to encourage them to commit capital for longer periods and shift from foreign portfolio investment to foreign direct investment. “We know that, for example, as interest rates start to come down, fixed income may be less attractive, but actually, if you consider the risk and the reward, it remains attractive. But what is even better is that the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) for equity investment and FDI gets more attractive, and this is where we want to go to attract more patient capital,” he said. Speaking at the forum, Oyedele said the government was strengthening collaboration between fiscal and monetary authorities. He added that reducing inflation would help lower borrowing costs and ease pressure on public finances. “If I want to even just sound selfish from the fiscal side, whatever we do to bring inflation to a single digit, thereby creating the conditions for interest rate to also be single digits will save the fiscal side as of 2026 numbers more than $10 billion. So, this is this is a top priority for us,” he said. He added that the stability and gradual appreciation of the naira were helping to moderate inflationary pressures. “The good thing is because of the way the central bank has been able to help us manage the FX environment generally, we have seen the naira not only being stable but steadily appreciative, and the impact on that on inflation is downward, right? So, which is good.” Oyedele said the government would focus on five major areas of reform: agriculture, power, inflation management, regulatory efficiency and data transparency. On power, he said, “You cannot power a $1 trillion economy in darkness. It’s impossible.” He explained that the government was examining market-reflective pricing, transmission challenges and efficiency in the electricity sector, which remain important considerations for investors seeking to establish or expand businesses in Nigeria. On regulatory reform, Oyedele said excessive regulation, unclear rules and administrative burdens imposed significant costs on businesses. “We estimate that overregulation, regulatory burden, lack of clarity, and all of those excessive burden that we post on businesses actually are costing us more than the combined revenue from corporate tax, personal income tax and VAT combined,” he said. He added that the government was developing a framework for economic policy to prevent the arbitrary introduction of new rules, fees and licences. On data transparency, Oyedele acknowledged concerns about the availability and consistency of Nigeria’s fiscal statistics, particularly the tax-to-GDP ratio. He said the Ministry of Finance was finalising arrangements to make relevant information available and accessible on its website. “So, we are currently finalising all of that, and it will be available on the website of the Ministry of Finance, finance.gov.ng. It will be updated timely. It will be accessible. It will be credible,” he said. Cardoso, in his remarks, said the government’s reforms were beginning to provide greater stability for investment and economic growth. He emphasised that lower inflation remained critical to improving the welfare of ordinary Nigerians. “The reason why we felt it was important to give ourselves this as a target is to recognise the fact that inflation is probably the biggest stance on the poor, and so it is critical that we bring it down to levels that are more manageable, rather than the situation where you feel okay, you’re lower double digits, and it’s okay. It isn’t okay,” he said. Cardoso said inflation had declined from about 34–35 per cent to approximately 15 per cent, describing the reduction as significant but insisting that the central bank would not become complacent. “Our medium-term target is to bring it down to single digits. Of course, as we embrace inflation targeting, that will obviously be a lot more open and transparent, and people will be able to have a clearer sense of the road of travel,” he said. He also pointed to Nigeria’s external reserves, which he said had reached their highest level in 18 years, describing them as a buffer against external shocks. According to Cardoso, the reforms had helped Nigeria withstand global pressures, including the effects of war and discussions around tariffs, while the exchange rate had remained stable and appreciated. Responding to concerns that ordinary Nigerians were yet to feel the benefits of the reforms, Cardoso said the stability provided by the policies had helped prevent a worse outcome. AFC Appoints Cardoso Board Chairman The Africa Finance Corporation (AFC), the continent’s leading infrastructure solutions provider, yesterday announced the appointment of Mr. Olayemi Cardoso as Chairman of its Board of Directors. A statement which announced this yesterday, stated that Cardoso brings extensive experience spanning international banking, investment management, economic policy and public sector leadership. “Since assuming office as Governor of the CBN in September 2023, he has led a far-reaching programme of monetary, financial-sector, and institutional reforms to restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen policy credibility, and rebuild investor confidence in Nigeria’s economy. “Under his leadership, the CBN has implemented significant reforms to Nigeria’s foreign exchange market, addressed longstanding foreign exchange obligations, strengthened monetary policy transmission, and enhanced institutional governance and transparency. “The Bank has also concluded a recapitalisation programme for the banking sector, aimed at strengthening the resilience and capacity of Nigeria’s financial system to support sustainable economic growth. “Prior to his appointment as Governor, Mr. Cardoso built a distinguished career in international banking and public service, including a 12-year tenure as Chairman of Citibank Nigeria and service as Commissioner for Economic Planning and Budget in Lagos State. “In the latter role, he contributed to economic planning and fiscal management in one of Africa’s largest economies. He holds a degree from Aston University in the United Kingdom and a master’s in public administration from Harvard Kennedy School, where he also served on the Alumni Board,” it added. It further stated that Cardoso’s appointment came as the AFC continued to expand its role in financing and developing strategic infrastructure assets that address Africa’s infrastructure gap, accelerate industrialisation and strengthen regional integration. “His experience in financial sector reform, institutional governance and capital markets will provide valuable perspective on the Corporation’s strategic direction as it mobilises investment to unlock Africa’s economic potential,” it added. President & CEO of AFC, Samaila Zubairu, was quoted to have said: “We are delighted to welcome Mr Cardoso as our Board Chairman. He shares our conviction that Africa’s lasting stability depends on its productive capacity. His leadership will strengthen AFC as we advance The Africa We Build 2050, mobilising African capital to build the infrastructure and industries that create jobs, prosperity and dignity for our people. We also sincerely thank Mrs Samuel-Ogbu for her dedication and contribution to AFC’s board during her tenure.” Commenting on the appointment, Cardoso said: “A more productive Africa is a more stable Africa. AFC has the credibility and track record to mobilise capital and build the infrastructure and industries that drive transformation. I look forward to working with the Board, management and member states to advance The Africa We Build 2050. Our measure of success must be the productive capacity we create, the industries we enable and the jobs we support.” Dangote Group Applauds FG’s Reforms, Says Policy Stability Boosted Confidence in Refinery Investment The Dangote Group also endorsed the government’s reforms, with its Group Chief Economist, Hassan Mammud, saying fiscal and monetary policy changes helped the Group stabilise its operations and improve investment projections. Mammud, who represented the President of the Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, at the forum, said the transparency and credibility of monetary policy supported the group’s investment in its refinery investment. He said policy consistency and incentives available to businesses operating in an export-free zone were important factors in building investor confidence. “The transparency and the credibility we have seen in that has significantly enabled the Dangote Group to have good projections and was able to come out of the woods from his investment of about $20 billion in the refinery,” he said. Mammud urged international investors to consider Nigeria, describing the country’s reform experience as a model for other African economies. “Please come into Nigeria, bring your investment. Nigeria is actually a symbol to other African countries now,” he said. Cardoso welcomed the group’s comments, noting that the reforms had helped address the challenges businesses faced when exporting at one exchange rate and importing at another. “The ability of Dangote to take bull by the horns and at least break that cycle and enter the value-added chain is one to be commended,” he said. The endorsement came as the government sought to use the investors’ forum and its new deal room to present specific projects, clarify investment conditions and encourage investors to commit capital to Nigeria.

title: Nigeria’s Sacrifices for Peace in Sierra Leone Will Never Be Forgotten, Says Ex-VP
body: • Calls for Africa’s economic independence Linus Aleke in Abuja A former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Mr Samuel Sam-Sumana, has expressed profound gratitude to Nigeria for its sacrifices in restoring peace to his country, saying the contributions of Nigerian troops would remain indelible in Sierra Leone’s history. The former Vice-President also called for Africa’s economic independence to discourage young people from migrating to Europe and America in search of better opportunities and living conditions, often at the risk of their lives, owing to a lack of opportunities at home. Sam-Sumana made these remarks when the leadership of the Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) paid him a courtesy visit in Abuja. He said Nigeria had played a pivotal role in supporting Sierra Leone during its conflict by providing troops and other forms of assistance that helped restore peace and stability. He acknowledged that military personnel and civilians had paid the ultimate price in the struggle, stressing the need to ensure that their sacrifices were never forgotten. “As a Sierra Leonean, I wish to express my profound gratitude for the role Nigeria and other countries played in helping Sierra Leone regain peace and stability,” he said. The former Vice-President described Nigeria as a big brother in West Africa, stressing that the country’s stability and prosperity had far-reaching implications for the subregion. “When Nigeria catches a cold, the rest of us sneeze,” he said, underscoring the interconnectedness of West African countries. Sam-Sumana also urged DECAN to sustain its engagement with the military and strengthen professional cooperation between defence correspondents and security institutions. He described journalists as indispensable partners in governance, accountability and national development, warning against the tendency of political leaders to regard critical reporting as an act of hostility. “Constructive criticism is essential to improving public institutions and ensuring that those entrusted with public responsibilities remain accountable,” he said.
