title: Novak Calls U.S. Diesel Deal a 'Positive Signal' for Russia's Economy
body:
Oil Prices Plunge 7% as U.S. and Iran Signal Room for Diplomacy
What I Cover My focus spans the global energy landscape and the technologies reshaping it, specifically focusing on oil and gas, renewables, and tech-driven market…
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Wednesday that the diesel agreement with the United States is linked to higher Russian refining and production and means additional taxes for the budget. He spoke to journalists at Russian Energy Week in Moscow, calling the agreement "a positive signal for our economy" , and saying it brings spending on the social sphere and opportunities for investment.
Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said on Tuesday that Russia has no export duties on diesel and that the exports will be reflected in companies' financial results, on which they pay taxes into the budget system. He said companies will be able to export diesel and earn revenue and foreign currency , which matters for the balance of payments, Interfax reported.
Novak said on October 12 that Russia could reach 3 million to 3.5 million tons a month of diesel supplies to world markets by the end of the year, as before the crisis. On Wednesday, he said supplies will go to world markets, including the United States, and that this is the volume Russia previously supplied , more than 10% of the world market.
Trump's October 9 post lists more than 300,000 tons "immediately," 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter."
Russian refinery throughput was 3.7 million barrels per day in July, the lowest in more than 20 years, against capacity of about 6.5 million, according to KSE . A September 15 report said three of Russia's six largest diesel refineries were shut or running at about a quarter of capacity after Ukrainian drone strikes. It put diesel exports below 1 million tons in June, citing trader estimates reported by Reuters, against about 2.5 million tons a month a year before that, or 3.3 million to 3.4 million with gasoil.
Russia fired 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones at Kyiv and Kharkiv overnight into October 14, CNN reported. Zelenskyy said at least 600,000 people lost power . He said Saturday that "Gifts to Putin will not lead to peace" .

title: GFiber and Qualcomm announce Wi-Fi 8 gateway
body: The Wi-Fi 8 (802.111bn) specification hasn't even been ratified by the IEEE yet, but that isn’t stopping manufacturers from getting an early jump on supported hardware. Late last month, TP-Link announced that it was taking preorders for its first Wi-Fi 8 consumer router , and we’re now learning that GFiber will soon offer its own branded Wi-Fi 8 Premium Gateway for its 20 Gig customers. Qualcomm, GFiber, and Gemtek made the announcement earlier this week, explaining that the gFiber Wi-Fi 8 Premium Gateway will leverage the Qualcomm Dragonwing NPro A8 Elite Platform. Qualcomm is already a known quantity in the wireless business, supplying chipsets that power Wi-Fi for devices ranging from smartphones to laptops to wireless routers and accompanying client adapters. The Dragonwing NPro A8 Elite Platform combines a penta-core CPU and an NPU to extract the most performance for connected devices. And given the artificial intelligence age that we now live in, we’d be remiss if we didn’t mention that the platform is “bringing together premium Wi-Fi 8 connectivity, high-performance networking, and native edge AI in a single architecture," according to Gautam Sheoran, SVP and GM for Connectivity, Broadband, and Networking at Qualcomm. “Combined with an open agentic AI framework, the platform provides a flexible foundation to deploy, customize, and scale agentic AI directly on the gateway." (Image credit: Qualcomm) While Qualcomm provides the chipset onboard, Gemtek will actually manufacture the gateway. According to GFiber, customers currently subscribed to the 25G-PON-based 20 Gig service will be the first to gain access to the gateway. Those customers are currently using an Actiontec Wi-Fi 7 gateway, but will be upgraded to a Wi-Fi 8 Premium Gateway once the certification process is completed. Given that the 20 Gig service is priced at $250 per month and only available in select U.S. markets, we hope that those upgrades are provided free of charge when the rollouts start in 2027 . Although there were no images provided of the new Wi-Fi 8 Premium Gateway, it’s said to feature a “new aesthetic design” that will encourage customers to place it front and center in the home, where signal propagation is best, instead of tucked away, out of sight, in a closet or in a far-off corner. While many Americans have access to 1 Gig, 2 Gig, and (to a lesser extent) 8 Gig fiber service, 20 Gig connections remain a rarity. But that isn’t stopping providers like gFiber from pushing forward. The company notes that its 50 Gig service, which is based on 50G-PON technology, begins residential trials during the spring of next year and will be fully supported by the Wi-Fi 8 Premium Gateway.

title: BlackRock's Larry Fink warns a data center moratorium could trigger a recession
body:
BlackRock CEO Larry Fink warned that a halt to data center construction could trigger an economic slowdown.
"If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession," Fink told CNBC Wednesday, after BlackRock reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings early Wednesday. BlackRock advanced about 1% in late morning trading.
"So much of our economy is based on the buildout of this capex," Fink added, referring to the massive investments made to develop artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Fink's warning comes as strong, local opposition to data center construction has emerged as a key issue in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, as communities struggle with rising utility costs, water use, environmental damage and questions over investment transparency.
While Fink acknowledged fears about the data center buildout, he also noted "most of it is on misinformation."
The stakes are high. Wall Street analysts estimate total AI capital expenditures could climb above $1 trillion in 2027 and total in excess of $5 trillion by 2030 .
"Data centers are not the problem. They're creating more new jobs than ever before," the BlackRock CEO explained. The scale of investment has created demand for construction workers, physical digital infrastructure, AI compute hardware and energy infrastructure to secure grid power, he said.

title: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary.
body:
AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary. ( via ) Indie game developer Popcar talks about the recent wave of AI-powered decompilation of existing games, enabling weird mashups between existing games, and producing a boom in game preservation projects to get old games working on new hardware (often in a browser using WebAssembly).
I like how this piece captures both the positives and the negatives of this new development:
Most people already realized the scary part by now. If AI can decompile games and software, then the entire tech industry is about to explode. Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like, and nobody can stop them. Companies can steal from competitors. Your paid game or app can be open-sourced against your will. This isn't exclusive to old video games, we can apply this to any software. [...]
This is also a big win for preservation. Old games can be ported, modified, enhanced, and made much more easily accessible than before. [...[
With console makers going all in on digital and games becoming entirely unplayable due to servers shutting down, this is fantastic news. We could own software we bought regardless of what the company thinks.
This is a link post by Simon Willison, posted on 14th October 2026 .

title: Standard Chartered pushes $2T stablecoin forecast to 2030 as transaction volumes grow
body:
The bank identified four distinct stablecoin markets, with USDC leading payments and AI transactions as competition intensifies over reserve yields.
Standard Chartered says stablecoin transaction activity continues to grow even as the market’s overall value has stalled, suggesting existing stablecoins are circulating more frequently rather than new supply driving growth.
In a report shared with Cointelegraph, the bank said it now expects stablecoin market capitalization to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than initially projected, after the market plateaued at roughly $309 billion this year.
Geoffrey Kendrick, StanChart’s head of digital assets research, said stablecoin usage continues to expand despite slower supply growth, with existing stablecoins changing hands more frequently as their use cases diversify.
Kendrick identified four distinct markets, each with different competitive dynamics. Tether’s USDt (USDT) dominates emerging-market savings, while Circle’s USDC (USDC) leads developed-market payments. USDC and Ethena’s USDe have established strong positions in crypto trading, while USDC also leads the much smaller market for transactions between AI agents.
The bank expects the most intense competition in developed market payments, where challengers such as USDG, M^0 and multibank stablecoin networks are pursuing alternatives to existing payment infrastructure.
According to Kendrick, how issuers and payment networks divide the yield generated by stablecoin reserves could ultimately determine which competitors gain market share.
Related: Crypto’s billions are back, but the premiums aren’t
Standard Chartered’s revised forecast comes as regulatory and accounting developments in the United States could influence how businesses use stablecoins.
Since the GENIUS Act passed in 2025, US regulators have proposed rules governing stablecoin issuance, reserve requirements and consumer protections. Some measures have also clarified the limits of those protections , including a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) proposal that would exclude stablecoin holders from pass-through deposit insurance.
The Treasury Department has also advanced implementation of the law. In August, it proposed rules restricting stablecoin issuance in the United States to federally or state-authorized issuers, with the licensing requirements expected to take effect in January 2027.
Separately, in August, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), which sets US accounting standards, proposed an update that could affect how companies report certain stablecoins on their balance sheets .
Blockchain payments company Tempo said the proposed changes could make it easier for businesses to use stablecoins for payments and settlement without introducing additional accounting complications.

title: ‘Whether we should ‘marry’ the EU is question for future’, Armenia’s foreign minister says about EU membership
body: Armenia’s foreign minister at the Warsaw Security Forum The Armenian parliament approved a law launching the country’s EU accession process in spring 2025. However, only now has Armenian society begun to hold “serious, in-depth” discussions about membership. Foreign Minister and Minister of International Trade Ararat Mirzoyan made the remarks on the sidelines of the Warsaw Security Forum. During a panel discussion entitled “Half-Readiness or a Gradual Approach: Rethinking EU Enlargement”, Mirzoyan was asked where the train taking Armenia towards Europe would ultimately stop. The minister replied that nobody knew — neither Armenia, nor the EU, nor its member states. He said the good news was that both Armenia and the European Union were enjoying their current process of engagement. “So let us enjoy these warm relations, discover new opportunities and explore new dimensions of cooperation. At some point in the future, we can sit down together and discuss whether we should ‘get married’,” Mirzoyan said. During the panel discussion, the minister also addressed the reopening of the Armenian-Turkish border and the peace process with Azerbaijan . He stressed that Armenia’s efforts to improve relations with its neighbours do not stem from its desire to integrate with European institutions. Moreover, he assured the audience that this process would continue regardless of other factors. “On the other hand, we should acknowledge that if our goal is to become a full member of the European Union, problems or conflicts with our neighbours are likely to become an obstacle along the way,” Ararat Mirzoyan noted. How Armenia is reacting to export restrictions on Russia: farmers’ views and official statistics Opinion: ‘Moscow’s main fear is that Armenia will choose European Union’ Preferential regime for Armenian exports to EU in response to Russian restrictions Armenia and the EU are pursuing more than just political dialogue “Our relations with the European Union have reached an unprecedented depth, covering a wide range of areas and forms of cooperation. We are holding a dialogue on visa liberalisation. The EU has established a monitoring mission in Armenia, which continues to operate and monitor the situation along the border with Azerbaijan. We recently welcomed a second mission. Although temporary, it operates on a permanent basis and helps us counter hybrid threats. Although we are not an EU candidate country, the Union has granted us preferential trade access with its member states. This is the latest development. The EU has approved autonomous trade measures to help Armenia diversify its export markets. We have also signed an agreement with the Union that will allow us to take part in various EU missions around the world. Moreover, although we are not a candidate country, we have received a Resilience and Growth Plan and assistance from the EU, including support through the European Peace Facility. Our cooperation therefore extends beyond support for political dialogue, the economy and trade. It also covers security, foreign policy and other areas. Together with the European Union, we continue to explore new opportunities as we seek to strengthen our ties even further.” Armenian and Turkish business leaders call for borders to reopen. Is it likely to happen? Political analyst Robert Ghevondyan says significant progress requires resolving political issues first, particularly those with Azerbaijan On unblocking transport links, the interests of major powers align “In my country, and probably across the entire South Caucasus region, the interests of the US and the EU do not conflict. On the contrary, they work together very well. The United States is actively involved in the South Caucasus. In particular, it is taking part in efforts to open and unblock transport links between Armenia and Azerbaijan. This will provide a vital transport connection, for example between Portugal and China, linking the West and the East. I believe the EU and its member states will also benefit from this process. Thus, many countries and major powers around the world share an interest in unblocking the South Caucasus.” 'TRIPP project will move forward slowly': US discusses regional connectivity agenda The US believes it is too early to begin construction of the Trump Route, which will connect Azerbaijan with its exclave of Nakhchivan, given the project’s technical complexity and geopolitical sensitivity. Opening the Armenian-Turkish border is entirely possible “We are normalising relations with Turkey . The border remains closed, but I believe the process has already reached a significant level of maturity. It is entirely possible that tomorrow morning we will wake up and see this headline in the news: ‘Armenia-Turkey border opens’.” Armenian and Turkish business leaders call for borders to reopen. Is it likely to happen? Political analyst Robert Ghevondyan says significant progress requires resolving political issues first, particularly those with Azerbaijan Peace with Azerbaijan and the situation in neighbouring countries “In our case, Armenia’s neighbours are a critically important factor. Let us look at them. Azerbaijan . We recently established peace and began bilateral trade. We are opening our territories to transport and transit, and unblocking regional communications. However, several sensitive issues still need to be resolved. To the west lies Turkey , with which we are engaged in intensive dialogue. We are normalising relations, but the border remains closed. To the south lies Iran, with its complex regional situation, specific conditions and challenges. To the north lie Georgia and Russia […]. **As for Georgia, imagine how much easier the situation would be if it continued on its path towards EU integration. That would bring about significant changes.” Opinion from Yerevan: Baku steps up pressure on Armenia with new tools According to political analyst Suren Surenyants, Azerbaijan is seeking to achieve its desired outcomes as quickly as possible, before the “window of opportunity” for exerting unilateral pressure on Armenia closes. Moscow’s reaction must be managed carefully “As for Russia, you can imagine how it might react to Armenia joining the EU, given the specific nature of our relationship with that country. Historically, we have had very close ties, and we continue to maintain close relations to this day. However, we must manage any potential reaction carefully. Nobody wants to make new enemies. Nor are we interested in harming any third party.” Real risks or empty threats? Reaction to Medvedev's statement about 'Ukrainisation' of Armenia Russia’s deputy Security Council chairman said: “The worst thing that could happen to Armenia is for it to turn into a new Ukraine.” Political analyst Ruben Mehrabyan comments on the statement. title: ICE Planning $100M 'Nightmare' Domestic Spy Program
body:
This article was featured in the Daily Prospect newsletter. Sign up for it here.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement is fast-tracking a $100 million domestic surveillance program to put 142 intelligence agents in more than two dozen cities and the District of Columbia, in what contracting and surveillance experts said would be a significant expansion of the agency’s ability to reach into private lives.
The new program is called the Enforcement and Removal Operations Overwatch and National Security Enforcement, or ERO ONE, described in documents posted last month on federal procurement websites.
Under the program, agents would analyze classified and unclassified information to identify “trends, patterns, relationships, threats, and intelligence gaps,” and provide ICE with briefings for Enforcement and Removal Operation missions, according to a statement of work published on September 18 . A forecasting document published a week earlier said that the solicitation will likely be released on December 10. Intelligence contracting experts said the timeline suggests ICE will award the contract around February.
“It looks dangerously like the construction of an internal spying agency,” said Jay Stanley, senior policy analyst with the American Civil Liberties Union’s Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project, who has written extensively on immigration agencies’ mass surveillance. “It’s a nightmare in the making.”
It’s also a weapon that the government will likely use against not only undocumented immigrants, but everyone else, too. That includes political enemies, intelligence experts said. Speaking with the Prospect on Monday as news broke that the Trump regime had raided progressive Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar’s D.C. home, former military intelligence analyst Michael Wriston said that “you’d expect to see more of this” under ERO ONE.
“Not just necessarily sitting members of Congress, but anyone, and especially members of the immigrant community,” Wriston said. “No one is safe. No one.”
THE PLAN DOES NOT SPECIFY WHAT OR WHOM ICE is looking for with this increased spying capability. But one of the components that caused former intelligence contractors’ concern was that ERO ONE agents will analyze both classified and nonclassified information to produce “network, link and relationship” analyses. That type of analysis involves researching not only a target, but also every other person to whom they’re connected, including household members, family members, friends, acquaintances, or the person with whom they carpool to work.
According to the statement of work, contractors will be tasked with conducting analytical research “to identify and assess relationships among individuals, organizations, locations, events, activities, data points, and other entities.” They will review information to identify “known, reported, or potential relationships; recurring patterns; organizational structures; associations; areas of convergence; temporal or geographic connections; and other linkages relevant to the assigned intelligence requirement.” Contractors will then “evaluate the significance and reliability” of the relationships and “prepare link charts, network diagrams, timelines, analytical summaries, written assessments, or other related products” for ICE to use.
Military intelligence agents compile the same type of research, Wriston said. He knows because he did that job.

“We’ve seen this time and time again. It’s the imperial boomerang,” said Wriston, who is also a data journalist and the founder of ICE watchdog group Project Salt Box , where he reported on ERO ONE the day the first document went live and has written about it since. “These are the kinds of things that happened in Afghanistan, Iraq, Yemen, Syria, for years. Now that methodology is being brought into the ICE space.”
Federal documents likewise do not detail the specific sources of information agents will analyze, only that all agents must possess previously awarded active top secret clearance, with eligibility to access Sensitive Compartmented Information. That’s a type of information that must be accessed through certain formal control systems managed by the Director of National Intelligence, a position held by Trump ally Jay Clayton. The agents will not make any decisions about what to do with the information they compile.
Wriston said that except for the fact that ICE officials are trying to make immigration a matter of national security, it’s unclear why they need this program when they already have the Homeland Security Investigations unit, which conducted the raid on Omar’s house, to research targets. His immediate worry, he said, is that the program will make it easier for the government to find terrified immigrants hiding at home because they think they’ll be safe there.
ICE PLANS TO SEND THE 142 AGENTS , plus two project managers, to locations in Atlanta, Boston, Buffalo, Chicago, Dallas, D.C., Denver, Detroit, El Paso, Harlingen (Texas), Houston, Laguna Niguel (California), Los Angeles, Miami, New Orleans, New York, Newark, Philadelphia, Phoenix, Salt Lake City, San Antonio, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, St. Paul, and Williston (Vermont), according to the statement of work.
Details in the document, and the rapid timeline, show that the Trump administration intends to use the program immediately, said Brian Murphy, a government contractor who worked for 25 years with ICE parent agency DHS. It’s rare for the government to only want workers with top secret clearance, he said.
“I’ve only seen it when there is an imminent need to work on something right now,” he told the Prospect . “Trump has two years in office. He can’t wait … they want to get rolling on this immediately.”
The program description is so broad that Murphy said he thinks the goal goes beyond targeting immigrants. “I think it’s darker than that,” because the agency could use the intelligence to attack people with identities and views the Trump regime doesn’t like. “The question for DHS is, what is the threat they’re trying to go after?”
“It looks dangerously like the construction of an internal spying agency.”
The federal government can easily change who qualifies as a threat and produce data that backs up the reasoning, Murphy said, and used as an example annual Homeland Threat Assessments. In 2020, Secretary of Homeland Security Chad Wolf identified white supremacist extremists as “the most persistent and lethal threat in the Homeland.” But by last year, that threat had disappeared from the report , except to appear once in a glossary of terms. The rest of the report focused heavily on Trump administration priorities as national security threats, including immigrants crossing the border with Mexico and transnational criminal organizations.
In addition, the murders of Renee Good and Alex Pretti have shown how the government views protesters against ICE abductions as an abiding threat. In a national security directive known as NSPM-7, President Trump identified anti-fascist protesters as domestic terrorists and proposed an architecture to disrupt and counter dissent.
“If you want to draw a narrative that the real threat to America is whatever you want it to be, you can very easily do that. You just stop gathering intel on militias,” Murphy said. “It’s like any other police state. If you ask it to find something to make my opponents the enemy, well, you can do that.”
Legal liability should be a major concern for anyone who bids on the ERO ONE contract, Murphy said, because it’s unclear whether the information they’d be charged with accessing had been gathered legally. He added, “It’s very, very concerning that they’re fast-tracking this.”
Stanley, the ACLU analyst, noted that immigration officials across agencies have been using an excessive amount of surveillance tools for years, including their “Stingray” cell tower simulators , automatic license plate readers, and tools that track location from cellphones . They use a facial recognition and biometric collection app called Mobile Fortify, a Palantir app called ImmigrationOS to track immigrants’ movements , and buy data from LexisNexis to identify someone’s family and work history . ERO ONE would draw on all of that information, plus an expanded group of sources to reach into the private lives of anyone it wants, intelligence experts said.
ICE already knows its potential bidders for ERO ONE, said Diana Brozi, the procurement specialist listed on the document. She told the Prospect it was unlikely the agency would hold an industry day and declined to provide further information.
DHS did not respond to a request for information or comment on the claim that the program could be used to spy on political enemies.

title: Build self-improving document processing using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
body: IDC research shows that document-related challenges cost organizations $19,732 for each information worker annually and reduce productivity by 21.3 percent. Organizations receiving invoices from hundreds of suppliers often face layouts that vary by issuer and change without notice. Template-based systems require constant maintenance at this scale. Staff can spend up to 30 percent of their time on document-related tasks, and manual data entry error rates range from 1–4 percent . Conventional intelligent document processing (IDP) solutions address some of this burden, but they require extensive upfront configuration for each document format and break when layouts vary across vendors. In this post, you learn how to build an agentic IDP system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that classifies, extracts, validates, and learns from business documents with minimal human intervention. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. Your agents automatically handle new document formats, such as supplier invoices, purchase orders, insurance claims, and loan applications. By the end of this post, you can: Deploy a multi-agent IDP system, often in under 20 minutes. Process new document types without manual template configuration. Let agents train themselves on each new document format and reuse what they learn, so later documents of that type go straight to extraction without retraining. Challenges with rule-based document processing Many IDP pipelines require you to define templates, extraction rules, and validation logic for every document format upfront. When a new vendor sends a purchase order with a different layout, the pipeline breaks. This creates three core challenges: Template rigidity: Each new document format requires manual configuration, and even minor layout changes can cause extraction failures. No learning: The same extraction errors repeat across similar documents because the system doesn’t retain knowledge from previous corrections. Scaling burden: Each new vendor or document variant multiplies the maintenance effort, and organizations processing documents from hundreds of sources face ongoing operational costs. An agentic approach addresses these challenges. Instead of static templates, AI agents analyze each document, generate extraction instructions, validate results, and learn from corrections automatically. Over time, your system builds a knowledge base of document formats, so you process similar documents with minimal additional configuration. Solution overview In this solution, eight specialized agents collaborate across two graph-based workflows running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The following diagram shows the multi-agent workflow graph built using Strands Agents , an open source SDK for building AI agents. Figure 1: Multi-agent orchestration workflow graph Identification workflow : The Analyzer agent extracts text using Amazon Textract and identifies the document type and sender. The Matcher agent searches for similar documents using vector similarity in Amazon S3 Vectors , a capability of Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). Training workflow (new document types): When no match is found, the Instructions agent generates extraction prompts, the Extractor agent extracts structured data, and the Validator agent checks results against schemas and business rules in Amazon Aurora DSQL . If validation fails, the Instructions Fixer agent refines the prompts and retries. On success, the Save Instructions agent persists the instructions for reuse. Automation workflow (known document types): When a match is found, the Extractor agent uses existing instructions. If validation fails, the Troubleshooter agent fixes the extracted data directly without modifying instructions. How it works The following diagram shows the infrastructure architecture for the solution. Figure 2: Agentic IDP infrastructure architecture on AWS Business documents arrive in Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) or direct upload to Amazon S3. Amazon EventBridge triggers an AWS Lambda function that creates a tracking job in Amazon DynamoDB and invokes AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AgentCore runtime orchestrates document processing through Strands Agents. Your agents securely access AWS resources through machine-to-machine credentials managed by AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon Cognito . Your Lambda functions become agent-compatible tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface of AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Agents extract text using Amazon Textract, classify documents using vector embeddings in S3 Vectors, and validate data against business rules in Aurora DSQL. Agents access enterprise data through MCP servers to validate extracted content against business rules. You monitor status and troubleshoot issues through a chat-enabled dashboard hosted on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). You gain visibility into agent performance through AgentCore Observability, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon CloudWatch telemetry. Deploy the solution Follow these steps to deploy the solution infrastructure and web UI to your AWS account. Prerequisites To deploy this solution, you must have: An AWS account . Access to Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Nova and Anthropic (Claude) models enabled. For model availability by AWS Region, refer to Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock . Access to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (Runtime, Gateway, Identity), S3 Vectors, and Amazon Aurora DSQL in a supported Region . AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) v2 installed. Docker installed and running (required for building and deploying container images). Python 3.11+ and Node.js 18+. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to create S3 buckets, Lambda functions, DynamoDB tables, Cognito user pools, Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories, and Amazon ECS services. Clone the repository and set up the environment: git clone https://github.com/aws-samples/agenticidp-guidance.git cd agenticidp-guidance uv venv source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -r requirements.txt cd ui/orchestrator npm install cd ../.. Deploy the stacks: uv run deploy.py --admin-email your-email@example.com This deploys six AWS CloudFormation stacks: Core (S3, Cognito, DynamoDB), Gateway (Lambda tools, AgentCore Gateway), Aurora (Amazon Aurora DSQL), Agent (AgentCore runtime, containers), UI Orchestrator (API endpoints), and Modern UI (React app on Amazon CloudFront ). Deployment takes approximately 15–20 minutes. Verify deployment by checking that each stack shows CREATE_COMPLETE in the CloudFormation console. Process files and review results After deployment, you receive an email with the CloudFront URL, username, and temporary password. Process a document Sign in to the web UI and choose Process Document . Upload a sample purchase order from infrastructure/sample_data/purchase_orders/training/ . The document enters the agent workflow: The Analyzer agent extracts text and identifies the sender and document type. The Matcher agent searches for similar documents in the vector store. For a new document type, the training workflow generates extraction instructions, extracts data, validates it, and saves the instructions for future use. For a known document type, the automation workflow extracts data using existing instructions and validates it. Review results in the Review Jobs and Instructions tab to verify extracted data, validation results, and generated instructions. Example: A new document type (training workflow) Suppose you upload the first purchase order from a new retailer, Two Wheel Store. The Matcher agent searches the vector store, finds no similar document, and routes the job through the training workflow. The Analyzer agent uses Amazon Textract to extract the raw document text: # PURCHASE ORDER FROM: Two Wheel Store Order #: PO-2026-0102-2584 Date: 2026-01-02 ## Items Ordered AC-021 Advanced Computer Qty: 1 $75.61 Colors: cr4321 @ $75.61 ... SB-004 Folding Classic Qty: 8 $9634.32 Colors: cb8901 I Sizes: S @ $1204.29 TOTAL: $14931.54 The Instructions agent generates extraction prompts from the schema, and the Extractor agent produces structured JSON: { "po_number": "PO-2026-0102-2584", "retailer_name": "Two Wheel Store", "order_date": "2026-01-02T00:00:00Z", "line_items": [ { "sku": "AC-021", "product_name": "Advanced Computer", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 75.61, "line_total": 75.61 }, { "sku": "SB-004", "product_name": "Folding Classic", "quantity": 8, "unit_price": 1204.29, "line_total": 9634.32 } ], "order_total": 14931.54 } The Validator agent checks the result against the schema and fails : validation_status: INVALID error: 'SB-004' does not match '^AB-[A-Z]{2}-\d{3}$' The vendor’s SKU format ( SB-004 ) doesn’t match Acme Bikes’ internal format ( AB-SB-004 ). The Instructions Fixer agent diagnoses the mismatch and adds an explicit SKU transformation rule to the extraction prompt: prefix vendor SKUs with AB- . On the second pass, the seven line items validate successfully, and the Save Instructions agent persists the refined prompt to the vector store. End-to-end time for this first run: 3 minutes 49 seconds. Example: A known document type (automation workflow) When a second purchase order from Two Wheel Store arrives, the Matcher agent finds the stored instructions from the first run with a confidence score of 3.946 (threshold: 3.7) and routes the job through the automation workflow: The Extractor agent applies the stored instructions directly, so the orchestrator skips prompt generation. The SKU transformation rule learned during training applies automatically ( EL-002 → AB-EL-002 , HB-071 → AB-HB-071 , PD-002 → AB-PD-002 ). The three line items validate on the first pass with an order total of $5,979.19. End-to-end processing completes in 1 minute 30 seconds, down from 3 minutes 49 seconds on the first run. Use the interactive chat The dashboard includes a chat interface for troubleshooting: Ask what tools do you have to see available agent capabilities. Ask list instructions to view stored extraction instructions. Ask what is the status of job XXXX to check processing progress. Ask what went wrong with job XXXX, how can we update the instructions? to diagnose failures. Understand how accuracy improves over time The system improves over time through two feedback loops: Training loop : When the Instructions Fixer agent refines extraction prompts after validation failures, the improved instructions are saved and reused for similar documents. Processing loop : When the Troubleshooter agent fixes extraction errors, it provides detailed analysis that helps identify patterns in document format variations. When changing models, use AgentCore Evaluations , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to confirm that extraction quality remains acceptable. The solution already uses AgentCore Observability, so it has the required instrumentation. Estimated cost You pay only for what you use, because the solution runs on serverless and on-demand resources with no idle costs. For a workload of 10 training documents and 1,000 processed documents each month in US East (N. Virginia), the estimated cost is approximately $58 per month. Foundation model (FM) inference through Amazon Bedrock represents approximately 85 percent of the total cost, at roughly $0.055 per document. Actual cost depends largely on the models assigned to each agent. Model choices are centralized in agents/orchestratorgraph/utils/config.py , so you can use lower-cost models for simpler tasks and stronger models where needed. For detailed pricing, refer to the Amazon Bedrock pricing page. Customize the solution for your use case You get a purchase order processing use case with a synthetic bike company dataset, a pre-built JSON schema, and a validation Lambda function that checks extracted data against product and vendor records in a mock ERP database. To process your own documents, you must replace the included schemas and validation logic with your own. Define your document schema Create a JSON schema that defines the fields you want to extract for each document type. The sample purchase order schema in agents/orchestratorgraph/doc_schema/purchase_order_schema.json provides a reference. Your schema should specify field names, data types, and whether each field is explicitly stated in the document or inferred from context. Build your validation process The included validator checks purchase order data against synthetic vendor and product tables in Aurora DSQL. Your production implementation requires a validation process tailored to your business rules. For example: An invoice validator might check vendor IDs against your accounts payable system and verify line item totals match the invoice total. A contract validator might verify that the document contains required clauses and that dates and party names match your records. A claims validator might check policy numbers, coverage limits, and claimant information against your policy management system. To add a new validator, create a Lambda function that accepts extracted JSON and returns a pass/fail result with detailed error messages, then register it as a tool in AgentCore Gateway. Refer to gateway/tools/po_validator_tool/ for the implementation pattern. Update agent prompts The agent prompts in agents/orchestratorgraph/prompts/ reference purchase order terminology. Update these prompts to reflect your document types and extraction requirements. The Orchestrator agent, Validator agent, and Instructions agent each contain document-type-specific language that you should adapt. Best practices Keep these recommendations in mind as you train and operate your agentic IDP system. Start with representative samples : Upload 5–10 documents per type during training, including edge cases with format variations, to build reliable extraction instructions. Use business rule validation : Connect validators to your reference data (vendor lists, product catalogs) in Aurora DSQL to catch extraction errors early. Monitor agent performance : Use AgentCore Observability and CloudWatch to track execution paths, identify bottlenecks, and measure extraction accuracy over time. Add document types incrementally : Create a JSON schema for each new document type and a corresponding validation Lambda function. The agents handle the rest. Add guardrails for production : Apply Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to enforce content filtering and grounding checks on agent outputs. This is especially important when you process sensitive document types such as insurance claims or loan applications. Review the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs : Consult the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and Generative AI Apps for security considerations when building applications that use large language models (LLMs). Clean up Important: Before running cleanup, export the data you want to retain. The destroy.py script permanently deletes processed documents (S3), job history (DynamoDB), validation data (Aurora DSQL), and learned extraction instructions (vector store). To avoid ongoing charges, remove the deployed resources: uv run destroy.py Verify that the six CloudFormation stacks are deleted on the console: AgenticIDP-Core-Dev, AgenticIDP-Gateway-Dev, AgenticIDP-Aurora-Dev, AgenticIDP-Agent-Dev, AgenticIDP-UIOrchestr-Dev, and AgenticIDP-ModernUI-Dev. Conclusion In this post, you learned how to build a self-improving document processing system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, where specialized AI agents collaborate to classify, extract, validate, and learn from business documents. This agentic approach adapts to new document formats automatically and improves accuracy over time through feedback loops, replacing manual template configuration with autonomous learning. As next steps: Deploy the sample solution and test with the included purchase order samples. Add your own document types by creating JSON schemas and validation rules. Explore how to integrate extracted data with downstream systems such as ERP, CRM, or content management tools. To learn more about the services and patterns used in this post, refer to the following resources: For a deep dive into the agent framework used in this solution, refer to Strands Agents SDK: A technical deep dive into agent architectures and observability . To understand how AgentCore Gateway transforms APIs into agent-compatible tools, refer to Introducing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway: Transforming enterprise AI agent tool development . For background on the Model Context Protocol and how it integrates with AWS services, refer to Unlocking the power of Model Context Protocol (MCP) on AWS . To learn how agents can retain context across sessions, refer to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory: Building context-aware agents . For details on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capabilities, refer to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation . For expert guidance on building document processing solutions, AWS Professional Services and AWS Partners can help. About the authors Erik Cordsen Erik is a Solutions Architect at AWS serving customers in Georgia. He is passionate about applying cloud technologies and machine learning to solve real life problem. When he is not designing cloud solutions, Erik enjoys travel, cooking, and cycling. Vivek Mittal Vivek is a Solution Architect at Amazon Web Services, where he helps organizations architect and implement cutting-edge cloud solutions. With a deep passion for Generative AI, Machine Learning, and Serverless technologies, he specializes in helping customers harness these innovations to drive business transformation. He finds particular satisfaction in collaborating with customers to turn their ambitious technological visions into reality. Sourabh Jain Sourabh is a Senior Solutions Architect with over 8 years of experience developing cloud solutions that drive better business outcomes for organizations worldwide. He specializes in architecting and implementing robust cloud software solutions, with extensive experience working alongside global Fortune 500 teams across diverse time zones and cultures.

title: Zetwerk Raises ₹2,251 Cr From Anchor Investors Ahead Of IPO
body: Manufacturing company Zetwerk has raised ₹2,251.2 Cr from anchor investors ahead of the opening of its initial public offering (IPO) for public subscription on October 15. The company allotted 14.91 Cr equity shares to anchor investors at ₹151 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band. Domestic mutual funds accounted for around 46% of the anchor book, picking up 6.80 Cr shares through 61 schemes across 22 fund houses. Notably, 40% of the anchor investor portion was reserved for domestic mutual funds, life insurance companies and pension funds. SBI Mutual Fund emerged as the largest among these investors, acquiring 1.02 Cr shares through two schemes. ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund also accounted for around 7% of the anchor allocation. Other participating fund houses included Bajaj Finserv, Abakkus, Baroda BNP Paribas, Motilal Oswal and Edelweiss. Global institutional investors accounted for a significant part of Zetwerk’s anchor book. Capital Group’s Smallcap World Fund Inc received the largest individual allocation, worth ₹288 Cr, accounting for 12.79% of the total anchor portion. Government Pension Fund Global and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority’s Monsoon fund were each allocated shares worth about ₹75 Cr. Meanwhile, Nomura India Investment Mother Fund received an allocation worth ₹50 Cr and ex-HDFC Mutual Fund CIO Prashant Jain’s fund 3P India lapped up shares worth ₹39.9 Cr. Among international investors, the anchor book featured the likes of Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, First State Investments and Societe Generale. Zetwerk’s ₹5,012 Cr IPO will open for public subscription on October 15 and close on October 17. At the upper end of the price band of ₹143-₹151 per share, the offering values the company at a post-issue market capitalisation of around ₹25,583 Cr, or approximately $2.7 Bn. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of ₹2,830 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 14.45 Cr shares, amounting to ₹2,182.3 Cr at the upper end of the price band. The company has increased the fresh issue from ₹2,600 Cr proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) . The OFS component has also expanded by 49.2% from approximately 9.7 Cr shares. Zetwerk’s promoters and cofounders, Amrit Pratik Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, will each sell up to 1.42 Cr shares. Other shareholders offloading their stakes include promoter group entity Creovate Innovation and funds associated with Peak XV Partners, Accel India, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Kae Capital. The company plans to deploy ₹2,160 Cr from the fresh issue towards repaying or prepaying borrowings of Zetwerk and certain subsidiaries. The remaining proceeds will be used for acquisitions and general corporate purposes. On the financial front, Zetwerk’s operating revenue rose to ₹15,739.3 Cr in FY26 from ₹11,331.9 Cr in FY25. However, its consolidated net loss widened to ₹1,606.2 Cr from ₹370.7 Cr in FY25 due to discontinued operations over the past fiscal. The FY26 loss included an exceptional charge of ₹796.4 Cr linked to changes in share conversion ratios and an impairment charge of ₹453 Cr related to its discontinued civil infrastructure business. In Q1 FY27, operating revenue grew 55.4% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹4,117.9 Cr from ₹2,649.4 Cr. Its total net loss narrowed 46.4% to ₹733 Cr from ₹1,368.5 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. Of the latest quarterly loss, ₹668.9 Cr was attributable to discontinued operations, while continuing operations accounted for ₹64.1 Cr. The year-ago quarter included exceptional charges of ₹803.2 Cr from continuing operations and the ₹453 Cr impairment charge in the discontinued business. The post Zetwerk Raises ₹2,251 Cr From Anchor Investors Ahead Of IPO appeared first on Inc42 Media .

title: Standard Chartered Debuts Bitcoin Trading For Wealthy UAE Clients
body: Bitcoin Magazine Standard Chartered Debuts Bitcoin Trading For Wealthy UAE Clients British multinational Standard Chartered on Wednesday announced a bitcoin trading service for affluent clients in the United Arab Emirates. The service is the first such service offered by an international bank in the UAE, Standard Chartered said . It comes after the bank last month debuted bitcoin trading for institutional clients in the Arab nation. Standard Chartered became one of the first global banks to enter the spot crypto trading space when in 2025 it set up a trading desk for bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies in London. JUST IN: Standard Chartered becomes the first international bank in the UAE to offer Bitcoin trading directly through eligible clients' bank accounts pic.twitter.com/uPVQV9D8SJ — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) October 14, 2026 “As client interest in digital assets continues to grow, this launch represents a significant milestone for Standard Chartered as we bring digital assets into our core wealth offering,” said Samir Subberwal, Standard Chartered’s global head of wealth solutions, ​retail products, data and analytics. “With digital assets moving into mainstream wealth conversations, clients are increasingly looking not only for access, but also for the security, trust and confidence that comes from investing through a regulated and trusted institution.” Rola Abu Manneh, Standard Chartered’s chief executive officer UAE, Middle East and Pakistan, added: “We are proud to be the first international bank in the UAE to launch a cryptocurrency trading offering.” The service will allow clients to buy bitcoin via their bank accounts. No third-party apps or wallets will be needed, the bank said. Standard Chartered said it will manage end-to-end custody and settlement through a closed-loop model, reducing exposure to third-party wallet risks. The British bank is expanding its crypto-related offerings worldwide. Earlier this month, it said it had plans to offer crypto custody services for institutional clients in Singapore. Standard Chartered already offers the service in the UAE, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong. Banks worldwide are integrating or offering bitcoin-related products and services. A number of U.S. and European banks have started offering crypto-related services by custodying assets for institutions. Others are offering trading via their flagship apps. This post Standard Chartered Debuts Bitcoin Trading For Wealthy UAE Clients first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

title: Iran stresses need to stop Israeli aggression in S Lebanon
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 14 (MNA) – In a telephone conversation with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun Wednesday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stressed the need to stop the Zionist regime's aggression in south Lebanon.
In a telephone conversation this Wednesday afternoon, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun discussed and exchanged views on developments in Lebanon and the region.
Araghchi emphasized the Islamic Republic of Iran's strong commitment to the necessity of halting the Zionist regime's attacks and acts of aggression against Lebanon and ending the occupation of the Arab country's southern regions. He also briefed the Lebanese President on the diplomatic moves and efforts undertaken by the Islamic Republic of Iran in recent days and weeks.
The Lebanese President emphasized the priority and necessity of diplomatic solutions for regional crises.
The expansion of bilateral relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Lebanon, as well as the continuation of contacts and dialogue between officials of the two countries, were among the other topics discussed during the call.

title: How the Army’s training ‘crucible’ bases are changing
body: A year ago, an Army brigade rotating through the service’s major training center in Hohenfels, Germany might launch a few hundred drones during a 14-day exercise. Soldiers would get even less use of the systems designed to counter those drones. The reasons ranged from German airspace restrictions over the training area to U.S. units simply arriving without any drones they knew how to use. Now, that number has skyrocketed, according to the general in charge there. “We went from about 400 [unmanned] systems and maybe 35 or 40 counter-UAS to, in the last rotation we did, we had almost 2,000 [unmanned aerial systems], with over 1,000 of that being consumable,” said Brig. Gen. Terry Tillis, commander of the 7th Army Training Command in Germany. “We picked that up as we watched what’s going on at [U.S. Central Command]; we watch what’s going on at the [U.S.-Mexico] border, we watch what’s going on in Ukraine. It’s all consumable munitions.” Tillis addressed recent changes and upgrades at the Army’s main European training center this week at the annual Association of the United States Army conference in Washington, D.C. He spoke along with the commanders of the service’s other three Combat Training Centers: the Joint Readiness Training Center at Fort Polk, Louisiana; the National Training Center at Fort Irwin, California; and the Joint Pacific Multinational Readiness Center, which is headquartered in Hawaii with a major training center in Alaska. Each center is designed as a major deployment for a brigade-sized force from a visiting unit. The hometown opposition forces, or OPFOR, at each center put visiting units through a 14-day “crucible” of combat simulation, testing units from light infantry to heavy mechanized units and even special operations. Units generally have to move through the sprawling training grounds of each center — at Fort Irwin, the range is larger than Rhode Island — and seize objectives, defend them, and fight off a host of problems that the Combat Training Centers planners throw at units. Top Stories This Week News Rangers sweep the Army’s Best Squad and Best Soldier awards By Matt White News After two F-16 crashes, Air Force revamps how crews inspect a ‘blind spot’ By Matt White News Army activates its fourth multi-domain task force By Nicholas Slayton The OPFOR at each center are notorious opponents, well trained on each exercise and intimately familiar with their home terrain. As a result, Tillis said this week, “the first four of five days don’t go too well,” for visiting units. Tillis said a major lesson that the Hohenfels teams have learned in the last year has been that success with drones goes much deeper than passing out quadcopters to soldiers as they head into “the box,” as each center refers to its notional battlefield. “I thought it was all about getting kit in the hands of soldiers,” Tillis said. “Like, we gotta get 1,000s of drones and I thought the answer was, give them the technology, they’ll figure it out. But it’s not enough to give the technology because they don’t have a chance to train.” The trainers at Hohenfels, he said, now bring Ukrainian units with extensive combat experience on each crucible. “We’ve been given a lot of help, a lot of help from our Ukrainian teammates,” Tillis said. “They actually compete on both sides, the red and the blue.” Tillis and U.S. officials at Hohenfels worked with German authorities to clear up airspace permission for U.S. units to fly so much. They also began mandating that soldiers who arrived for training did so with enough experience to use them. Short-Range Air Defense vehicles with 4th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, 52nd Air Defense Artillery Brigade, prepare to move at the Joint Multinational Readiness Center in Hohenfels, Germany, Aug. 27, 2026. Army photo by Sgt. Luis Garcia. To get soldiers prepared for rotations in the U.S., units that deploy to Fort Polk, Louisiana, or Fort Irwin must now have owned and worked with any drones they want to use in their training for at least 180 days . It was working with Ukrainians, Tillis said, that made him realize that U.S. training centers had not done enough to use so-called consumable systems, the small, cheap one-way strike drones that are meant to be destroyed in use. “They came back with 40 or 50 of their actual operators and brought right around 600 systems,” Tillis said. “About 550 were consumable.” The Army’s newest center is the Joint Pacific Multinational Readiness Center, which is focused on threats “West of the International Date Line,” said Col. Alphonse J. LeMaire, the commander of the training center. “We are purpose-built for the Pacific theater,” LeMaire said at AUSA. Unlike the other centers, the Pacific training center operates in two opposite environments. The center puts on crucible training in jungle and tropical conditions on Oahu and at the Pohakuloa Training Area, Hawaii, which opened in 2021, and an Arctic center at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska, which held its first formal rotation a year later in 2022. The center also has stood up what LeMaire calls a mobile training unit in Guam. That unit, he said, puts on training events throughout Asia, including upcoming rotations with elements of the Hawaii-based 25th Infantry Division in the Philippines. Both the Alaska and Hawaii centers, he said, expect to add a company-sized reconnaissance unit to the opposing forces, to develop experts in operating as fast-moving, hard-to-spot forces in both the mountains and jungle environments. The post How the Army’s training ‘crucible’ bases are changing appeared first on Task & Purpose .

title: 'It Can Take Years': Coinbase Presses for Bitcoin Quantum Migration to Start Now
body:
Coinbase is pressing Bitcoin’s developers to begin preparing for the quantum-computing threat before it’s too late, laying out a detailed technical wish list for how the network should harden itself and arguing the work can’t wait for certainty that a threat has arrived.
In a blog post published Tuesday, the exchange, which says it custodies roughly 5% of all Bitcoin in existence, framed the shift to quantum-resistant cryptography as a complex, multi-year undertaking that needs to start now.
“Bitcoin consensus changes and ecosystem migrations can take years,” the company wrote, warning that waiting for the announcement of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer, the kind capable of breaking Bitcoin’s signatures, would leave too little time to respond.
The concern centers on how Bitcoin secures wallets. A sufficiently powerful quantum machine could, in theory, derive a private key from an exposed public key and drain the funds, a hypothetical milestone the industry calls “Q-Day.”
Coinbase stressed that a fix involves far more than picking a new signature scheme: any transition would need to protect both existing and newly created coins, fit Bitcoin’s limited block space, keep working for ordinary wallets and institutional custody alike, and offer a migration path for coins that never move.
The post reads less like a mandate than a set of requirements from one of the network’s largest stakeholders. Coinbase backed a flexible “container” design, pointing to proposals such as BIP-360, that would let new post-quantum signature systems be swapped in over time without a full redesign.
It also floated a staged “1-of-2” construction, letting the same funds be spent with either a classical key or a quantum-safe one during the transition. The company emphasized that whatever scheme Bitcoin adopts should be compatible with multi-party computation, the key-splitting technique custodians like Coinbase rely on to guard against theft.
Thornier still is the question of dormant, lost, or exposed coins, including Satoshi-era holdings, which Coinbase said should be treated as a separate governance problem. It cautioned that any rescue mechanism must itself be quantum-safe, so an attacker who only knows an exposed public key couldn’t exploit it.
The push builds on Coinbase’s steady drumbeat of quantum warnings .
The exchange convened a quantum advisory board in January o study the risks and develop precisely the sort of guidance it offered this week. The company also joined a Bitcoin Security Consortium in July alongside BlackRock and Strategy, pledging a combined $15 million toward quantum-proofing Bitcoin.
